Works are often mentioned in the **Apocalypse** <note>original: "Apocalypsis," from the Greek for "unveiling" or "revelation."</note>, but what is meant by works few know. This is known, that ten men may do works which appear alike in externals, but which are still unlike with them all, because they proceed from a different end and from a different cause; and the end and the cause make the works to be either good or evil: for every work is a work of the mind; hence such as the mind is, such is the work. If the mind is <term>charity</term><note>True charity here is defined not just as giving to the poor, but as the spiritual impulse to act with love and justice toward others.</note>, the work becomes charity; but if the mind is not charity, the work does not become charity: still both may appear alike in externals. Works appear to men in their external form, but to the angels in their internal, and to the Lord such as they are from their inmosts to their outmosts. In their external form works appear no otherwise than as fruits do on the surface, but in their internal form works appear as fruits do below the surface, where there are numberless edible parts, and in the midst the seeds, in which again are innumerable things, which are far within all sight of the eyes, and indeed, above the intellectual sphere of man. Such are all works; the internal quality of which, the Lord alone sees, and the

83. **Be mindful therefore whence thou hast fallen:** That it signifies remembrance of their error, is manifest from the things just said above.

Nevertheless, all those perform <term>meritorious works</term><note>Actions performed with the expectation of earning a reward or "points" with God, rather than out of pure love for one's neighbor.</note> who put the <term>truths of faith</term><note>The intellectual concepts and doctrines of religion.</note> in the first place and the <term>goods of charity</term><note>Practical acts of love and kindness.</note> in the second; but not those who put the goods of charity in the first place. The reason for this is that genuine charity does not wish to claim merit, for it simply loves to do good: it exists within the good act, acts from that goodness, and looks toward the Lord from it. From the light of truth, the person sees that all goodness comes from the Lord alone; on which account, they are naturally averse to the idea of merit. 

Now, since those who prioritize the truths of faith first can do no other works than those which are meritorious—yet know from their own doctrines that such an attitude is to be hated—this follows the statement that if they do not hold charity in the first place, they perform works that are held in aversion. It is said that this is against the Lord's merit and justice, for those who place merit in their own works claim justice for themselves. They argue that justice is on their side because they have "earned" it; yet this is actually the highest form of injustice, because the Lord alone has merit, and He alone is the source of the good within them. That the Lord alone is justice is taught in Jeremiah: *Behold, the days shall come, when I will raise up unto David a just branch; and this is His name which they shall call Him, Jehovah our Justice* <note>original: "Jehovah Justitia Nostra"</note> (xxiii. 5, 6; xxxiii. 15, 16).

87. ***He that hath an ear, let him hear what the Spirit saith unto the churches***, signifies that he who understands these things should obey what the Divine Truth of the Word teaches to those who will be part of the <term>New Church</term><note>A spiritual community or state of being characterized by a new, direct understanding of God and a life of active love, symbolized by the New Jerusalem.</note>, which is the New Jerusalem. By "hearing" is signified both to perceive and to obey; because a person listens so that they may understand, and once they understand, they may act. That both of these things are signified by "hearing" is evident from our common speech, in which we talk about "hearing" someone, and also "hearing" or "hearkening to" someone. The latter signifies obedience, while the former signifies perception. 

That to hear signifies both of these things is due to <term>correspondence</term><note>A foundational concept in Swedenborg’s thought where every physical thing or action reflects a specific spiritual reality.</note>; for in the <term>province of the ears</term><note>In Swedenborg's vision of the "Grand Man" (the spiritual structure of heaven), different communities of angels correspond to different parts of the human body based on their specific functions and character.</note> in heaven are those who are in a state of perception and, at the same time, in a state of obedience. <header>No. 88.] THE APOCALYPSE REVEALED.</header>

Regarding spiritual hearing, the Lord frequently said, *He that hath an ear to hear, let him hear* (Matthew 11:15; 13:43; Mark 4:9, 23; 7:16; Luke 8:8; 14:35). The same instruction is given to all the churches, as is evident from verses 11, 17, and 29 of this chapter, and from verses 6, 13, and 22 of the following one. In these verses, "the Spirit" which "speaks to the churches" signifies the <term>Divine Truth</term><note>The light of God’s wisdom and reality as it is expressed through the Word or scripture.</note> of the Word; and "the churches" represent the universal church throughout the Christian world. That "the Spirit of God"—which is also the "Holy Spirit"—means the Divine Truth proceeding from the Lord can be seen in the *Doctrine of the New Jerusalem concerning the Lord* (number 51). Because the entire church is meant, the text does not say "what the Spirit says to the church" in the singular, but rather "what the Spirit says to the churches" in the plural.

88. ***To him that overcometh*** signifies someone who struggles against their own <term>evils and falsities</term><note>Internal selfish impulses and the mistaken beliefs used to justify them.</note> and is <term>reformed</term><note>The process of having one’s mind and character reshaped by Godly principles.</note>. Since the letters to the seven churches describe the state of everyone in the Christian church who is capable of receiving the <term>doctrine of the New Jerusalem</term><note>The core spiritual teachings for a new era of faith, emphasizing love and practical living.</note> and living according to it—and who can therefore be transformed through the battle against evil and error—the phrase *He that overcometh* is addressed to each one. This is seen here with the Ephesian church: *To him that overcometh I will give to eat of the tree of life*. To the church in Smyrna: *He that overcometh shall not be hurt by the second death* (chapter 2:11). To the church in Pergamos: *To him that overcometh will I give to eat of the hidden manna* (2:17). To the church in Thyatira: *To him that overcometh, and keepeth my works unto the end, I will give power over the nations* (2:26). To the church in Sardis: *He that overcometh shall be clothed in white garments* (chapter 3:5). To the church in Philadelphia: *Him that overcometh will I make a pillar in the temple of my God* (3:12). And to the church in Laodicea: *To him that overcometh I will give to sit with Me in my throne* (<unclear>iii.</unclear> 21). In all these instances, "he that overcometh" refers to the person who battles against their own wrongdoing and false ideas and is thereby spiritually renewed.

89. ***I will give to eat of the tree of life***, signifies the <term>appropriation</term><note>The process of taking spiritual values into oneself until they become part of one’s character, similar to how the body absorbs nutrients from food.</note> of the good of love and charity from the Lord. By "eating" in the Word <note>Swedenborg uses "the Word" to refer to the Sacred Scriptures or the Bible.</note> is signified to appropriate; and by the "tree of life" is signified the Lord in respect to the good of love. Hence, by eating of the tree of life is signified the appropriation of the good of love from the Lord. The reason why "to appropriate" is signified by eating is because, just as natural food, when it is eaten, is appropriated to the life of a man’s body, so spiritual food, when it is received, is appropriated to the life of the soul.

The reason why the Lord, in terms of the good of love, is signified by the "tree of life," is because nothing else is signified by the **Tree of Life** in the garden of Eden; it is also because a person possesses heavenly and spiritual life from the good of love and charity which is received from the Lord. A tree is mentioned in many places in scripture; by it is meant a member of the church, and in a universal sense the church itself; and by its fruit is meant the good of life. This is because the Lord is the Tree of Life, from whom comes all the good found in a member of the church and in the church as a whole: but more will be said on this in its proper place. 

It is said "the good of love and charity," because the good of love is <term>celestial good</term><note>A high state of spiritual life characterized by a direct, heart-felt love for the Lord.</note>, which is that of love to the Lord; and the good of charity is <term>spiritual good</term><note>A state of spiritual life characterized by love toward one's neighbor and acting from a sense of duty or truth.</note>, which is that of love towards the neighbor. What these types of "good" are and their specific qualities will be explained in the following pages. Regarding these points, some information may be found in the work *Heaven and Hell* (numbers 13-19).

90. ***Which is in the midst of the paradise of God***, signifies interiorly in the truths of wisdom and faith. "In the midst" signifies the inmost (numbers 44, 383); here it means <term>interiorly</term><note>Deep within the inner mind or spirit, rather than on the surface of one's thoughts or actions.</note>. "The paradise of God" signifies the truths of wisdom and faith; for this reason, "the tree of life which is in the midst of the paradise of God" signifies the Lord with the good of love and charity deep within the truths of wisdom and faith. God is also present within truths; for good is the <term>being</term><note>original Latin: *esse*; the underlying essence or core of life.</note> of life, and truth is the <term>manifestation</term><note>original Latin: *existere*; the outward existence or form that arises from the underlying essence.</note> of life that comes from it.

It establishes a distinction between celestial love (for God) and spiritual love (for the neighbor).</summary>

...garden in Isaiah 58:11; 61:11; Jeremiah 31:12; Amos 9:14; and Numbers 24:6. A person of the church is also like a garden in terms of their intelligence when they are grounded in the <term>good of love</term><note>A key concept in Swedenborg’s thought, referring to the practice of doing good deeds specifically because one is motivated by love for the Lord and others.</note> from the Lord; for the spiritual heat that brings them to life is love, and spiritual light is the intelligence that flows from it. It is a known fact that gardens in our world flourish because of these two things—heat and light—and the same is true in heaven. Paradisal gardens filled with fruit trees appear in heaven, varying according to the wisdom of the inhabitants that comes from their love for the Lord. Around those who possess intelligence but lack that underlying love, no garden appears, but only grass. 91. ***And unto the angel of the church in Smyrna write***, signifies to those and concerning those who live good lives but hold false ideas regarding <term>doctrine</term><note>Religious teachings or official church beliefs.</note>. We know these are the people being described by the "church in Smyrna" through the spiritual meaning of the message written to them.

92. ***These things saith the First and the Last***, signifies the Lord, and emphasizes that He alone is God. The fact that the Lord calls Himself "the First and the Last," as well as "the Beginning and the End," "the Alpha and the Omega," and "He who is and who was and who is to come," can be seen in Chapter 1:4, 8, 11, and 17. The meaning of these titles was explained previously (see sections 13, 29-31, 38, 57), where it is clear they signify that He alone is God.

93. ***Who was dead and is alive***, signifies that He was neglected in the church, and His <term>Human</term><note>Swedenborg often uses "the Human" (Latin: *Humanum*) as a noun to refer to the physical and psychological nature of Jesus Christ.</note> was not acknowledged as Divine, even though in that Human nature He alone is Life, and from Him alone comes eternal life. The reason these things are meant by these words can be found in the previous explanations (sections 58-60). These words, along with those that come right before, are spoken because the primary mistake of the people described by this church is that they do not acknowledge the Lord’s **Divine Human**, and therefore they do not turn to Him.

94. ***I know thy works***: This signifies that the Lord sees all of a person’s <term>interiors and exteriors</term><note>In Swedenborg’s philosophy, "interiors" refers to a person's hidden motives and thoughts, while "exteriors" refers to their outward actions and speech. The Lord is said to see both simultaneously.</note> at once, which is clear from the explanations provided earlier (n. 76). In this specific context, it means He sees that they hold <term>falsities</term><note>Incorrect or misleading religious ideas, as opposed to "truths."</note>, yet they still attempt to live a <term>good</term><note>In this context, a "good" refers to an act of virtue or a positive quality of the heart.</note> life. They believe their actions are truly good, when in reality they are not.

95. ***And affliction and poverty***, signifies that they are immersed in false ideas and, as a result, lack genuine spiritual goodness. "To know their affliction" signifies seeing that they are in falsities, and "to know their poverty" signifies seeing that they are not in possession of spiritual goods. In the <term>Word</term><note>Swedenborg typically uses "the Word" to refer to the Bible, emphasizing its character as Divine revelation.</note>, "affliction" is associated with falsities (as noted in n. 33), and "poverty" refers to a lack of goodness; indeed, spiritual poverty is nothing else. We often read in the Bible of "the poor and the needy"; in the spiritual sense, "the poor" refers to someone who lacks truths, and "the needy" refers to someone who lacks goodness. The words "yet thou art rich" are added in parentheses because they are missing from certain ancient manuscripts.

96. ***And the blasphemy of them that say they are Jews, and are not***, signifies the false claim that they possess the <term>good of love</term><note>The practice of doing good specifically out of love for the Lord and one's neighbor, which Swedenborg views as the core of true religion.</note>, when they actually do not. In this instance, "blasphemy" signifies a false assertion. By "Jews," the text does not mean the Jewish people, but rather those who are in the "good of love," or the quality of love itself. Therefore, the "blasphemy of those who say they are Jews, and are not" refers to people falsely claiming to have this love. The reason "Jews" represents those in the good of love is because in the Word, "Judah" <note>original: "Judah"</note> in its highest sense refers to the Lord regarding His Divine Good (the essence of His love), while "Israel" refers to the Lord regarding His Divine Truth (the essence of His wisdom). Consequently, "Jews" signifies those who receive love from the Lord, and "Israel" signifies those who receive truth from the Lord. That "Jews" carries this meaning is evident from many passages that will be presented later (n. 350).

Consequently, good without truth is not truly good, and truth without good is not truly truth. While they may appear to be good or true in their outward form, they are not. The union of good and truth is called the **heavenly Marriage**. It is from this marriage that the church is formed within a person, and it is from this marriage that heaven exists within them. **98.** ***Fear none of the things which thou shalt suffer:*** This signifies: do not despair when you are <term>infested</term><note>In this context, to be "infested" means to be spiritually harassed or pressured by negative thoughts and impulses.</note> by evils and attacked by <term>falsities</term><note>Spiritual errors or incorrect religious concepts.</note>. **99.** ***Behold, the devil will cast some of you into prison,*** signifies that their good way of life will be harassed by evils that come from hell. The reason being "cast into prison" or confinement by "the devil" has this meaning is because "the devil" refers to the hell where people live in evil; therefore, it refers abstractly to the evil that exists there and comes from there (see note 97). To be "sent into prison" means to be infested, because those who are harassed by evils from hell feel as if they are bound in a prison. They desire to do good, yet they find they can think of nothing but evil. This causes an internal struggle and anxiety from which they cannot be released, making them feel almost as if they were in chains. 

The reason for this is that their "good" is not truly good as long as it is attached to false ideas; wherever it connects with falsity, there is an element of evil within it. This is the point that is being attacked. However, this <term>infestation</term><note>A period of spiritual trial or "cleansing" where a person's inner motives are tested.</note> does not happen in the natural world, but in the spiritual world, and thus after death. I have often been allowed to see these infestations. Those undergoing them lament, saying that they have done good and wish to do good, yet they currently cannot because of the evils surrounding them. Still, not everyone is infested in the same way; the struggle is more severe for those who have more deeply confirmed themselves in their false beliefs. This is why it says, "the devil shall cast *some of you* into prison." That the reinforcement of a false belief is harmful can be seen in the work *Doctrine of the New Jerusalem concerning the Sacred Scripture* (numbers 91-97).

**100. *That you may be tested*,** signifies being attacked by falsities fighting against you. **101.** **And you shall have affliction ten days,** signifies that this trial is to last for a full duration—that is, as long as they are willing to remain in <term>falsities</term><note>In this context, "falsities" refers to incorrect religious ideas or spiritual errors that cloud a person's judgment.</note>.

The reason "ten days" signifies a full duration of a state is because "days" signify states of life, and "ten" signifies what is full or complete. (number 154, etc.). Those who focus on good works alone, but possess no spiritual truths, are like people who act without understanding; and actions without understanding are lifeless. In the eyes of angels, they appear like images carved out of wood. Those who believe they have earned special merit through their works appear like those same carved images, but naked and without any covering. 108. ***These things says He who has the sharp two-edged sword,*** signifies the **Lord** <note>Referring to Jesus Christ as the source of divine wisdom.</note> in His role as the truths of <term>doctrine</term><note>The formal teachings or principles of the church based on the Bible.</note> from the **Word** <note>The Bible, interpreted here as containing deeper spiritual laws.</note>, by which evils and <term>falsities</term><note>Spiritual errors or mistaken beliefs that lead a person away from what is true.</note> are cleared away. 109. ***I know your works.*** This signifies that the Lord sees everything about a person—both their inner intentions and their outer actions—at the same time, as explained previously (number 76). 121. ***And I will give him a white stone***, signifies truths favoring and united to good. A "white stone" signifies this because, in ancient legal judgments, votes were collected by using stones, and white stones were used for those which were affirmative. That it is "affirmative truths" that are signified is because white is associated with truths (see sections 167, 379). 

Hence it is that by a white stone are signified truths favoring good. That they are also united to the good is because the good draws them and unites them to itself. For all good loves truth, and joins to itself whatever accords with itself, especially the good of heavenly love: this so unites truth to itself that they make altogether one. 

Hence it is that they see truths from good alone. These are meant by those who have the law written on their hearts, spoken of in the book of **Jeremiah**:

> *I will put my law in the midst of them, and will write it upon their hearts; neither shall they teach any longer every one his companion or every one his brother, saying, "know **Jehovah**" <note>The Hebrew name for God, representing the Divine Being in His aspect of pure Love.</note>; for every one shall know Me* (Jeremiah 31:33, 34).

All who are in the **third heaven** <note>The highest level of the spiritual world, characterized by a direct, heart-based perception of God’s love.</note> are such. They do not speak of truths from any memory, but see them clearly while they are hearing others speak of the truths, especially while they are reading the Word. The reason is because they are in the **marriage itself of good and truth** <note>A state of spiritual wholeness where what a person loves (good) and what a person thinks (truth) are in perfect harmony.</note>. Charity is considered a spiritual feeling because it is essentially love toward the neighbor. **Ministry** is its practical operation, because those who perform the works of charity are called "ministers" in the Word of God. 

A person who worships God is sometimes called a "servant" and sometimes a "minister." In spiritual language, a "servant of God" is someone who focuses on **truths**, while a "minister of God" is someone who lives in **goodness** <note>The original Latin "bonum" (good) here refers to the active essence of love.</note>. The reason for this distinction is that truth serves goodness, while goodness ministers to truth. That the one who focuses on truths is called a servant was shown earlier (number 3); however, that the one who lives in goodness is called a minister is evident from these passages: 

> *You shall be called the priests of Jehovah, the ministers of your God* (Isaiah 61:6). 

> *My covenant shall not become void with the Levites my ministers* (Jeremiah 33:21). 

They are called ministers because the priests represented the Lord specifically in His role as **Divine Good**.

Killing the "prophets" represents destroying the truths found in the Bible. Wanting to kill Elijah represents wanting to do the same to the Bible itself. 138. **Except she repent of her works**: This signifies that if they are not willing to stop separating faith from charity <note>In this context, "charity" refers not just to almsgiving, but to the active life of love and good works.</note>, and from falsifying the Word <note>The "Word" refers to the Sacred Scriptures or the Bible.</note>, it will lead to the consequences mentioned; this is clear without further explanation.

139. **And her sons I will kill with death**, signifies that all the truths from the Word known to them will be turned into falsities <note>A "falsity" is a technical term in this work meaning a spiritual error or a truth that has been distorted.</note>. In the Word, "sons" signify truths, and in the opposite sense, they signify falsities; therefore, "to kill sons" signifies to turn truths into falsities, for in this way they perish. This is the true meaning of the phrases "the slain" and "the pierced of Jehovah" found in Scripture. To "kill her sons with death" also signifies the condemnation of their falsities. The reason that "sons" signify truths (and "falsities" in the opposite sense) is because "generations" in the spiritual sense of the Word refer to spiritual growth. The same applies to terms of kinship and family; consequently, names like father, mother, sons, daughters, brothers, sisters, sons-in-law, and daughters-in-law represent spiritual states. From a spiritual birth, no other "sons" or "daughters" are born except truths and goods <note>See paragraphs 542 and 543 for further detail on these spiritual relationships.</note>.

140. **That all the churches may know that I am He that searcheth the reins and hearts**, signifies that the church may know that the Lord sees the specific truth and good that every person possesses. By "the seven churches," the universal church is signified, as established previously. To "search the reins and hearts" signifies to see everything a person believes and everything they love—consequently, the specific quality of their truth and their goodness. This meaning is derived from <term>correspondence</term> <note>Correspondence is the core concept in Swedenborg's writing, suggesting that every physical organ or object reflects a specific spiritual function or reality.</note>; for the literal sense of the Word consists entirely of these correspondences. The correspondence here is based on the fact that the <term>reins</term> <note>original: "renes"; an archaic term for the kidneys.</note> purify the blood from impurities (specifically those called urinous), and the heart purifies it from foul or unclean things. In the same way, the truth of faith purifies a person from falsities, and the good of love purifies them from evils. Because of this, the ancients associated love and—

But because they do not love the truth, nor justice, nor can be so far enlightened as to know what truth and justice are, they are therefore, after some days, deposed. I have seen such ones transferred from one society to another, and an administration given to them everywhere, but after a short time as often deposed.

**VII.** After frequent dismissions, some from weariness do not wish, and some from fear of the loss of reputation do not dare, to seek for offices any more; on which account they withdraw, and sit sad: and they are then led away into a desert, where there are huts, which they enter; and there some work is given them to do: and as they do it, they receive food; and if they do not do it, they are hungry, and receive none; on which account necessity compels them. The food there is similar to the food in our world; but it is from a **spiritual origin**, and is given from heaven by the Lord to all, according to the **uses** <term>uses: meaningful actions or work that benefit others; Swedenborg emphasizes that the heart of heaven is being useful</term> which they do.

**VIII.** After some time, they become disgusted with work and leave their huts. If they were **priests** in the world, they often feel a desire to build. Immediately, there appear piles of hewn stones, bricks, beams and boards of wood, as well as heaps of reeds and rushes, clay, lime, and **bitumen** <term>bitumen: a naturally occurring tar or asphalt used as mortar in ancient times, symbolizing a binding material that lacks spiritual life</term>. When they see these materials, their desire to build is ignited. They begin to construct a house, picking up a stone, then a timber, then a reed, then mud, putting them one upon another without any real order—though in their own minds, it seems orderly.

However, whatever they build during the day collapses during the night. The following day, they gather what has fallen from the rubbish and try to build again. This cycle continues until they grow weary of building. This happens because they had previously "heaped together" **falsities** <term>falsities: distorted or incorrect religious principles that lack the light of truth</term> to justify the doctrine of **salvation by faith alone** <term>faith alone: the belief that intellectual belief or trust in God is sufficient for salvation, excluding the necessity of a life of active charity</term>. Just as their theological systems are built on unstable ground, their spiritual "houses" have no structural integrity and cannot stand.

**IX.** Eventually, worn out by their failures, they go away and sit in solitary idleness. Because food is not provided from heaven to those who are idle, they begin to suffer from hunger and can think of nothing else but how to satisfy it. While in this state, they are approached by others whom they beg for **alms** <note>original: "eleemosynas," referring to charitable donations or handouts</note>. These newcomers ask, “Why do you sit here idle? Come with us to our houses; we will give you work to do and feed you.”

They rise up gladly and follow them to their houses, where each is assigned a task and given food in exchange for their labor. However, because those who have confirmed themselves in the **falsities** of faith cannot perform works of **good use** <term>use: the principle that a person’s spiritual value is found in being useful to others and society</term>, they only perform "evil uses." Even then, they do not work faithfully; they only work to maintain an appearance for the sake of honor or profit. Soon, they abandon their work and prefer only to socialize, talk, walk about, and sleep. Because they can no longer be persuaded by their masters to work, they are eventually cast out as useless.

Such is the lot of those who have set aside the life of **charity** <term>charity: the active love of the neighbor expressed through useful service and good works</term>, and hence have not lived it in the world.

As regards the **hells** in general, they consist of nothing but such caverns and workhouses, but those of the **satans** differ from those of the **devils**. The **satans** are they who were in **falsities** <term>falsities: distorted concepts or intellectual lies that a person uses to justify their actions</term> and from those into **evils**, and the **devils** are they who were in **evils** <term>evils: malicious intentions or selfish desires of the heart</term> and from those into **falsities**. 

The satans appear in the **light of heaven** <note>original: "luce coeli"; in Swedenborg’s thought, the light of heaven is Divine Truth, which acts like an X-ray, revealing the true spiritual state of a person regardless of their outward appearance</note> like corpses, and some black like mummies; and the devils in the light of heaven appear dark and fiery, and some coal-black, like soot: yet all, as to their faces and bodies, appear as **monsters**; but in their own light, which is like the light from **burning coals** <note>This "coal-fire" light represents the heat of their own self-love and lusts, which provides them a distorted kind of vision</note>, they appear not as monsters, but as men. This is given to them in order that they may be able to associate together.

<summary>This page defines the two primary categories of inhabitants in the hells—satans and devils—distinguishing them by whether their corruption began in the mind or the heart. It describes how the light of heaven reveals their inner monstrous nature, while their own dim light allows them to maintain a human appearance to one another.</summary>

# THE APOCALYPSE REVEALED.

...manifest from the things written to it when understood in the <term>spiritual sense: the deeper, symbolic meaning of the Bible that relates to the soul's inner life</term>. By **dead worship** is meant worship alone—which is to frequent churches, to hear the preachings, to come to the <term>Holy Supper: the sacrament of the Eucharist or Communion</term>, to read the Word and books of piety, to speak of God, of heaven and hell, of the life after death, and especially of piety, to pray morning and evening; and still not to desire to know the truths of faith, nor to wish to do the goods of <term>charity: the active love for one's neighbor through useful service</term>, believing that they have salvation through worship alone. 

Whereas worship without truths, and without a life according to them, is only the external sign of charity and faith, within which there can lie hidden evils and falsities of every kind, if charity and faith are not in it. Genuine worship consists of these: or else worship is like the skin or outside of a fruit, within which there lies hidden a rotten and worm-eaten pulp, which fruit is dead. That such worship is prevalent at this day is known.

**155.** *These things saith He that hath the seven spirits of God and the seven stars,* signifies the Lord from whom are all truths, and all knowledges of good and truth. That by "the seven spirits of God" is meant the **Divine Truth** proceeding from the Lord, or the **Divine Verity**, may be seen above (n. 14); and that by "the seven stars" are meant all the knowledges of good and truth from the Word (n. 51), from which is the church in heaven (n. 65). Those things are now said by the Lord, because dead worship and living worship are treated of; and worship has life from truths, and from a life according to them.

**156.** *I know thy works,* signifies that the Lord sees all their <term>interiors: a person's inner thoughts, motives, and intentions</term> and <term>exteriors: a person's outward actions and speech</term> at once; as above (n. 76).

**157.** *That thou hast a name that thou livest, and art dead,* signifies that it seems to themselves and to others, and is believed by themselves and by others, that they are spiritually alive, when yet they are spiritually dead. By "having a name" is signified to seem and to be believed to be such; here that they are alive, when yet they are dead. For...

# THE APOCALYPSE REVEALED. [CHAPTER III]

**spiritual life** <term>spiritual life: the inner state of the soul that is truly "alive" because it is connected to God through both belief and action</term>, which properly is life, is not found in worship alone, but is located within worship. Within the ritual, there must be **Divine Truths** <note>original: "Veritates Divinae"</note> from the Word <note>the Bible</note>; and when a person lives according to them, there is life in their worship. The reason for this is that the external appearance of something takes its quality from its internal contents; and the internals of worship are the truths of one's life.

These are the people meant by these words of the Lord: *Then shall ye begin to stand without, and to knock at the door, saying, Lord, open unto us: but He, answering, shall say, I know you not whence ye are. And ye shall begin to say, We have eaten before thee, and drank before thee; and thou hast taught in our streets: but I will say unto you, I know you not whence ye are; depart from me, all ye workers of iniquity* (Luke xiii. 25-27). 

It has also been granted to me to hear many in the **spiritual world** <note>the realm where souls transition after death before heaven or hell</note> saying that they have very often attended **Holy Communion** <note>the sacrament of the Eucharist or Lord’s Supper</note>, and thus have "eaten and drank the holy thing," and have just as often been absolved from their sins; they claimed they listened every **Sabbath-day** <note>the day set aside for rest and religious observance</note> to those who taught, and prayed devoutly morning and evening at home; among other things. 

But when the interiors <note>the inner motivations and secret thoughts</note> of their worship were laid open, they appeared full of iniquities and hellish; for this reason, they were rejected. And when they asked, "Why is this happening?" they received the answer that they were not at all concerned about Divine truths; and yet a life not lived according to Divine truths is not "life," at least not the kind they have in heaven. *to die*, signifies, in order that the things which are of their worship may receive life, and not be extinguished. Because of this, those who are in dead worship need nothing more than to learn truths and live according to them. In this way, the remaining things that are "ready to die" are strengthened.

160. ***For I have not found thy works full before God***, signifies that the **interiors** <term>interiors: the inner motivations, thoughts, and intentions of a person's heart and mind</term> of their worship are not **conjoined** <term>conjunction: a spiritual connection or union between a person and the Lord</term> to the Lord. That by "works" are meant both the interiors and **exteriors** <note>outward actions and behaviors</note>, and that by "I know thy works" is meant that the Lord sees all of a person’s inner and outer life at once, may be seen above (n. 76); these are called "full before God" when they are conjoined to the Lord. It must be understood that dead worship, or worship that is only external, creates a *presence* of the Lord but not *conjunction*; however, external worship in which the interiors are alive creates both presence and conjunction. This is because the conjunction of the Lord is with those things in a person which are *from* the Lord—which are truths originating in **good** <term>good: the impulse of love and charity that motivates a person's actions</term>. Unless these are present in worship, the works are not "full before God," but are empty. In the **Word** <note>the Holy Scriptures or Bible</note>, a person is called "empty" if there is nothing within them but falsities and evils, as seen in Matthew 12:44 and elsewhere. Conversely, a person is called "full" when they contain truths and goods.

161. ***Remember therefore how thou hast received and heard***, signifies that it should be brought to their attention that all worship is **natural** <term>natural: focused on the physical world, self-interest, or basic external rules</term> in its beginning, and afterwards becomes **spiritual** <term>spiritual: focused on eternal life, love for others, and the light of divine truth</term> through truths from the Word and a life lived according to them; and more besides. These are the things meant by these words, as it is also true that everyone knows from the Word and from the doctrine of the church...

Evils and **falsities** <term>falsities: mistaken beliefs that lead one away from a good life</term> take this outward good away like a thief. This happens gradually while in this world, and completely after death, often without the person realizing how the loss occurred. Although the text says the *Lord* comes as a thief, in the **spiritual sense** <note>the deeper, symbolic meaning of the Bible</note>, it actually means that **hell** is what takes and steals it. 166. **Who have not defiled their garments**, signifies those who live in **truths** <term>truths: spiritual principles and ideas from the Word that provide light to the mind</term>, and have not corrupted their worship with the evils of life and the **falsities** <term>falsities: distorted or incorrect spiritual beliefs that arise from a selfish or worldly life</term> that spring from them. 

In the Word <note>Swedenborg uses "the Word" to refer specifically to the Sacred Scriptures/the Bible</note>, **garments** signify the truths that "clothe" what is good; in the opposite sense, they signify the falsities that "clothe" what is evil. This is because a person, in their essence, is either their own good or their own evil; therefore, truths or falsities are the "clothing" that surrounds that essence. All angels and spirits appear dressed according to the truths of their "good," or according to the falsities of their "evil." For more on this subject, see the work *Heaven and Hell*, published in London (numbers 177–182). 

From this it is clear that "not defiling their garments" means to remain in truths and not to pollute one's worship with bad living or the false ideas resulting from it. That garments signify truths in the Word (and falsities in the opposite sense) is evident from these passages: 

*Awake, awake, put on thy strength, O Zion; put on the garments of thy comeliness, O Jerusalem* (Isaiah 52:1). 

*O Jerusalem, I have clothed thee with needlework, I have shod thee with badger’s skin, I have girded thee with fine linen, and adorned thee with ornaments; thou art arrayed in gold and silver, and thy garments are fine linen, silk, and needlework, whence thou hast become exceedingly beautiful. But thou hast taken off thy garments, and hast adorned thy high places with various colors, that thou mightest commit whoredom upon them; thou hast also taken thy garments of needlework, and hast made images of a male, with which thou committedst whoredom* (Ezekiel 16:10–18). 

The **Jewish church** is described here—that it was given truths because it possessed the Word, but that its people falsified those truths. In this context, to **commit whoredom** <note>original: "scortari"</note> means to falsify or corrupt spiritual truths. 

*The king’s daughter is all glorious within, and her clothing is of woven gold; in needlework shall she be brought to the king* (Psalm 45:13, 14). 

"The king's daughter" represents the church in its affection for truth. 

*Daughters of Israel, weep over Saul, who arrayed you in double-dyed scarlet with delicacies, and put an ornament of gold upon your garment* (2 Samuel 1:24). 

This is said of Saul because, in his role as king, he signifies **Divine Truth** <note>the light of God's wisdom as it is revealed to humanity</note>.

He uses various Old Testament passages to show how beautiful clothing represents pure truth, while stained or misused clothing represents truth that has been corrupted by a bad life.</summary>

167. **And they shall walk with me in white**, signifies that they shall live with the Lord in His spiritual kingdom, because they are in truths from Him. Those who are in truths from the Lord are called "worthy" because they are joined to Him; for all worthiness in the spiritual world comes from this connection with the Lord. It is clear from these points that the phrase "they shall walk with me in white, for they are worthy" means they shall live with the Lord because they receive truths from Him. It is said that they shall live with the Lord in His spiritual kingdom because the whole of heaven is divided into two kingdoms: the **heavenly** <note>original: "celestial"—the kingdom characterized by the good of love</note> and the **spiritual** <note>the kingdom characterized by the truths of wisdom</note>. 

In the heavenly kingdom are those who live in the "good of love" from the Lord, and in the spiritual kingdom are those who live in the "truths of wisdom" from the Lord. These latter inhabitants are said to "walk with the Lord in white," and they are indeed seen wearing white garments in the spiritual world. That "to walk" signifies to live, and "to walk with God" signifies to live with Him (because life flows from Him), is evident from the following passages:
> **He walked with Me in peace and rectitude** (Malachi 2:6). 
> **Thou hast delivered my feet from stumbling, that I may walk before God in the light of the living** (Psalm 56:13).

# 173. **These things saith He that is Holy, He that is True**, signifies the Lord as to the **Divine Truth** <note>The wisdom and laws of order that radiate from God.</note>. Hence it is that His proceeding Divine, which is the Divine Truth, is called the **Holy Spirit**; and the Holy Spirit is here "He that is Holy, He that is True." “Holy” is very often mentioned in the Word, and everywhere with reference to Truth; and because all truth, which is truth in itself, is from good, and from the Lord, it is that truth which is called holy: but good, from which the truth is, is called “Just.” 

Hence it is, that the angels who are in the truths of wisdom, and are called **spiritual** <note>Those whose primary focus is on understanding and applying wisdom.</note> are said to be **holy**, and the angels who are in the good of love, and are called **heavenly** (**celestial**) <note>The highest rank of angels, who act directly from a heart of love rather than through reasoning.</note>, are said to be **just**; and the same of men in the church. It is hence also, that the prophets and apostles are called **holy**; for by prophets and apostles the truths of the doctrine of the church are signified. Hence also it is, that the Word is called **Holy**; for the Word is the Divine Truth: also that the Law in the Ark in the **Tabernacle** <note>The portable dwelling place of God's presence during the Exodus.</note> was called “the **Holy of Holies**,” and also “the **Sanctuary**.” 

It is also from this that **Jerusalem** is called holy; for by Jerusalem is signified the church which is in Divine truths. It is also from the same cause that the altar, the tabernacle, and the garments of Aaron and his sons, were called holy, after they had been anointed with oil; for oil signifies the **good of love**, and this **sanctifies** <note>To make something holy or set it apart for God's service.</note>: and every sanctified thing has reference to truth. That the Lord is alone Holy, because He is the Divine Truth itself, is manifest from these passages:

> *Who shall not glorify thy name, O Lord, because thou alone art Holy?* (Apoc. xv. 4).

But on this subject, something not previously known shall be explained. The Lord alone is the God of heaven and earth (Matthew 28:18); therefore, those who do not go directly to Him do not see the way to heaven and, consequently, do not find the door. Even if they are permitted to approach it, it remains shut and is not opened to the one who knocks. 

In the spiritual world, there are actually paths that lead to heaven, and there are gates here and there; those who are led to heaven by the Lord travel the paths that lead there and enter through those gates. That there are paths there may be seen in the work *Heaven and Hell* (sections 479, 534, 590), as well as gates (sections 429, 430, 583, 584). Everything beheld in the heavens exists through <term>correspondences</term> <note>The spiritual law where inner realities, like thoughts and feelings, are mirrored by outward, visible surroundings.</note>; this includes the paths and the gates. Paths correspond to and signify truths, while gates correspond to and signify entrance. 

Since the Lord alone leads humanity to heaven and opens the door, He calls Himself "the Way" and "the Door." He is called "the Way" in the Gospel of John: *I am the Way, the Truth, and the Life* (14:6); and "the Door" in the same Gospel: *I am the Door of the sheep; by Me if any one enter in, he shall be saved* (10:7, 9). Because there are both paths and doors in the spiritual world, and angelic spirits actually walk those paths and pass through those doors when they enter heaven, doors, gates, and portals are frequently mentioned in the Word <note>Swedenborg uses "the Word" to refer specifically to the Sacred Scriptures.</note>, where they signify entrance. This can be seen in the following passages: 

*Lift up your heads, O ye gates; lift up, ye doors of the world; that the King of glory may come in* (Psalm 24:7, 9). 

*Open ye the gates, that the just nation that doeth truth may come in* (Isaiah 26:2). 

*The five prudent virgins went in to the wedding and the door was shut: and the five foolish virgins came, and knocked; but it was not opened* (Matthew 25:10–12). 

*Jesus said, Strive to enter in through the strait gate; because many shall seek to enter in, and shall not be able* (Luke 13:24–25; as well as other places).

182. ***Them that say they are Jews, and are not, but do lie*** signifies those who claim that the church is with them, when in fact there is no church among them. Those who belong to the church are symbolized here by "Jews" because the church was originally established among them; for this same reason, their city, **Jerusalem**, signifies the Church in regard to its <term>doctrine</term> <note>The body of teachings or principles held and taught by the church.</note>. This refers to people who are in <term>falsities of doctrine</term> but not <term>falsities from evil</term> <note>A crucial distinction in this theology: being "wrong" about a fact or teaching is different from "choosing a lie" to justify bad behavior. The former can be corrected by a good heart.</note>; they have incorrect beliefs but still lead a good life. These people, unlike those with evil intentions, receive and acknowledge truths when they hear them. The reason for this is that "good loves truth," and truth derived from a good heart naturally rejects what is false. To receive and acknowledge these truths is signified by "coming and worshipping at thy feet." This does not mean worshipping at the feet of men, but at the Lord’s feet, for it is from Him that they receive truth joined with good. This is why the same idea is expressed in the Psalms of David: *Exalt Jehovah our God, and worship at his footstool* <note>original: "Ps. xcix. 5"</note> (Psalm 99:5).

187. ***Behold, I come quickly***, signifies the Lord's coming, and then a <term>New Church</term> <note>Specifically the "New Jerusalem," a state of direct spiritual connection with the Divine that Swedenborg believed was beginning in his time.</note> from these. The Lord said here, "Behold, I come quickly," because by the words just preceding, the last judgment is meant; and the last judgment is also called the Lord's coming, as in Matthew: *The disciples said to Jesus, What shall be the sign of thy coming, and of the <term>consummation of the age</term>?* <note>original: "consummatio saeculi." Traditionally translated as "end of the world," but interpreted here as the end of a specific religious era or "church."</note> (xxiv. 3). The consummation of the age is the last time of the church, when a last judgment takes place. That by the words, "Behold, I come quickly," is also meant a new church, is because after a last judgment the church is re-established by the Lord. That church is now the **New Jerusalem**, into which those are to come who are in truths from good from the Lord, to whom this saying is addressed.

On which account wisdom perishes with a man when he ceases to do the truths, that is, to live according to them: he then also ceases to love wisdom, consequently the Lord. By wisdom is meant wisdom in spiritual things. From this as a fountain is derived wisdom in other things, which is called <term>intelligence</term> <note>Intelligence refers to the ability to perceive how truths relate to the world and to one's own life, acting as a bridge between spiritual wisdom and daily knowledge.</note>; and by means of this, knowledge, which is from the affection for knowing truths. Nor does a king's crown signify any thing else: for a <term>king</term> <note>In the "science of correspondences," a king symbolizes the Divine Truth, because truth is what governs and rules the mind.</note> in the spiritual sense is the Divine Truth (number 20); and from the Divine Truth is all wisdom. 192. ***And he shall no more go out***: This signifies that they will remain there forever, which is clear without further explanation.

193. ***And I will write upon him the name of my God***: This signifies that the **Divine Truth** <note>The wisdom or light that flows from God into the human mind.</note> will be written in their hearts. To "write upon anyone" signifies to engrave or inscribe something so that it becomes a part of them; and "the name of my God" signifies the Divine Truth. We should mention here why the phrase "my God" refers specifically to Divine Truth. In countless places in the Old Testament, the phrase **JEHOVAH GOD** is used; it is also used separately, sometimes as "JEHOVAH" and sometimes as "GOD." By **JEHOVAH** is meant the Lord in terms of His **Divine Good** <note>The quality of God’s love and mercy.</note>, and by **GOD** is meant the Lord in terms of His **Divine Truth**. Or, to put it another way, by JEHOVAH is meant the Lord’s **Divine Love**, and by GOD His **Divine Wisdom**. Both are mentioned together because of the **heavenly marriage** <note>The perfect union of love and wisdom, or goodness and truth, which exists in everything created by God.</note> found in every part of the Word; this is the marriage of love and wisdom, or the marriage of good and truth; regarding this marriage, see the work *Doctrine of the New Jerusalem concerning the Sacred Scripture* (n. 80-90).

When Jerusalem signifies the Church, these details can signify nothing else but the components of its doctrine. It is from doctrine, and nothing else, that a church is a church. Because the church, in respect to its doctrine, is meant by the city Jerusalem, it is therefore called the *City of Truth* (Zechariah 8:3, 4) and in many places *the holy city*; and this is because "holy" is predicated of truths that come from the Lord (n. 173).

### 199. *These things saith the Amen, the faithful and true Witness*
signifies the Lord as to the **Word** <term>the Word</term><note>A central concept in this theology referring to Divine Truth or the Bible, viewed as the living presence of God's wisdom on earth.</note>, which is the **Divine Truth** from Him. That "**Amen**" <note>original: "Amen." A Hebrew term meaning truth or certainty, used here as a title for the Lord to signify that He is Truth itself.</note> is the Divine confirmation from the truth itself, which is the Lord, and thus from the Lord, may be seen above (n. 23): and that "the faithful and true witness," when speaking of the Lord, is the **Divine Truth** which is from Him in the **Word** (n. 6, 16). Whether you say that the Lord testifies of Himself, or that the **Word** testifies of Him, it is the same; since the **SON OF MAN** <note>A title for Jesus emphasizing His role as the personification of the Word and the teacher of Truth.</note>, who here speaks to the Churches, is the Lord as to the **Word** (n. 44). These things are premised to this church, because those in the church are here treated of, who believe both from themselves and from the **Word**; and they who believe from the **Word**, believe from the Lord.

signifies the **Word**. The **Divine Truth** is the **Word**; and therefore, when the Lord calls Himself "the **Word**," He also calls Himself "the **Light**" (John i. 4, 8, 9). The same idea is expressed by David: *By the Word of Jehovah* <note>original: "Word of Jehovah." **211. I counsel thee to buy of Me gold tried in the fire, that thou mayest be rich**, signifies admonition to procure to themselves the good of love from the Lord through <term>the Word</term><note>The Word refers to the Sacred Scripture, which Swedenborg views as the direct source of divine truth.</note>, that they may be wise. For "to buy" signifies to procure to one's self; "of Me" signifies from the Lord through the Word; "gold" signifies good, and "gold tried in the fire" the good of heavenly love; and to be enriched therefrom signifies to understand and be wise. 

The reason that gold signifies good, is because the metals in their order signify such things as are of good and truth; gold signifies heavenly <note>original: "celestial"</note> and spiritual good, silver the truth of those goods, brass natural good, and iron natural truth. These are signified by the metals of which the statue of Nebuchadnezzar consisted, *the head of which was gold, the breast and arms silver, the belly and thighs brass, the legs iron, and the feet part iron and part clay* (Daniel 2:32, 33); by which are represented the successive states of the church as to the good of love and the truth of wisdom. 

Because the states of the church succeeded each other in this manner, the ancients therefore gave similar names to the periods, calling them the golden, the silver, the brazen, and the iron ages; and by the golden age they meant the first period, when the good of heavenly love reigned. Heavenly love is love to the Lord from the Lord: from this love they then had wisdom. That gold signifies the good of love, see below (n. 913).

**212. And white garments, that thou mayest be clothed**, signifies that they should procure for themselves the genuine truths of wisdom. **213. That the shame of thy nakedness do not appear**, signifies lest the good of heavenly love should be profaned and adulterated. No one can know what "the shame of nakedness" signifies, except he who knows that the members of generation in both sexes, which are also called the genitals, correspond to heavenly love. That there is a <term>correspondence</term><note>Correspondence is a central concept in Swedenborg's thought, meaning that every physical thing in the world acts as a mirror or "correspondent" to a spiritual reality.</note> of man and all his members with the heavens, may be seen in the work on "Heaven and Hell," published at London in the year 1758 (n. 87-102); and that the genital members correspond to heavenly love in the "Heavenly Arcana" <note>original: "Arcana Coelestia"</note>, also published at London (n. 5050-5062). 

Now because those members correspond to heavenly love, which is the love of the third or inmost heaven, and a man is born of his parents into loves opposite to that love, it is manifest that if he does not procure to himself from the Lord the good of love and the truth of wisdom, which are signified by the gold tried in the fire, and by the white garments, he must appear in the opposite love, which in itself is profane. This is signified by "uncovering the nakedness," and "manifesting the shame of it," in the following passages: 

> *Blessed is he that watcheth and keepeth his garments, lest he walk naked, and they see his shame* (Apocalypse xvi. 15). *Daughter of Babylon and of Chaldea, sit on the earth; uncover thy locks, uncover the thigh, pass over the streams; let thy nakedness be uncovered, and let thy reproach also be seen* (Isaiah xlvii. 1-3). *Woe to the city of bloods* <note>original: "urbs sanguinum," a literal translation of the Hebrew idiom for a city characterized by violence or spiritual corruption.</note>, *because of the multitude of her whoredoms: I will uncover the skirts upon thy face, and will show the nations thy nakedness, and the kingdoms thy disgrace* (Nahum iii. 1, 4, 5). *Contend with your mother, lest perchance I set her naked* (Hosea ii. 2-4). *When I passed by thee, I covered thy nakedness, and washed thee, and clothed thee: but thou committedst whoredom; not recollecting thy youth, when thou wast naked* <note>The author is quoting Ezekiel 16:8, 9, 22 here, which describes the spiritual history of the church.</note>.

An angel answered, "It was not implanted, because to do of one's self belongs to God alone; but it is continually given, that is, continually adjoined: and so far as the man then does good and believes truth

On hearing these things, some of the company said, “These things we understand.” But a voice was heard from the side, crying, “We do not understand;” and another voice, “We do not wish to understand.” When it was asked from whom those voices came, it was found that they were from those who had confirmed themselves in the falsities of faith, and who wished to be regarded as oracles, and thus to be adored. The angels said, “Do not wonder; there are very many such at this day. To us in heaven, they appear like carved images, made with such art that they can move their lips and make sounds like musical organs; yet they do not know whether the breath by which they sound is from hell or from heaven, because they do not know whether a thing is false or true. They reason and reason; they also confirm and confirm; yet they never see whether a thing actually *is* so. But you may know...”

### THE EXPLANATION.

225. *After these things I saw, and behold, a door opened in heaven*, signifies a manifestation concerning the arrangement of the heavens by the Lord for the last judgment, which is to be executed according to His Divine truths in the Word. By a door opened, when speaking of heaven, is signified admittance <note>original: "introitus"; the act of entering or being allowed access to a spiritual state or place.</note>, as above (n. 176); here also manifestation, because he says, "I saw, and behold." And because the things were then seen that are related in this chapter, which are concerning the arrangement of the heavens for the last judgment by the Lord, to be executed according to His Divine truths in the Word, therefore by "I saw, and behold, a door opened in heaven," a manifestation concerning those things is signified.

## THE APOCALYPSE REVEALED. [CHAP. IV.

**226.** *And the first voice which I heard, as of a trumpet speaking with me, said, Come up hither;* signifies the Divine influx <term>Divine influx<note>The constant flow of life, wisdom, and love from God into the human soul and the created world.</note></term>, and the resulting elevation of the mind, which leads to a clear and manifest perception of spiritual truths. That a voice heard from heaven represents the Divine Truth flowing in may be seen in the earlier explanations (sections 37 and 50), and thus represents the Divine influx. That "a voice like a trumpet" signifies a clear and manifest perception can also be seen above (section 37); and "come up hither" signifies the elevation of the mind.

In the spiritual world <note>According to the author, the spiritual world is a real dimension where people go after death, and its environment reflects their internal state of mind.</note>, the higher a person's consciousness ascends, the purer the light they enter. In this light, the understanding is opened by degrees; in other words, the mind is raised to a higher level. This is why the text says the observer was then "in the spirit," meaning he was brought into a spiritual state where heavenly things appear clearly. 

The reason this voice sounded like a trumpet is that this section deals with the arrangement of the heavens for the Last Judgment <note>In this context, the Last Judgment refers to a spiritual reorganization of heaven and the church, which the author believes took place in the spiritual world.</note>. Voices like trumpets are heard in heaven whenever gatherings and organizational changes are being made. For this reason, among the ancient Israelites—whose rituals were symbolic of heaven and the church—it was commanded that trumpets of silver be made. The sons of *Aaron* <term>Aaron<note>The brother of Moses and the first High Priest, representing the Lord's leadership and the quality of love in the church.</note></term> were to sound these trumpets for callings to assembly, for beginning journeys, on days of celebration, during festivals, at the start of each month, over sacrifices as a memorial, and for war (Numbers 10:1–10). However, trumpets and their sounding will be discussed further in the explanation of the eighth chapter, which describes the seven angels given seven trumpets.

**227.** *And I will show thee the things which must be hereafter,* signifies revelations concerning what will happen before the Last Judgment, concerning the judgment itself, and what follows after it. These things are signified because the primary subject of the Apocalypse <term>Apocalypse<note>From the Greek 'apokalypsis,' meaning an 'unveiling' or 'revelation.' It refers here to the Book of Revelation.</note></term> is the state of the church at its final stage. Therefore, it focuses on the events leading up to the Last Judgment, the judgment itself, and the state of the church following those events, as was mentioned previously (section 2).

It also identifies the main theme of the Book of Revelation as the spiritual transition surrounding the Last Judgment.</summary>

# THE APOCALYPSE REVEALED. [No. 229]

**228.** ***And immediately I was in the spirit***, signifies that he was let into a spiritual state, in which the things that exist in heaven manifestly appear. To "be in the spirit" means to be brought into a spiritual state through a <term>Divine influx<note>The author uses this term to describe the way God’s life, wisdom, and love flow into the human soul, similar to how light and heat flow from the sun.</note></term>. In this spiritual state, a person is able to see the inhabitants and objects of the spiritual world just as clearly as one sees the physical world while in the body. This state and its specific qualities were discussed previously (in section 36).

**229.** ***And behold, a throne was set in heaven***, signifies the judgment in a <term>representative form<note>In this context, a "representative" is a physical-looking symbol in a vision that stands for a deeper spiritual reality or a future event.</note></term>. While a "throne" can signify heaven itself (as seen in section 14), it is clear from the following passages that a throne also signifies the act of judgment:

*   *When the Son of Man shall come in His glory, and all the holy angels with Him, then shall He sit upon the throne of His glory* (Matthew 25:31). This passage refers to the <term>Last Judgment<note>The author interprets the Last Judgment not as the end of the physical world, but as a spiritual reorganization of heaven and the church.</note></term>.
*   *O Jehovah, thou hast judged me, thou sattest upon the throne a judge of justice. Jehovah will prepare His throne for judgment* (Psalms 9:4, 7, 8). 
*   *I saw when the Ancient of Days <note>A title for God emphasizing His eternal nature.</note> did sit; His throne was as a flame of fire; a thousand and thousands ministered unto Him, and a myriad of myriads stood before Him: the judgment was in session and the books were opened* (Daniel 7:9, 10). 
*   *Jerusalem is built; thither the tribes go up; and there are set thrones for judgment* (Psalms 122:3, 5). 
*   *I saw thrones, and they sat upon them, and judgment was given unto them* (Revelation 20:4). 

The throne built by King Solomon (mentioned in 1 Kings 10:18–20) also signified both a kingdom and the seat of judgment, because in ancient times, kings sat upon thrones specifically when they were performing their judicial duties.

It is stated that the throne signifies judgment in a *representative form* because the things John witnessed were visions. These visions were seen exactly as he described them—with animals, a dragon, beasts, a temple, and an ark—but they functioned as symbols representing things that would happen in the future. Similar symbolic visions were experienced by the ancient prophets, as mentioned before (in section 36).

<summary>This page explains that being "in the spirit" allows for clear sight of the spiritual world and identifies the "throne in heaven" as a symbolic representation of God's judgment.</summary>

# THE APOCALYPSE REVEALED. [CHAP. IV.]

**230.** ***And upon the throne One sitting***, signifies the Lord. This is clearly shown by what follows and by various passages in the Word <note>The "Word" is the author’s term for the Bible.</note> where it is stated that the Lord is the one who will carry out judgment. For example:

*   *When the Son of Man shall come in His glory... then shall He sit upon the throne of His glory... and He shall separate them one from another* (Matthew 25:31, 32).
*   *For the Father judgeth no man, but hath committed all judgment unto the Son... and hath given Him authority to execute judgment also, because He is the Son of Man* (John 5:22, 27).

**231.** ***And He that sat was in appearance like a jasper and a sardine stone***, signifies the appearance of the Lord's Divine Wisdom and Divine Love in <term>ultimates<note>In this system of thought, "ultimates" refer to the most external or physical level of reality, which serves as the foundation for spiritual things. In the context of the Bible, the "ultimate" is the literal, written word.</note></term>. A "stone" in the Word signifies truth in its most basic, foundational form; a "precious stone" signifies truth that is transparent because of the "good" or love within it (as seen in section 915).

In the spiritual world, there are two primary colors from which all others originate: white and red. 

1.  **White** comes from the light of the Sun in heaven. This is spiritual light, which is a brilliant white.
2.  **Red** comes from the fire of that same Sun. This is <term>heavenly (celestial) light<note>The author distinguishes between "spiritual" (relating to the intellect and wisdom) and "celestial" (relating to the heart and love). Red light represents the warmth of love.</note></term>, which has a flame-like quality.

The spiritual angels, who focus on the truths of wisdom from the Lord, live in that bright-white light and wear white clothing. The heavenly angels, who focus on the "goods" of love from the Lord, live in that flamy light and wear red clothing.

Because of this, precious stones in heaven reflect these two colors. They signify things belonging either to the truth of wisdom or the good of love. 

*   The **Jasper**, because it is a brilliant white, represents the truths of wisdom. 
*   The **Sardius** <note>original: "sardius", also called a sardine stone or carnelian.</note>, because it is red, represents the goods of love.

These stones represent the Divine Wisdom and Divine Love in their most external form ("ultimates") because all precious stones in heaven actually originate from the literal sense of the Word. Their inner glow or transparency comes from the spiritual meaning hidden within that literal text. This concept is explained further in the *Doctrine of the New Jerusalem concerning the Sacred Scripture* (sections 44 and 45). The foundation of the Word—its literal stories and laws—are the "goods and truths" that create the appearance of these gems in heaven, though this is a concept many find difficult to believe.

<summary>This page identifies the figure on the throne as the Lord in His role as Judge and explains that the jasper and sardius stones symbolize His Divine Wisdom and Love as they appear in the literal foundation of the Word.</summary>

# THE APOCALYPSE REVEALED. [CHAP. IV.]

**231.** [Continued] ...by anyone in our world, because people do not generally know that everything existing in the spiritual world consists of <term>correspondences<note>The author’s core concept that every physical object or appearance is a direct reflection of a specific spiritual reality or "origin."</note></term>, and that everything in the natural world derives its spiritual origin from them. That this is the origin of precious stones in heaven is something I have been allowed to know through conversations with angels and to see with my own eyes; however, their actual formation comes from the Lord alone. 

By contrast, black colors derive their origin from hell. There are two types of blackness: 
1.  The one opposite to white: This blackness is found with those who have falsified the truths of the Word <note>The "Word" refers to the Sacred Scriptures or Bible.</note>.
2.  The one opposite to red: This blackness is found with those who have adulterated the "goods" or or deeds of love in the Word. 

The latter blackness is "diabolical," while the former is "satanic." The significance of the jasper and the sardius <note>original: "sardius", a deep red stone often identified as carnelian.</note> can be seen further in the explanation of chapter 21, verses 11 and 18-20.

**232.** ***And a rainbow was around the throne, in appearance like an emerald***, signifies their appearance also around the Lord. In the spiritual world, rainbows of many kinds appear. They appear in many colors, just as they do on earth, but they also appear in a single color. This specific rainbow was of one color, as it is described as being like an emerald. This appearance was "around the Lord" because it is said to have been "around the throne." To be "around Him" also signifies being in the angelic heaven. 

The Divine sphere that surrounds the Lord originates from His Divine Love and His Divine Wisdom at the same time. When this sphere is represented in the heavens, it appears differently depending on the "kingdom" or level of heaven:
*   In the **heavenly (celestial) kingdom**, it appears red like a ruby.
*   In the **spiritual kingdom**, it appears blue like lapis-lazuli.
*   In the **natural kingdom**, it appears green like an emerald.
In every instance, it appears with an inexpressible splendor and radiance.

**233.** ***And around the throne were twenty-four thrones, and upon the thrones I saw twenty-four elders sitting***, signifies the arrangement of all things in heaven for the last judgment. **240.** *Full of eyes before and behind*, signifies the **Divine Wisdom** within it. For a person, **eyes** represent understanding; but when the **Word** describes the **Lord**, they signify His **Divine Wisdom** (see sections 48, 125). This same meaning applies when **eyes** are attributed to the **Word**, because the **Word** originates from the **Lord** and is about the **Lord**, and therefore in essence is the **Lord**. A similar description is found in the Book of **Ezekiel** regarding the **cherubs**—that *they were full of eyes* (Ezekiel 10:12). The phrase "before and behind," when applied to the **Word** as it comes from the **Lord**, signifies the **Divine Wisdom** and the **Divine Love** contained within it.

**241.** *And the first animal was like a lion*, signifies the **Divine Truth** of the **Word** in its power. It is clear that a **lion** represents truth in its power—specifically the **Divine Truth** of the **Word**—because the **lion** possesses power above every other animal on earth. This is also evident from the **lions** in the <term>spiritual world<note>In Swedenborg’s descriptions, the spiritual world contains representative animals that are outward manifestations of the inner states or affections of spirits and angels.</note></term>, which appear as symbolic images of the power of **Divine Truth**. Furthermore, in the **Word**, lions consistently signify **Divine Truth** in its power. For more on the power of **Divine Truth** within the **Word**, see the *Doctrine of the New Jerusalem concerning the Sacred Scripture* (section 49) and the work *Heaven and Hell* (sections 228–233). It is for this reason that **Jehovah**, or the **Lord**, is compared to a **lion** and is even called a **lion**; as seen in the...

*repay to Jehovah the calves of our lips* (Hosea 14:2). The "calves of the lips" are confessions coming from an affection for truth. In Malachi: *Unto you that fear my name shall the Sun of Righteousness arise, with healing in His wings, that ye may grow up as fattened calves* (4:2). A comparison is made with fattened calves because they signify those who are filled with <term>knowledges<note>In this context, "knowledges" (often pluralized in this theology) refers to specific facts or intellectual understandings of spiritual truths and goodness.</note></term> of truth and good, arising from a genuine desire to know them. In David: *The voice of Jehovah maketh the cedars of Lebanon to skip as a calf* (Psalm 29:6). By the "cedars of Lebanon," the knowledges of truth are signified; hence it is said that "the voice of Jehovah maketh them to skip as a calf." The voice of Jehovah is the **Divine Truth**, which here affects and enlivens those knowledges. 

As the Egyptians loved knowledges, they originally made calves for themselves as a symbol of their affection for them. But they later began to worship the calves as gods, and from then on, calves in the Word signify the affection for knowing <term>falsities<note>A technical term for "false beliefs" or "errors" that have been adopted as truth.</note></term>; as seen in Jeremiah 46:20, 21; Psalm 68:30; and elsewhere. The same meaning is therefore applied to the calf which the sons of Israel made for themselves in the desert (Exodus 32), and also to the calves of Samaria (1 Kings 12:28-32; Hosea 8:4, 5; 10:5). For this reason, it is said in Hosea: *They make to themselves a molten thing of silver; sacrificing a man, they kiss the calves* (13:2). To "make to themselves a molten thing of silver" signifies to falsify truth; to "sacrifice a man" signifies to destroy wisdom; and to "kiss the calves" signifies to acknowledge falsities from a place of affection. 

In Isaiah: *There shall the calf feed, there shall he lie down, and consume its branches* (27:10). The same is signified by a calf in Jeremiah (34:18-20). Since all Divine worship originates from the affections for truth and good, and the resulting knowledges of them, the sacrifices—in which the worship of the church among the sons of Israel principally consisted—were made from various animals, such as lambs, she-goats, kids, sheep, he-goats, calves, and oxen. Calves were used because they signified the affection for <insert>natural truth</insert>.

243. *And the third animal having a face like a man*, signifies the **Divine Truth** of the Word as to wisdom. Wisdom that is truly human consists in being wise in these things: that there is a God, what God is, and what belongs to God; these the **Divine Truth** of the Word teaches. ...understanding. Many things are symbolized by eagles, and by flying eagles are meant the <term>knowledges</term> <note>The term "knowledges" refers to specific spiritual truths or facts learned from the Word that form the basis for human intelligence.</note> from which understanding is born; this is because when they fly, they perceive and see. They also have sharp eyes so that they may see clearly; and "eyes" symbolize the understanding (see numbers 48 and 214). "Flying" symbolizes the act of perceiving and instructing; and in the highest sense, which refers to the Lord, it symbolizes looking out for and providing. That eagles signify such things in the Word is evident from these passages:

> *They that wait for Jehovah shall have their strength renewed; they shall mount up with wings as eagles* (Isaiah 40:31).

"To mount up with wings as eagles" means to be elevated into the <term>knowledges</term> of truth and good, and from there into intelligence.

> *Is it by your intelligence and according to your word that the eagle lifts himself up and searches out his food? His eyes look forward from afar* (Job 39:26, 29).

The faculty of knowing, of understanding, and of looking forward is described here by the eagle, emphasizing that this does not come from one's own intelligence.

> *Jehovah who satisfies your mouth with good, so that you may be renewed in your youth like the eagle* (Psalms 103:5).

"To satisfy the mouth with good" means to provide understanding through <term>knowledges</term>; for this reason, the comparison is made with the eagle.

> *A great eagle, with great wings and long feathers, came upon Lebanon and took a twig of a cedar, and put it in a fruitful field, and it grew. And there was another great eagle, to which the vine applied its roots* (Ezekiel 17:1–8).

The two eagles here describe the Jewish and Israelite churches, specifically in regard to their <term>knowledges</term> of truth and the intelligence that follows. However, in the opposite sense, eagles symbolize the <term>knowledges</term> of what is false, which leads to a perverted understanding; as seen in Matthew 24:28, Jeremiah 4:13, Habakkuk 1:8, and elsewhere.
