[The fact that these wings] also serve as guards will be seen below. By the number **six** is signified "all" in relation to truth and good; this is because six arises from **three** and **two** multiplied by each other. In the language of <term>correspondences</term> <note>The "science of correspondences" is Swedenborg’s system for interpreting the Bible, where physical objects or numbers represent specific spiritual realities.</note>, **three** signifies all as to truth (see number 505), and **two** signifies all as to good (see number 762).

By **wings** are signified powers, because birds use them to raise themselves up; for birds, wings take the place of arms for men, and powers are symbolized by arms. Since powers are signified by wings, and each animal had six wings, the specific power of each animal is revealed by what was said above:

*   By the **wings of the lion** is signified the power of fighting against evils and falsities from hell; this power comes from the Divine Truth of the Word from the Lord.
*   By the **wings of the calf** is signified the power of affecting the natural mind; for the Divine Truth of the Word moves those who read it in a holy state.
*   By the **six wings of the man** is signified the power of being wise concerning what God is and what belongs to God; for this power is uniquely human when reading the Word.
*   By the **wings of the eagle** is signified the power of knowing truth and good, and thus of acquiring intelligence for oneself.

We also read in the book of Ezekiel concerning the wings of the <term>cherubs</term> <note>Cherubim, or "cherubs," are described by Swedenborg as symbols of the Lord's providence and the protection of the inner meanings of the Word from being misunderstood or profaned.</note>:

> *...that the wings kissed each other, and that they also covered their bodies, and that the likeness of hands was under them* (Ezekiel 1:23, 24; 3:13; 10:5, 21).

By **kissing each other** is signified acting in conjunction and with one mind. By **covering the bodies** is signified keeping guard so that interior truths—which are those of the <term>spiritual sense</term> <note>The spiritual sense is the deeper, symbolic meaning of the Bible that lies beneath the literal stories.</note> of the Word—should not be violated. By the **hands under the wings** are signified powers.

Concerning the **Seraphim**, it is also said:

> *...that they had six wings, with two of which they covered the face, with two the feet, and they flew with two* (Isaiah 6:2).

By the **Seraphim**, the Word is likewise signified—specifically the <term>doctrine</term> drawn from the Word. By the wings with which they covered the face and the feet, guards are likewise signified; and by the wings with which they flew, powers are signified, as mentioned above. To **fly** signifies to perceive and to instruct, and in the highest sense to look...

Lord, because He is the <term>Divine Truth</term> <note>In this theology, Divine Truth is the spiritual light that provides the mind with wisdom and understanding.</note> and the <term>Divine Good</term> <note>Divine Good is the spiritual warmth or love that gives life and motivation to the heart.</note>, the kingdom belongs [to Him] by <term>merit and justice</term> <note>This refers to the Lord's right to rule because He alone conquered the powers of hell and restored order to the heavens.</note>. ### THE EXPLANATION.

256. **And I saw in the right hand of Him that sat upon the throne a book written within and on the back**, signifies the Lord as to His Divine Itself from eternity, who has omnipotence and omniscience, and who is the Word, who also knows from Himself the states of life of all in the heavens and on the earth, in every particular and in general. By “Him that sitteth upon the throne” is meant the Lord as to the Divine Itself, from which is His Human: for it follows that the Lamb took the Book out of the right hand of Him that sat upon the throne (verse 7 <note>original: *vers. 7*</note>); and by the Lamb the Lord as to the Divine Human is meant. By the “Book written within and on the back” is meant the Word in every particular and in general: by “within,” in every particular, and by “on the back,” in general. By within and on the back is also meant the interior sense of the Word which is spiritual, and its exterior sense which is natural. By the right hand is meant Himself as to <term>omnipotence</term> <note>All-powerful nature.</note> and <term>omniscience</term> <note>All-knowing nature.</note>, because the exploration of all in the heavens and on earth, upon whom the last judgment is to be executed, and their separation, are treated of. The reason the <term>Word</term> <note>Referring here to the Lord as the living expression of God’s wisdom.</note> knows the states of life of all in the heavens and on earth from Himself is because He is the <term>Divine Truth</term> <note>The spiritual light that informs the mind and reveals the reality of the soul.</note> itself, and the Divine Truth itself knows all things from itself. But this is an <term>arcanum</term> <note>original: *arcanum*; a profound spiritual secret or hidden truth.</note>, which is revealed in the *Angelic Wisdom concerning the Divine Love and the Divine Wisdom* <note>A reference to another work by the author, published in 1763, which explores the relationship between God's essence and the created world.</note>. That the Lord, as to the <term>Divine Itself</term> <note>The essential, infinite nature of God that existed before time.</note> from eternity, was the Word—that is, the Divine Truth—is manifest from this in John: *In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God* (i. 1); and again, that the Lord as to the Human also became the Word: *And the Word became flesh* (i. 14). 

It may hence be evident what it means, that the Book was in the right hand of Him that sat upon the throne, and that the Lamb took the Book therefrom (verse 7). Since the Lord is the Word, and the Word is the Divine Truth, which in general makes heaven and the church, and in particular makes an angel so that heaven may be in him, and a man so that the church may be in him; and because the Word is here meant by the Book, from which and according to which all are to be judged; therefore, “to be written in the Book,” “to be judged from the Book,” and “to be blotted out of the Book,” frequently occur where the state of the eternal life of any one is treated of; as in these passages:

**257.** ***Sealed with seven seals***, signifies that it is altogether hidden from angel and man. That “sealed with a seal” signifies being hidden is obvious; therefore “sealed with seven seals” signifies being completely or altogether hidden. In this symbolic language, **seven** signifies "all" or "completeness" (see point no. 10), and thus also "altogether." That it was altogether hidden from angel and man is stated shortly after in these words: “and no one in heaven, nor upon the earth, neither under the earth, was able to open and read the Book, neither to look thereon” (verses 3, 4). Such is the state of the Word to all to whom the Lamb—that is, the Lord—does not open it. Because this passage deals with the <term>exploration</term> <note>The process of examining the inner spiritual state of individuals.</note> of everyone before the last judgment, it refers to the states of life of every person, in general and in particular, which are altogether hidden until revealed.

**258.** ***And I saw a mighty angel proclaiming with a great voice***, signifies the Divine Truth from the Lord flowing in deeply into the thought of angels and men, and the beginning of an investigation. By an “angel proclaiming,” in the spiritual sense, the Lord is meant; this is because an angel does not proclaim or teach from himself, but from the Lord, though it appears as if it is from himself. The angel is called **mighty** because he speaks with power, and that which is proclaimed with power flows deeply into a person's thought. A **great voice** signifies the Divine Truth from the Lord in its power or strength. That an “investigation” is also signified is clear because the angel asks the question, “Who is worthy to open the Book?” as the text continues.

That when the Lord was in the world, He subjugated the hells, and reduced all things in the heavens to order, and also glorified His <term>Human</term> <note>A technical term for the Lord’s physical and spiritual humanity being made Divine.</note>, may be seen above (n. 67); and also in the *Doctrine of the New Jerusalem concerning the Lord* (n. 12–14). **266.** ***Which is of the tribe of Judah, the root of David,*** signifies that this was accomplished by the Divine Good united to the Divine Truth in His humanity. In the <term>Word</term>, "Judah" signifies the church that is in the "good of love" to the Lord; in its highest sense, it signifies the Lord Himself in His Divine Good—the essence of His Divine Love. "David" signifies the Lord in His Divine Truth—the essence of His Divine Wisdom. That David carries this meaning can be seen in the *Doctrine of the New Jerusalem concerning the Lord* (n. 43, 44); and that Judah carries the former meaning can be seen in the same work (n. 96, 266, 350). 

From these points, it is clear that the phrase, “*Behold, the Lion hath prevailed, which is of the tribe of Judah, the root of David*,” signifies that the Lord conquered the hells and restored order to all things through the union of Divine Good and Divine Truth in His humanity. This deeper meaning cannot be seen in the literal text, which appears to say only that it was He who was born into the world from the tribe of Judah and the lineage of David. Yet these words contain within them a spiritual sense. In this spiritual sense, names of people represent specific qualities or concepts—as has been noted before. Thus, "Judah" does not literally mean the man Judah, nor does "David" mean the king David; rather, Judah represents the Lord’s Divine Good, and David represents His Divine Truth. This is the resulting meaning. This interpretation is provided here because the Apocalypse, in its spiritual sense, is now being revealed to the world.

**267.** ***To open the Book, and to loose the seven seals thereof,*** signifies to know the inner life and spiritual states of every person in heaven and on earth, and to judge every individual according to those states; as discussed previously (n. 258, 259).

-> 270 <-

for incense. The latter altar was in the Tabernacle, and was called the golden altar; but the former was outside the Tabernacle, and was called the altar of burnt-offering. The reason for this was that there are two kinds of "good" from which all worship flows: **heavenly (celestial) good** and **spiritual good**. <term>Heavenly good</term> <note>In this context, heavenly or "celestial" good refers specifically to the love a person feels directly toward the Lord.</note> is the good of love to the Lord, and <term>spiritual good</term> <note>Spiritual good refers to the love felt toward one’s neighbor.</note> is the good of love to the neighbor. 

The worship performed through sacrifices was worship from heavenly good, and the worship by incense was worship from spiritual good. Whether you call it "worship" or "confession," it is the same thing; for all true worship is an act of confession. The same meaning signified by incense is also signified by the vials in which the incense was held; since the container and the contents—much like an instrument and the person using it—act together as a single cause. That worship from spiritual good is signified by incense can be seen in the following passages: 

> *From the rising of the sun even unto its going down, my name shall be great among the nations, and in every place **incense** shall be offered to my name* (Malachi 1:11). 
> 
> *They shall teach Jacob thy judgments, they shall offer **incense** before thee, and a burnt-offering upon thine altar* (Deuteronomy 33:10). 
> 
> *Burnt-offerings of fatlings will I offer unto thee, with **incense*** (Psalm 66:13, 15). 
> 
> *They shall come from the regions around Judah bringing burnt-offerings, meat-offerings <note>original: "mincha"; in historical biblical contexts, this usually refers to a grain or flour offering.</note>, and **frankincense*** (Jeremiah 17:26). 
> 
> *They shall come from Sheba, they shall bring gold and **frankincense**, and shall declare the praises of Jehovah* (Isaiah 60:6).

By **frankincense**, the same thing is signified as by **incense**, because frankincense was the primary spice from which incense was prepared. In the same way, we read in Matthew: 

> *The wise men from the east opened their treasures, and offered to the infant Lord gold, **frankincense**, and myrrh* (2:11). 

The reason they offered these three specific gifts was that **gold** signifies heavenly good, **frankincense** signifies spiritual good, and **myrrh** signifies natural good; and from these three types of "good" comes all true worship.

281. ***Because thou wast slain, and hast redeemed us to God by thy blood***, signifies liberation from hell, and salvation by conjunction with Him. What in particular is signified by each of these things there is no need of unfolding by the <term>spiritual sense</term> <note>The deeper, symbolic meaning of the Word that lies beneath the literal stories and descriptions.</note>; such as what is meant by His being slain, by His redeeming us to God, and what by His blood: for they are <term>arcana</term> <note>original: "arcana." It shall here only be proved from the Word, that **Jehovah** Himself came into the world, was born a Man, and became the **Redeemer** and **Saviour** to all who by a life of <term>charity</term> <note>In this context, charity is not just giving to the poor, but the active love for one's neighbor and doing what is good and just.</note> and its faith are conjoined to His <term>Divine Human</term> <note>The teaching that the Lord made His human nature divine, allowing a direct connection between God and humanity.</note>; and that Jehovah is the Lord from eternity: consequently that the Lord's Divine Human, with which there must be conjunction, is the Divine Human of **Jehovah** Himself. 

Here, therefore, shall be adduced the passages which prove that **Jehovah** and the **Lord** are one; and because they are one, and not two, that the Lord from eternity, who is Jehovah Himself, is by the assumption of the Human the Redeemer and Saviour. This is manifest from these:

It is to be known that the tongue, as an organ, signifies doctrine, and as speech, it also signifies religion.

He who knows that the "tongue" signifies <term>doctrine</term> <note>The specific teachings or system of beliefs held by a church.</note> can understand what is signified by the words of the rich man in hell to Abraham, *that he would send Lazarus, that he might dip the tip of his finger in water, and cool his tongue, that he should not be tortured in the flame* (Luke 16:24). Water signifies truth, and "tongue" signifies doctrine; it was by the <term>falsities</term> <note>In this context, "falsity" refers to religious errors or beliefs that lead one away from the truth.</note> of his doctrine that he was tortured, and not by a physical flame. For no one in hell is actually in a physical flame, but "flame" there is the appearance of the love of falsity, and "fire" is the appearance of the love of evil.

**283.** *And hast made us kings and priests unto our God*, signifies that from <unclear>the</unclear> Lord they are in wisdom from <term>Divine truths</term> <note>Truths that originate from God's wisdom.</note> and in love from <term>Divine goods</term> <note>Goodness and love that originate from God's nature.</note>, and thus they are images of His Divine Wisdom and His Divine Love; as mentioned above (sections 20, 21).

**284.** *And we shall reign upon the earth*, signifies that they will be in His kingdom—He in them, and they in Him. By "reigning upon the earth," nothing else is meant but to be in the Lord's kingdom and to be one with Him there; according to these words of the Lord: *That all that believe in Me may be one; and may be one as Thou, Father, art in Me, and I in Thee; that they also may be one in us. I have given them the glory which thou gavest Me, that they may be one as we are one; I in them, and Thou in Me; that where I am, they may be with Me also* (John 17:20–24). 

As, therefore, they are thus one with the Lord, and together with the Lord make the kingdom which is called the Kingdom of God, it is manifest that nothing else is signified by "reigning." This is why the Lord's kingdom is also called *the kingdom of the saints* (Daniel 7:18, 27); and why it is said of the apostles that *with the Lord they are to judge the twelve tribes of Israel* (Matthew 19:28), although the Lord alone judges and reigns. 286. **And I saw, and I heard a voice of many angels around the throne and the animals and the elders, signifies confession and glorification of the Lord by the angels of the lower heavens.** That the confession and glorification of the Lord was made by the angels of the three heavens may be seen above (n. 275); it was made by the angels of the higher heavens (from verses 8 to 10), and now it is made by the angels of the lower heavens (verses 11, 12). This is the reason why he saw and heard the animals and the elders first by themselves, and then together with the others.

Here, the quantity described represents the quality of their state.

<meta>This page continues the technical explanation of how specific numbers in the Bible represent spiritual qualities. Specifically, it concludes the analysis of "myriads" and "thousands" from Revelation 5:11 and begins the interpretation of verse 12 regarding the Lord's "Divine Human" nature.</meta>

->THE APOCALYPSE REVEALED. [CHAP. V]<-

In the spiritual sense, numbers relate to quality. Here, the quality of the angels is described by their being "myriads of myriads and thousands of thousands." A <term>myriad</term> <note>Commonly referring to ten thousand, but used here to represent an immense or uncountable number.</note> is associated with truths, and a "thousand" is associated with goods. The reason a myriad refers to truths and a thousand to goods is that a myriad is the larger number and a thousand is the smaller; truths are manifold and complex, but <term>goods</term> <note>In this context, "goods" refers to the various forms of love and kindness that motivate a person, while "truths" refers to the ideas and wisdom that guide them.</note> are simple and unified. Furthermore, in the Word, whenever truths are discussed, goods are also discussed because of the "marriage" of truth and good present in every part of the Bible; otherwise, the text might have only mentioned "myriads of myriads." 

Because these two numbers signify these specific spiritual qualities, they are mentioned together in other passages: 
* *The chariots of God are two myriads, thousands of angels of peace; the Lord is in them, Sinai in the sanctuary* (Psalm 68:17). 
* *I saw when the <term>Ancient of Days</term> <note>A title for God representing His eternal and unchanging nature.</note> did sit; thousands of thousands ministered to Him, and myriads of myriads stood before Him* (Daniel 7:9, 10). 
* Moses says of Joseph, *His horns are the horns of a unicorn; with them shall he strike the peoples together to the ends of the earth; and these are the myriads of Ephraim and the thousands of Manasseh* (Deuteronomy 33:17). 
* *Thou shalt not fear for the pestilence that spreadeth in thick-darkness, and for the destruction that wasteth at noonday: a thousand shall fall at thy side, and a myriad at thy right hand* (Psalm 91:5-7). 
* *Our flocks are thousands, myriads in our streets* (Psalm 144:13). 
* *Is Jehovah delighted with thousands of rams, with myriads of rivers of oil?* (Micah 6:7). 
* When the ark rested, Moses said, *Return, O Jehovah, unto the myriads of the thousands of Israel* (Numbers 10:36). 

In all these places, "myriads" relates to truths, and "thousands" relates to goods.

### 289. *And blessing*

This signifies all these things present in Him, and from Him in others. By "blessing" is meant every good thing which a person receives from the Lord, such as power and wealth, and the things that go with them; but it especially refers to all spiritual good, such as love and wisdom, charity and faith, and from those, the joy and happiness that belong to eternal life. Because all these things come from the Lord, it follows that they are fundamentally in Him; for unless they were in Him, they could not be given to others from Him. 

For this reason, the Lord is called "Blessed" in the Word, and also "Blessing," which is to say *Blessing Itself*. That <term>Jehovah</term> <note>The personal name of God in the Hebrew Bible, often translated as "The LORD."</note> (that is, the Lord) is called "Blessed" is evident from these passages: 

* *The High Priest asked Jesus, "Are you the Christ, the Son of the Blessed?"* (Mark 14:61). 
* *Jesus said, "You shall not see me hereafter, until you say, Blessed is He that comes in the name of the Lord"* (Matthew 23:39; Luke 13:35). 
* *Melchizedek blessed Abram, and said, "Blessed be God Most High, who has delivered your enemies into your hand"* (Genesis 14:18–20). 
* *Blessed be Jehovah the God of Shem* (Genesis 9:26). 
* *Blessed be Jehovah, who has heard my voice* (Psalm 28:6). 
* *Blessed be Jehovah, because He has shown His marvelous kindness* (Psalm 31:21). 
* *Blessed be Jehovah from everlasting even to everlasting* (Psalm 41:13. See also Psalm 66:20; Psalm 68:17, 35; Psalm 72:18, 19; Psalm 89:52; Psalm 119:12; Psalm 124:6; Psalm 135:21; Psalm 144:1; Luke 1:68).

TO THESE THINGS I WILL ADD THIS RELATION.** In the <term>natural world</term> <note>The physical world of time and space where we currently live.</note> man has a twofold speech, because he has a twofold thought, an exterior and an interior: for a man can speak from interior thought, and at the same time from exterior thought; and he can speak from exterior thought, and not from the interior, and even against the interior: hence come simulations, flatterers, and hypocrisies. But in the <term>spiritual world</term> <note>The realm of existence after death where thoughts and feelings are directly expressed.</note> man's speech is not twofold, but single. He there speaks as he thinks: otherwise the sound is harsh, and offends the ear. But still he can be silent, and thus not divulge the thoughts of his mind: on which account, when a hypocrite comes among the wise, he either goes away, or hurries himself into a corner of the room, and makes himself inconspicuous, and sits mute. ### THE EXPLANATION.

295. *And I saw when the Lamb had opened the first of the seals*, signifies the exploration <note>The "exploration" refers to a spiritual audit or examination where the Lord looks into a person's heart and mind to see how they truly understand and live out the teachings of the Bible.</note> by the Lord of all upon whom the last Judgment was about to come, as to their understanding of the Word <note>The "Word" is the term used here for Sacred Scripture or the Bible.</note>, and thence as to the states of their life. These things are signified, because there now follows in order the exploration of all those upon whom the last Judgment was about to come, as to the states of their life; and this by the Lord according to the Word. This, therefore, is what is signified by the Lamb's opening the seals of the Book <note>original: "Liber". In this spiritual sense, the "Book" represents the inner life of humanity which only the Divine can read.</note>. That to open the Book, and to loose its seals, signifies to know the states of the life of all, and to judge each according to his own, may be seen above (n. 259, 265-267, 273, 274).

296. *And I heard one of the four animals saying, as with a voice of thunder*, signifies according to the Divine Truth of the Word. That the Word is meant by the four animals or cherubs <note>Cherubs are described here not just as angels, but as symbols of the Lord's protection and the divine guards of the inner meaning of the Bible.</note>, may be seen above (n. 239, 275, 286); and that perception of the Divine Truth is meant by a voice of thunder, see n. 236. It is here called a voice of thunder, because by this animal the lion is meant, by which the Divine Truth of the Word as to power is signified (n. 241).

It describes how those who have confirmed themselves in evil attempt to hide from divine truth, which is symbolized by the powerful "voice of thunder" from the cherubim.</summary>

Hence it is that this animal is said to speak as with a voice of thunder; for it is afterwards said that the second animal spoke, and then the third, and the fourth.

297. **Come and see**, signifies a manifestation concerning the first in order. It was said above, that the exploration <note>In this spiritual context, "exploration" refers to the Lord’s process of examining the inner thoughts and intentions of people to see how they truly understand the Bible.</note> of all upon whom the Judgment was about to come is described in this chapter, as to the states of their life; and this by the Lord according to the Word <note>The "Word" is the term used throughout this work to refer to the Sacred Scriptures or the Bible.</note> (n. 295). Here, therefore, the exploration of those who were the first in order is described—what they were as to their understanding of the Word, and from that, the states of their life. That the Church exists from the Word, and that the quality of a Church depends on its understanding of the Word, may be seen in the *Doctrine of the New Jerusalem concerning the Sacred Scripture* (n. 76-79).

298. **And I saw, and behold, a white horse**, signifies the understanding of truth and good from the Word with these people. The understanding of the Word is signified by a horse, and by a white horse the understanding of truth from the Word; for white is associated with <note>original: "praedicatur", meaning a quality attributed to something.</note> truths (n. 167). That a horse signifies the understanding of the Word is shown in a separate small work titled *The White Horse*; but as only a few passages are cited there, more will be brought forward here as evidence. This is clearly shown by the fact that horses were seen to go out of the Book <note>The "Book" refers to the scroll with seven seals mentioned in Revelation 5.</note> which the Lamb <note>The "Lamb" refers to the Lord, Jesus Christ, in His role as the redeemer.</note> opened; and that the living creatures said, "Come and see": for the Word is signified by the animals (n. 239, 275, 286); and also by the Book (n. 256); and by the <term>Son of Man</term> <note>A title for the Lord (Jesus Christ) specifically regarding His identity as the Divine Truth or the Word itself.</note>, who is here the Lamb. From these things it is now clear that nothing else but the understanding of the Word is meant here by the horse. This may be even more clearly evident from these words later in the Apocalypse:

> I saw heaven opened, when, behold, a **White Horse**; and He that sat upon him is called the **Word of God**: and He has upon His clothing and upon His thigh a name written, **King of kings and Lord of lords**.

**300.** *And there was given unto him a crown,* signifies his badge of combat. The reason that a **crown** signifies a badge of combat, is because in ancient times kings wore their crowns in battles; as may be evident from histories, and in some degree from 2 Samuel 1:10; where the man said to David concerning Saul, *that when he died in the battle, he took the crown which was upon his head, and the armlets that were upon his arms:* as also from the things that are related of the king of Rabbah and David (2 Samuel 12:29, 30). And because <term>temptations</term> <note>In Swedenborg’s theology, "temptations" are not just lures to sin, but intense spiritual trials that test and strengthen a person's faith.</note> are spiritual combats, which the martyrs endured, crowns were therefore given to them as badges of victory (no. 103). It is manifest from these things that their badge of combat is here signified by the crown, on which account it also follows, *And he went forth conquering and to conquer.*

"The new wine" is the **Divine Truth** of the New Testament, and thus of a New Church; and "the old wine" is the **Divine Truth** of the Old Testament, and thus of the Old Church. The like is signified by these words of the Lord at the wedding in Cana of Galilee: *Every man at first setteth forth good wine; and when they have had enough, the poorer: thou hast kept the good wine until now* (John ii. 1-10). <note>The "good wine" kept until the end symbolizes the deeper spiritual truths of the Gospel, which were revealed after the literal laws of the Old Testament.</note> The same is also signified by the wine in the Lord's parable of the man wounded by robbers, that *the Samaritan poured in oil and wine into his wounds* (Luke x. 33, 34). For by the man wounded by robbers are meant they who were spiritually wounded by the Jews by evils and falsities; to whom the Samaritan brought help by pouring in oil and wine into his wounds; that is, by teaching good and truth, and, as far as he was able, by healing him. <note>In the internal sense, "oil" represents the good of love or charity, while "wine" represents the truth of faith or wisdom.</note> Holy truth is also signified by new-wine and wine elsewhere in the Word, as Isaiah i. 21, 22; xxv. 6; xxxvi. 17; Hosea vii. 4, 5, 14; xiv. 6-8; Amos ii. 8; Zechariah ix. 15, 17; Psalm civ. 14-16. Hence it is that the church which is in truths from the Lord is signified in the Word by "a vineyard."

That wine signifies holy truth may also be evident from its opposite sense, in which it signifies truth falsified and profaned; as in these places: *Whoredom, wine, and new wine occupied the heart; their wine has failed; they have committed whoredom continually* (Hosea iv. 11, 17, 18). <term>Whoredom</term> <note>original: "scortatio"; in the symbolic language of prophecy, this refers to the act of corrupting sacred truths by mixing them with false ideas.</note> signifies the falsification of truth; here wine and new wine signify the same. *A cup is in the hand of Jehovah, and He hath mixed it with wine; He hath filled it with the mixture, and poured it out; and the dregs of it shall all the wicked of the earth suck out and drink* (Psalm lxxv. 8). *A cup of gold is Babylon in the hand of Jehovah, making drunk the whole earth; of the wine of it have the nations drunk, therefore they are insane* (Jeremiah li. 7). <note>Babylon represents a state of the church where the desire for power rules over the truth, leading to spiritual "insanity" or confusion.</note> *Babylon hath fallen, because she hath made all nations drink of the wine of the wrath of her whoredom: if any one worship the beast, he shall drink of the wine of the wrath of God*

That the power of killing the fourth part of the habitable earth was not given to him that sat upon the pale horse is manifest. 330. **And I saw when he had opened the sixth seal**, signifies the exploration <note>In this context, an "exploration" refers to a spiritual examination or uncovering of a person's true internal character.</note> of the state of life of those who were interiorly evil, upon whom the judgment was to come. **Secondly**, that as long as they were conjoined with the ultimate heaven, so long were the internals of their will and love closed up; owing to which they did not appear before others as evil. But when they were separated from the ultimate heaven, their interiors were then opened; which were totally in opposition to their exteriors, from which they dissembled, and pretended that they were angels of heaven, and that the places where they dwelt were heavens. These heavens so-called were those which passed away at the time of the last judgment (Apocalypse 21:1). But more may be seen on this subject in the little work on the *Last Judgment* (numbers 70, 71); and in the *Continuation concerning the Last Judgment* (number 10).

**331. And, behold, there was a great earthquake**, signifies that the state of the church with these individuals was altogether changed, and that they were filled with terror. The reason that earthquakes signify changes of state in the church is because the "earth" signifies the church (see n. 285). Furthermore, in the spiritual world, whenever the state of the church is perverted anywhere and a change is made, an actual earthquake occurs; because this foreshadows their impending destruction, the people there are struck with terror. For the lands <margin>See note, page 278.</margin> in the spiritual world appear similar to the lands in the natural world (see n. 260); however, because the lands there—like all other things in that world—have a spiritual origin, they change according to the state of the church among those who dwell upon them. When the state of the church is corrupted, the ground quakes and trembles; indeed, it sinks down and is moved out of its place. That this actually happened when the last judgment <note>Swedenborg recorded that he witnessed the "Last Judgment" as a spiritual event in the year 1757.</note> was impending and taking place can be seen in the short work titled *The Last Judgment*.

**332. That the **sun** signifies the Lord in terms of His **Divine Love**, and consequently the "good of love" received from Him, can be seen in earlier notes (see n. 53). In the opposite sense, the sun signifies the Lord's Divinity being denied, which leads to the "good of love" being **adulterated** <note>Adulterated: in Swedenborg's usage, this means taking something fundamentally good and mixing it with selfish or evil motives.</note>. Because the sun signifies the good of love, the **moon** signifies the **truth of faith**; for just as the sun is red and fiery, the moon is white with the light reflected from the sun. In spiritual symbolism, fire signifies the good of love, and light signifies the truth proceeding from that good. (Regarding the moon, see the references in n. 53). 

The reason the sun is described as becoming **black as sackcloth of hair** is that good which has been adulterated is essentially evil, and evil is represented as black. The moon is said to have **become as blood** because "blood" signifies **Divine Truth**, but in the opposite sense, it signifies Divine Truth that has been **falsified** <note>Falsified: the act of distorting or misinterpreting truths from the Word to justify wrong behavior or false beliefs.</note> (see n. 379, 684). A nearly identical description of the sun and moon is found in the Book of Joel: 

*The sun shall be turned into darkness, and the moon into blood, before the great and terrible day of Jehovah comes* (Joel 2:31).

That the **stars** signify these "knowledges" was established previously (see n. 51). It is evident that "falling from heaven to the earth" means to be dispersed or to perish. In the spiritual world, stars actually appear to fall from the sky to the ground when the understanding of good and truth vanishes from the minds of those living there.

**334. *As a fig-tree casteth its unripe figs when shaken by a great wind***, signifies the reasonings of the **natural man** <term>Natural man: the part of a person’s mind focused on worldly, physical, and sensory life, as opposed to the spiritual part focused on God and heaven.</term> when it is separated from the spiritual. 

The reason this verse carries this meaning, even though it is framed as a comparison, is that all comparisons in the **Word** <note>The Word: Swedenborg’s term for the Bible, which he believed contains deep spiritual meanings beneath the literal text.</note> are based on **correspondences** <term>Correspondence: a spiritual law where physical things (like trees or wind) mirror and represent specific spiritual realities (like goodness or thoughts).</term>. In this spiritual sense, the image is inseparable from the subject being discussed. 

A **fig-tree**, by correspondence, signifies a person's "natural good"—the basic, outward acts of kindness and morality—when joined to their "spiritual good." However, in this specific context, it signifies the opposite: natural good that has been separated from the spiritual, which is not truly "good" at all. Because the natural man, when cut off from the spiritual, uses **reasonings** to distort the "knowledges of good and truth" (represented by the stars), the image of a fig-tree shaken by a great wind is used. 

That **wind** and **storms** signify reasoning is clear from many passages in the Word, though they need not be listed here since this is a comparison. The reason a **fig-tree** signifies natural good in a person is that every tree represents something of the church within a person. The following passages confirm this:

*   **All the host of heaven shall fall down, as a leaf falleth from the vine, and as a fig falleth from the fig-tree** (Isaiah 34:4).
*   **I will consume them; there shall be no grapes on the vine, nor figs on the fig-tree; and the leaf shall fall** (Jeremiah 8:13).
*   **All thy bulwarks are like a fig-tree with its first fruits, which, if they be shaken, fall into the mouth of the eater** (Nahum 3:12).

This same meaning applies in other places, such as Jeremiah 24:2, 3, 5, 8; 29:17, 18; Isaiah 38:21; Hosea 2:12; 9:10; Joel 1:7, 12; Zechariah 3:10; Matthew 21:18–21; 24:32, 33; Mark 11:12–14, 19–23; and Luke 6:44; 13:6–9. In these passages, the fig-tree consistently represents this natural state of being.

And when they entered, they saw their **king** <note>This refers to King George II (1683–1760), who was the grandfather of George III, the monarch reigning in 1766 when Swedenborg published this work.</note>, — the grandfather of the king that reigns at this day (1766); and they were glad. Who goes to a man's soul and thus to his body? When a man is approached as to his body which one sees, is not his soul also approached, which one does not see?" At this they were silent.

When the bishops returned, they saluted their brethren and related what had happened to them in heaven, and how two heavenly forms of gold, most beautiful to the sight, were given by the king to the bishops—but that they had fallen out of their hands. 

They then left the open air and went into a nearby grove; there they conversed among themselves, looking around to see whether anyone was listening. Despite their caution, they were overheard. They spoke first concerning **unanimity** and **concord**, and then concerning **sovereignty** and **dominion**. The bishops spoke, and the rest signaled their agreement. 

And suddenly—which I wondered at—they no longer appeared as many individuals, but as **one great person**, whose face was like the face of a **lion** <note>A lion's face here represents the power and ferocity of those who claim divine authority for the sake of personal rule.</note>, having upon his head a **turreted mitre** <term>turreted mitre: A tall, tower-like ceremonial hat, often symbolizing a claim to both spiritual and worldly power.</term> upon which was a crown. He spoke in a lofty tone and walked with a proud step; and looking back, he said, "To whom else, of right, belongs the sovereignty, but to me?" 

The king looked down from heaven and saw them, first all appearing as one person, and then as many acting in unison; and he observed that most of them, as he said, were in a secular dress.

## THE EXPLANATION.

342. **Afterwards I saw four angels standing upon the four corners of the earth**, signifies the entire heaven now in the effort to execute the <term>last judgment</term> <note>The author describes a spiritual event occurring in the "world of spirits" rather than a physical destruction of the world.</note> upon those who were in the <term>world of spirits</term> <note>An intermediary realm between heaven and hell where people first arrive after death to be prepared for their final destination.</note>. Many things now follow concerning the state of the spiritual world just before the last judgment, which no one can know except by revelation from the Lord; and because it was given me to see how the last judgment was accomplished, and the changes which preceded, and the arrangements which followed it, I am able to relate what things are signified in this chapter, and what in the following, by all the things in them. By the **four angels** here the entire heaven is signified; by the **four corners of the earth** is signified the entire world of spirits, which is in the midst between heaven and hell: for the last judgment was executed upon those who were in the world of spirits, but not upon any one in heaven, nor upon any one in hell. The reason that heaven is signified by the angels is that in the highest sense the Lord as to the <term>Divine Human</term> <note>This refers to the belief that the Lord's human nature was made fully divine, allowing God to be approachable by humanity.</note> is meant by an angel (n. 344); and because heaven is heaven from the Lord, heaven is also signified by the angels. The reason that the entire heaven is here signified by the four angels, is that they were seen to stand upon the four corners of the earth; and by the four corners the four quarters are signified. Why the effort of the entire heaven to execute the last judgment is signified, is because the Lord, when the judgment was impending, caused the heavens to approach over the world of spirits; and by the approach of the heavens such a change was effected in the state of the <term>interiors</term> <note>The inner levels of a person’s mind, including their deepest intentions and thoughts.</note> of the mind with those who were below, that they saw nothing but terrors before their

That the **corners** signify the quarters <note>The four directions: East, West, South, and North, representing all aspects of the spiritual world.</note>, and hence the **four corners** all the quarters, may be evident from the following passages: *Ye shall measure without the city the corner towards the east, the corner towards the south, the corner towards the west, and the corner towards the north* (Numbers 35:5). *Thou shalt make planks for the tabernacle* <note>The portable sanctuary of the Israelites, symbolizing the dwelling place of God.</note> *for the corner of the south and for the corner of the north of it* (Exodus 26:18, 20, 23). *And the court to the corner of the south, to the corner of the north, to the corner of the west, and to the corner of the east* (Exodus 27:9, 11—13). 

The four quarters are also often called the **four corners** in Ezekiel, as chapter 47:18—20, and chapter 48. It is well known that a <term>last judgment</term> <note>In this context, the "Last Judgment" refers to a specific spiritual event where the "world of spirits"—an intermediate state between heaven and hell—is cleared of those who are inwardly evil but outwardly appeared good.</note> takes place when the evil have increased to such a degree under the heavens in the <term>world of spirits</term>, that the angels in the heavens cannot remain in their state of love and wisdom; for they then lack a support and foundation. Because this occurs due to the increase of evil people below, the Lord—in order to preserve the state of the angels—flows in more and more strongly with His <term>Divine</term> <note>God’s direct influence or presence.</note>. This continues until the angels can no longer be protected by any <term>influx</term> <note>The constant flow of life, love, and wisdom from God into spirits and humans.</note> unless the evil below are separated from the good. Consequently, the evil flee away and cast themselves into hell.

By **sealing upon their foreheads**, it does not mean to literally place a physical seal there, but rather to distinguish and separate those who live in the **good of love** <note>Swedenborg uses this term to describe the state of a person whose primary motivation is selfless love for others and the Divine.</note> from the Lord; this is because the **forehead** symbolizes the quality of a person's love. The reason this refers to those who possess truths derived from goodness is that these individuals are what is meant by the "servants of God" (as discussed in section 3).

The **forehead** symbolizes the "good of love" because the face is the reflection of a person’s inner feelings and affections, and the forehead is the highest part of the face. Furthermore, the brain—which is the source of everything in a person's life—is located directly behind the forehead. Because the forehead signifies love (whether it be a good love in a righteous person or an evil love in a wicked person), to be **"sealed upon the forehead"** signifies being identified and set apart according to the nature of one's love.

This same symbolism appears in the book of **Ezekiel**: *Go through the middle of Jerusalem and set a mark upon the foreheads of those who groan over the abominations* (Ezekiel 9:4-6). Since the forehead signifies love, this is also why it is said of the gold plate on **Aaron’s mitre** <note>A ceremonial head-covering or turban worn by the High Priest.</note>—upon which was engraved *Holiness to Jehovah*—that it was placed *on the front of his mitre, so that it might be upon Aaron’s forehead perpetually, that they may be accepted before Jehovah* (Exodus 28:36-38).

Similarly, it was commanded that these words, *Thou shalt love thy God with all thy heart and with all thy soul*, should be *bound as a sign upon the hand and as a frontlet upon the forehead* (Deuteronomy 6:5, 8; 11:18). The scriptures also mention *having the name of the Father written upon their foreheads* (Revelation 14:1) and *the name of God and the Lamb upon their foreheads* (Revelation 22:4).

It is important to understand that the Lord looks at the angels in their **foreheads**, and they, in turn, look at the Lord through their **eyes**. This is because the Lord views everyone from the perspective of the "good of love," while He desires that they look back at Him from the "truths of wisdom." In this way, a **conjunction** <note>A spiritual union or connection between the Divine and the human.</note> is created. **348.** ***And I heard the number of the sealed, a hundred forty-four thousand,*** signifies all who acknowledge the Lord as the God of heaven and earth, and are in truths of doctrine from the good of love from Him through the Word. These people are signified by the **one hundred forty-four thousand** out of the **twelve tribes of Israel**, because by the twelve tribes of Israel is signified the church <note>Swedenborg defines "the church" not as an institution, but as the collective body of people who possess spiritual truth and love.</note> composed of those who are in goodness and truth from the Lord, and who acknowledge Him as the God of heaven and earth. All these are meant by the number **one hundred forty-four thousand**; for the same thing is signified by that number as by **twelve**, since it arises from the multiplication of twelve by twelve, and then from multiplication by a hundred and a thousand.

In spiritual numerology <note>Swedenborg argues that numbers in the Bible describe qualities rather than quantities.</note>, any number multiplied into itself, and then by ten, a hundred, or a thousand, signifies the same as the original number; thus the number **one hundred forty-four thousand** means the same as **one hundred forty-four**, and this the same as **twelve**, because twelve times twelve makes one hundred forty-four. In the same way, the **twelve thousand** sealed out of every tribe, multiplied by twelve, makes one hundred forty-four thousand. 

The number **twelve** signifies "all," and is used when discussing truths derived from goodness, because twelve arises from the multiplication of **three** and **four** into each other. In the internal sense of Scripture, the number **three** signifies everything regarding truth, and the number **four** signifies everything regarding goodness; hence **twelve** here signifies all things as to truth from the good of love. It is clearly evident from the numbers throughout the **Apocalypse** <note>The Book of Revelation.</note> that all numbers signify specific properties of things, determining their spiritual quality or quantity; for unless they had this symbolic meaning, many passages would have no coherent sense. The twelve tribes of Israel represented and therefore signified the church in terms of that marriage, and each individual tribe signified some universal <term>truth of good or good of truth<gloss>In Swedenborg's thought, "truth of good" refers to the intellectual understanding of how to be kind, while "good of truth" refers to the actual practice of living according to what is right.</gloss></term> within it. 

However, the specific meaning of each tribe has not been revealed to anyone until now. Nor could it have been revealed previously, lest the holiness that lies hidden within them—when they are united as one—should be <term>profaned<gloss>To treat something sacred with irreverence or to distort its spiritual meaning for selfish or worldly ends.</gloss></term> by a wrongly connected explanation. This is because their meaning is determined by their conjunction; they represent one thing in the series in which they are named according to their births (*Genesis 29, 30, 35:18*). 

The series there is as follows: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Dan, Naphtali, Gad, Asher, Issachar, Zebulun, Joseph, and Benjamin. 

It is another thing entirely in the series in which they are named when they arrived in Egypt: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Zebulun, Gad, Asher, Joseph, Benjamin, Dan, and Naphtali (*Genesis 46:8–24*). 

And it is different again in the order in which they are blessed by their father Israel <note>Israel is the name given to the patriarch Jacob after he wrestled with the angel; here, it refers to his final blessings over his sons.</note>: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Zebulun, Issachar, Dan, Gad, Asher, Naphtali, Joseph, and Benjamin (*Genesis 49*). 

Another order is found when they are blessed by Moses: Reuben, Judah, Levi, Benjamin, Joseph, Ephraim, Manasseh, Zebulun, Gad, Dan, Naphtali, and Asher (*Deuteronomy 33*). In this list, Ephraim and Manasseh are found, but Simeon and Issachar are not. 

And there is yet another order in which they encamped and marched: the tribes of Judah, Issachar, and Zebulun to the east; the tribes of Reuben, Simeon, and Gad to the south; the tribes of Ephraim, Manasseh, and Benjamin to the west; the tribes of Dan, Asher, and Naphtali to the north; and the tribe of Levi in the middle (*Numbers 2:1 to the end*). 

Finally, there is another sequence used when they are named elsewhere, such as in *Genesis 35:23–26*; *Numbers 1:5–16*, *7:1 to the end*, *13:4–15*, *26:5–57*, *34:17–28*; *Deuteronomy 27:12, 13*; *Joshua 15–19*; and *Ezekiel 48:1 to the end*. Because of this specific spiritual arrangement, when <term>Balaam<gloss>A prophet in the Old Testament who was hired to curse the Israelites but, upon seeing them arranged in their camps, was compelled by God to bless them instead.</gloss></term> saw Israel dwelling according to their tribes, he said, *How...*

*How goodly are your tabernacles, O Jacob, and your dwelling-places, O Israel* (Numbers 24:1–4, etc. <note>original Latin: "quam bona tentoria tua, Jacob, habitacula tua, Israel." In the breastplate of judgment, which was the <term>Urim and Thummim<gloss>Sacred stones worn by the High Priest, which Swedenborg interprets as "Lights and Perfections" representing divine truth and its radiance.</gloss></term>, there were twelve precious stones corresponding to the names of the sons of Israel (Exodus 28:15–21). In that context, the tribes signified different aspects of the spiritual series depending on the inquiry made and the divine answer received. But what they signify in the specific series in which they are named here in the Apocalypse—which is different again—will be explained in the sections that follow. The reason that tribes signify religion, and the twelve tribes signify the church in all its aspects, is that the words for "tribe" and "scepter" are one and the same in the Hebrew language; and a scepter represents the kingdom, and the Lord's kingdom is both heaven and the church.

350. **Of the tribe of Judah twelve thousand sealed** signifies heavenly <term>celestial<gloss>In Swedenborg's theology, "celestial" refers to the highest level of heaven, characterized by pure love for the Lord, as opposed to "spiritual," which is characterized by love for the neighbor or truth.</gloss></term> love, which is love to the Lord, and this is present in all who will be in the New Heaven and in the New Church. In the highest sense, Judah signifies the Lord in terms of heavenly love; in the spiritual sense, it signifies the Lord's heavenly kingdom and the Word; and in the natural sense, it signifies the doctrine of the heavenly church drawn from the Word. But in this specific instance, Judah signifies heavenly love. Because it is named first in the list, that love is signified in everyone who will be in the Lord's New Heaven and New Church. This is because the tribe named in the first position represents the "all" in the rest: it acts as their head and as a universal principle entering into everything that follows. It gathers them together, qualifies them, and affects them; such is the nature of love to the Lord. That "twelve thousand" signifies all who are in that state of love may be seen above (section 348). It is well known that after the time of Solomon, the twelve tribes of Israel were divided into two kingdoms: the Jewish and the Israelitish. The Jewish kingdom represented the heavenly kingdom, or the Lord’s <term>priesthood<gloss>Representing the Lord's Divine Love or "Good."</gloss></term>; and the Israelitish kingdom represented the spiritual kingdom, or the Lord’s <term>royalty<gloss>Representing the Lord's Divine Wisdom or "Truth."</gloss></term>. However, the latter was destroyed when there remained nothing spiritual with them, whereas the Jewish kingdom was preserved for the sake of the Word.

351. **Of the tribe of Reuben twelve thousand sealed**, signifies wisdom from heavenly <note>original: "celestial," the highest degree of love in Swedenborg's theology, characterized by direct perception of truth from the Lord.</note> love with those who will be in the Lord’s New Heaven and New Church. The partner of natural love is knowledge, of spiritual love is intelligence, and of heavenly love is wisdom. These things are signified by Reuben, because he was named from sight <note>In Hebrew, the name Reuben (*Re'u-ben*) literally means "See, a son!"</note>, and spiritual-natural sight is knowledge, spiritual sight is intelligence, and heavenly sight is wisdom.

Such is also the wisdom from heavenly love. And because Reuben from his birthright represented and thence signified the wisdom of the men of the church, he therefore exhorted his brethren not to kill Joseph, and grieved when Joseph was not found in the pit (Genesis 37:21, 22). 353. **Of the tribe of Asher twelve thousand sealed, signifies** mutual love, which is the love of performing <term>uses</term><note>In Swedenborg's writings, "uses" refers to the practical application of spiritual truths through service and helpful actions toward others.</note> for the community or society, among those who will belong to the Lord's New Heaven and New Church. That these things are signified by Asher can be seen to some extent from the blessing given by his father, Israel: *From Asher, his bread shall be rich, and he shall yield the delicacies of a king* (Genesis 49:20); and from his blessing by Moses: *Blessed above children is Asher; let him be acceptable to his brothers; as his days, so shall his fame be* (Deuteronomy 33:24, 25). He was also named from the word for "blessing"; and those who are in the love of doing services for the community and for society experience a state of blessedness in heaven beyond others.

That the tribe of Naphtali represents angels and people regarding this inner perception is confirmed by several passages in the Word:

This describes the state after one has undergone temptation, characterized by an eloquent and free expression that flows from inner perception.

The historical accounts in the Word—including names and tribes—carry the same symbolic meaning as the prophecies.

Something shall here be said concerning love towards the neighbor, or charity. Love towards the neighbor is the love of obeying the Lord's precepts, which are especially those that are contained in the second table of the **Decalogue**; <term>Decalogue</term><note>The Ten Commandments. The man who will not do such things because they are sins, loves his neighbor. For he does not love his neighbor, who holds him in hatred, and from hatred wishes to kill him; he does not love the neighbor who wishes to commit adultery with his wife; nor does he love his neighbor, who wishes to steal and plunder his goods: and so with the rest. This also Paul teaches in these words: *He that loveth another hath fulfilled the law: for this, Thou shalt not commit adultery, Thou shalt not kill, Thou shalt not steal, Thou shalt not be a false witness, Thou shalt not covet; and if there be any other commandment, it is comprehended in this precept, Thou shalt love thy neighbor as thyself: charity is therefore the fulfilling of the law* (Romans 13:8–10).

357. **Of the tribe of Levi twelve thousand sealed**, signifies the affection for truth from good, from which is intelligence, with those who will be of the Lord's **New Heaven and New Church**. <note>The "New Heaven and New Church" refers to the spiritual renewal and the new era of Christianity that Swedenborg believed was beginning in the spiritual world.</note> By **Levi** in the highest sense love and mercy are signified, in the spiritual sense charity in act, which is good of life, and in the natural sense consociation and conjunction. <note>Consociation refers to a spiritual fellowship or grouping of like-minded souls.</note> He was named also from *adhering* <note>The name Levi is derived from the Hebrew root *lavah*, meaning to join or adhere.</note> by which in the Word <note>Swedenborg uses "the Word" to refer to the Sacred Scriptures.</note> conjunction by love is signified.

358. **Of the tribe of Issachar twelve thousand sealed**, signifies the "good of life" <note>“Good of life” refers to practical morality and living according to the Lord’s commandments.</note> with those who will be of the Lord's New Heaven and New Church. The third in any class signifies the "ultimate" or final result, which is produced from the former two, like an effect from its causes. The effect of spiritual love toward the neighbor (signified by **Simeon**) acting through the affection for truth (signified by **Levi**) produces the "good of life" (signified by **Issachar**). He was also named from "hire" or reward (Genesis 30:17, 18), <note>original: "שָׂכָר" (sakar), meaning hire or wages.</note> and thus represents action or good works.

### 363.
**After these things I saw, and behold, a great multitude, which no one could number**, signifies all the rest who are not among those specifically listed, yet who belong to the Lord's **New Heaven** and **New Church** <term>New Church: A spiritual community defined by a new, internal understanding of the Word and a life of charity.</term>, making up the lowest level of heaven and the external church, whose true nature no one knows but the Lord alone.

That the rest, who are not included in the previous list but are still in the Lord's heaven and church, are signified by the "great multitude," is evident from verses 9, 10, and 13–17. In those verses, it is said that *they stood before the throne and before the Lamb, clothed in white robes, and palms in their hands; and that they shall serve Him in His temple; and He that sitteth upon the throne shall dwell among them*; among other descriptions.

In the spiritual sense, to "number" signifies to know the nature or quality of something. This meaning of numbering will be explained further in the following paragraph. However, who specifically is meant by this "great multitude" cannot be understood without a certain <term>arcanum: A hidden spiritual secret or mystery</term> which must first be revealed.

This <term>arcanum</term> is as follows: The whole of heaven, together with the church on earth, appears before the Lord as **one Man** <note>This refers to the "Grand Man" (Latin: *Maximus Homo*), a central concept in Swedenborg's work where the entire spiritual universe is organized in the form of a human body. Different groups of people correspond to different organs and functions based on their specific spiritual character.</note>. Because it exists as one Man, there are those who constitute the head (and thus the face with all its sensory organs), and there are those who constitute the body with all its members. 

Up to this point, the text has listed those who make up the face and its senses. Those now mentioned—the "great multitude"—are they who constitute the body and its limbs. This has been revealed to me, as well as the fact that those in the first class of the tribes (verse 5) correspond to the forehead down to the eyes; those in the second class (verse 6) correspond to the eyes and the nose; and those in the third (verse 7) correspond to the ears and...

### 364.
The reason why "to number" in the spiritual sense signifies to know the nature or quality of something is because a number in the Word <note>The "Word" refers to the Sacred Scripture or the Bible.</note> does not signify a literal count, but rather the quality of a thing (n. 10). Therefore, in this passage, the phrase *a great multitude which no one could number* means, in the natural sense, that the crowd was vast. However, in the spiritual sense, it means that no one but the Lord alone knows their internal quality. 

For the Lord’s heaven consists of countless societies, and these societies are distinguished according to the various types of affections <note>original: "affectionum"; in this context, "affections" means the fundamental loves or desires that drive a person's spirit.</note> in general, and the same applies to everyone within each society. The Lord alone knows the specific quality of every individual's affection and organizes everyone into order based on it. This knowledge of spiritual quality is what the angels understand by "numbering." This same meaning is found in these passages of the Word: 

*When Belshazzar <note>The last king of Babylon, whose story is told in the Book of Daniel.</note> drank wine from the vessels of the temple of Jerusalem, it was written on the wall: "Thou art numbered, thou art numbered"* <note>original: "Mene, Mene"; from the Aramaic, traditionally interpreted as "God has numbered your kingdom and finished it."</note> (Dan. v. 2, 5, 25). 

*I shall go to the gates of hell, I am numbered* (Isa. xxxviii. 10). 

*A voice of the tumult of the kingdoms; Jehovah Zebaoth <note>original: "Jehovah Zebaoth"; translated as "The Lord of Hosts," signifying the Lord's power over the spiritual "armies" or truths of heaven.</note> numbereth the host of battle* (Isa. xiii. 4). 

*Behold who hath created these, that bringeth out their host by number* (Isa. xlm. 26). 

*Jehovah who numbereth the host of the stars* (Ps. cxlvii. 4). 

*The flocks shall yet pass under the hands of...*

### 367.
**Clothed in white robes, and palms in their hands**, signifies communication and conjunction with the higher heavens, and confession from Divine truths. ### 368.
**And crying with a great voice, saying, Salvation unto our God who sitteth upon the throne, and unto the Lamb**, signifies a heartfelt acknowledgment that the Lord is their Savior. "To cry with a great voice" signifies acknowledgment from the heart. "Salvation unto our God who sitteth upon the throne and unto the Lamb" signifies that the Lord is salvation itself, that the salvation of all people comes from Him, and thus that He is the Savior. 

By "Him who sits upon the throne" and by "the Lamb," the Lord alone is meant. "He who sits upon the throne" refers to His Divine essence, from which all things exist, and "the Lamb" refers to His <term>Divine Human: The concept that God took on a human form, glorified it, and made it Divine, allowing humanity to connect with the infinite God through a visible, personal form.</term>; this was also mentioned previously (n. 273). Both terms are used because He became the Savior through the Divine essence by means of His Divine Human. That they are one is clear from the passages where it is said, *the Lamb in the midst of the throne* (Revelation 5:6; 7:17). 

The Lord is frequently called "Salvation" in the Word, meaning He is the Savior; as in these examples: *My salvation shall not delay, and I will place salvation in Zion* (Isaiah 46:13). *Say to the daughter of Zion, Behold, thy salvation cometh* (Isaiah 62:11). *I gave thee, that thou mayest be my salvation to the end of the earth* (Isaiah 49:6). *This is Jehovah whom we have waited for, we will rejoice and be glad in His salvation* (Isaiah 25:9). In the Hebrew language, salvation is called *Joschia* <note>original: "Joschia"; This is a Latinized spelling of the Hebrew *Yeshu’ah*, which means salvation and is the root of the name Jesus (*Yeshua*).</note>, which is the name Jesus.

However, the "angels" mentioned here refer to those in the lower heavens. Therefore, the phrase describes everyone throughout the whole of heaven. "Standing" signifies to hear and perform what He teaches (n. 366).

->### THE APOCALYPSE REVEALED. [CHAP. VII]<-

### 370.
**And fell upon their faces before the throne, and worshipped God**, signifies their heart's humility and the worship of the Lord arising from that humility. It is evident that falling upon one’s face and worshipping represents a state of deep humility in the heart. Humility before the Lord and the act of worshipping Him is signified by falling before the throne and worshipping God, because "God" refers to His Divine nature—meaning both the Divine Source and the <term>Divine Human: The concept that God took on a human form, glorified it, and made it Divine, allowing humanity to connect with the infinite God through a visible, personal form.</term> (n. 368). These are not separate, but are one God, because they exist as one person.

### 371.
**Saying, Amen**, signifies Divine Truth and its confirmation; as discussed previously (see n. 23, 28, 61). 
<note>In this context, "Amen" is not just a closing word, but a technical term for the endorsement of Truth.</note>

### 372.
**Blessing, and glory, and wisdom, and thanksgiving**, signifies the <term>Spiritual Divine: Aspects of God specifically relating to His Wisdom and Truth, rather than His Love.</term> attributes of the Lord. Any acknowledgment and confession of the Lord generally includes two fundamental realizations: that He is Divine Love itself and Divine Wisdom itself. Consequently, all love (and everything associated with it) in heaven and in the church comes from Him; the same is true for all wisdom. 

Whatever proceeds from the Lord’s Divine Love is called the **Heavenly Divine**, and whatever proceeds from His Divine Wisdom is called the **Spiritual Divine**. 

*   The Lord’s **Spiritual Divine** is meant by the terms "glory, wisdom, and thanksgiving." 
*   The **Heavenly Divine** is meant by "honor, power, and might," which follow in the text. 

"Blessing," which precedes these, refers to both aspects together (see n. 289). It is established that "glory" is associated with Divine Truth, and thus with the Spiritual Divine (n. 249). It is clear that "wisdom" relates to the same. "Thanksgiving" also belongs to this category because it arises from Divine Truth; a person gives thanks through the understanding provided by that Truth.

### 373.
**And honor, and power, and might**, signifies the <term>Heavenly Divine: Aspects of God specifically relating to His Love and Goodness.</term> attributes of the Lord. As stated in the previous paragraph, these three—honor, power, and might—when used in the Word in reference to the Lord, refer to His Heavenly Divine, His Divine Love, or His Divine Good.

However, these words can only be distinguished by those who study the <term>Spiritual Sense: The deeper, symbolic meaning of scripture that lies beneath the literal stories and descriptions.</term> From that perspective, it becomes clear which words relate to "good" or love, and which relate to "truth" or wisdom. ### 374. 
***Unto our God for ever and ever.*** This signifies that these attributes exist in the Lord and proceed from the Lord for all eternity, as is clear from the previous discussion; "for ever and ever" simply means to eternity.

### 375. 
***Amen***, signifies the agreement or consent of everyone. In this verse, the word “Amen” appears at both the beginning and the end. When used at the beginning, it signifies Truth and its confirmation (as seen in section 371); but when used at the end, it signifies confirmation and the shared consent of all that what has been said is indeed the truth.

This is signified by dwelling among them, because “*to dwell*” in the Word <note>The "Word" refers to the Sacred Scriptures or the Bible.</note> relates to good, and *to serve*, to truth. 

Here this <term>hidden spiritual truth</term> <note>original: "arcanum." This refers to a deep theological mystery or a secret of the spiritual world.</note> is now to be disclosed—that the marriage of the Lord with the church consists in this, that the Lord flows into angels and men with the good of love, and that the angels and men receive Him or His good of love in truths; that thereby a marriage of good and truth is effected, which marriage is the church itself, and becomes heaven with them. Because the Lord’s <term>influx</term> <note>A technical term describing the way Divine life and energy flow from God into the human soul and the created world.</note> and the reception of Him are such, the Lord therefore looks at angels and men in the forehead, and they look in turn at the Lord through the eyes: for the forehead corresponds to the good of love, and the eyes correspond to truths from that good, which thus by conjunction become truths of good. 

But the <term>influx</term> of the Lord with truths into angels and men is not like the <term>influx</term> of good with them; for it is mediate <note>Meaning it acts through an intermediary or middle stage, rather than directly.</note>, flowing forth from good as light from fire, and is received in the understanding by them, and in the will as far as they do the truths. This therefore is the marriage of love and wisdom, or of good and truth, from the Lord, with them that receive it in the heavens and on earth. This <term>hidden spiritual truth</term> is disclosed, that it may be known how it is to be understood that the Lord continually fills their truths with good.

**381.** *They shall not hunger any more, nor thirst any more,*

...signifies that hereafter goodness and truths shall not be lacking to them. By **not hungering** is signified not to have a lack of what is good, and by **not thirsting** is signified no lack of truth; for hunger relates to bread and food, and thirst to wine and water. In the spiritual language of the Bible, bread and food signify goodness, while wine and water signify truth (see section 323).

382. ***Neither shall the sun fall upon them, nor any heat***, signifies that hereafter they shall not have <term>concupiscences</term> <note>original: "concupiscentiae." In this context, it refers to intense, driving cravings for things that are spiritually or morally harmful.</note> toward evil, nor toward the <term>falsity of evil</term> <note>This refers to false ideas or delusions that spring from a person's underlying selfish or harmful motives.</note>. 

**The sun shall not fall upon them** signifies that they shall not have cravings for evil. **Nor shall any heat fall upon them** signifies that they shall not have cravings for what is false. The reason the sun signifies <term>Divine Love</term> and the affections for goodness that come from it—or, in the opposite sense, "diabolical love" and the cravings for evil—can be seen in earlier notes (see section 53). 

However, "heat" specifically signifies the lust for the falsity of evil because falsehood is produced from evil in the same way that heat is produced from the sun. When the human will loves what is evil, the understanding begins to love what is false, and it becomes "heated" by the desire to prove that its falsehoods are true. Evil that has been confirmed by the mind is what we call the "falsity of evil"; therefore, the falsity of evil is simply evil taking a visible or intellectual form. 

"Heat" and "to be hot" carry this same meaning in the following passages of Scripture:

*   *Blessed is the man who trusts in Jehovah; he shall not see when heat comes* (Jeremiah 17:7, 8). 
*   *You have been a refuge to the needy from the storm, and a shade from the heat. He tempers the heat with the shadow of a cloud* (Isaiah 25:4, 5). 
*   *When they are heated, I will make them drunk, that they may sleep a perpetual sleep* (Jeremiah 51:39). 
*   *They are all hot as an oven; not one among them calls unto me* (Hosea 7:7). 
*   *He does not look toward the way of the vineyards; drought and heat consume the waters of the snow* (Job 24:18, 19). 
*   *The fourth angel poured out his bowl <note>original: "phialam," often translated as "vial" or "bowl."</note> upon the sun, and it was given to him to scorch men with a great heat; and they blasphemed the name of God* (Revelation 16:8, 9). 
*   *That you may say to the prisoners, "Go forth"; they shall not hunger nor thirst, neither shall the heat strike them* (Isaiah 49:9, 10).

**383.** ***For the Lamb who is in the midst of the throne shall feed them***, means that the Lord alone will teach them. By the "Lamb in the midst of the throne" is meant the Lord in His <term>Divine Human</term> <note>original: "Divinum Humanum." This is the central concept in Swedenborg's theology that God became human in Jesus Christ, uniting the infinite Divine with a human form to make Himself accessible to people.</note> at the very center, and therefore in every part of heaven. To be "in the midst" means to be at the inmost core and thus present in everything (see section 44). The "throne" represents heaven (section 14), and the "Lamb" is the Lord in His Divine Human (sections 269, 291). Because He is at the core and thus present in all things, He alone "feeds"—that is, teaches—everyone. 

If one asks how He alone can teach everyone, let it be known that it is because He is God, and because He is present throughout the entire heaven just as the soul is present in its body; for heaven, as it originates from Him, is like a single "Grand Man." To "feed" means to teach, because in the Bible the church is called a "flock," and the people of the church are called "sheep" and "lambs." Therefore, to feed means to teach, and the "shepherd" represents the one who teaches. This is shown in many passages, such as:

*   *Jesus said to Peter, "Feed my lambs"; the second and third time He said, "Feed my sheep"* (John 21:15–17).

Since "living fountains of water" represent both the Lord and the Word, and "waters" represent truths (section 50), this signifies the Divine truths of the Word when they have become part of a person's life.

Does He not also give us the ability to do those things which belong to charity? Do you not see how absurd it is to call charity 'earthly'? Charity is heavenly; and because you do not practice the good of charity, your faith is actually what is earthly. Perhaps you are <term>vivified</term> <note>original: "vivificatur." This refers to being "made alive" or "animated" spiritually.</note> unconsciously. The reason why there was darkness when the window was made on the right side, is because light flowing in from heaven on that side affects the **will**; and the cause of its being light when a window was made on the left side, the window on the right being shut, is because light flowing in from heaven on the left side affects the **understanding**: and every man can be in the light of heaven as to the **understanding**, provided the **will** is closed as to its evil.

->THE APOCALYPSE REVEALED. [CHAP. VIII.<-

"who stood before God," *signifies* the entire spiritual heaven in the Lord's presence, hearing and doing the things which he teaches. "And there were given unto them seven trumpets," *signifies* the exploration and disclosure of the state of the church and thence of the life of those who are in <term>faith alone</term> <note>The doctrine that salvation is achieved through belief or "faith" without the necessity of "good works" or charity.</note>. "And another angel came and stood at the altar, having a golden censer," *signifies* spiritual worship, which is from the good of <term>charity</term> <note>In this theological context, charity refers to the active love of one's neighbor and the performance of good deeds.</note> by the truths of faith. ### THE EXPLANATION.

387. There are two kingdoms into which the Universal Heaven is distinguished, the ***Heavenly (Celestial) Kingdom*** and the ***Spiritual Kingdom***. The Heavenly Kingdom consists of those who are in love to the Lord, and thence in wisdom; and the Spiritual Kingdom of those who are in love towards the neighbor, and thence in intelligence: and because love towards the neighbor is at this day called **charity**, and intelligence **faith**, the latter kingdom consists of those who are in charity and thence in faith. Now because heaven is distinguished into two kingdoms, hell is also distinguished into two kingdoms opposite to them, — into the ***Diabolical Kingdom*** and the ***Satanic Kingdom***. The Diabolical Kingdom consists of them that are in the love of ruling from the love of self, and thence in foolishness; for that love is opposite to heavenly love, and its foolishness is opposite to heavenly wisdom: but the Satanic Kingdom consists of those that are in the love of ruling from the pride of their own intelligence, and thence in insanity; for that love is opposite to...
