Among the children of Israel, there were two Altars: the one outside the tent and the one inside.

*   The altar outside the tent was called the **Altar of Burnt-offering**, because burnt-offerings and sacrifices were performed there.
*   The altar inside the tent was called the **Altar of Incense** and also the **Golden Altar**.

The reason for there being two altars was that the worship of the Lord originates from two types of love: **heavenly** (or <term>celestial</term> <note>Direct love for the Lord, associated with the highest degree of heaven.</note>) love and **spiritual** love. Heavenly love is found in those who are in His heavenly kingdom, while spiritual love is found in those who are in His spiritual kingdom. For more on these two kingdoms, see above (n. 387). Regarding the two altars, one may look to the following passages in the writings of <term>Moses</term> <note>The first five books of the Bible (the Torah).</note>: the **Altar of Burnt-offering** is described in Exodus 20:21 to the end, 27:1–8, and 39:36–43, as well as Leviticus 7:1–5, 8:11, and 16:18, 19, 33, 34; the **Altar of Incense** is described in Exodus 30:1–10, 31:8, 37:25–29, 40:5, 26, and Numbers 7:1. 395. **And the angel took the censer and filled it with fire from the altar, and cast it unto the earth**, signifies spiritual love in which is <term>heavenly love</term> <note>original: "amor coelestis"; often translated as "celestial love," meaning the highest form of love—direct love for the Lord.</note>, and the <term>influx</term> <note>The spiritual process of life and energy flowing from the Divine through the heavens and into the lower worlds.</note> of it into the lower parts, where those were who are in **faith separate from charity**. Spiritual love, which is charity, derives its essence from heavenly love, which is love to the Lord. Without the latter love there is nothing living in spiritual love, or charity...

This was for the reason that the fire of that altar signified the Lord's **Divine Love**, and hence love to the Lord. By **casting the censer unto the earth** is signified <term>influx</term> <note>The constant flow of life and influence from the spiritual world into the minds of people on earth or in lower spiritual regions.</note> into the lower parts.

396. **And there were voices and thunders and lightnings and an earthquake**, signifies that after communication was opened with them, there were heard reasonings concerning **faith alone** <note>The theological doctrine that salvation is achieved through belief alone, without the necessity of good works or a life of charity.</note> and confirmations in favor of it, and the state of the church with them was perceived to be tottering to destruction. That **lightnings, thunders, and voices** signify enlightenments, perceptions, and instructions, by influx from heaven, may be seen above (number 236). But here, with those who were in faith alone, and who had no enlightenment, perception, and instruction, by influx from heaven, reasonings about faith alone and argumentations and confirmations in favor of it are signified by the **voices**, the **thunders**, and the **lightnings**. By the **earthquake** changes of state of the church are signified (number 331); here that the state of the church with them was perceived to be tottering to its destruction. For earthquakes take place in the <term>world of spirits</term> <note>The intermediate realm where people go immediately after death to be prepared for heaven or hell.</note>, when the state of the church in the societies is perverted and inverted. The reason that the censer was cast by the angel unto the earth before the seven angels began to sound the trumpets was, that communication might be opened by influx between those who were in the spiritual heaven, and those below who were in faith alone;

The sounding of the second angel was into the sea; and by the earth and the sea, everywhere in the Apocalypse, when both are named, the entire church is meant. By the earth is meant the church composed of those who are in its <term>internals</term> <note>The "internals" refer to the inner spiritual life, where a person’s motives and deep understanding of truth reside.</note>, and by the sea the church composed of those that are in its <term>externals</term> <note>The "externals" refer to the outward expressions of faith, such as participating in rituals or possessing a basic, literal knowledge of scripture without deeper reflection.</note>. For the church is both internal and external—internal with the <term>clergy</term> <note>Specifically those who teach and lead based on a deep study of doctrine.</note>, and external with the <term>laity</term> <note>The general congregation or those who follow the teachings in a more practical, everyday manner.</note>; or internal with those who have studied its doctrines interiorly and have confirmed them from the <term>Word</term> <note>The Word refers to the Sacred Scripture or the Bible, viewed as the source of Divine Truth.</note>, and external with those who have not done so. 

The latter and the former are they who are meant by the earth and the sea in these passages in the Apocalypse: *That the wind should not blow upon the earth, nor upon the sea* (vii. 1). *That they should not hurt the earth nor the sea* (vii. 3). *The angel coming down out of heaven set his right foot upon the sea and his left upon the earth* (x. 2, 8: also, verse 5). *I saw a beast coming up out of the sea, and another beast coming up out of the earth* (xiii. 1, 11). *Praise God, who made the heaven, the earth, and the sea* (xiv. 7). *The first angel poured out his vial upon the earth, and the second angel his upon the sea* (xvi. 2, 3). 

By the earth and the sea the church internal and external, and thus the entire church, is signified, because in the <term>spiritual world</term> <note>In Swedenborg's theology, the spiritual world is structured according to the internal states of its inhabitants; thoughts and affections create the surrounding landscape.</note> they who are in the internals of the church appear upon dry land, and they that are in the externals appear as if in the seas; but the seas are appearances arising from the general truths in which they abide. That the earth signifies the church may be seen in entry n. 285. That the "world" stands for the same may be seen in entry n. 551.

By this word is signified <note>The original Latin likely referred to *gramen* (grass). The OCR "Word" is likely a transcription error for "By 'grass' is signified."</note> the good and truth of the church or of faith, which first takes root in the **natural man**. <term>Natural man</term> <note>In this context, the "natural man" refers to the external part of our personality that deals with the physical world and its senses, as opposed to the "spiritual man" which deals with internal, heavenly things.</note> The same meaning is also carried by the "herb of the field." Because faith lives from goodness and truth, the image of **all the green grass being burnt up** signifies that every living element of faith has perished. A living faith dies when there is no longer an affection for what is good or a clear perception of what is true (see the explanation provided just above). 

That "grass" carries this meaning is also due to <term>correspondence</term>; <note>A central concept in this work, "correspondence" is the idea that every physical object in the world mirrors a specific spiritual or mental reality.</note> for this reason, those in the **spiritual world** who separate faith from **charity** <note>Charity here means the active love of one's neighbor and doing what is right, rather than just donating money.</note>—not only in their religious teachings but also in how they live—dwell in deserts where no grass grows. 

Just as a **fruit-tree** signifies a person’s affections for good and their perceptions of truth, so **green grass** signifies the very first things of the church that are conceived and born within a person. Conversely, grass that is **not green** signifies that these early spiritual states have been destroyed. In general, all the elements found in gardens, forests, fields, and plains signify something about the church in a person, because they all correspond to spiritual states. 

That **grass** has this meaning is evident from these passages of Scripture: 

*   *The voice said, "Cry out"; and he said, "What shall I cry? All flesh is grass: the grass withereth, and the flower fadeth because the wind hath blown upon it; truly the people is grass: the grass withereth, and the flower fadeth, but the Word of our God shall stand for ever"* (Isaiah 40:5–8). 
*   *The inhabitants were as an herb of the field, a green herb, the grass of the roofs; and a field scorched before the corn is grown up* (Isaiah 37:27; 2 Kings 19:26). 
*   *I will pour my blessing upon thy seed, and they shall spring up as among the grass* (Isaiah 44:3, 4). 

This is also seen elsewhere, such as in Isaiah 51:12; Psalm 37:2; Psalm 103:15, Psalm 129:6; and Deuteronomy 32:2. That the term **green** (or "growing green") signifies being spiritually alive is manifest in Jeremiah 17:8 and 11:16; Ezekiel 17:24 and 20:47; Hosea 14:8; and Psalms 37:35, 52:8, and 92:10. 

The same events described here in the **Apocalypse** <note>The Book of Revelation.</note> also occurred in **Egypt**, namely, that *from hail and fire mingled, every tree and every herb of the field was burnt up* (Exodus 9:28–35; Psalm 78:47–49; Psalm 105:32, 33).

**402.** *And the second angel sounded*, signifies an exploration and a making clear of the specific quality of the church’s state among those who are only in the external or outward forms of that faith. The act of an angel **sounding a trumpet** signifies the exploration and manifestation of the church’s condition—and consequently the state of life—among those whose religion consists of <term>faith alone</term>. <note>"Faith alone" (Latin: *sola fide*) refers to the theological doctrine that salvation comes through belief without the necessity of good works.</note> This has been discussed previously (see number 397). 

These words specifically address those who are in the outward aspects of that faith. This is because the text is now dealing with those who were "in the sea," whereas the previous section dealt with those "upon the earth." Those who are in the internal or deeper parts of the church—the **clergy**—are signified by the "earth"; meanwhile, those in the external or surface-level parts of the church—the <term>laity</term> <note>The "laity" refers to the general members of a church congregation as distinguished from the ordained clergy.</note>—are signified by the "sea" (see number 398). In the **spiritual world**, these people actually appear as if they are in the sea (see numbers 238, 290).

**403.** *And as it were a mountain burning with fire was cast into the sea*, signifies the appearance of <term>infernal love</term> <note>Swedenborg uses the term "infernal love" to describe a self-centered, destructive love that is the opposite of heavenly, selfless love.</note> among those who are in the outward reaches of the church and hold to faith alone. 

As established, the "sea" signifies the church among those in the external world, commonly called the **laity**, because those in the internal world are called the **clergy** (see numbers 397, 402). In the language of <term>correspondence</term>, <note>The author's system where natural objects represent spiritual realities.</note> a **mountain** signifies love; therefore, a **mountain burning with fire** signifies a love that is infernal or hellish (see numbers 494, 599). This love becomes visible and manifest among the people described here, appearing clearly before the angels. 

The reason for this is that "faith alone" is a faith separated from **charity** (see number 388); and where there is no charity—that is, no spiritual love toward one's neighbor—only infernal love remains. There is no middle ground or "neutral" love, except in the case of the "lukewarm," who are discussed elsewhere in the Book of Revelation (Chapter 3, verses 15 and 16).

**404.** *And a third part of the sea became blood*, signifies that all the general truths among them were falsified. By the term **a third part**, the text signifies "all" (see number 400). By **blood**, the falsification of the truth of the Word is signified (see number 379). The **sea** signifies the church among those who are in the externals of...

The reason for this is that the <term>Word</term> <note>original: "Verbum"; referring to the Sacred Scriptures as Divine Truth.</note> communicates with heaven. The <term>spiritual sense</term> <note>The inner, symbolic meaning of scripture that relates to the soul and heaven.</note> of the Word also flows in into its <term>natural sense</term> <note>The literal or historical meaning of the Bible text.</note>, as the sun with its light into the moon, which presents the light of the sun <term>mediately</term> <note>Acting as an intermediary; reflecting light indirectly rather than being the source.</note>. Every one is enlightened according to his spiritual affection for truth and good, and at the same time according to the genuine truths by which he has opened his <term>rational</term> <note>The faculty of the human mind that allows for reasoning and understanding spiritual concepts.</note>. By the triple "woe, woe, woe," the highest degree of lamentation is expressed; for in the <term>spiritual sense</term> <note>The underlying symbolic meaning of the Bible where numbers have specific qualities.</note>, a three-fold repetition makes a statement superlative, because the number <term>three</term> <note>In Swedenborg's system of "correspondences," the number three signifies completeness, fullness, or the total extent of a thing.</note> signifies what is complete and full.

“Drink wine from the Word <term>Word</term> <note>In Swedenborg’s writings, "The Word" refers to the Sacred Scripture (the Bible), which is considered to be Divine Truth itself.</note> understood. After this he turned himself to the clergy, and said, “Ministers of God, do not mislead the flock.” 

On hearing these things, the greatest part of the flock to the left withdrew and associated themselves with the flock to the right. <note>This imagery alludes to the biblical separation of the sheep and the goats, where the right hand represents those who live according to the truth.</note> Some also of the clergy then said, “We have heard what we have not heard before. We are shepherds; we will not leave the sheep.” And they withdrew together with them, and said, “That man spoke a true word. Who, that acts from the Word, and thus from the Lord—His mouth and will—can say, ‘I do this of myself’? We now see the Divine Providence <term>Divine Providence</term> <note>The laws and operations of God's government regarding the salvation and spiritual development of human beings.</note>, why a conjunction <term>conjunction</term> <note>The spiritual union between a person and God, often compared to a marriage of the heart and the mind.</note> of faith and works has not been found out, which has been acknowledged by the ecclesiastical body. It could not be found out, because it cannot be given. For there is not faith in the Lord, who is the Word; and hence neither is there faith from the Word.” 

But the rest of the priests went away, and swung their caps, and shouted “**Faith alone, faith alone**; it will live still!” <note>original: "sola fide." These priests represent the stubborn defense of the doctrine that belief is the only requirement for heaven, regardless of how one lives their life.</note>

## THE SPIRITUAL SENSE

**The Contents of the whole Chapter.** Concerning the exploration and manifestation of the state of the life of those in the Church of the Reformed <note>The "Church of the Reformed" refers to the Protestant denominations arising from the Reformation.</note> who are called learned and wise from the confirmation of faith separated from charity <note>The concept of "faith alone," or believing in God without the necessity of performing good works (charity).</note>, and of justification and salvation by it alone: these are treated of, vers. 1—13. Concerning the exploration and manifestation of those therein who are not so learned and wise, and are in faith alone, and live as they list <note>Live according to their own desires or whims.</note>: these are treated of, vers. 13—20. Lastly, concerning those therein who know nothing but that faith is the all by which man is saved, and not any thing besides this, vers. 20, 21.

**The Contents of each Verse.** “The fifth angel sounded,” *signifies* the exploration and manifestation of the state of the life of those in the Church of the Reformed who are called learned and wise from their confirmation of faith separate from charity, and of justification and salvation by it alone. “And I saw a star fallen from heaven unto the earth,” *signifies* spiritual Divine Truth flowing in out of heaven into the church with them, exploring and manifesting. “And there was given unto him the key of the pit of the abyss <note>original: "puteus abyssi"; the "pit of the abyss" symbolizes the opening of the deeper reaches of the mind where false or hellish ideas are stored.</note>,” *signifies* the opening of their hell. “And he opened the pit of the abyss, and there went up a smoke out of the pit as the smoke of a great furnace,” *signifies* the falsities <term>falsities: specific deceptive beliefs that arise from evil motivations</term> of the lusts of the natural man arising from their evil loves. “And the sun and the air were darkened from the smoke of the pit,” *signifies* that thence

**"And the rest of the men, who were not killed by these plagues,"** *signifies* those in the church of the Reformed <note>The "Reformed" refers to the Protestant denominations arising from the Reformation, particularly those following the teachings of Calvin or Luther.</note>, who are not so spiritually dead from visionary reasonings, and from the love of self, from the pride of their own intelligence, and from the lusts thence, as the former, and still make **faith alone** <term>faith alone: the doctrine that salvation is granted by belief in God's grace entirely independent of one's actions or "good works"</term> the head of their religion. **"Yet repented not of the works of their hands,"** *signifies* that neither did they shun as sins the things of their own which are evils of every kind. **"That they should not worship demons,"** *signifies* that thus they are in the evils of their lusts, and make one with their like in hell. **"And idols of gold and silver and brass and stone and wood,"** *signifies* that thus they are in worship from mere falsities. **"Which neither can see nor hear nor walk,"** *signifies* in which there is nothing of spiritual and truly rational life. **"And repented not of their murders nor of their enchantments nor of their whoredoms nor of their thefts,"** *signifies* that the heresy of faith alone induces in the hearts stupidity, **tergiversation** <note>tergiversation: a tendency to evade the truth, use ambiguous language, or stall in one’s moral duties</note>, and hardness, so that they do not think any thing of the precepts of the **decalogue** <term>decalogue: the Ten Commandments, which the author views as the essential foundation for a spiritual life</term>, nor indeed of any sin that it is to be shunned because it is with the devil and against God.

419. **And the fifth angel sounded,** *signifies* the exploration and manifestation of the state of the life of those in the Church of the Reformed, who are called learned and wise from their confirmation of faith separate from charity <note>charity: in this context, the active love of the neighbor expressed through useful service and ethical living</note>, and of **justification** <term>justification: the theological process by which a person is made or declared righteous in the sight of God</term> and salvation by it alone. That these are treated of in what now follows as far as to vers. 12, is evident from the particulars when understood in the **spiritual sense**. That by sounding is signified to explore and manifest the state of the church and thence of the life with those whose religion is faith alone, may be seen above (n. 397).

**420.** **"And I saw a star fallen from heaven unto the earth,"** *signifies* spiritual Divine Truth flowing from heaven into the church among those people, examining and revealing [their state]. Spiritual Divine Truth is represented here by the **star**, because it fell from the spiritual heaven mentioned previously (in sections 387 and 388); and the **earth** signifies the church among those who are focused on its internal matters (as in section 398). By "spiritual Divine Truth," the author means intelligence born from spiritual love—which is love toward one's neighbor. Because this intelligence is commonly called **faith** today, and that love is called **charity**, the star signifies faith derived from charity. More precisely, it represents the truth of faith that comes from the good of charity. A "star" has the same meaning in the singular in Revelation 2:28 and 22:16; for "stars" in the plural signify the knowledge of what is good and true (section 51), and intelligence is gained through this knowledge. That this represents Divine Truth examining and revealing the state of the church is clear from the verses that follow.

**421.** **"And there was given unto him the key of the pit of the abyss,"** *signifies* the opening of their hell. A **key** signifies the power to open, as well as the act of opening (sections 62, 174, 840). The **abyss** signifies the specific hell inhabited by those who have convinced themselves of **justification** <term>justification: the theological process of being declared righteous or "right" with God</term> and salvation through **faith alone** <term>faith alone: the doctrine that belief in God's grace is the only requirement for salvation, regardless of one's actions or "works"</term>. These individuals are all from the **Church of the Reformed** <note>The "Church of the Reformed" refers to the various Protestant denominations that broke away from the Catholic Church during the Reformation.</note>. 

However, this specifically refers to those who—in their own eyes and the eyes of many others—appear to be learned and scholarly, yet appear to the angels in heaven as having no understanding of matters regarding heaven and the church. This is because those who confirm the doctrine of "faith alone" into their deepest thoughts effectively shut off the higher levels of their intellect. Eventually, they reach a point where they can no longer see any spiritual truth in its proper light. The reason for this is that the act of confirming a falsehood is, in itself, a denial of the truth. Consequently, when they hear any spiritual truth—meaning a truth from the **Word** <note>The "Word" is a term for the Holy Scriptures or the Bible.</note> that serves as a guide for doctrine and life for those in the church...

422. ***And he opened the pit of the abyss, and there went up a smoke out of the pit as the smoke of a great furnace,*** signifies the falsities <note>falsities: in this context, specific lies or errors in thinking that stem from a person's selfish desires.</note> of the lusts of the **natural man** <term>natural man: a person who lives according to their worldly impulses and sensory experiences, rather than according to spiritual or divine principles</term> arising from their evil loves. "A great furnace" signifies the same thing, since a furnace smokes from fire.

The infernal spirits are not in any material fire, but in spiritual fire, which is their love; and therefore they do not feel any other fire. By **"not hurting the grass of the earth, nor any green thing,"** is signified not to be able to take away any truth and good of faith; for the **truth of faith**, which is the first thing springing up in a person's mind, is signified by **grass** (n. 401): and by a **green thing** is signified the living principle of faith, which comes from a state of goodness (n. 401). 

By **not hurting any tree** is signified not to be able to take away the affection for and perception of truth and good; for a person, in regard to these inner perceptions, is signified by a **tree** (n. 400). 

By **them that have not the seal of God upon their foreheads** those are signified who are not in charity and consequently not in faith; for the **forehead** signifies love and charity (n. 347); and to have a **seal** signifies to know and distinguish these individuals from others (n. 345). 

The reason that those who have confirmed the doctrine of **faith alone** <term>faith alone: the theological belief that salvation is achieved through belief or intellectual assent without the necessity of good works</term>—even to the point of the hidden **arcana** <term>arcana: deep secrets or hidden mysteries</term> of justification and salvation by it—cannot take away any truth and good of faith, nor affection and perception, from any but those who are not in the faith of charity, is because scarcely anyone except the **prelate** <term>prelate: a high-ranking church official or clergyman</term> who teaches and preaches them, actually comprehends those things. 

The **layman** <term>layman: a member of the congregation, as distinguished from the clergy</term> hears them; but they pass in through one of his ears, and out at the other. The mystery-preaching priest himself may know this from the fact that he has himself expended all the force of his talent in absorbing them in his youth, and afterwards in trying to retain them in his later years; he even esteems himself "super-learned" because of them. 

What then shall the layman do—who simply thinks of faith as something born from charity—when he hears these mystic notions? It may be seen from this, that "faith alone" as a means of justification is the faith of the **clergy**, and not of the **laity**, except for those who live carelessly. These people draw from those mysteries only this one idea: that faith alone saves; that they cannot do good of themselves; and that they...

**427. And it was given to them that they should not kill them, but that they should torment them five months,** signifies that it is of the Lord’s **Divine Providence** <term>Divine Providence: the constant and all-wise government of the Lord over the spiritual and physical worlds</term> that they cannot take away from those who are not in the **faith of charity** <term>faith of charity: a living faith that is inseparable from active love for one's neighbor</term> the faculty of understanding and willing truth and good, but can only induce a stupor for a short time. 

By “its being given to them” is signified that it is of the Divine Providence of the Lord, as mentioned just above. “Not to be able to kill them” signifies not to be able to take away from those who are not in the faith of charity the faculty of understanding and willing truth and good; for when this faculty is taken away, the person is **spiritically killed**. 

By “tormenting them five months” is signified *to induce a stupor for a short time.* *Five* signifies a little, or for a short time; and to *torment* signifies to induce a stupor, because this is signified by a scorpion (n. 425), and by torment as of a scorpion, as follows (n. 428). That the faculty of understanding truth and of willing it—or **rationality** and **liberty**—cannot be taken away from a person, is shown in many places in the *Angelic Wisdom concerning the Divine Providence* <note>original: "Sapientia Angelica de Divina Providentia," a work by Swedenborg exploring how God maintains human freedom</note> (n. 73, 74, 82—86, 92—98, 138—149, 322). 

“**Five months**” signify a little, or a short time, because this is what the number *five* signifies: for times—whether they be hours, days, weeks, months, or years—do not signify actual time, but rather a state of being; and the numbers determine the quality of that state (n. 4, 10, 348, 947). That **five** signifies "some," and also "a little," may be evident from these passages: 

*A thousand shall flee at the rebuke of five (Isaiah 30:17).* 

*Five shall pursue a hundred (Leviticus 26:8).* 

*Jesus said, that the kingdom of the heavens is like unto ten virgins, of whom five were prudent, and five foolish (Matthew 25:1, 2).* 

By the ten virgins, everyone in the church is signified; by **five** is signified a certain part or some. Similar things are signified by ten and five in the parable which says that the pounds were given to the servants so that they might trade, and that...

*from a pound one acquired ten pounds, and another five* (Luke 19:13–20). "Ten pounds" signify much, and "five pounds" signify a little: this symbolism is also found in other passages, such as Isaiah 17:6; 19:18, 19; and Matthew 14:15–22.

**428. And their torment was like the torment of a scorpion when he striketh a man,** signifies that this arises from their **persuasive power** <term>persuasive power: a psychological or spiritual force that can overwhelm another person's judgment, making them believe something is true regardless of the evidence</term>. This follows from what was just stated (n. 427): for "torment" signifies the **stupor** <term>stupor: a state of mental numbness or paralysis where the ability to perceive truth is temporarily suspended</term> which their persuasive power induces upon the understanding, just as a scorpion’s sting affects the physical body. The scorpion signifies that persuasive power (n. 425). In the spiritual world, a persuasive power is active which takes away the capacity to understand truth and induces a stupor, and thus pain, in the **mind** <note>original: "animus," referring to the lower or natural mind</note>; however, this specific persuasive power is unknown in the natural world.

**429. And in those days men shall seek death, and shall not find it, and shall desire to die and death shall flee from them,** signifies that those who adhere to the doctrine of **faith alone** <note>original: "fide separata," or faith separated from charity</term> wish for the understanding to be shut up and the will to be closed in matters of faith. By doing so, they wish to avoid possessing any spiritual light or life; yet, it is still provided by the Lord that the understanding and will should not be closed, so that spiritual light and life are not completely extinguished within the human being. 

"In those days" signifies the final state of the church, when the doctrine concerning faith alone has been universally accepted. "Men shall seek death" signifies that they wish for the understanding to be shut up regarding matters of faith; "and shall not find it" signifies that the Lord’s providence ensures this does not happen. "And shall desire to die" signifies that they also wish for the will to be closed in those same matters; "and death shall flee from them" signifies that it is provided that this cannot be done. If the understanding and will were truly closed, spiritual light and life would be destroyed, and the person would **spiritually die**. "Seeking" is a term used in relation to the understanding, "desiring" relates to the will, and "death" refers to the loss of both. It is evident that this is the meaning of these words.

What otherwise would it mean that “men should seek death in those days, and not find it; and desire to die, and death should flee from them?” For by death, no other death is meant but **spiritual death**, which is brought on when the understanding is removed from the things that should be believed. For in such a state, a person does not know whether they think and do truth or falsity, and thus whether they are with the angels of heaven or with the devils of hell.

**430. *And the likenesses of the locusts,*** signifies the appearances and images of those who have confirmed in themselves **faith separate from charity** <term>faith separate from charity: the theological position that belief alone is necessary for salvation, regardless of one's moral actions or love for others</term>. For the images, which are representative forms of the affections and thoughts of angels and spirits in the spiritual world, appear as if they are alive—just like the animals, birds, and fishes spoken of above.

**431. *Were like unto horses prepared for war,*** signifies that because they can reason, they appeared to themselves as if they were fighting from the understanding of truth from **the Word** <term>the Word: the Sacred Scriptures, understood as divine truth</term>. By the terms "like" or "likenesses," appearances are signified, as noted just above (n. 430).

**432. *And upon their heads were as it were crowns like gold,*** signifies that they appeared to themselves as conquerors. By "crowns upon their heads like unto gold" are signified badges of victory, because kings formerly wore golden crowns in battles (n. 300); for it was said that they were

**433. *And their faces were as the faces of men,*** signifies that they appeared to themselves to be wise. In the Word <term>the Word: a term used to refer to the Holy Scriptures or the Bible</term>, a "man" signifies one who is wise and intelligent (n. 243); and his "face" represents wisdom and intelligence. Because of this, the phrase "their faces were as the faces of men" signifies that they appeared wise to themselves. They are also referred to as wise, learned, and scholarly, even though they are actually among "the foolish virgins who had no oil in their lamps" (Matthew 25:1, 2). Oil signifies love and charity. They are also among "the foolish ones who hear the Lord"—meaning they read the Word—"and do not do it" (Matthew 7:26).

**434. *And they had hair as the hair of women,*** signifies that they appeared to themselves to be moved by an affection for truth. In the Word, a "man" (*vir*) <note>original: "vir," referring to a male specifically as a symbol of the intellect</note> signifies the understanding of truth, and a "woman" signifies the affection for truth. This is because a man is born to be an understanding being, while a woman is born to be an affectionate being; for more on this, see the work *Angelic Wisdom concerning Marriage* <note>The author refers to his own theological treatise on the spiritual nature of gender and marriage</note>. By "hair" in the Word is signified the outermost part of a person's life, which is the **sensual** <term>sensual: the lowest level of human thought, which relies entirely on the physical senses and often leads to spiritual delusion</term>, as described in n. 424. 

This sensual level is what makes them appear to be in an affection for truth, when in reality they are in an affection for what is false; however, they believe this falsity to be the truth. The fact that a "woman" signifies an affection for truth is evident from many passages in the Word. This is why the Church is called a wife, a woman, a daughter, and a virgin; for a Church is only a Church through its love or affection for truth, and it is from this affection that the understanding of truth is born. The Church is called a woman in these passages:

**435. *And their teeth were as those of lions*,** signifies that the **sensual things** <term>sensual things: the lowest level of human thought, which relies entirely on the five senses and physical appearances</term> which are the **ultimates** <term>ultimates: the final, most external, or physical manifestation of a spiritual reality</term> of the life of the natural man, appeared to them to have power over all things. The teeth signify the ultimates of the natural life of man, which are called things sensual, as discussed above (n. 424). 

There are two kinds of sensual things: one which belongs to the will, and another which belongs to the understanding. The sensual things of the will are signified by "the hair of women," which was just addressed (n. 434); and the sensual things of the understanding are signified by the teeth. These sensual things—or, what is the same, "sensual men" who stay in false beliefs because they have confirmed them to themselves—appear to themselves to possess such power over all things that they cannot be defeated. For this reason, the teeth of the locusts (by which such sensual things are signified) were like those of lions. By the "lion" is signified power (n. 241).

**438.** **And they had tails like unto scorpions**, signifies the truths of the Word <note>The "Word" refers to the Sacred Scriptures or the Bible</note> falsified, by which they induce stupor <term>stupor: a state of mental numbness or a dulling of the senses, where a person can no longer perceive spiritual truth</term>. By the tail is signified the ultimate <note>the final or lowest part</note> of the head, because the head continues through the spine of the back into the tail; for this reason, the head and the tail make a single unit, representing the first and the last parts. 

When, therefore, "faith alone" <term>faith alone: the theological doctrine that salvation is achieved through belief or trust in God's grace without the necessity of good works</term>—which is claimed to justify and save—is signified by the head, then the tail signifies all the collective arguments used to confirm that faith. These arguments are drawn from the Word, but they are the truths of the Word falsified. Anyone who creates a religious principle from their own intelligence and makes it the "head" (the leading idea) will then take supporting points from the Word and make them the "tail." In doing so, he brings a stupor upon others, hurting them intellectually. 

This is why it is said that they **"had tails like unto scorpions,"** and immediately after, that **"there were stings in their tails, and their power was to hurt men."** This is because the scorpion signifies a persuasive power that numbs the understanding (see number 425). As for the tail being a continuation of the brain through the spine to its final point, one can ask an anatomist, and he will confirm it; or one might observe a dog or another wild beast with a tail. If you coax and caress him, you will see the hair along the back smooth down and the tail move in harmony; conversely, the hair will rise up if the animal is irritated. 

The primary concept of the understanding, which is adopted as a starting principle, is also signified by the head, while the final result or application is signified by the tail, as in these passages:

By the river Euphrates in the Word <note>The "Word" refers to the Sacred Scriptures or the Bible.</note> those interiors of the human mind which are called **rational** <term>rational: the intermediate level of the mind that connects spiritual insight with worldly knowledge</term> are signified; which, with them who are in truths from good, are full of wisdom, but with those that are in falsities from evil, are full of insanity. The reason that these things are signified in the Word by the river Euphrates, is because that river separated the land of Canaan from Assyria; and by the land of Canaan the church was signified, and by Assyria its rational; and hence by the bounding river those interiors of the mind which are called rational are signified in both senses.

For there are three things which make the man of the church:—the **Spiritual**, the **Rational** or **Intellectual**, and the **Natural**, which is also the faculty of knowing. The spiritual of the church was signified by the land of Canaan and by the rivers in it; the rational or intellectual of the church, by *Ashur* or *Assyria*, and by its river the Euphrates; and the natural of the church, which also is the faculty of knowing, by *Egypt* and its river the *Nile*: but on these subjects see more below (n. 503). 

By "the four angels bound at the river Euphrates" are signified those interiors with the men of the church, which are said to be bound because they are not manifested <note>That is, these inner thoughts and motivations are hidden or suppressed by external social pressures or fears.</note>. For they are infernal spirits which are meant by these four angels, because it is said of them that they were prepared to kill a third part of men, as soon follows (n. 446): and the interiors of men make one with spirits, either infernal or heavenly; since they dwell together. By loosing them is signified to take away external bonds, that the interiors of their minds may appear. These are the things that are signified by those words. 

That by the Euphrates are signified the interiors of the mind of man bordering upon the spiritual things of the church in him, may be evident from the passages in the Word where Ashur or Assyria is named: but the Euphrates occurs in the opposite sense, in which it signifies the interiors full of falsities and thence of insanities, in these passages: *Behold, God bringeth up over them the* <note>original: "Ecce Deus ascendere facit super eos..." referring to Isaiah 8:7</note>

# THE APOCALYPSE REVEALED. [CHAP. IX.

"...whatever a man does of himself, do not **merit** <note>In this context, 'merit' refers to the belief that one's own actions deserve a reward from God.</note> and his own **righteousness** <note>original: *iustitia*, meaning moral uprightness or being 'right' with God.</note> lie concealed? And further, if anyone sins against one thing, he sins against all, because they cohere together. Why did the Lord come into the world, and suffer so grievous a cross, unless that he might take away from us the condemnation and curse of the law, might propitiate God the Father, and might alone become merit and righteousness, which should be **imputed** <note>original: *imputatio*. A theological term meaning to credit Christ’s holiness to a human's spiritual 'account.'</note> to man by faith? On any other ground, what good did His coming do? Or to whom did it do any good? Since therefore Christ suffered for us, and fulfilled the law for us, and took away its right of condemnation, can evil then any longer condemn us? And can good save us? Wherefore we who have faith are in the full liberty of thinking, willing, speaking, and doing whatever we list, provided we do not incur the loss of reputation, honor, and gain, and do not bring upon us the penalties of the civil law, from which come disgrace and injury."

Some, who were wandering more remotely in the north <note>In Swedenborg’s spiritual geography, the 'North' represents a state of coldness or obscure light regarding spiritual truths.</note>, said that "the good works which are done for the sake of **salvation** are injurious, pernicious, and cursed." Among these were also some **presbyters** <note>original: *presbyteri*, referring to church elders or priests.</note>. These are the things that I heard; but they prated and muttered more, which I did not hear. Besides, they spoke shamelessly with all license, and were lascivious both in words and actions, without the restraint of fear for any misdeed, except by pretence for the sake of the appearance of respectability. 

Such are the interiors of the mind, and thence the exteriors of the body, of those who make **faith alone** <note>original: *sola fide*. The doctrine that belief is the only requirement for salvation, often used here to criticize the dismissal of moral living.</note> the all of **religion**. But all these things which were said by them fall to the ground, if the Lord the Saviour Himself is approached immediately, and believed in, and good is done, for the sake of salvation; and if they are done by man as of himself, with the belief, however, that it is from the Lord: and unless these things are done by a man as of himself, there is

450. **Having breastplates of fire, jacinth, and brimstone**, signifies their argumentations—imaginary and visionary—arising from infernal love, their own intelligence, and the lusts derived from them. By the **breastplates** <note>In Swedenborg's system, a breastplate protects the heart and lungs, symbolizing the protection of one's core arguments or beliefs.</note> are signified the argumentations with which they fight for **faith alone** <note>The doctrine that salvation comes through belief alone, without the need for good works or moral living.</note> (n. 436): by **fire** <note>original: *ignis*</note> heavenly love is signified, and in the opposite sense, infernal love (n. 452, 465, 494): by **jacinth** <note>original: *hyacinthus*. A blue gemstone or color, here representing a specific type of logic or intelligence.</note> is signified intelligence from spiritual love, and in the opposite sense, intelligence from infernal love, which is **one's own intelligence** <term>one's own intelligence: *propria intelligentia*, or reasoning that relies solely on the ego rather than divine truth</term>, spoken of below: and by **brimstone** <note>original: *sulphur*</note> is signified lust from that love through one's own intelligence (n. 452). It follows from this, that such things are signified by the breastplates of fire, of jacinth, and of brimstone. 

The reason why their argumentations for faith alone are thus described, is because all those that believe themselves to be justified—that is, absolved from sins—by means of faith alone, never think of **repentance**; and an impenitent man remains in nothing but sins. All sins are derived from, and therefore partake of, infernal love, one's own intelligence, and the lusts that spring from them. Those who are in such a state not only act from these motives, but also speak, think, and will—and consequently reason and argue—from them. These qualities constitute the man, because they are his life; however, such a person is a **man-devil** <note>A term used by the author to describe a person whose internal spirit has become completely aligned with hellish principles.</note>, and his life is an infernal life. 

Indeed, those who live a moral life only for the sake of themselves and the world do not realize this. The cause is that their **interiors** <note>The "internal man" or the hidden spiritual self.</note> are of such a hellish character, while their **exteriors** <note>The "external man" or the personality shown to the world.</note> appear similar to the exteriors of those who live a Christian life. Yet let them know that any person, when they die, enters into their interiors because they become a spirit; and this is their internal man. The interiors then force the exteriors to conform to them, and they become one and the same. On this account, the moral actions of their life in the world then become like the **scales of fishes**, which are wiped away.

<note>original: "ex ore ipsorum"</note> **mouths**, signifies that it is through these things—false doctrines and evil desires—that the members of the church perish spiritually. **A third part of men being killed** signifies that the people of the church perish because of the three things mentioned just above (n. 452). In this context, "to be killed" means to be killed spiritually, which is the death of the soul. **A third part** refers to everyone who is influenced by these falsities, as has been noted frequently.

The meaning of the **fire, smoke, and brimstone**, and their **issuing out of their mouths**, was explained in the previous section (n. 452). Because of these false beliefs, it is not recognized throughout the Christian world that the **fire** described here is actually the **love of self and the world**, and that this specific love is what is meant by "the devil." Furthermore, the **smoke** from that fire represents the **pride of one's own intelligence**, which is meant by "satan." Finally, the **brimstone** ignited by that fire and pride represents the **lusts of evil and falsity**. These lusts make up the "crew" of the devil and satan, which is what hell consists of. When these spiritual realities are not understood, it is impossible to know what sin truly is, for sin derives all its pleasure and appeal from these very things.

454. **And their power was in their mouth**, signifies that these individuals only prevail through speech that reinforces their specific doctrine of faith. **Power in the mouth** refers to the persuasive power of discourse used to confirm a religious teaching. This includes a polished and elegant style of speaking, a feigned religious zeal, and the clever use of "confirmations" of falsity—especially those drawn from the **appearances** <note>Swedenborg uses "appearances" to describe literal meanings of the Bible that can be misinterpreted if not understood through their deeper spiritual sense.</note> in the Word (the Bible). It also involves the use of personal authority and the "closing of the understanding" (demanding blind faith). Through these methods, their discourse achieves everything, while the actual truth and the Word itself achieve nothing. Truth only shines for those who live in **charity** <term>charity: In this context, the active life of doing good and loving one's neighbor, which Swedenborg argues is the necessary foundation for true faith.</term> and, consequently, in true faith; the Word does not teach anyone else.

455. **For their tails were like unto serpents, having heads, and with them do they hurt**, signifies the reason for this: that they are **sensual** <term>sensual: Referring to the lowest level of human thought, which is focused entirely on the physical world and the information provided by the senses, rather than spiritual insight.</term> and their thinking is inverted. They speak truths with their mouths, but they falsify those truths based on the core principle that serves as the "head" of their religious doctrine; in this way, they deceive.

By **serpents** in the Word are signified the <term>sensual things<note>In this theological context, "sensual things" refers to the very lowest level of the human mind—the part that relies entirely on physical senses and material appearances rather than spiritual or rational insight.</note></term> which are the ultimates of man’s life, treated of above (n. 424). The reason is, that serpents creep on the ground and lick up the dust: and sensual things are the lowest things of the understanding and will: for they stand forth next to the world, and are nourished from its objects and its enjoyments, which affect only the material senses of the body.

**Noxious serpents**, which are of many kinds, signify the sensual things which are derived from the **evil affections**, which make up the interiors of the mind with those who are insane from the falsities of evil; and **harmless serpents** signify the sensual things which are derived from the **good affections**, which make up the interiors of the mind with those who are wise from the truths of good. The sensual things that grow out of the evil affections are signified by serpents in these passages:

*They lick the dust like a serpent* (Micah 7:17). 
*Dust shall be the serpent’s meat* (Isaiah 65:25). 
*He said to the serpent, Upon thy belly shalt thou go, and dust shalt thou eat all the days of thy life* (Genesis 3:14).

The **sensual** is thus described, which, because it communicates with hell, where all are sensual, turns heavenly wisdom into infernal insanity in spiritual things. *Rejoice not, Philistia, for out of the serpent’s root shall go forth a <term>basilisk<note>A legendary reptile, often called a "king of serpents," whose breath or glance was thought to be fatal; here it represents a more extreme form of spiritual falsehood.</note></term>.*

## 457. The Refusal to Repent

**Yet repented not of the works of their hands**, signifies that neither did they shun as sins the things of their own, which are evils of every kind. 

The reason that by the "works of a man's hands" the man's own nature—consisting of evils and the <term>falsities<note>In this context, falsities are not just mistakes, but incorrect beliefs that people use to justify their harmful behaviors.</note></term> derived from them—is signified, is because everything that proceeds from a person is represented in sum by the hands. The powers of the mind, and consequently the body, are directed into the hands and find their completion there; for this reason, the hands signify "power" in a spiritual sense. 

Consequently, the "works of a man's hands" signify those things that belong to his own self-will and self-understanding. A person's own inclinations in the will are evils, and their own thoughts in the understanding are the falsities that spring from those evils. 

It is said of the people described here that they "repented not" because those who make <term>Faith Alone<note>A theological doctrine (sola fide) teaching that salvation is achieved solely through belief or trust in God’s grace, regardless of a person’s actions or "works."</note></term> the entirety of religion often say to themselves: 

> "What is the need for repentance, when sins are already forgiven and we are saved by faith alone? What do our actions contribute to this? I know that I was born in sin, and that I am a sinner. If I simply confess this and pray that my faults are not <term>imputed<note>To "impute" is a legalistic term meaning to assign credit or blame. In this theology, it refers to God "counting" Christ's righteousness as the believer's own.</note></term> to me, is not the act of repentance finished? What more is needed?" 

Because of this mindset, such a person does not think about his sins at all, eventually reaching a point where he no longer even recognizes them as sins. Therefore, he is carried along continually by the enjoyment and pleasure he finds in them—living in them and for them. He is like a ship with a favorable wind and a steady current that is being driven directly upon the rocks, while the...

**458.** **That they should not worship demons** signifies that in this state, people are consumed by the evils of their own lusts and are spiritually united with those in hell. Such individuals are already joined with these spirits; for every person is spiritually linked to spirits through their <term>affections<note>In this context, "affections" refers to the deep-seated desires or loves that drive a person's will.</note></term>, to such an extent that they act as one.

Because such a person does not examine themselves for sin and has no desire to remove it through repentance, they stay as they are. Since every evil is essentially a "bundle of lusts," it follows that anyone who does not shun evil as a sin against God—which can only be done through heartfelt repentance—becomes a demon after death.

**459.** ***And idols of gold and silver and brass and stone and wood*** symbolizes that they are engaged in a form of worship based entirely on <term>falsities<note>In this context, "falsities" refers to religious ideas that are not only incorrect but are used to justify or excuse selfish behavior.</note></term>. **460.** ***Which neither can see, nor hear, nor walk*** symbolizes that within these false systems of worship, there is no spiritual or truly rational life. These words are used because idolaters believe their physical idols can actually see and hear, treating them as gods. However, the deeper meaning is that in the falsities of worship, there is no capacity for spiritual perception. 

In the symbolic language of the Word:
*   **To see** and **to hear** signify to understand and to perceive (see nos. 7, 25, 87).
*   **To walk** signifies to live (see no. 167).

Therefore, when taken together, these three actions signify a life that is both spiritual and truly rational. Since idols represent false religious ideas, and such ideas contain no real spiritual or rational vitality, they are described as unable to see, hear, or walk. It would be too obvious a fact to mention that physical statues cannot move or sense things unless there was a deeper spiritual reality being described—namely, the inner state of the worshiper.

That this second table of the Decalogue is a table of repentance is obvious; for it does not list good works that must be done, but rather evil works that must *not* be done—such as: "*You shall not kill, You shall not commit adultery, You shall not steal, You shall not testify falsely, You shall not covet the things that belong to your neighbor*." If these instructions are not considered part of one's religion, the result is exactly what is written: "*And they repented not of their murders, nor of their enchantments, nor of their whoredoms, nor of their thefts.*"

462. As it is not known at this day what is meant by *enchantments*, it will be briefly told. Enchantments are mentioned just above in place of the eighth precept of the **Decalogue** <note>The Ten Commandments.</note>, “Thou shalt not testify falsely;” for the remaining three evils, which are murders, whoredoms, and thefts, are there named. By “testifying falsely” is signified in the natural sense to act as false witness, to lie, and defame; and in the spiritual sense, to confirm and persuade that <term>falsity<note>In this context, a spiritual lie or a distortion of divine truth.</note></term> is truth and that evil is good: from which it is manifest, that by enchanting is signified to persuade to falsity, and so to destroy truth.

Enchantments were in use among the ancients, and were effected in three ways.

*First:* They kept the hearing of another, and thus his mind, continually in their words and sayings, not relaxing any thing from them; and at the same time breathing and inspiring thought conjoined with affection through the breath in the sound of the speech, in consequence of which the hearer could not think any thing of himself; and thus the falsifiers infused their falsities by force.

*Secondly:* They infused a persuasion; which was done by keeping the mind away from every thing contrary, and holding it intent in the sole idea of the things said by them: hence the <term>spiritual sphere<note>An invisible aura or influence that Swedenborg believed emanates from every person, reflecting their internal state and intentions.</note></term> of their mind dispelled the spiritual sphere of the other’s mind, and suffocated it. This was the spiritual witchcraft which the <term>magi<note>Ancient wise men or practitioners of hidden arts, often associated with the East.</note></term> of old used; and it was called the binding and tying of the understanding. This kind of enchantment was of the spirit or thought alone, but the former was also of the mouth or the speech.

*Thirdly:* The hearer kept his mind so fixedly on his own belief, as almost to stop his ears against hearing any thing from the speaker; which was done by keeping in the breath of the mouth, and sometimes by a tacit mumbling, and so by continual denial of the sentiments of his adversary. This kind of enchantment was that of those

**THE CONTENTS OF THE WHOLE CHAPTER.** The exploration and manifestation of those who are in the <term>Churches of the Reformed</term> <note>This refers to the various Protestant denominations that emerged from the Reformation, such as the Lutheran and Calvinist traditions.</note> is still treated of; here what they believe concerning the Lord as being the God of heaven and earth, as He taught (Matthew 28:18); and as to His <term>Humanity being Divine</term> <note>A central tenet in this theology: that Jesus Christ's human nature was glorified and made one with His Divine essence, meaning God is fully present in a Divine Human form.</note>: and that this is not received there, and that it can with difficulty be received as long as the dogma concerning <term>justification by faith alone</term> <note>The doctrine that salvation is granted through belief in Christ's merit alone, regardless of a person's life or "good works."</note> is seated in their hearts.

### THE EXPLANATION.

464. In this chapter and the one following, the focus is on the Lord: specifically, that He is the God of heaven and earth, and that He is also God in regards to His Human nature; consequently, that He is **Jehovah** <note>original: "Jehovah." This name is used here to emphasize that the Lord of the New Testament is the same eternal God of the Old Testament.</note>. That these two chapters address this theme can be seen from the specific details of their **spiritual sense** <note>The deeper, symbolic meaning of the Bible that lies beneath the literal stories and words.</note>, as well as from their conclusion in the next chapter (chap. xi. 15-17).

465. *And I saw another mighty angel coming down from heaven*, signifies the Lord in His Divine Majesty and Power. It is clear that this "angel" is actually the Lord Himself based on the description: he is surrounded by a cloud, has a rainbow over his head, a face like the sun, and feet like pillars of fire. Furthermore, he stands upon the sea and the earth, cries out like a roaring lion, and speaks with the sound of thunder. That God is one, and that the Lord is that God (n. 45).

voices which the seven thunders uttered are the things which are treated of just above (n. 472), which, because they are the very essentials of the **New Church** <note>Swedenborg used this term to describe a new spiritual era or "dispensation" of Christianity based on a direct relationship with Jesus Christ and a life of active love, rather than just belief in dogma.</note>, are mentioned thrice. By writing, in the natural sense, is signified to commit to paper, and thus to posterity, for remembrance. But in the **spiritual sense** <note>Swedenborg’s method of interpretation, which looks for deeper, symbolic meanings within the literal words of the Bible.</note> by writing is signified to commit to the heart for reception. Hence by sealing up and not writing those things, is signified that they are not committed to the heart and received, until after the dragon, the beast, and the false-prophet were cast out of the **world of spirits** <note>In this theology, the "world of spirits" is an intermediate realm between heaven and hell where people first go after death to be prepared for their final home. The reason is, because by the dragon, the beast, and the false-prophet those are signified who are in **faith separate from charity** <note>Often referred to as "Faith Alone," this was Swedenborg's primary criticism of the Protestant theology of his time, which he argued prioritized intellectual belief over a life of good deeds.</note>; and these constantly and tenaciously adhere to their faith, that God the Father is to be approached, and not the Lord immediately; also that the Lord is not the God of heaven and earth as to His **Human** <note>original: *Humanum*. <meta>This page continues the interpretation of Revelation 10:6. It moves from the identification of the angel as the Lord to explaining the spiritual meaning of an oath made by God, contrasting the representative nature of the Israelite church with the teachings of the New Testament.</meta>

*this house shall be a desolation* (Jer. 22:5). *Jehovah has sworn by His soul* (Jer. 51:14; Amos 6:8). *Jehovah has sworn by His holiness* (Amos 4:2). *Jehovah has sworn by His right hand, and by the arm of His strength* (Isa. 62:8). *Behold, I have sworn by my great name* (Jer. 44:26). 

The fact that Jehovah—that is, the Lord—swore <note>original: "juravit"</note> by Himself, signifies that the **Divine Truth** <note>In this theology, Divine Truth is the spiritual reality and light that emanates from God, serving as the ultimate witness to what is real.</note> provides testimony; for He is the Divine Truth itself, and it testifies from itself and by itself. In addition to these passages declaring that Jehovah swore, see also Isaiah 14:24; 54:9; Psalms 89:3, 35; 95:11; 110:4; 132:11. 

The reason the scriptures state that Jehovah swore is that the church established among the children of Israel was a **representative church** <note>A "representative church" is one where external ceremonies and laws were designed to act as physical symbols of deeper, internal spiritual states.</note>. Consequently, the **conjunction** <note>A term describing the spiritual marriage or union between God and humanity.</note> of the Lord with the church was represented by a **covenant** <note>A "covenant" is a sacred agreement or bond between two parties.</note>, such as a contract made between two people who swear to uphold their agreement. Because an oath was a standard part of a covenant, it is said that Jehovah swore; however, this does not mean that He literally took an oath, but rather that the Divine Truth confirms and attests to it. 

That an oath was a formal part of a covenant is clear from these passages: *I have sworn unto thee, and have entered into a covenant with thee, that thou shouldest be mine* (Ezek. 16:8). *To remember the covenant, the oath which He swore* (Luke 1:72, 73; Ps. 105:9; Jer. 11:5; 32:22; Deut. 1:34; 10:11; 11:9, 21; 26:3, 15; 31:20; 34:4). 

Because a covenant was a symbol of the union of the Lord with the church, and vice versa, and because the oath was a part of that covenant—to be sworn based on the truth itself—the children of Israel were permitted to swear by Jehovah, and thus by the Divine Truth (Exod. 20:7; Lev. 19:12; Deut. 6:13; 10:20; Isa. 48:1; 65:16; Jer. 4:2; Zech. 5:4). However, after the symbolic rituals of that church were **abrogated** <note>To be "abrogated" means to be formally abolished or set aside in favor of a new spiritual law.</note>, the use of oaths in covenants was also abolished by the Lord (Matt. 5:33–37; 23:16–22).

476. *That time should be no longer*, signifies that there would not be any state of the church, nor any church, unless one God were acknowledged, and that the Lord is He. By "time" **state** <note>In this theology, "time" in the spiritual world is not measured by clocks, but by changes in a person's inner condition or "state" of being.</note> is signified; and as the church is here treated of, the state of the church is signified: hence by "time being no longer" is signified that there will not be any state of the church. By taking the **little book** is signified to receive the **doctrine** <term>doctrine</term> <note>In this context, "doctrine" refers to the specific system of teachings concerning the nature of God and the path to salvation.</note> concerning the **Lord**: by eating it up is signified to acknowledge it: by making the belly bitter is signified that it will be disagreeable and difficult on account of **falsifications**, for truth falsified is signified by bitter (no. 411): by being sweet as honey in the mouth, is signified that the first reception is agreeable and pleasant. These things now applied to that doctrine which is meant by the **little book** open in the angel's hand (no. 469, 472), signify that the reception from acknowledgment that the **Lord** is the **Saviour** and **Redeemer** is agreeable and pleasant; but that the acknowledgment that He alone is the **God of heaven and earth**, and that His **Human is Divine**, is disagreeable and difficult by reason of **falsifications**. 

The principal falsifications on account of which that doctrine will be perceived to be disagreeable and difficult are:
* That they did not acknowledge the **Lord** to be one with the **Father**; which, however, He taught: 
* and that they did not acknowledge the **Lord's Human** to be **Divine**, which yet is the **Son of God** <note>original: "Son of God (Luke 1:35)"</note>: 
* and thus, it may be said, they made **God three**, and the **Lord two** <note>This refers to the theological debate over the Trinity; the author suggests that dividing God into three persons and Christ into two separate natures (human and divine) creates a spiritual obstacle.</note>; besides the falsities flowing from them. 

From the latter falsities flows **faith alone** <term>faith alone</term> <note>The doctrine that salvation comes through belief or "faith" without the necessity of living a life of active charity or good works.</note>, and **faith alone** afterwards confirms the former falsities. That from these there arises so great bitterness and internal repugnance, that they cannot, after death, even name the **Divine Human** from acknowledgment in the thought, may be seen above (no. 294).

482. *And I took the little book out of the angel's hand, and eat it up; and it was in my mouth sweet as honey, and when I had eaten it up, my belly was made bitter*, signifies that it was so done, and thus made manifest what would be the reception of that doctrine, before they who are meant by the **dragon**, the **beast**, and the **false-prophet**, were removed. As this is a consequence of what is said above, it is not further explained. We read that the prophet **Ezekiel** also *eat up, by command, the roll of a book; and that in his mouth it was sweet as honey* <note>original: "Ez. ii. 8—10 ; iii. 1—3"</note>.

### THE THIRD RELATION. 

In the northern quarter of the **spiritual world** <term>spiritual world: in this context, the realm inhabited by souls after death, which is organized into different regions reflecting the inhabitants' internal states</term> I heard a sound like the roar of waters; and I therefore went up toward it. When I was near, the roar ceased, and I heard a sound like that of a great crowd of people. 

Then, a house appeared that was full of holes and surrounded by a rough wall, from which that sound proceeded. I approached the door-keeper and asked him who was inside. He said that they were the "wisest of the wise," who decide among themselves concerning supernatural things. He spoke this out of his own simple belief. I asked whether it was permitted to enter, and he said that it was, "provided you say nothing. I may admit you, because I have leave to admit **gentiles** <note>original: "gentiles"; here referring to people outside this specific theological circle or those with different beliefs</note>, who stand with me at the door." 

I therefore entered; and behold, it was a **circus** <note>In the 18th-century sense, a circular arena or theater designed for public assembly</note>, and in the midst of it was a pulpit. An assembly of the "wise," as they were called, were discussing the **arcana of faith** <term>arcana: from the Latin "arcanum," meaning deep or hidden mysteries that are not easily understood by the common mind</term>. The matter or proposition then submitted for discussion was whether the good which a person does in the state of **justification by faith** <term>justification by faith: the theological doctrine that a person is made right with God through belief alone, rather than by their own deeds</term>, or in the progress of it after that act, is the "good of religion" or not. 

They said unanimously that by the "good of religion" was meant the good which contributes to salvation. The discussion was sharp; but those prevailed who said that the good which a person does in the state or progress of faith is only moral, civil, and political good, which contributes nothing to salvation—only faith can do that. 

They proved their point in this way: "How can any work of man be joined with **free-grace** <term>free-grace: the belief that salvation is a gift from God that cannot be earned through human effort</term>? Is not salvation a matter of free-grace? How can any good deed of man be joined with **Christ's merit** <term>Christ's merit: the belief that only the righteous acts of Jesus have the power to save humanity</term>? Is not salvation by that alone? And how can human operation be joined with the operation of the Holy Spirit? Does it not do everything without the person's help? Are not these three things alone the saving power in the act of faith? And these three things also remain as the only saving powers in the ongoing state or progress of faith. For this reason..."

### THE SPIRITUAL SENSE.

**THE CONTENTS OF THE WHOLE CHAPTER.** This chapter continues to describe the state of the church among the **Reformed** <note>This refers to the various Protestant denominations that emerged from the Reformation.</note>. It examines the character of those who claim to follow "faith alone" while inwardly opposing the two essential foundations of the New Church: first, that the Lord alone is the God of heaven and earth and that His Human nature is Divine; and second, that people must live according to the laws of the **Decalogue** <term>Decalogue (The Ten Commandments)</term>. The text explains that these two essentials were presented to them (verses 3–6) but were completely rejected (verses 7–10). However, these truths were later revived by the Lord (verses 11–12), while those who rejected them faced spiritual ruin (verse 13). Finally, the state of the New Church is revealed from the perspective of the New Heaven (verses 15–19).

**THE CONTENTS OF EACH VERSE.** “And there was given to me a **reed like unto a staff**,” <note>A "reed" or measuring rod symbolizes the power or faculty to explore and analyze the quality of a thing—in this case, the church.</note> *signifies* that the author was granted the ability and power to perceive the true state of the church both in heaven and in the world. “And the angel stood, saying, Arise and measure the temple of God and the altar and them that worship in it,” *signifies* the presence of the Lord and His instruction to examine and understand the state of the church within the New Heaven. “And the **court** <note>In the architecture of the ancient Temple, the "court" was the outer area; here it represents the external or visible church on earth.</note> which is without the temple cast out, and measure it not,” *signifies* that the current state of the church on earth is to be set aside and is not yet ready to be fully understood. “For it is given to the **Gentiles**,” signifies that the state of that church has been ruined and left empty by the evils found in people's lives. “And the holy city shall they trample down **forty-two months**,” <note>In prophetic language, "forty-two months" symbolizes a completed period of time until nothing of the old truth remains.</note> *signifies* that the church has scattered every truth of the Word until nothing of value is left. “And I will give unto my **two witnesses**,” *signifies* those who acknowledge from their hearts that the Lord is the God of heaven and earth, that His Human is Divine, and who are joined to Him through a life of service and obedience.

By “a reed” is signified feeble power, such as man has of himself <note>In this spiritual system, a reed represents human ability, which is inherently fragile and easily broken without divine support.</note>; and by a staff great power is signified, such as man has from the Lord: and therefore, by there being given a reed like unto a staff is signified power from the Lord. That it is the faculty and power of knowing and seeing the state of the church in heaven and in the world, is manifest from the things that follow in this chapter even to the end.

That feeble power, such as man has of himself, is signified by a reed or cane, is manifest from these passages: *Behold, thou hast trusted upon a staff of bruised reed, upon Egypt, upon which when a man leaneth, it entereth into his hand, and pierceth it* (Isaiah 36:6). *That the dwellers in Egypt may know that I am Jehovah, because they have been a staff of reed to the house of Israel; when they held thee by the hand, thou wast broken, and didst pierce every shoulder for them* (Ezekiel 29:6, 7). By Egypt is signified the natural man <term>Natural man: A person who focuses only on worldly or physical concerns, relying on their own logic rather than spiritual wisdom.</term> who trusts to his own powers, on which account it is called “a staff of bruised reed.” Feeble power is signified by a reed in Isaiah: *A bruised reed shall He not break, the smoking flax shall He not quench* (Isaiah 42:3). 

But by a staff is signified great power, which is from the Lord, here that of knowing the state of the church, because the temple and the altar were measured by the staff; and by measuring <note>To "measure" spiritually means to explore or examine the quality and character of a person or a church.</note> is signified to know, and by the temple and the altar the church is signified, spoken of in what follows. Power is signified by a staff, because wood, of which staves were made among the ancients in the church, signifies good; and because it is in place of the right hand, and supports it; and by the right hand power is signified. Hence it is that a sceptre is a short staff, and by a sceptre is signified the power of a king. Sceptre and staff are also the same word in the Hebrew language <note>The original Hebrew word is *shebet*, which can refer to a rod, a staff, or a royal sceptre.</note>. That a staff signifies power is manifest from these passages: *Say ye, How is the strong staff broken, the beautiful staff; descend from glory, and sit in thirst* (Jeremiah 48:17, 18). *Jehovah will send the staff*

Heaven. By the angel is meant the Lord, here as in numbers 5, 415, and elsewhere; since an angel does nothing from himself, but acts from the Lord: on which account He said, *I will give to my two witnesses* (verse 3); and they were the Lord’s witnesses. By his "standing," the Lord’s presence is signified; and by his "saying" is signified His command.

<margin>..</margin>By "arising and measuring" is signified to see and to know. That to measure signifies to know and to search out the quality of the state <note>In this context, "quality of the state" refers to the essential spiritual character or condition of the church or an individual’s mind.</note>, will be seen below. By the temple, the altar, and them that worship in it, the state of the church in the New Heaven is signified: by the temple, the church as to the truth of doctrine (n. 191); by the altar, the church as to the good of love (n. 392); and by “them that worship” is signified the church as to worship arising from these two. By "them that worship" is here signified adoration, which is worship; since the spiritual sense is abstracted from persons (n. 78, 79, 96) <note>The "spiritual sense" often removes specific individuals from the meaning to focus on universal qualities or principles, such as "faith" or "love," rather than "the person who believes" or "the person who loves."</note>; which is here manifest also from this, that he is said to measure them that worship. Those three are also the things which make the church: the truth of doctrine, the good of love, and worship proceeding from them. 

That it is the church in the New Heaven which is meant, is manifest from the last verse of this chapter, where it is said that *the temple of God was opened in heaven, and the ark of the covenant was seen in the temple* (verse 19). The measuring of the temple is spoken of in the beginning of this chapter, so that the state of the church in heaven might be seen and known before it should be conjoined to the church in the world.
