That by **forty-two months** is signified even to the end when not any truth and good of the church remains, is because the like is signified by forty-two as by **six weeks**; for six times seven are forty-two: and by **six weeks**, "complete even to the end" is signified. For the number **six** signifies this; and a **week** signifies a <term>state</term> <note>In this context, a "state" refers to a spiritual condition or stage of development rather than a geographical location.</note>, and the **seventh week** a holy state, which is the new state of the church when the Lord begins His reign. There are two tables <note>The "two tables" refer to the two stone tablets of the Ten Commandments (the Decalogue) given to Moses.</note> upon which those precepts are written—the one for the Lord, the other for man. The First Table teaches that many Gods are not to be worshipped, but only One; the Second Table teaches that evils are not to be done. When, therefore, one God is worshipped and a person does not commit evil, a conjunction <note>A spiritual connection or joining together.</note> takes place; for as far as a person stops doing evil—that is, repents—so far they are accepted by God and perform good actions through Him.

But who is this One God? A trinal <term>trinal</term> <note>Refers to the Trinity (Father, Son, and Holy Spirit).</note> God or a triune God is not one God when that trinity is thought of as three separate persons. Rather, He in whom the trinity exists within one single person is the One God; and that God is the Lord. No matter how much you complicate your ideas, you will never clearly understand that God is One unless He is also One in person. The entire Word—both the Old Testament prophecies and the New Testament apostolic writings—teaches that this is the case, as can be clearly seen in the *Doctrine of the New Jerusalem concerning the Lord*.

491. ***And they shall prophesy a thousand two hundred and sixty days*** signifies that these two things—the acknowledgment of the Lord and a life according to the precepts of the <term>Decalogue</term> <note>The Ten Commandments.</note>—which are the two essentials of the New Church, are to be taught until the end of the old era and the beginning of the new.

That these two things (acknowledging the Lord and living by the Ten Commandments) are the two essentials of the New Church and are meant by the "two witnesses" was shown just above (n. 490). That "prophesying" signifies teaching is also established (n. 8, 133). The "one thousand two hundred and sixty days" signifies the period until the end and the beginning—that is, the end of the former church and the beginning of the New Church. This specific number carries this meaning because it is numerically equivalent to "three and a half." When 1,260 days are reduced to years, they equal three and a half years; and in spiritual symbolism, three and a half signifies a completion and a new start (n. 505). In the following chapter, this same number signifies...

In another part of the Word, it is written:
> *And the Woman fled into the desert, where she hath a place prepared of God, that they may nourish her there a thousand two hundred and sixty days* <note>original: "Apoc. xii. 6." This refers to Revelation 12:6.</note>.

492. **Clothed in sackcloth** signifies a state of mourning during this period because the truth is not being received. To be "clothed in sackcloth" represents mourning over the <term>vastated</term> <note>From the Latin *vastatio*, meaning a state where spiritual truth has been laid waste or emptied of its life.</note> truth within the church. This is because, in the spiritual language of the Word, garments represent the truths that clothe the mind (see numbers 166, 212, 328, 378, 379). Therefore, wearing sackcloth—which is not a proper garment—symbolizes the grief that occurs when truth is absent; and where there is no truth, the church cannot exist. 

The people of ancient Israel expressed mourning through various physical actions that were meaningful because of <term>correspondences</term> <note>The symbolic relationship between a physical action or object and a deeper spiritual reality.</note>. These included:
*   Putting ashes on the head
*   Rolling in the dust
*   Sitting on the ground in long silence
*   Shaving their hair
*   Wailing and howling
*   Tearing their clothes
*   And wearing sackcloth

Each of these actions pointed to a specific spiritual failure or "evil" within the church for which the people were being disciplined. When they performed these rituals, they were representing a state of <term>repentance</term> and humility, which is why their prayers were heard. 

That mourning over the "laid waste" or <term>vastated</term> truth in the church was represented by wearing sackcloth can be seen in these passages:

> *The lion has come up from the thicket, he has gone forth out of his place to lay waste the earth; for this, put on your sackcloth, wail, and howl* <note>original: "Jer. iv. 7, 8." Jeremiah 4:7-8.</note>.

> *Daughter of my people, gird yourself with sackcloth and roll in ashes, because the destroyer shall come suddenly upon you* <note>original: "Jer. vi. 26." Jeremiah 6:26.</note>.

> *Woe to you, Chorazin, and Bethsaida! For if the mighty works done in you had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago in sackcloth and ashes* <note>original: "Matt. xi. 21; Luke x. 13."</note>.

> *The king of Nineveh, after he heard the words of Jonah, laid aside his robe, put on sackcloth, and sat in ashes... and commanded that both man and beast should be covered with sackcloth* <note>original: "Jonah iii. 5, 6, 8." Jonah 3:5, 6, 8.</note>.

There are many other similar examples in the Scriptures.

493. **These are the two olive-trees and the two candlesticks, which are standing before the God of the earth**, signifies that these people possess love and intelligence (or charity and faith) derived from the Lord. 

The **olive-tree** symbolizes love and charity, as will be explained shortly. The **candlestick** symbolizes enlightenment in divine truths (see number 43), which leads to intelligence and faith; this is because true intelligence and faith are born from being enlightened by such truths. 

To be **standing before God** means to listen to and perform what He commands (see number 366). In this context, it signifies that these two qualities—love and intelligence—are present in those who embrace the two "essentials" of the <term>New Church</term> <note>The author uses "New Church" to refer to a new spiritual era or state of Christianity focused on the direct acknowledgment of the Lord and a life of charity.</note> mentioned previously. 

It is clear, then, that by describing the "two witnesses" as "two olive-trees and two candlesticks," the text means they represent love and intelligence, or charity and faith. These two elements are what truly build a church: love and charity form its life, while intelligence and faith form its doctrine. 

An olive symbolizes love and charity because the olive-tree represents the <term>celestial</term> <note>In this context, "celestial" refers to the highest level of spiritual life, characterized by a direct, heart-felt love for the Lord, rather than just an intellectual understanding.</note> church. Consequently, the olive (the fruit) symbolizes celestial love, which is love directed toward the Lord. This is why "holy oil"—used to consecrate all sacred things in the church—was made from olives. 

*   The **oil of holiness** was a mixture of olive oil and spices (Exodus 30:23, 24).
*   **Olive oil** was also used to light the lamps of the candlestick in the Tabernacle every evening (Exodus 27:20; Leviticus 24:2).

Similar symbols appear in the book of Zechariah:

*I am like a green olive-tree in the house of God* (Psalms 52:8). And in Jeremiah: *Jehovah hath called thy name a green olive-tree, fair, with beautiful fruit* (11:16, 17). There are many other such examples. Since the church was signified by Jerusalem, many things within and around it also carried symbolic meaning for the church. Near the city stood the **Mount of Olives**, which signified Divine Love. For this reason, *Jesus was teaching in the Temple during the days, and at night He went out and abode in the Mount of Olives* (Luke 21:37; 22:39; John 8:1). It was *upon that mountain that Jesus spoke with the disciples about the <term>consummation of the age</term> <note>The "consummation of the age" refers to the end of a specific spiritual era or "church," followed by the start of a new one.</note>, and of His coming at that time* (Matthew 24:3, etc.; Mark 13:3, etc.). And *from that mountain also He went to Jerusalem and suffered* (Matthew 21:1; 26:30; Mark 11:1; 14:26; Luke 19:29, 37). This fulfilled the prediction in Zechariah: *His feet shall stand in that day upon the Mount of Olives, which is before Jerusalem on the east* (14:4). Because the olive-tree signifies the <term>celestial</term> <note>Specifically, the "celestial" refers to the highest level of heaven or the soul, characterized by love for the Lord.</note> element of the church, the *cherubs in the midst of the Temple of Jerusalem were made of olive-wood; likewise the doors of the <term>oracle</term> <note>The "oracle" refers to the inner sanctum or the Most Holy Place (Holy of Holies) within the Temple.</note> and the doorposts* (1 Kings 6:23–33).

To wish to "hurt" the two witnesses signifies a desire to destroy those two essentials of the New Church: namely, the acknowledgment of the Lord as the God of heaven and earth (even as to His Human), and a life according to the precepts of the **Decalogue** <note>The Ten Commandments.</note>. That these are the "witnesses" was shown above (number 490). "Fire shall proceed out of their mouth" signifies infernal love, and "shall devour their enemies" signifies that those who harm them will perish because of that love. Such things are said in the Word because they are **appearances**, and the Word in the sense of the letter is written by <term>appearances and correspondences</term> <note>"Appearances" refer to spiritual truths presented in a way humans can perceive (like saying the sun "rises"), while "correspondences" are the specific links between natural things and spiritual realities.</note>. Besides many other places).

Those who turn themselves away from the two essentials of the <term>New Church</term> <note>The two "essentials" frequently mentioned by Swedenborg are the acknowledgment of the Lord’s divinity and a life lived according to the Ten Commandments.</note> cannot receive any truth from heaven. By "heaven" is here meant the angelic heaven; hence by "rain," the truth of the church originating from there is signified. Therefore, by "shutting heaven so that rain should not fall," it is signified that they cannot receive any truth of the church from heaven. The truth of the church from heaven is the truth of doctrine derived from the <term>Word</term> <note>The Bible or Sacred Scripture, viewed as the source of Divine communication.</note>. 

It is said that the witnesses have this power; but the meaning here is the same as explained above (no. 494): they do not actually possess the power to shut heaven themselves. Rather, those who turn themselves away from the two essentials of the New Church shut it against themselves, because they remain in their own <term>falsities</term> <note>In Swedenborg's vocabulary, "falsities" are not just mistakes, but spiritual errors that arise from a lack of love or goodness.</note>. That rain signifies the Divine Truth from heaven is evident from these passages: 

*My doctrine shall flow down as the rain, my word shall distil as the dew* (Deuteronomy 32:2). 

*If ye serve other gods, **Jehovah** will shut up the heaven, that there be no rain* (Deuteronomy 11:11, 14, 16, 17). 

*I will lay waste my vine, and I will command the clouds that they rain no rain upon it* (Isaiah 5:6). 

*The showers have been withholden, and there hath been no latter rain; but yet thou hadst the forehead of a harlot* (Jeremiah 3:3). 

*As the rain cometh down from heaven, so shall my Word be which goeth forth out of my mouth* (Isaiah 55:10, 11). 

*Ye children of Zion, rejoice and be glad in **Jehovah**, because He shall give you the former rain in justice* (Joel 2:23). 

*Thou, O God, didst send a plentiful rain* (Psalm 68:9). 

*He shall come down like rain upon the mown grass, in His days shall the righteous flourish* (Psalm 72:6, 7). 

*Jehovah shall come unto us as the rain, as the latter rain watereth the earth* (Hosea 6:3). 

*My word shall drop upon them, and they shall wait for me as for the rain, and he shall open his mouth to the latter rain* (Job 29:22, 23). 

*Son of man, say, thou art the land that is not cleansed, which has no rain in the day of anger, there is a conspiracy of the prophets in the midst of it* (Ezekiel 22:24, 25). 

(Besides other places, such as Isaiah 30:23; Jeremiah 5:24; 10:12, 13; 14:3, 4;)

502. **Which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt**, signifies the two infernal <note>meaning "hellish" or belonging to the lower spiritual realms</note> loves, which are the love of ruling from the love of self, and the love of governing from the pride of one's own intelligence, which are in the church where God is not one and the Lord is not worshipped, and where they do not live according to the commandments of the <term>Decalogue</term> <note>The Ten Commandments.</note>. By Sodom in the <term>spiritual sense</term> <note>The internal or symbolic meaning of the Bible that lies beneath the literal stories.</note> the love of ruling from the love of self is signified, treated of in what follows; and by Egypt is signified in the spiritual sense the love of governing from the pride of one's own intelligence, which also will be spoken of presently: and as these two loves are signified, it is therefore said "Sodom and Egypt spiritually." The reason that these loves are in the church where God is not one and the Lord is not worshipped, and where they do not live according to the precepts of the Decalogue, is because man is born into these two loves, and comes into them while he is growing up: and these loves cannot be removed except by God the Saviour, and by a life according to His commandments. And they cannot by God the Saviour, unless He is approached; nor can a life according to His commandments be given, unless the man is led by Him. It may indeed be given, but not a life in which there is any thing of heaven and thence of the church. This life is given only by Him who is life. That the Lord is that life may be seen in John 1:1, 4; 5:26; 6:33, etc.; 11:25, 26; 14:6, 19; and in many other places. That the love of ruling from the love of self and the love of governing from the pride of one's own intelligence are the heads of all the loves in hell, and thus of all the evils and thence the falsities in the church, is not at this day known. ### 503.
What *Egypt* signifies in the <term>Word</term> <note>The Holy Scripture, which the author interprets as having a hidden spiritual meaning.</note> shall be told. *Egypt* signifies the <term>natural man</term> <note>The part of the human mind focused on the physical world, the senses, and factual knowledge.</note> conjoined to the <term>spiritual man</term> <note>The inner mind that is open to heaven and divine truth.</note>, and then the affection for truth, and knowledge and intelligence therefrom; and in the opposite sense it signifies the natural man separated from the spiritual, and then the pride of one’s own intelligence, and thence insanity in spiritual things. 

*Egypt* signifies the natural man conjoined to the spiritual, and affection for truth and knowledge and intelligence thence, in the following passages: 

*In that day there shall be five cities in the land of Egypt swearing to Jehovah of Hosts* <note>original: "Jehovah Zebaoth," a Hebrew title for God meaning 'Lord of Armies' or 'Lord of Hosts'.</note>. *In that day there shall be an altar to Jehovah in the midst of the land of Egypt; then shall Jehovah be made known unto Egypt, and the Egyptians shall know Jehovah in that day* (Isaiah 19:18-21). 

*In that day shall there be a highway out of Egypt into Assyria; that Assyria may come into Egypt, and Egypt into Assyria; and that the Egyptians may serve with Assyria: in that day shall Israel be the third with Egypt and Assyria, a blessing in the midst of the land; whom Jehovah of Hosts shall bless, saying, Blessed be my people Egypt, and Assyria the work of my hands, and Israel mine inheritance* (Isaiah 19:23-25). 

*Egypt* here is the natural, *Assyria* is the rational <note>The faculty of the mind that uses logic and reasoning.</note>, and *Israel* is the spiritual: these three make the man of the church. Hence *the king of Egypt was called the son of the wise, the son of the kings of antiquity; and Egypt was called the cornerstone of the tribes* (Isaiah 19:11, 13): and *it is said of Solomon, that his wisdom excelled the wisdom of the Egyptians* (1 Kings 4:30): and *that he took the daughter of Pharaoh to wife, and brought her into the city of David* (1 Kings 3:1): and *that he built for the daughter of Pharaoh a house beside the porch* (1 Kings 7:8).

<summary>This page explains that "Egypt" in the Bible symbolizes the natural mind's knowledge and intelligence, which can either serve spiritual life or lead to intellectual pride when separated from God.</summary>

For a person is born natural, becomes rational, and afterwards spiritual; and thus the "vine out of Egypt" is planted and takes root. For the sake of that symbolic representation, *Abraham also stayed in Egypt* (Genesis 12:10, etc.). And *Jacob with his sons was commanded to go down into Egypt, and also stayed there* (Genesis 46). For this reason also the land of Canaan, by which the <term>church</term> <note>In this context, the "church" refers to the spiritual state of humanity or the internal presence of God's truth on earth.</note> is symbolized, is described as extending *even to the river of Egypt* (Genesis 15:18; 1 Kings 4:21; Micah 7:12). 

Furthermore, Egypt is likened to the *garden of Eden, the garden of God* (Ezekiel 31:2, 8, 9; Genesis 13:10); and the various types of knowledge belonging to the natural man are called *the desirable things of Egypt* (Daniel 11:43); and *the fine linen in needlework from Egypt* is mentioned (Ezekiel 27:7. See also other places where Egypt is spoken of in a positive sense, such as Isaiah 27:12, 13; Ezekiel 29:13-16; 31:1-8; Hosea 11:11; Zechariah 10:10, 11; 14:16-18; Psalm 68:31, 32; 2 Kings 19:23, 24). 

But in the opposite sense, Egypt signifies the natural man when it is separated from the <term>spiritual man</term> <note>The inner mind that is open to heaven and divine influence.</note>. In this state, it represents the pride of one’s own intelligence, which leads to insanity regarding spiritual things, as seen in the following passages:

506. *And shall not suffer their bodies to be put into sepulchres*, signifies that they have condemned and will condemn them. Hence it was, that in the church among the children of Israel, which was a <term>representative church</term><note>A church where physical rituals and laws were designed to represent deeper, internal spiritual realities.</note>, it was established that they who were regarded as condemned should be cast forth and not buried; as is manifest from these passages: *Jehovah said concerning them, they shall die grievous deaths, they shall not be mourned nor buried ; they shall be as dung upon the face of the earth, and their carcasses shall be for food to the birds* <note>original: "carcassses... cibi avibus" - quoting Jeremiah 16:4.</note>

507. ***And they that dwell upon the earth shall rejoice over them and be glad***, signifies the delight of the heart's affection and the soul's affection within the church on that account, specifically among those who held to <term>faith alone</term><note>A theological doctrine which argues that salvation is achieved through belief in Christ’s atonement without the necessity of performing good works. Swedenborg frequently critiques this as a "dead" faith.</note> in both their teachings and their lives. By "them that dwell on the earth" are meant those who are in the church—in this context, those in the church where the doctrine of "faith alone" prevails. In the spiritual sense of the Word, the "earth" signifies the church itself (n. 285).

To "rejoice" and "be glad" signifies experiencing the delight of the affection of the heart and the soul. Delight of the heart’s affection relates to the **will**, while delight of the soul’s affection relates to the **understanding**. In the language of the Word, the "heart" and "soul" symbolize a person's will and intellect respectively. This is why the text says both "rejoice" and "be glad," even though they might seem to mean the same thing. In these two terms, there is a <term>marriage of the will and the understanding</term><note>In Swedenborg’s philosophy, every part of the Divine Word contains a "marriage" or union of Good (pertaining to the will/love) and Truth (pertaining to the understanding/wisdom). This duality is reflected in the use of pairs of similar words.</note>, which is also the marriage of good and truth that exists in every single detail of the Word: see the *Doctrine of the New Jerusalem concerning the Sacred Scripture* (n. 80-90). This is why both "rejoice and be glad," or "joy and gladness," are mentioned together in many other places in the Word, such as these:

*Behold joy and gladness (Isaiah 22:13).*
*They shall obtain joy and gladness (Isaiah 35:10; 51:11).*
*Joy and gladness are cut off from the*

508. **And shall send gifts one to another**, signifies <term>consociation</term><note>A spiritual joining or fellowship. In Swedenborg’s view, this is not just social gathering, but a deep connection of souls through shared love and belief.</note> by love and friendship. To send gifts signifies to be joined together by love and friendship, because a gift fosters connection; for it produces love and causes friendship. “To one another” signifies mutually.

509. **Because those two prophets tormented them that dwell upon the earth**, signifies that those two essentials—the one concerning the Lord and the <term>Divine Human</term><note>The doctrine that God's humanity is itself Divine, making God visible and approachable to the human mind through the person of Jesus Christ.</note>, and the other concerning a life according to the commandments of the <term>Decalogue</term><note>The Ten Commandments.</note>—are in opposition to the two essentials received in the <term>Reformed Church</term><note>Generally referring to the Protestant churches that arose from the Reformation, particularly those emphasizing salvation through faith alone.</note>. Of these, the one relates to a Trinity of Persons, and the other to salvation by faith alone without the works of the law; and that owing to that opposition the two essentials of the New Church, which is the <term>New Jerusalem</term><note>A symbolic representation of a new era of Christianity or a "New Church" characterized by direct spiritual understanding and a life of charity.</note>, are looked upon with contempt, dislike, and aversion. That these things are signified—when by the "two prophets" or "witnesses" the two essentials of the New Church are meant, and when by "them that dwell upon the earth" are meant those who are in the two essentials of the Reformed church—follows as a necessary conclusion. By "tormenting" is signified to be a matter of contempt, dislike, and aversion.

510. **And after the three days and a half the spirit of life from God entered into them, and they stood upon their feet**, signifies that the two essentials of the <term>New Church</term><note>In Swedenborg’s theology, the "New Church" (often associated with the New Jerusalem) represents a new era of spiritual understanding where the inner meaning of the Bible is revealed.</note>, at the end of the former era, when the New Church is beginning and advancing, are <term>vivified</term><note>original: "vivificantur"; meaning to be filled with life or animated by a spiritual force.</note> by the Lord with those who receive them. By "the three days and a half" is signified the transition from an end to a beginning (no. 505); and thus from the end of the church which currently exists, to the beginning of the New; here referring to those among whom the New Church commences and progresses: because it is now said of the witnesses, that "the spirit of life entered into them, and they stood upon their feet." By the **spirit of life from God**, spiritual life is signified; and by **standing upon the feet** is signified natural life agreeing with the spiritual life, and thus being made alive by the Lord. This is signified because by the "spirit of life" the internal of man is meant, which is called the <term>internal man</term><note>The inner, spiritual part of a person’s mind that is capable of thinking and willing in alignment with heaven.</note>, which viewed in itself is spiritual: for the spirit of man thinks and wills; and to think and will is in itself spiritual. By "standing upon the feet" the external of man is signified, which is also called the <term>external man</term><note>The outward, natural part of a person that interacts with the physical world through speech and action.</note>, which in itself is natural; for the body speaks and does what its spirit thinks and wills, and to speak and do is natural. That the feet signify natural things, may be seen in numbers 49 and 468. 

It shall be told what in particular is meant by this. Every man who is reformed, is reformed first as to his internal man, and afterwards as to the external. The internal man is not reformed by only knowing and understanding the truths and goods by which man is saved, but by willing and loving them; but the external man by speaking and doing the things which the internal man wills and loves: and as far as it does this, so far the man is <term>regenerated</term><note>The process of being spiritually reborn; a total transformation of a person's character from selfish to divine.</note>. He is not regenerated before, because his internal is not before in *effect* <note>meaning "in operation" or "manifested"</note>, but only in the *cause*; and the cause, unless it is in effect, is dissipated. It is like a house built upon the ice, which falls to the bottom when the ice is melted by the sun. In a word, it is like a man without feet to stand and

By “come up hither” is signified their being taken up into heaven, whence they are and where they are, and the protection of them.

**524.** *And the nations were angry*, signifies those who are in **faith alone** <term>Faith Alone: A theological position that holds that salvation is granted through belief or intellectual assent alone, regardless of one's actions or moral life.</term>, and consequently in evils of life, who became enraged and harassed those who oppose their doctrine. By "the nations" are meant those who live in evil, or, in an abstract sense, the evils of life themselves (see numbers 147, 483); but in this specific context, it refers to those who adhere to "faith alone." These individuals are considered to be in evils of life because their religion teaches that the law does not condemn them, provided they maintain faith that Christ took away that condemnation. Their "being angry" signifies not only their rage but also their active infestation or harassment of those who do not share their faith; this will become clearer in the descriptions of the **Dragon** <term>The Dragon: A symbolic figure in Revelation representing those who separate faith from charity and attack the internal truths of the Church.</term> (Chapter 12:17) and the chapters that follow.

**525.** *And thy wrath is come, and the time to judge the dead*, signifies their destruction and the **last judgment** upon those who possess no spiritual life. By "thy wrath" <note>original: "ira tua"</note> is signified the last judgment (number 340), and thus their eventual destruction. This is called the "Lord's wrath" because it appears to the wicked as if the Lord casts them into hell out of anger, when in reality, the evil person casts themselves down. 

It is much like a criminal <note>original: "malefactor"</note> blaming the law for his punishment, or blaming a fire for being burned after thrusting his hand into it, or blaming a sword for a wound received while rushing upon the point held by someone defending themselves. This is how it happens to everyone who sets themselves against the Lord and, in their anger, rushes against those whom the Lord protects. By "the dead" who are to be judged, the text refers in a universal sense to all who have died and left this world; however, in a more precise spiritual sense, it refers to those who have no **spiritual life** <note>In Swedenborg’s terminology, "life" is equivalent to love and wisdom from the Lord, while "death" is the absence of these.</note>. **526.** *And to give reward to His servants the prophets, and to the saints*, signifies the happiness of eternal life to those who are in truths of **doctrine** <term>Doctrine: The core teachings or principles of the Church derived from a systematic understanding of the Word (the Bible).</term> from the Word, and in a life according to them.

By "reward" is meant here the happiness of eternal life arising from the enjoyment and pleasantness of the love and affection for good and truth. For every affection of love has within itself its own enjoyment and pleasantness, and the affection for the love of good and truth contains enjoyment and pleasantness such as the angels of heaven possess. Every affection remains with a person after death. **527.** *And to them that fear thy name, both small and great*, signifies who love the things which are the Lord's in a greater or less degree. That "to fear" here signifies to love, is because every one who loves, fears also to do evil to him whom he loves. Genuine love is not given without that fear.

Consequently, he who loves the Lord, fears to do evil, because evils are contrary to Him; for they are contrary to His Divine laws in the Word, which is from Him, and thus Himself; yea, they are contrary to His Divine **essence** <term>Essence: The fundamental nature or most important quality of a being; here, God's essential nature is defined as the desire to save everyone.</term>, which is that He wishes to save all; for He is the **Saviour**; and He cannot save a man, unless he lives according to His laws and commandments. Actual repentance is to examine one’s self, to know and acknowledge his sins, to hold himself guilty, to confess them before the Lord, to implore help and power to resist them, and so to desist from them, and to lead a new life; and to do all this as of himself <note>Swedenborg emphasizes that a person must act "as of himself"—taking personal responsibility and initiative—while acknowledging that the actual power to change comes from God.</note>. Do so once or twice in a year, when you come to the **Holy Communion**; and afterwards, when the sins of which you have found yourselves guilty recur, then say to yourselves, ‘We do not will these, because they are sins against God.’ This is actual repentance. Who cannot understand, that he who does not examine and see his sins, remains in them? For all evil is delightful to man from birth. For it is delightful to him to revenge, to commit adultery, to defraud, to blaspheme, and especially to rule from the love of self <term>love of self</term> <note>In this theology, the "love of self" is the root of all evil, referring to the desire to serve one's own ego and dominate others rather than serving God and the neighbor.</note>. Does not the delight prevent you from seeing them? And if perchance it is said that they are sins, do you not from the enjoyment of them excuse them? yea, persuade yourselves, and confirm it by falsities, that they are not sins? and so remain in them, and do them afterwards more than before? and this even until you do not know what sin is; yea, whether there is such a thing. It is otherwise with every one who actually repents. The evils which he knows and acknowledges, he calls sins, and therefore begins to shun and turn away from them, and to feel the delight of them as undelightful. And as far as he does this, he so far sees and loves goods, and at length feels the delight of them, which is the delight of heaven. In a word, as far as one rejects the devil, he is adopted by the Lord; and is taught, led, withheld from evils, and kept in good, by Him. This is the way, and there is no other, from hell to heaven.” It is matter of wonder that the Protestants <note>Referring to the various Reformed and Lutheran denominations of the 18th century.</note> have a certain deep-rooted opposition, repugnance, and aversion, to actual repentance, which is so great that they cannot compel themselves to examine themselves, and see their sins, and

### THE EXPLANATION.

532. **And a great sign was seen in heaven,** *signifies* a revelation from the Lord concerning His New Church in the heavens and on the earth, and concerning the difficult reception of and assault upon its Doctrine. By a "sign from heaven" is here meant a revelation of things to come.

and by "the great sign seen in heaven," a revelation concerning the <term>New Church</term><gloss>In Swedenborg's writings, the "New Church" refers to a new spiritual era or "dispensation" of Christianity based on love and a deeper understanding of the Bible.</gloss> is meant; for the Woman clothed with the sun, who is discussed in this chapter, signifies that Church. The male child which she brought forth signifies its doctrine <note>The "male child" represents the core teachings or system of thought of this new spiritual era.</note>. Her being pained to bring forth signifies the difficult reception of these new ideas. The dragon’s wishing to devour the male child, and his persecuting the Woman afterwards, signifies the assault made upon this Church and its teachings. These are the things meant by the "great sign seen in heaven." 

In the Word <note>The "Word" is the term used throughout this text to refer to the Sacred Scriptures or the Bible.</note>, a **sign** relates to future things, in which case it is a **revelation**; or it relates to truth, in which case it is a **testimony**; or it relates to the quality of a state or a thing, and then it is a **manifestation** <note>original: "manifestatio," referring to the outward showing of an inner spiritual condition</note>. 

A sign relates to future things, acting as a revelation, in the following passages:
*Let them declare to us what shall happen, that we may know the latter end of them; or make us to hear things to come; show us the signs for the future* (Isaiah 41:22, 23). 
*The disciples said to Jesus, What shall be the sign of thy coming, and of the consummation of the age?* <note>The "consummation of the age" refers to the end of a spiritual era, often translated as "the end of the world."</note> (Matthew 24:3; Mark 13:4; Luke 21:7). 
*There shall be signs from heaven, and signs in the sun, the moon, and the stars* (Luke 21:11, 25). 
*And then shall appear the sign of the Son of Man* (Matthew 24:30). 
*It was said to king Hezekiah, This shall be a sign to thee, that Jehovah will do this thing; the shadow shall be brought back in the degrees of Ahaz. Afterwards Hezekiah said, What is the sign that I shall go up into the house of Jehovah?* (Isaiah 38:7, 8, 22; and elsewhere). 

That a sign relates to the truth (acting as a testimony) and to the quality of a state (acting as a manifestation) is evident from other places in the Word.

533. **A Woman clothed with the sun, and the moon under her feet**, signifies the Lord’s New Church in the heavens, which is the New Heaven, and the Lord’s New Church about to be established on the earth, which is the <term>New Jerusalem</term><gloss>A prophetic symbol from the Book of Revelation representing a new, restored state of humanity and the church.</gloss>. That the Lord’s New Church is signified by this Woman is evident from everything in this chapter when understood in its spiritual sense.

By *the head of the statue of Nebuchadnezzar of pure gold* (Daniel 2:32), nothing else is signified but the wisdom of the **first age** <note>original: "prima aetas"</note>, which was with the men of the **most ancient Church** <note>In Swedenborg’s theology, the "Most Ancient Church" represents the spiritual state of humanity in the earliest era, often associated with the symbolism of Adam in Eden.</note>. In the opposite sense insanity and folly are signified by head: in David: *God shall wound the head of his enemies, the hairy crown of him that goeth on in his trespasses* (Psalm 68:21). Nor is any thing else signified by the *serpent’s head* wnich should be trodden down (Genesis 3:15): nor by *smiting the head over many countries* (Psalm 110:5, 6). Also by putting dust upon the head, and by inducing baldness, and by putting the hand upon the head, when they were ashamed or lamented that they had acted insanely or contrary to wisdom (Isaiah 7:20; 15:2; Ezekiel 7:18; 27:30; Jeremiah 2:37; 14:3, 4; Lamentations 2:10; 2 Samuel 13:19). 539. ***And ten horns***, signifies much power. A horn signifies power (n. 270); and ten signifies "much" (n. 101). It is said that the Dragon had much power, because the salvation of man by **faith alone** without the works of the law—which faith is symbolized by the Dragon—captivates the minds <note>original: "animus," referring here to the natural mind or the seat of impulses and worldly desires.</note> and then the justifications used to support it are convincing. It is captivating because when a person hears that the condemnation of the law is removed, and that by simply believing this, the Lord’s merit is credited to them, they feel they can indulge in the pleasures of their mind and body without the fear of hell. This is the source of the power signified by the Dragon’s ten horns. That such power exists is clearly evident from the widespread acceptance of that faith across the entire Reformed Christian world.

For a stone, in the **Word**, signifies truth in **ultimates** <term>Ultimates: The final or lowest level of existence; in this context, it refers to the physical or literal wording of the Bible.</term>, hence a precious stone signifies that truth is transparent.

The truths of the **Word** falsified and profaned <note>To "falsify" is to misinterpret truth for selfish reasons; to "profane" is to treat holy things with contempt or use them to justify evil.</note> are also called diadems, because they shine of themselves, regardless of who possesses them; just as diadems on earth do, no matter whose hand they are in. It has sometimes been granted to me to see adulterous women, when they first came from the earth into the **world of spirits** <term>World of spirits: An intermediate realm in the afterlife where individuals stay immediately after death before being prepared for Heaven or Hell.</term>, ornamented with diadems; and Jews also selling diadems, which they procured for themselves from heaven; from which it was manifest that their evils and falsities do not change the light and splendor of the truths of the **Word**.

They assert that whatever proceeds from man's will and judgment is not good; and therefore that the goods of **charity** <term>Charity: The practice of living according to God's commandments by doing good works and showing love toward one's neighbor.</term>, or good works, because they are done by man, contribute nothing towards salvation; but **faith alone** <term>Faith Alone: A theological doctrine (Sola Fide) teaching that salvation is granted through belief alone, regardless of a person’s actions or moral life.</term>: whereas the only thing by which man is man, and by which he is **conjoined** <term>Conjunction: A spiritual union or bond between the individual and the Divine.</term> to the Lord, is that he can do good and believe truth **as of himself**; that is, as from his will according to his judgment. If this one thing were taken away, all power of conjunction of man with the Lord and of the Lord with man would also be taken away at the same time: for this is the power of reciprocating love which the Lord gives to every one who is born a man; which also He preserves in him to the end of his life, and for ever afterwards. 

If this were taken away from a man, every truth and good of the **Word** would also be taken away from him, to such a degree that the **Word** would be nothing but a dead letter and an empty volume. For the **Word** teaches nothing else but the conjunction of man with the Lord by **charity** and **faith**, both of them from the man as of himself. *The Spirit shall be poured upon us from on high; then the wilderness shall be a fruitful-field, and judgment shall dwell in the wilderness* (Isaiah 32:15, 16 <note>The OCR reads "26," but the reference is likely Isaiah 32:16, as the chapter only contains 20 verses.</note>). *I will open fountains in the midst of the valleys, and make the wilderness a lake of waters; I will plant in the wilderness the cedar, the shittim-tree <note>The "shittim-tree" refers to the acacia, the wood used in the construction of the Ark of the Covenant.</note>, and the oil-tree* (Isaiah 41:18, 19). *He shall turn the wilderness into a lake of waters, and the dry land into water-springs* (Psalm 107:35, 36). *I will make a way in the wilderness and rivers in the desert, to give drink to my people, my chosen* (Isaiah 43:19, 20). *Jehovah will make her wilderness like Eden, and her desert like the garden of Jehovah; gladness and joy shall be found therein* (Isaiah 51:3). *The habitations of the wilderness drop* (Psalm 65:12, 13). *Let the wilderness lift up the voice, let the inhabitants of the rock sing* (Isaiah 42:11). 

**III. That by a wilderness a state of temptation <term>temptation (a period of intense spiritual struggle or inner trial)</term> is signified, in which a person is as it were without truths, because he is surrounded by evil spirits, who bring temptation, and then as it were take away truths from him, is manifest from:** 

Matthew 4:1-3; Mark 1:12, 13; Luke 4:1-3; Ezekiel 20:34-37; Jeremiah 2:2, 6, 7; Hosea 2:13-16; Psalm 107:4-7; Deuteronomy 1:31, 33; 8:2-4, 15, 16; 32:10.

...is signified the state of the church, so that, meanwhile, preparation may be made for it among many people. By **a thousand two hundred and sixty days**, is signified the end of one state and the beginning of another <note>original: "n. 491"; this refers to Swedenborg's internal numbering system used across his works</note>; that is, the end of the former church and the beginning of the New Church. This is the same meaning as "a time, times, and half a time" (verse 14, number 562); thus it also refers to the appointed state—that is, until it comes into existence as has been provided.

It is a matter of the Lord's **Divine Providence** <term>Divine Providence: The government of the Lord's Divine Love and Wisdom, which works to lead humanity toward heaven while respecting human freedom.</term> that the church should at first be among a few people and should increase gradually among many. This is because the falsities of the former church must first be removed, as truths cannot be received before that happens. Truths that are received and implanted before falsities are removed do not remain; they are also dissipated by the **dragonists** <term>Dragonists: Those who separate faith from charity, believing that salvation comes through belief alone regardless of how one lives.</term>. The case was the same with the early Christian Church, which increased gradually from a few to many. 

Another reason is that a **New Heaven** must first be formed, which will make one with the church on the earth. On this account we read that *he saw a New Heaven, and the Holy Jerusalem coming down from God out of Heaven* (Apoc. 21:1, 2). It is certain that a New Church, which is the **New Jerusalem**, will exist, because it is foretold in the Apocalypse, chapters 21 and 22. It is also certain that the falsities of the former church must first be removed; for these are treated of in the Apocalypse as far as the twentieth chapter.

### THE WAR IN HEAVEN

No other war can take place in heaven, where it is said to have arisen; nor can it occur in heaven once it is formed of angels. Rather, it took place in the **former heaven** <note>In Swedenborg's theology, the "former heaven" refers to an intermediate spiritual state composed of those who were outwardly moral but inwardly lacked true faith or charity; this "heaven" passed away during the Last Judgment in the spiritual world.</note> which passed away, as spoken of in Apocalypse 21:1; regarding that heaven, see the explanation provided there. For that heaven passed away in consequence...

Many people today who believe that "faith alone" is sufficient think that the **blood of the Lamb** mentioned here refers to the Lord’s suffering on the cross. They think this because they make the Lord’s suffering the central point of their religious doctrine, claiming that He took the punishment of the law upon Himself, satisfied the demands of God the Father, and reconciled humanity to Him—among other similar ideas. 

However, this is not the case. Instead, "the Lord came into the world so that He might conquer the <term>hells: In Swedenborg’s terminology, this refers to the collective power of all evil and false influences.</term> and <term>glorify His Human: The process by which Jesus made His human nature completely one with His Divine nature.</term>; and the suffering of the cross was the final battle through which He fully conquered the hells and fully glorified His Human." This can be explored further in the work *The Doctrine of the New Jerusalem concerning the Lord* (numbers 12–14). 

From this, one can see that the "blood of the Lamb" does not refer to the suffering on the cross in the way modern doctrine suggests. Instead, the **blood of the Lamb** signifies the **Divine Truth** proceeding from the Lord, which is the Divine Truth found in the <term>Word: A term for the sacred scripture or the Divine revelation of God's wisdom.</term>. This is evident because the Lord is the Word; and because He is the Word, the Divine Truth within it is His "Blood," and the Divine Good within it is His "Body." This can be understood in this way: Is not every person defined by their own goodness and their own truth? Since goodness belongs to the will and truth belongs to the understanding, every person is essentially their will and their understanding. What else makes a human? Is a person, in their very essence, anything other than these two things? In the same way, the Lord is Goodness itself and Truth itself—that is, Divine Good and Divine Truth—and these two together constitute the Word.

To "love their life" <note>original: *animam suam*, referring to the soul or the lower self-centered life.</note> means to love oneself and the world; for "life" here refers to a person's own inherited life—the ego—which every person has from birth. This natural ego loves itself and the world above all things. For this reason, by *not* loving...

...not to love their life signifies not to love themselves and the world more than the Lord and the things which belong to the Lord. "Even unto death" signifies a willingness to die rather than abandon these values; consequently, it is to love the Lord above all things, and the neighbor as oneself (Matthew 22:35-39), and to wish to die rather than recede from these two loves. The same meaning is found in these words of the Lord: *He that would find his life, shall lose it; and he that will lose his life for Jesus’ sake, shall find it* (Matthew 10:39; Luke 17:33). *He that loveth his life shall lose it; but he that hateth his life in this world shall keep it unto life eternal* (John 12:25). *Jesus said, If any man will come after Me, let him deny himself; for whosoever will save his life, shall lose it; but whosoever will lose his life for my sake, shall find it: what doth it profit a man, if he shall gain the whole world, but lose his own soul? or what shall a man give in exchange for his soul* (Matthew 16:24-26; Mark 8:35-37; Luke 9:24, 25). By loving the Lord is meant to love to do His commandments (John 14:20-24). The reason is because He is His own commandments; for they originate from Him, and consequently He is present within them. Thus, He is in the man in whose life those commandments are inscribed—and they are inscribed upon a person by the act of willing and doing them.

557. **For this rejoice, O heavens, and ye that dwell in them,** signifies a new state of heaven, characterized by the fact that they are in the Lord, and the Lord is in them. Since the New Church rejects the old dogma that "the understanding must be kept in obedience to faith," <note>original: *intellectum sub obsequium fidei*; a common theological demand in Swedenborg's time that believers accept mysteries without using their reason.</note> it has received this principle instead: that the truth of the church must be *seen* in order to be believed (section 224). Because truth cannot be seen except through the rational mind, the text says "before the truths rationally understood." 

How can any person be led by the Lord and joined to heaven if they have closed up their understanding regarding the very things that relate to salvation and eternal life? Is it not the understanding that must be enlightened and taught? What is the understanding when it is closed up by religion, but **thick-darkness**? And it is a kind of thick-darkness that actively rejects the light of illustration. Furthermore, who can truly acknowledge any truth and keep it unless they actually see it? A truth that is not seen is merely a phrase not understood. While people focused only on physical and worldly things might keep such phrases in their memory, the wise cannot. Indeed, the wise cast empty words out of their memory—words that have not entered through the understanding. Examples of such words include:
*   That the one God is "three as to persons."
*   That the Lord born from eternity is not the same as the Lord born in time (essentially saying one Lord is God and the other is not). 
*   The idea that a life of <term>charity: The spiritual practice of doing good and being useful to others.</term>, which consists of good works...

<meta>This page continues the exposition of the Apocalypse, moving from the symbolic state of the author "on the sand of the sea" to a narrative account of a spiritual debate regarding the source of theological truth.</meta>

->### No. 566.<-

566. To this I will add this <term>Memorable Relation: A visionary account of an experience in the spiritual world, used to illustrate a theological point.</term>. A question arose among some spirits as to whether anyone can see any doctrinal theological truth in <term>the Word: The Holy Scriptures, which Swedenborg describes as having a literal sense and a deeper spiritual sense.</term>, except from <term>the Lord: In this work, this title refers specifically to Jesus Christ as the one God of heaven and earth.</term>. They all agreed on this: that no one can, except from God, because *a man can receive nothing except it be given him from heaven* (John 3:27). For this reason, the dispute was whether it is possible for anyone unless he goes immediately to the Lord.

On the one hand, they said that the Lord is to be approached directly because He is the Word. On the other hand, they argued that doctrinal truth may also be seen when God the Father is immediately approached. Consequently, the dispute centered upon this point: Whether it is lawful for any Christian to go immediately to God the Father, and so to climb above the Lord; and whether this is not an act of insolence and audacity, both indecent and rash, because the Lord says that *no one comes to the Father but through Him* (John 14:6).

But they left this point and argued that a man can see a doctrinal truth in the Word from his own <term>natural light: The Latin term 'lumen' refers here to human intellectual light or common sense, as opposed to spiritual light ('lux') from heaven.</term> <note>original: "lumen"</note>. However, this was rejected. Therefore, they insisted that it might be seen by those who pray to God the Father.

Upon this, a passage was read to them from the Word. They then prayed upon their knees that God the Father would enlighten them. Regarding the passage read to them, they claimed that this and that was the truth within it; but it was actually false. This was repeated several times, even to the point of being tedious. At length, they confessed that it was not possible. On the other side, those who went immediately to the Lord saw truths and informed the others.

After this dispute was thus decided, some spirits came up out of the <term>abyss: A symbolic region of the spiritual world representing the depths of false beliefs.</term> who appeared at first like <term>locusts: In Swedenborg’s symbolism, locusts represent falsities in the most external parts of the human mind.</term>, but afterwards as men. These were people who, while in the world, had prayed to the Father and confirmed themselves in the doctrine of <term>justification by faith alone: The belief that salvation is granted through faith or trust in God's mercy without the necessity of doing good deeds.</term>. "**And upon his horns ten diadems,**" *symbolizes* the power to misinterpret and falsify many truths of the Word.

"**And upon his heads a name of blasphemy,**" *symbolizes* the denial of the Lord’s Divine Human <term>Divine Human</term><note>A key theological concept signifying that Jesus Christ’s human nature is itself Divine, and that God is one in Him.</note>, and a church doctrine that is not based on the Bible, but is instead constructed from human intelligence.

"**And the beast which I saw was like unto a leopard,**" *symbolizes* a heresy that destroys the church because it is built upon distorted biblical truths.

"**And his feet like a bear's,**" *symbolizes* being filled with fallacies because the literal sense of the Bible is read but not truly understood.

"**And his mouth as the mouth of a lion,**" *symbolizes* the use of logic and reasoning to make lies appear as truths.

"**And the dragon gave him his power and his throne and great authority,**" *symbolizes* that this specific heresy prevails and dominates because the laity has accepted it.

"**And I saw one of his heads, as it were wounded unto death,**" *symbolizes* the realization that the doctrine of "faith alone" does not actually align with the Word of God, where performing good works is frequently commanded.

"**And his deadly wound was healed,**" *symbolizes* the method used to bypass this contradiction, which is explained further on.

"**And the whole earth wondered after the beast,**" *symbolizes* that this doctrine and faith were then embraced with great enthusiasm.

"**And they worshipped the Dragon who gave authority to the beast,**" *symbolizes* the acknowledgment that these teachings come from the leaders and teachers, who ensured the doctrine prevailed by having the general public accept it.

"**one killeth with the sword he must be killed with the sword,**" *signifies* that he who destroys the soul of another by falsities <note>In this theological context, "falsities" refer to spiritual errors or distorted truths that lead the mind away from genuine goodness.</note> shall be destroyed and perish by falsities.

"**And he doeth great signs,**" *signifies* testifications <note>Or "attestations"—the proofs or arguments used to convince others.</note> that what they teach are truths, although they are falsities. 

"**So that he maketh fire to come down from heaven unto the earth before men,**" *signifies* proofs that their falsities are truths. 

"**And seduceth them that dwell on the earth by the signs which it was given him to do before the beast,**" *signifies* that by testifications and proofs they lead the men of the church into errors. 

"**Saying to them that dwell on the earth that they should make an image to the beast which hath the wound by a sword and did live,**" *signifies* that they induce the men of the church to receive for doctrine, that faith is the only medium of salvation, for the reason here explained <note>An "image" represents a constructed system of thought or a dogma that is treated as a living reality.</note>. 

"**And it was given him to give breath to the image of the beast, that the image of the beast should both speak,**" *signifies* that it was permitted them to confirm that doctrine by the Word, by which it is *as it were vivified as it is taught.* <note>To "give breath" or "life" to a doctrine means to use the authority of the Bible to make a human-made idea seem divinely inspired and active.</note>

"**He that hath understanding, let him count the number of the beast,**" *signifies* that anyone who receives spiritual enlightenment from the Lord may recognize the true quality of the arguments and "confirmations" used by these teachers to support their doctrine from the Word.

"**For it is the number of a man,**" *signifies* the actual quality or state of the Word as it is used, and consequently the state of the church.

"**And his number is six hundred sixty-six,**" *signifies* that the spiritual quality of this system is one where every single truth of the Word has been falsified or distorted by them. <note>original: "sexcenti sexaginta sex" — In Swedenborg's system of numerology, the number 666 represents the total profanation and corruption of all that is holy and true.</note>

<meta>This page continues the interpretation of Revelation Chapter 13, following the previous discussion on the mark of the beast. Here, the author clarifies the symbolic identities of the two "beasts" described in the biblical text, distinguishing between the faith of the general church members (laity) and that of the religious leaders (clergy).</meta>

# No. 567.] THE APOCALYPSE REVEALED. #

Who the **dragon** is may be seen in **number** 537 <note>original: "n. 537"; referring to a previous section of this work where the dragon is defined as the doctrine of "faith alone" separated from charity.</note>. The same topic of faith continues to be treated in this chapter; and by this **beast**, which was seen coming up out of the sea, is meant that faith as it exists among the **laity** <term>laity</term><note>The general members of a church, as distinguished from the ordained ministers or clergy.</note>; but by the **beast out of the earth** (*verse 11*), that faith among the **clergy** is meant. 

That the **dragon** continues to be discussed here is evident from these words in this chapter: *That the Dragon gave to the beast that came up out of the sea his power, and throne, and great authority (verse 2): and that they worshipped the dragon who gave authority to the beast (verse 4): and concerning the beast out of the earth, that he spake as the dragon (verse 11): and that he exercised all the authority of the first beast before the Dragon (verse 12).* 

The reason that the laity are meant by the **beast out of the sea**, and the clergy by the **beast out of the earth**, is because the external aspects of the church are signified by the **sea**, and the internal aspects by the **earth** (*number* 398, and elsewhere); and the laity are engaged in the externals of church doctrine, while the clergy are engaged in its internals: for this reason, the beast out of the earth is also called "the false prophet" in the passages that follow. 

These figures are placed within the **Reformed** <term>Reformed</term><note>Protestant churches that emerged from the Reformation, such as the Lutheran or Calvinist traditions.</note> churches because the Reformed are the subject of the text until **chapter 16** inclusive; the **Roman Catholics** are discussed in **chapters 17 and 18**; and afterward follows the **Last Judgment**, and finally the **New Church**. 

They appeared as **beasts** because a dragon is a beast, and because a "beast" in **the Word** <term>the Word</term><note>The Holy Scriptures or Bible, viewed here as containing a deep, symbolic spiritual meaning.</note> signifies man in terms of his **affections** <term>affections</term><note>In this philosophy, "affections" refer to the underlying desires or loves that drive a person's character.</note>—harmless and useful beasts represent man’s good affections, and harmful and useless beasts represent man’s evil affections. It is for this reason that the people of the church are generally called **sheep**, a congregation of them is called a **flock**, and the one who teaches is called a **pastor** <note>original: "pastor," meaning shepherd</note>. 

This is also why the Word—in regards to its power, affection, understanding, and wisdom—is described previously by **four animals**, which were a lion, a calf, an eagle, and a man (*chapter 4*); and the understanding of the Word is represented by **horses** (*chapter 6*). The reason for this is that in the **spiritual world** a man’s affections appear at a distance like beasts, as has often been stated.

In regard to the **Second** point—that it is blasphemy not to take the doctrine of the church from the Word, but to evolve it from their own intelligence—this is so because the church exists from the Word, and is defined by how the Word is understood; see the *Doctrine of the New Jerusalem concerning the Sacred Scripture* (n. 76–79). I then asked them: "What does the Decalogue require? Is it not this: *Thou shalt not kill, Thou shalt not commit adultery, Thou shalt not steal, Thou shalt not testify falsely*? Are these the 'works of the law' which you separate from faith? Do you truly say that faith alone, without keeping these laws, justifies and saves?"

These truths are holy only when they come from the Lord and remain in the person, and the Lord is present in them when the truths of His Word are in them (John 15:7). By virtue of these truths from the Lord, the angels are called **holy** (Matthew 25:31; Luke 9:26), and the **<unclear>p</unclear>rophets** likewise (Luke 1:70; Revelation...).

The same is signified by Christ as is signified here by the Lamb—namely, the Lord in respect to the <term>Divine Truth</term> <note>The reality of God as expressed through wisdom and the Word; it is the light that illuminates the human mind.</note> of the Word. Therefore, their saying, "Lo, here is Christ," signifies their claim that their teaching is the Divine Truth of the Word. The things which the Lord foretold in that chapter of Matthew concerned the last period or state of the Church, which is there meant by the <term>consummation of the age</term> <note>original: "consummatio saeculi." This refers to the end of a specific spiritual era or church cycle, rather than the physical destruction of the world.</note>.

596. **And he exerciseth all the authority of the first beast before him**, signifies that they confirmed the <term>dogmas</term> <note>The established doctrines or formal principles of a religion.</note> which are symbolized by the dragon and have been accepted by the laity, and that through these confirmations, those doctrines gain power. That this is the meaning can be seen from the earlier explanations regarding the authority given by the dragon to the beast that rose out of the sea (numbers 575, 579). Since this second beast, which represents the false-prophet, exercised that authority in the presence of the dragon, it signifies nothing other than that the clergy made those doctrines prevail by providing intellectual and theological justifications for them.

597. **And he causeth the earth and them that dwell therein to worship the first beast, whose deadly wound was healed**, signifies that it was thus firmly established through these justifications that it should be acknowledged as a holy thing of the church: that because no one can perform a good work of themselves or fulfill the law, the only means of salvation is faith in the righteousness and merit of Christ, who suffered for humanity and thereby removed the condemnation of the law.

However, even after the era of physical signs and miracles ended, their symbolic meaning remains: the evidence or witnessing of truth. In this specific passage, the **signs** signify the "proofs" offered by the beast (or the false prophet) to make his falsehoods appear true; once a person is convinced by these arguments, the falsehoods no longer seem like lies. and the great, the rich and the poor, the free and the bond, are meant all in that church, of whatever condition, learning, and intelligence they are. 605. *That he should give them a mark upon their right hand, and upon their foreheads*, signifies that no one is acknowledged as a <term>Reformed Christian</term> <note>At the time of writing (1766), "Reformed" referred generally to the Protestant churches that emerged from the Reformation, particularly those adhering to the doctrines of Luther or Calvin.</note>, but he who receives that doctrine in faith and love. By giving a mark is signified to acknowledge as a Reformed Christian, or that one is of the confession which that doctrine teaches: the mark is the acknowledgment that he is such, as also the confession that he is. By the **right hand** is signified the whole of man as to intellectual power, and thus as to faith; for the right hand signifies a man's power (n. 457 <note>original: "n. 457" - a reference to an earlier paragraph in this work.</note>). By the **forehead** is signified the whole of man as to voluntary power <note>The "voluntary power" refers to the faculty of the Will, or what a person loves and desires.</note>, and thus as to love; for the forehead signifies love (n. 347).

**610. This meaning is derived because **six** signifies the same as three multiplied by two. **Three** signifies "fullness" or "all," and relates to truths (no. 505); **two** signifies the "marriage" or union of good and truth. Since six is composed of these two numbers multiplied together, it signifies every truth in the Word—though here, it is truth that has been corrupted. That these truths are indeed falsified by them can be seen in earlier sections (no. 566). 

The reason the number **666** is specifically mentioned is that the number six is tripled; this tripling represents a state of total completion. The fact that it is multiplied by a hundred (to make 600) and by ten (to make 60) does not change the essential meaning; it only shifts the scale (see no. 348). For the attributes of the **Divine essence** <term>Divine essence: the fundamental nature or "what-ness" of God, which is Love and Wisdom itself</term> are many; as omnipotence, omniscience, omnipresence, mercy, grace, eternity, and others. And there are attributes that proceed from the Divine essence; which are creation and preservation, salvation and redemption, enlightenment and instruction. 

Every one who thinks of God from **person** <note>person: a way of thinking that focuses on an individual entity or outward form rather than the underlying nature</note> only, makes three Gods; saying that One God is the Creator and Preserver, Another the Saviour and Redeemer, and a Third the Enlightener and Instructor. Yet every one who thinks of God from essence, makes God One; saying, God created and preserved us, redeemed and saves us, and enlightens and instructs us. 

This is the reason that they who think of the trinity in God according to person, and thus materially, cannot, from the ideas of their thought, which is material, do otherwise than from one God make three. But still, contrary to their thought, they are obliged to say, that there is in each a communion of all the attributes; and this solely for the reason that they have also thought of God obscurely from essence. 

Wherefore, my pupils, think of God from His essence, and from that of His person; and not from His person, and from this of His essence: for to think of His essence from His person is to think materially of His essence also; but to think of His person from His essence is also to think spiritually of His person. They do not think that the understanding, when shut up by **religion**, is as blind as a mole, with nothing but thick-darkness in it. 

Such thick-darkness rejects all spiritual light, prevents the **influx** <term>influx: the constant flow of life, light, and love from God into the human mind</term> of light from the Lord and from heaven, and establishes a barrier against it in the **corporeal-sensual** <term>corporeal-sensual: the lowest level of human thought, which relies entirely on physical senses and bodily urges</term>, far below the rational, in matters of faith. This essentially puts their faith "close to the nose," fixing it in the very cartilage of the nose, where they can no longer even catch the "scent" of spiritual things; because of this, some have become so sensitive that when they perceive the scent of spiritual things, they fall into a swoon—by "scent," I mean perception. 

These are the people who make God into three. They say indeed, from **essence**, that God is one; but still, when they pray according to their faith—asking that God the Father would have mercy for the sake of the Son, and send the Holy Spirit—they clearly make three Gods. They cannot do otherwise; for they pray to one, to have mercy for the sake of another, and to send a third." And then their master taught them concerning the Lord, that He is the One God, in whom there is a **Divine trinity**.

<summary>The author explains that a literal or "material" way of thinking prevents a person from understanding the Bible, effectively blinding their spiritual perception. He critiques the traditional view of the Trinity, arguing that praying to three distinct "persons" divides God into three, whereas true understanding sees the Trinity within the single person of the Lord.</summary>

### THE EXPLANATION.

612. **And I saw, and behold, a Lamb standing upon the mount Zion, and with Him a hundred forty-four thousand,** signifies the Lord now in the New Heaven. This heaven is composed of people from the Christian churches who acknowledged the Lord alone as the God of heaven and earth, and who lived according to the truths of doctrine derived from the good of love from Him through the Word. 

By "I saw," these things are signified as well as those that follow in this chapter. By the "Lamb" is meant the Lord in His <term>Divine Human</term> <note>original: "Divinum Humanum"; Swedenborg’s term for God’s personhood as expressed through Jesus Christ, which he believes is fully Divine.</note> (see sections 269, 271). By "mount Zion" is signified the heaven where those who live in love to the Lord reside, which will be discussed in more detail later. 

By the "hundred forty-four thousand" are signified all those who acknowledge the Lord alone as the God of heaven and earth, and who possess the truths of doctrine arising from the good of love from Him through the Word (see section 348, etc.). These individuals were discussed previously in chapter seven; however, in 그곳 <note>In that place (referring to chapter 7).</note> it was said they were "sealed on their foreheads"—meaning they were identified and separated from the rest. Here, the text describes them being gathered together into a unified group.

613. ***Having His Father’s name written in their foreheads*** signifies their acknowledgment of the Lord’s <term>Divine</term> <note>In Swedenborg’s theology, "The Divine" refers to the infinite, essential nature of God.</note> and <term>Divine Human</term> <note>The concept that God became human in the person of Jesus Christ and, through the process of "glorification," made that human nature completely one with the infinite Divine, making God visible and approachable to humanity.</note> from a state of love and faith. By the "name of the Father" is meant the Lord in relation to the Divine source from which all things originate (which is called the Father), and simultaneously in relation to the Divine Human (which is called the Son). This is because they are one and the same person, united just as the soul is to the body. Therefore, in heaven, when "God the Father" is mentioned, no other is meant than the Lord; and in the New Heaven, the Lord is also called Father. 

The reason that the name of the Father is said here to be in their foreheads is also because the <term>Divine Good</term> <note>The aspect of God’s nature that is pure love and benevolence.</note> of the Lord’s Divine Love is what is meant by the "Father." This is the consistent meaning of "the Father" throughout the Gospels whenever the Lord names Him. Conversely, the <term>Divine Truth</term> <note>The aspect of God’s nature that is pure wisdom and light.</note> of His Divine Wisdom is meant by the "Son." These two were united—like the soul to the body and the body to the soul—when the Lord glorified His Human (see references 21 and 170). Because they are one, it is stated in another place, *the name of God and of the Lamb in their foreheads* (Chapter 22:4). 

Regarding those who are treated of here, it is said that they had the Father’s name written in their foreheads because the "one hundred forty-four thousand" sealed out of the twelve tribes of Israel represent the angels of the higher heavens. These angels are all in the good of <term>celestial love</term> <note>The highest form of love in heaven: a direct, heart-felt love for the Lord, rather than a love based on intellectual understanding or obedience.</note>; and by the "Father," as has been said, that specific "good" of love is meant. That the angels discussed here are specifically those of the higher heavens can be seen in the explanation of the seventh chapter (particularly in reference 363). By the phrase "written in their foreheads," the text signifies an internal acknowledgment within them that springs from love and faith. By "written" or "inscribed" is signified this acknowledgment in them; and by the "forehead" is signified love, and the resulting intelligence or faith (references 347 and 605). 615. **And as the voice of a great thunder**, signifies the Lord speaking through the New Heaven from the Divine Love. The Lord never speaks in any other way when He speaks from the higher heavens; and this is what is meant by a voice as of many waters and by a voice of great thunder. “Many waters” are the Divine Truths of the Divine Wisdom, and “a great thunder” is the Divine Good of the Divine Love.

By this the idea of their thought concerning three has been confirmed; and then they are not able to think of the Son as God, equal with the Father, and one with the Father; but of the Son as equal with another man, although He alone, as to His Human, is **Justice**, and is called ***Jehovah our Justice***<note>original: "Iehovah Iustitia nostra." The Lord likewise confirms this by so often saying *that they must believe in Him, that they may have eternal life*; see above (number 553). 

Who can not see that all these things were said by the Lord concerning Himself in His Human; and that He never would have said, nor could have said, that He was in men and men in Him, and that we must believe in Him in order to have eternal life, unless His Human was Divine? By asking the Father "in His name" is not meant to go to God the Father immediately, nor to ask for His sake; but to go to the Lord, and to the Father through Him, because the Father is in the Son, and they are one, as He teaches. This is what “in His name” signifies; as may also be evident from these passages: *He that believeth not in the Son is judged already, because he hath not believed in the name of the only begotten Son of God* (John 3:17, 18). *These things are written, that ye may believe that Jesus is the Christ the Son of God, and that believing ye may have life in His name* (John 20:31). *Jesus said, Whosoever shall receive this child in my name, receiveth Me; and he that receiveth Me, receiveth Him that sent Me* (Luke 9:48). *Whatsoever ye shall ask in my name, that will I do* (John 14:13). 

Besides other places, where the expression "in the name of the Lord" occurs: (Matthew 7:22; 18:5, 20; 19:29; 23:39; Mark 9:37; 16:17; Luke 13:35; 19:38; 24:47; John 1:12; 2:23; 5:43; 12:13; 15:16; 16:23, 24, 26, 27; 17:6). What the name of God is, and that the name of the Father is the Lord as to the <term>Divine Human</term><note>Swedenborg’s term for the Lord’s body and persona, which serves as the visible and accessible form of the otherwise invisible Infinite God.</note>, may be seen above (numbers 81, 165, 584).
