619. ***Bought from the earth***, signifies that they are those who could be <term>regenerated</term><note>The process of being spiritually reborn or transformed by the Lord, turning from worldly impulses toward a life of love and faith.</note> by the Lord, and thus be redeemed, in the world. By the "bought from the earth," those redeemed in the world are signified. That <term>redemption</term><note>In this context, being set free from the influence of "hell" (evil and falsity) and brought into a close spiritual connection with the Divine.</note> is liberation from hell and salvation by <term>conjunction</term><note>A spiritual joining or union between the individual and the Lord.</note> with the Lord, may be seen in section 281; and as this is effected by regeneration, those who are regenerated—and thus redeemed by the Lord—are signified by the "bought." Since all people can be regenerated and thus redeemed if they are willing, yet few choose to be, "bought from the earth" signifies those who were willing to be regenerated. The specific qualities of these people will now be described in verses 4 and 5.

620. ***These are they who were not defiled with women, for they are virgins***, signifies that they did not <term>adulterate</term><note>To corrupt or distort a pure spiritual truth by mixing it with selfish or false ideas.</note> the truths of the church, nor defile them with the <term>falsities of faith</term><note>Religious beliefs that are incorrect or misleading, often used to justify harmful behaviors.</note>; rather, they loved truths simply because they are truths. That a "woman" signifies the church based on an affection for truth—and in the opposite sense, a church based on an affection for what is false—may be seen above (sections 434 and 533). In this instance, it refers to the church based on an affection for truth, because the text says they were "not defiled with women." To be "defiled with women" carries the same spiritual meaning as committing adultery or fornication. That these acts signify the corruption and falsification of the Word <note>The Holy Scriptures or Divine Revelation.</note> may be seen above (section 134). "For they are virgins" signifies that they loved truths because they are truths, and thus acted from a spiritual affection. The reason virgins represent such people is that a "virgin" signifies the church as a bride who desires to be joined to the Lord and to become a wife. A church that wishes to be joined to the Lord loves truths for their own sake, for it is through truths—when one lives according to them—that this spiritual union is achieved. This is why Israel, Zion, and Jerusalem <note>original: "Ierusalem"</note> are called "virgins" and "daughters" in the Word; for by Israel, Zion, and Jerusalem, the church itself is signified. Something will here be said respecting the **first-fruits**. It was commanded in the Israelitish church, *that the first-fruits of the produce of the fields, of all the corn, oil, and wine, the fruits of the trees, also of the fleece, should be given to Jehovah as holy, and were given by Jehovah to Aaron, and after him to the High Priest* (Exodus 22:29; 23:10; Numbers 13:20; 15:17–21; 18:8–20; Deuteronomy 18:4; 26:1, etc.). *Also, That they should celebrate the feast of the first-fruits of the harvest and of bread* (Exodus 23:14–16, 19, 26; Leviticus 23:9–15, 20–25; Numbers 28:26, to the end). 

The reason was, because the **First-fruits** signified that which is born first, and afterwards grows up, as an infant into a man, and a shoot into a tree; and they thence signified everything that follows until it is complete; for all that follows is in the first as the man is in the infant, and the tree is in the shoot. Because this *first* exists before the successions <note>The "successions" refer to the stages of growth that follow the beginning.</note>, and the same is true in heaven and the church, therefore the first-fruits were holy to the Lord, and the feast of the first-fruits was celebrated. Similar things are signified by first-fruits in Jeremiah 24:1, 2; Ezekiel 20:40; Micah 7:1; Deuteronomy 33:15, 21.

624. **And in their mouth was found no guile**, signifies that they do not from cunning and design speak and persuade to falsity and evil. By the **mouth** is signified speech, preaching, and teaching (see number 452): and by **guile**, persuasion to evil by means of falsity, properly from cunning and design, is signified. For he who persuades to anything from cunning or deceit, persuades from design also: for cunning or deceit proposes to itself a goal, conceals its purpose, and performs it when opportunity offers. By a **lie** in the Word <note>Swedenborg frequently refers to the Bible as "The Word."</note> falsity and false-speaking are signified, and by **deceit** is signified each of these done from design; these are signified in the following passages:

> *Jesus said of Nathaniel, Behold an Israelite indeed, in whom is no guile* (John 1:47).
> *The remnant of Israel shall not speak a lie, neither shall a deceitful tongue [be found in their mouth]* <note>original: "The remnant of Israel shall not speak a lie, neither shall a deceitful tongue..." citing Zephaniah 3:13.</note>

<meta>This page continues the analysis of Revelation 14, specifically concluding the explanation of section 639 regarding the "blessed dead" and beginning section 640 regarding their "rest." it clarifies that "death" in this spiritual context refers to the process of overcoming one's selfish nature through spiritual trials.</meta>

->No. 640.] THE APOCALYPSE REVEALED<-

that the member of the **New Church** <term>New Church<gloss>A spiritual community or state of mind characterized by a direct relationship with the Lord and a life governed by charity and faith.</gloss></term> will be tested by **temptations** <term>temptations<gloss>Internal spiritual struggles where a person's faith and character are tested against their own selfish or worldly desires.</gloss></term> regarding their character—specifically whether they live according to the commandments and have faith in the Lord; see the previous section <note>n. 638; "n." is an abbreviation for "number," referring to the numbered paragraphs used throughout this work for cross-referencing.</note>, and what follows, ***and they shall rest from their labors;*** which signifies that those who have endured these trials will have peace in the Lord; this is discussed below (section 640). 

By **temptations** here are meant spiritual trials suffered by those who have faith in the Lord and live according to His precepts while they are driving away the evil spirits that are with them—spirits who act as one with the person's own selfish lusts. These temptations are symbolized by the **cross** in these passages: *Whoever does not take up his cross and follow Me is not worthy of Me* (Matthew 10:38). *Jesus said, If anyone desires to come after Me, let him deny himself, take up his cross, and follow Me* (Matthew 16:24; Luke 9:23–25; 14:26, 27). 

This is also what Paul means by "crucifying the flesh": *Those who belong to Christ crucify the flesh with its passions and desires* (Galatians 5:24). The reason that those who have afflicted their soul, "crucified their flesh," and endured temptations are called **the dead** is because through these means they have **mortified** <gloss>put to death or subdued</gloss> their former way of life, and consequently have become as if "dead" to the values of the world. For the Lord said, *Unless a grain of wheat falls into the ground and dies, it remains alone; but if it dies, it produces much fruit* (John 12:24). 

Nor are any others meant by "the dead" in these words of John: *Jesus said, As the Father raises the dead and gives them life, even so the Son gives life to whom He will* (5:21). And in the same book: *Jesus said, The hour is coming when the dead shall hear the voice of the Son of God, and those who hear shall live* (5:25). This is also the meaning of the **resurrection of the dead** (Luke 14:14; Revelation 20:5, 12, 13; and elsewhere); see above (section 106). And in the Psalms: *Precious in the eyes of Jehovah is the death of His saints* (Psalm 116:15). Jesus also said, *Whoever loses his life for My sake will find it* (Matthew 10:39; 16:25; Luke 9:24, 25; 17:33; John 12:25).

642. **And I saw, and behold, a white cloud, and upon the cloud one sitting like unto the Son of Man**, signifies the **Lord** in His role as the **Word** <term>the Word<gloss>The Divine Truth or the Bible, which Swedenborg views as the Lord Himself in written form.</gloss></term>. By a **cloud**, the Word in the **sense of the letter** <gloss>the literal, surface-level meaning of scripture</gloss> is signified, and by a **white cloud**, the Word in the literal sense as it is understood interiorly; and by the **Son of Man** is meant the Lord as to the Word: for this reason it is said, "one sitting upon the cloud like unto the Son of Man." That the Word in its literal sense is signified by a cloud may be seen above (n. 24, 513). A "white cloud" signifies the literal sense as it is seen from within because "white" is used to describe truths that are in the light (n. 167, 367); and there are spiritual truths deep within the literal sense which are in the light of heaven. That the Lord as the Word is meant by the **Son of Man** may be seen above (n. 44); and it is extensively confirmed in the *Doctrine of the New Jerusalem concerning the Lord* (n. 19–28). The Lord often said that *they should see the Son of Man coming in the clouds of heaven*. He says this in Matthew 17:5; 24:30; 26:64; Mark 14:61, 62; Luke 9:34, 35; 21:27: and no one knows that anything else is signified by it except that when He comes to judgment, He will physically appear in the clouds of heaven. Yet this is not the meaning; the meaning is that when He comes to judgment, He will appear in the literal sense of the Word. And as He has now come, He has therefore appeared in the Word by revealing that there is a **spiritual sense** in every particular <note>Swedenborg claims that his own writings are the "revelation" of this spiritual sense, marking the Lord's "Second Coming" in a spiritual, rather than physical, manner.</note>.

The spiritual kingdom is the kingdom of the Lord’s Wisdom, because the angels there are in wisdom from Divine Truths from the Lord; and the heavenly kingdom is the kingdom of the Lord’s Love, because the angels there are in love from the Lord, and thence in all good. That there are two kingdoms into which all the heavens are distinguished may be seen in the work concerning *Heaven and Hell*, published at London, 1758 (nos. 20–28), and in the *Angelic Wisdom concerning the Divine Love and Divine Wisdom*, published 1763 (nos. 101, 381).

The good of love does not perform anything by itself, but acts through the truth of wisdom; nor does the truth of wisdom perform anything by itself, but acts from the good of love. By "casting the clusters of the vine into the winepress" is signified the process of <term>exploration</term> <note>In this context, "exploration" refers to a spiritual examination or "testing" of a person's inner motives and outward actions.</note> of their works, for "works" are what these clusters represent (as seen above, n. 649). 

But because it is specifically called the **winepress of the anger of God**, it signifies an exploration revealing that their works were evil; for the "anger of God" is a term used in the Word in relation to evil itself (n. 635). The reason that a **winepress** symbolizes exploration is because, in a literal winepress, the new wine is squeezed out of the clusters and oil is pressed out of the olives. From the quality of the wine or oil that is produced, one can perceive the actual quality of the grapes or olives themselves. 

Since the <term>Christian church</term> <note>Swedenborg frequently uses this term to refer to the organized religious institutions of his day, which he believed had lost their spiritual essence.</note> is symbolized by the **vine**, and its "works" are symbolized by the **clusters**, the act of casting them into the winepress represents the spiritual examination of the people within that church. However, because they have separated <term>faith</term> <note>Original: "fides."</note> from <term>charity</term> <note>Original: "caritas." Swedenborg argues that faith is meaningless and "dead" if it is not expressed through active love and good deeds (charity).</note> and have claimed that faith alone can save a person without the "works of the law," only evil works can actually proceed from such a state. Therefore, it is called the **great winepress of the anger of God**.

653. ***And blood came out of the winepress, even unto the bridles of the horses***, signifies violence done to the **Word** <note>In this context, "The Word" refers to the Holy Scriptures, which the author views as the ultimate source of Divine Truth.</note> by dreadful <term>falsifications</term> <note>Falsification refers to the act of twisting the meaning of scripture to justify selfish or incorrect beliefs.</note> of truth, and the understanding so closed up thereby that man can scarce be taught any longer, and thus be led of the Lord by **Divine Truths**. By the blood is signified violence done to the **Word** (n. 327), and the Divine Truth of the **Word** falsified and profaned (n. 379): for by the blood out of the winepress is meant the grape-juice and wine from the trodden clusters; and by grape-juice and wine similar things are signified (n. 316). By "**the bridles of the horses**" are signified the truths of the **Word**, by which the understanding is led; for a horse signifies the understanding of the **Word** (n. 298): hence the truth by which the understanding is led is signified by a bridle. "**Even unto the bridles of the horses**," is even into the mouth in which the bridle is inserted; and a horse is watered and fed through the mouth; therefore it also signifies, that such violence was done to the **Word** by dreadful falsifications, that man can scarce be taught any longer, and thus be led of the Lord by **Divine Truths**. That by which the understanding is led is also signified by a bridle (Isaiah 30:27, 28; 37:29): and the Divine Truth of the **Word** is signified by the blood of grapes (Genesis 49:11; Deuteronomy 32:14); but here in the opposite sense.

654. ***For a thousand six hundred furlongs***, signifies mere falsities of evil. The same is signified by furlongs as by ways, since furlongs are ways measured; and by ways are signified leading truths (n. 176), and in the opposite sense falsities: and by a thousand six hundred are signified evils in their whole aggregate. For by 1600 the same is signified as by 16, and the same by 16 as by 4, as 16 arises from 4 multiplied into itself: and four relates to good, and the conjunction of good and truth (n. 322); consequently, in the opposite sense, to evil and the conjunction of evil and falsity, as here. And as the multiplication of a number by 100 does not take away its signification, but exalts it, <note>Swedenborgian numerology suggests that numbers in the Bible have specific spiritual meanings; here, 1600 represents the total completion of evil, derived from the number four which usually relates to goodness or structure.</note>

It also interprets the number 1600 as a symbol for the total culmination of evil and falsehood.</summary>

I say this because I have noticed that you are skilled in <term>metaphysical art</term> <note>Abstract, philosophical reasoning. The speaker suggests this "art" is often used to complicate simple truths.</note>; an art we call ‘mystification’ and some call ‘incantation.’

Indeed, if you are willing to believe it, the difference is as vast as that between heaven and hell. That which is the **primary** forms the head and the breast, and that which follows from it forms the feet and their soles. But let us first agree on what charity is and what faith is: **charity** is the affection of the love of doing good to the neighbor for the sake of God, salvation, and eternal life...”

And the wise man of the city said, "Let it be so, that it is only for the sake of God." After this agreement the wise man of the city said, "Is not affection the primary <note>The "primary" refers to the most important element that must come first in sequence and priority.</note>? and is not thought derived from it?"

But he that was sent by the dragon <note>original: "draconigena"; a reference to the "dragon" in the Book of Revelation, symbolizing those who separate faith from a life of charity.</note> said, "This I deny."

But he received for answer, "You cannot deny it. Does not a man think from affection? Take away affection, and can you think any thing? It is altogether as if you should take away sound from speech. If you take away sound, can you speak any thing? Sound also is of the affection, and speech is of the thought; for the affection sounds, and the thought speaks. And it is also like flame and light. If you take away the flame, does not the light perish? It is the same with charity, because this is affection; and with faith, because this is thought. Can you not thus comprehend that the primary is the all in the secondary, altogether as the sound is in speech? From which you may see, that if you do not make that to be the primary which is the primary, you are not in the other. 

Wherefore, if you take faith, which is in the second place, and put it in the first, you will appear no otherwise in heaven than as a man inverted, whose feet stand upwards, and his head downwards; or like a mountebank <note>mountebank: A street performer or acrobat; here used to describe someone acting in a way that is contrary to the natural order of heaven.</note>, who, with his body upside down, walks upon the palms of his hands. When ye appear such in heaven, what then are your good works, which are charity, but such as that mountebank would do with his feet, because he cannot with his hands? Hence it is that your charity, as ye also have seen, is natural <term>natural: in this context, referring to actions done from the physical or worldly self rather than from a spiritual connection to God.</term>, and not spiritual, because it is inverted."

### THE SPIRITUAL SENSE

**THE CONTENTS OF THE WHOLE CHAPTER.** The preparation for disclosing the last state of the church, and for laying open the evils and falsities in which its members are (verses 1, 5-8): from whom those are separated who have confessed the Lord, and have lived according to His precepts (verses 2-4).

**THE CONTENTS OF EACH VERSE.** “And I saw another sign in heaven, great and marvellous,” *signifies* a revelation by the Lord concerning the state of the church on earth, what it is as to love and faith. “Seven angels having the seven last plagues,” *signifies* the evils and falsities in the church, such as they are in its last state, disclosed universally by the Lord. “For in them is consummated <note>The term "consummated" refers to a process being brought to its final completion; here it marks the point where the church has reached its absolute end before a new one can begin.</note> the anger of God,” *signifies* the devastation of the church, and then its end. “And I saw as it were a sea of glass mingled with fire,” *signifies* the farthest boundary of the spiritual world, where those were gathered together who had a religion, and worship from it, but not good of life. “And them that had the victory over the beast, and over his image, and over his mark, and over the number of his name,” *signifies* those who have rejected faith alone <note>The author is referring to the doctrine of "salvation by faith alone" without regard for one's actions or "charity," which he critiques throughout this work.</note> and the doctrine of it, and so have not acknowledged and imbibed its falsities, nor falsified the Word. “Standing by the sea of glass, having the harps of God,” *signifies* the Christian Heaven in the boundaries, and the faith of charity in those who were there. “And they were singing the song of Moses the servant of God, and the song of the Lamb,” *signifies* confession from charity, and thus from a life according to the precepts of the law, which is the Decalogue <note>The Ten Commandments.</note>, and from faith in the Divinity of the Lord's Human. “Saying, Great and marvellous are thy works, O Lord God Almighty,” *signifies* that all things of the world, of heaven, and of the church were created and made by the Lord from Divine Love by Divine Wisdom. “For just and true are

### THE EXPLANATION.

656. *And I saw another sign in heaven, great and marvellous,* signifies a revelation from the Lord concerning the state of the <term>church</term> <note>In this context, "church" refers to the internal spiritual condition of humanity, or the collective state of religious belief and practice on earth.</note> on earth, what it is as to love and faith. These are the things which are treated of in this chapter and the following, and therefore these are signified by the great and marvellous sign in heaven. That revelation from the Lord concerning heaven and concerning the church, and concerning their state, is signified by a sign in heaven, may be seen above (n. 532, 536). It is concerning love and faith, because it is called great and marvellous; and "great" in the <term>Word</term> <note>A term used here for the Sacred Scriptures or the Bible.</note> relates to such things as are of <term>affection</term> <note>The underlying emotional drive or desire of the heart, specifically toward good or evil.</note> and love, and "marvellous" to such as are of thought and faith.

657. *Seven angels having the seven last plagues,* signifies the evils and <term>falsities</term> <note>Spiritual errors or misconceptions that arise from a lack of true faith or an inclination toward evil.</note> in the church, such as they are in its last state, disclosed universally by the Lord. By the seven angels the universal heaven is signified. But as heaven is not heaven from the things belonging to the angels, but from the Lord, therefore by the seven angels the Lord is signified; nor can any one else disclose the evils and falsities that are in the church. That heaven is signified by angels, and in the highest sense the Lord, may be seen above (n. 5, 258, 344, 465, 644, 647, 648). By "plagues" are signified evils and falsities — evils of love and falsities of faith: for these are the things which are described in the following chapter, and are signified by the evil and noxious sore, by the blood as it were of one dead from which every living soul died, and by the blood into which the waters of the rivers and fountains were turned; by the heat of the fire that afflicted men; by the unclean spirits like frogs that were demons; also by the great hail. The evils and falsities which are signified by all these things are the plagues here; by the "last plagues" those in the last state of the church are meant.

<summary>This page provides a spiritual interpretation of the "sign in heaven" and the "seven angels with plagues" from Revelation 15, explaining them as divine revelations of the spiritual decay in the church's final state. It clarifies that "great" refers to the heart's love, while "marvellous" refers to the mind's faith.</summary>

<term>plagues</term> <note>original: "plagae" — While we usually think of plagues as biological diseases, the author uses the term here to describe the spiritual decay of the human soul.</note> (Ex. ix. 14 ; xi. 1). From this it is manifest, that by plagues nothing else is signified but spiritual plagues, which affect men as to their souls, and destroy them ; as also Isa. xxx. 26 ; Zech. xiv. 12, 15 ; Ps. xxxviii. 5, 11 ; Apoc. ix. 20 ; xvi. 21 ; Ex. xii. 13 ; xxx. 12 ; Num. xi. 33 ; Luke vii. 21 ; and elsewhere.

658. ***For in them is consummated the anger of God***, signifies the <term>devastation</term> <note>In this context, "devastation" refers to the process where a spiritual community loses its internal integrity and collapses.</note> of the church and then its end. By a <term>consummation</term> <note>A technical term meaning the "ending" or "final completion" of a specific era or state of the church.</note> the devastation of the church is signified, and then its end ; which is treated of in what follows. By the **anger of God** is signified evil in men, which, because it is against God, is called God's anger : not that God is angry with man ; but that man, from his own evil, is angry against God. Because it appears to the man—while he is punished and tormented for that evil in the <term>afterlife</term> <note>The author uses "hell after death" to describe the natural consequence of choosing a life governed by hatred rather than love.</note>—as if the punishment were from God, the Word attributes anger, fury, and even evil to God in its literal sense. This is because the <term>literal sense</term> is written based on appearances and **correspondences** <note>The "science of correspondences" is the author's central theory that everything in the physical world (and the literal text of the Bible) reflects a deeper spiritual reality.</note> : but this is not the case in the **spiritual sense** ; for in that sense there is no mere appearance, but only the truth in its own light. Concerning this anger, see above, n. 525, 635. 

It is said that the anger of God is consummated in those plagues, and that by this the devastation of the church and then its end are signified: the reason shall be told. Every church declines over time by moving away from the good of love and from the truths of faith, until nothing of them remains. This is caused by the gradual increase of evil and falsity. When there is no longer any love or faith, nothing remains but evil and falsity ; and when it reaches this point, the end of the church has come. At this end, a person no longer knows the difference: they believe evil is good and that falsity is truth, because they love these things and find enjoyment in them, and therefore convince themselves they are right. This is the end signified by "consummation," and it is called devastation in the following passages: *I have heard a consummation and decree from...*

**662.** *And they were singing the Song of Moses the servant of God and the Song of the Lamb*, signifies a confession <note>In this context, "confession" refers to an open acknowledgment or profession of faith and heart-felt conviction.</note> arising from charity—and thus from a life lived according to the precepts of the Law, which is the **Decalogue** <note>The Ten Commandments.</note>—and from faith in the Divinity of the Lord's Human. To sing a "new song" is to acknowledge from a joy of heart and from deep affection that the Lord alone is the Savior, Redeemer, and the God of heaven and earth, as may be seen above (n. 279, 617) <note>These numbers refer to previous sections in Swedenborg's work.</note>. However, in this instance, it is not called a "new song," but the *song of Moses the servant of God* and the *song of the Lamb*. 

By the **song of Moses** is signified a confession coming from a life lived according to the precepts of the Law (the Decalogue), which constitutes charity. By the **song of the Lamb** is signified a confession coming from faith in the Divinity of the <term>Lord's Human</term> <note>original: "Divinum Humanum." A central concept in Swedenborg's theology, referring to the belief that Jesus Christ’s human nature became fully divine, allowing God to be present with humanity.</note>; for the Lord, in terms of His Divine Human, is meant by the "Lamb" (n. 269, 291, 595). 

In a broad sense, **Moses** represents all the Law written in his five books <note>The Pentateuch: Genesis, Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, and Deuteronomy.</note>, but in a specific sense, he represents the Law called the Decalogue. Because this Law serves as a guide for a person’s life, the text says, "the song of Moses *the servant of God*"; for in the Word <note>The Holy Scriptures.</note>, a "servant" signifies that which is useful or serviceable (n. 380)—in this case, serviceable for leading a good life. 

The reason that "Moses" refers to the Law in a general sense is that his five books are collectively called the Law. That all the commands, judgments, and statutes given by him are called the Law may be seen above (n. 417). That everything written in those books is referred to as "the Law of Moses," or simply "Moses," is evident from these passages: 

*Philip said, We have found Jesus, of whom Moses in the Law, and the Prophets, did write (John 1:45).* 

*In the Law Moses commanded that such should be stoned (John 8:5).* 

*The days of their purification, according to the Law of Moses, were fulfilled (Luke 2:22).* 

*All things must be fulfilled which are written in the Law of Moses and in the*

### 665. **Who shall not fear thee, O Lord, and glorify thy name,**
signifies that He alone is to be loved and worshipped. By fearing God is signified to love Him; and by glorifying His name is signified to worship Him. That He alone is to be loved and worshipped is meant by "who shall not," and by "thou alone art Holy." That to fear God is to love Him by fearing to do contrary to Him, and that this fear is in all love, may be seen above (<term>n. 527, 628</term> <note>These numbers refer to earlier sections of this commentary where the author defines "holy fear" as the desire of those who love God not to harm the relationship.</note>). To glorify His name is to worship Him, because by the name of **Jehovah** <note>original: "Jehovah" — the Hebrew name for God, representing His divine essence.</note> is signified every thing by which He is worshipped (n. 81); and by glorifying is signified to acknowledge and confess.

### 666. **For thou alone art Holy,**
signifies that He is the Word, the Truth, and Enlightenment. That the Lord is the Only Holy One, may be seen above (n. 173); and that the Divine Truth is what is called holy (n. 173, 580): and because the Word is the Divine Truth, and the Lord is the Word; and as the Divine Truth enlightens spiritually, for it is the light in heaven, but from the Lord; therefore by "thou alone art Holy," is signified that the Lord is the Word, the Truth, and Enlightenment. 

Since the Word is Divine Truth, and the Divine Truth enlightens spiritually, it is therefore said that the Word was dictated of **Jehovah** by the **Holy Spirit**, and that the Holy Spirit enlightens and teaches man. But who does not know that God is **omnipresent** <note>Present everywhere at the same time.</note>, and that what is Holy proceeds from Him, and that it enlightens where it is received. Who cannot conclude from this, that the **Holy Spirit** is not a God by itself, distinct from Jehovah or the Lord, as a person from a person; but that it is Jehovah Himself or the Lord? 1. And I heard a great voice out of the temple, saying to the seven angels, Go and pour out the **vials** <term>vials</term> <note>Also translated as "bowls." 2. 3. 4. And the third angel poured out his vial upon the rivers and upon the fountains of waters; and they became blood.

5. And I heard the angel of the waters say, Thou art just, O Lord, who art, and who wast, and art Holy, <note>original: "qui es, et qui eras, et sanctus" — a declaration of the Lord's eternity and the justice of His divine order.</note> because thou hast judged these things.

7. And I heard another out of the altar saying, Yea, Lord God Almighty, true and just are thy judgments.

8. And the fourth angel poured out his vial upon the sun; and it was given him to scorch men with fire. <note>The "sun" here represents divine love, but when it flows into those who are in evil, it is perceived as a "scorching heat" of lust or anger.</note>

9. 10. And the fifth angel poured out his vial upon the throne of the beast; and his kingdom became dark, and they gnawed their tongues for distress.

11. And they blasphemed the God of heaven for their pains and for their sores, and repented not of their works.

### THE SPIRITUAL SENSE.

**THE CONTENTS OF THE WHOLE CHAPTER.** In this chapter, the evils and falsities <note>In this theological context, "falsities" are not just mistakes, but systemic false beliefs that distort spiritual truth.</note> in the church of the Reformed <note>The "Reformed" refers to the Protestant denominations that emerged from the Reformation, particularly those following the doctrines of Luther or Calvin.</note> are disclosed by influx <note>original: "influxus." This refers to the spiritual process where influence or light flows from the divine realm into the human mind or the church structure.</note> out of heaven (verse 1). Into the clergy (verse 2): Into the laity <note>The "laity" refers to the general congregation, as distinguished from the ordained clergy.</note> (verse 3): Into their understanding of the Word <note>The "Word" is the technical term for the Sacred Scriptures or the Bible.</note> (verses 4, 5, 6, 7): Into their love (verses 8, 9): Into their faith (verses 10, 11): Into their interior reasonings (verses 12, 13, 14, 15): Into all things of them together (verses 17-21).

**THE CONTENTS OF EACH VERSE.** "And I heard a great voice out of the temple, saying to the seven angels, Go, and pour out the vials of the anger of God upon the earth," *signifies* influx from the Lord from the inmost of heaven into the church of the Reformed, where are they who are in faith separated from charity <note>This is a central critique in this work: the idea that one can be saved by "faith alone" without living a life of active love and good works (charity).</note> as to doctrine and as to life. "And the first went forth, and poured out his vial upon the earth," *signifies* into those who are in the interiors of the church of the Reformed, and study the doctrine of justification by faith alone, and are called the clergy. "And there came an evil and noxious sore," *signifies* interior evils and falsities destructive of all good and truth in the church. "Upon the men that had the mark of the beast, and that worshipped his image," *signifies* in those who live faith alone and receive the doctrine of it. "And the second angel poured out his vial upon the sea," *signifies* influx among those there who are in its externals, and in that faith, and are called the laity. "And it became blood as of one dead, and every living soul died in the sea," *signifies* infernal falsity with them, by which every truth of the Word and thence of the church and of faith was extinguished. "And the third angel poured out his vial upon the rivers and upon the fountains of waters," *signifies* influx into the understanding of the Word with them. "And they became blood," *signifies* the truths of the Word falsified— <note>The text terminates mid-sentence; the full thought concludes on the following page regarding the falsification of scripture.</note>

### THE EXPLANATION.

**676.** *And I heard a great voice out of the temple, saying to the seven angels, Go and pour out the vials of the anger of God upon the earth,* signifies <term>influx</term><note>The process of spiritual influence or energy flowing from the Divine into the human world or the church.</note> from the Lord from the inmost of heaven into the church of the <term>Reformed</term><note>A term used here to describe the Protestant churches resulting from the Reformation.</note>, where are they who are in <term>faith separated from charity</term><note>A central critique in this work, referring to the belief that salvation comes through intellectual belief (faith) alone, without the necessity of a life of active love and good deeds (charity).</note> as to doctrine and as to life, to take away truths and goods from them, and to open the falsities and evils in which they are, and thus to separate them from those who believe in the Lord, and from Him are in charity and its faith. These in a summary are the things which are contained in this chapter.

By the temple is signified the temple of the tabernacle of the testimony, spoken of in the preceding chapter, xv. 5; by which the inmost of heaven is signified, where the Lord is in His holiness in the Word, and in the law which is the <term>Decalogue</term><note>original: "Decalogus"; The Ten Commandments, viewed here as the fundamental law of spiritual and civil life.</note> (n. 669). By a great voice thence is signified the Divine command, that they should go and pour out the vials. By the seven angels the Lord is meant, as above (n. 657). By pouring out the vials, in which were the plagues, upon the earth, is signified an influx into the church of the Reformed: by pouring out the vials is signified influx, and by the earth the church is signified (n. 285).

The church with the Reformed is still treated of; but in the following chapter the church among the Roman Catholics, and afterwards the last judgment, and at length the <term>New Church</term><note>A reference to a new spiritual age or community, symbolized by the New Jerusalem.</note>, which is the <term>New Jerusalem</term><note>original: "Nova Hierosolyma"; A symbolic city representing a new state of the church characterized by direct love for the Lord and mutual charity.</note>, are treated of (see the *Preface* and n. 2.) Chapters viii. and ix., above, treat of the seven angels that had the seven trumpets with which they sounded; and as many similar things occur there, it shall here be told what is signified by those seven angels, and what by these. By the seven trumpets with which the seven angels sounded, is signified exploration and manifestation of the falsities and evils in which they are who are in faith separated from charity;

When this is done, they enter into their evils and falsities, and are separated from the good. These are the things which are described and signified in this chapter by the casting forth of the vials in which were the seven last plagues. 

In the vials there were not those evils and falsities which are signified by the plagues, but there were genuine truths and goods, whose effect was such as is described. For the angels went out of the <term>temple of the tabernacle of the testimony</term><note>The most holy part of the spiritual world, representing the direct presence of the Divine Law or the Ten Commandments.</note>, by which is meant the inmost of heaven, where there are nothing but truths and goods in Divine holiness (chap. xv. 6). 677. **And the first went forth, and poured out his vial upon the earth**, signifies an <term>influx</term><note>The spiritual flow of life and truth from God into the human mind.</note> into those who dwell in the inner workings of the <term>Reformed</term><note>Protestant churches that emerged from the Reformation.</note> church and study the doctrine of <term>justification by faith alone</term><note>The teaching that a person is made right with God by belief alone, regardless of their actions or "works."</note>; these individuals are called the **clergy**. In this specific context, it refers to those within the church who are in its "interiors"—those who study the doctrine of justification by faith alone. These people claim to understand the deep, inner mysteries of this doctrine. However, these "interiors" are actually just various arguments used to confirm one single position: that faith alone saves without the works of the law. They know no other inner truths. Because this group consists mainly of priests, professors of theology, and seminary lecturers—in short, the teachers and pastors—this first influx was directed into them, the ones called the **clergy**. We know they are the ones meant here because the text says the first angel poured his vial upon the **earth** and the second upon the **sea**. Here, "earth" signifies the church among those who are in its internal or intellectual leadership, while "sea" signifies the church among those who are in its external or general membership, as established elsewhere (n. 398, 403, 404, 420, 470). It is also clear they are meant because the text says a "sore" came upon them.

678. **And there came an evil and noxious sore**, signifies internal evils and false ideas that are destructive to all goodness and truth within the church. This is because the sore came "upon the men that had the <term>mark of the beast</term><note>A symbol for the outward acknowledgment and lived reality of a false belief system.</note> and worshipped his image," which signifies that specific faith and the lifestyle it produces. internal evils and <term>falsities</term><note>In this context, a "falsity" is not just a mistake, but a truth that has been intentionally distorted to justify wrong behavior.</note> that destroy all goodness and truth within the church. The word **noxious** signifies "destructive," as evil inevitably destroys good, just as falsehood destroys truth. A **sore** symbolizes these things because physical sores on the body are the result of a diseased state of the blood or some other internal infection. The same principle applies to "sores" in a spiritual sense: these arise from hidden <term>lusts</term><note>Original Latin: *concupiscentiae*. These are the deep-seated, driving desires or cravings of the will that lead a person toward selfish ends.</note> and the pleasures found in them; these are the internal causes. The evil itself, which is represented by a sore and appears as something "enjoyable" in a person’s outward behavior, actually hides the underlying cravings that created it.

It should be well understood that the inner parts of the human mind exist in both **successive order** and **simultaneous order**. They exist in **successive order** when they move from the higher (prior) levels down to the lower (later) levels. However, they exist in **simultaneous order** in the <term>ultimates</term><note>The "ultimates" are the final, most outward expressions of a person—their actual words and deeds where their inner thoughts and feelings finally come to rest and take shape.</note>, or the most outward things. In these outward things, the inner levels exist from the center to the edges. This concept has been fully explained in the work *Angelic Wisdom concerning the Divine Love and Divine Wisdom* (sections 173–281), which discusses the "degrees" of reality; from that work, it is clear that the final, outward act is actually the sum total of everything that led up to it.

It follows, then, that all of a person's evil cravings exist together at once (in simultaneous order) within the specific evil act that the person perceives in themselves. Every evil that a person notices in their own life is in these "ultimates." Therefore, when a person rejects an evil action, they are also rejecting the cravings for it at the same time—though they cannot do this by their own power, but only through the Lord. A person can indeed stop an outward evil act on their own, but they cannot remove the inner *craving* for it. For this reason, when a person wants to reject evil by fighting against it, they must look to the Lord; for the Lord works from the innermost parts of a person out to the most outward parts, entering through the soul to purify the whole being.

These points have been made to show that a **sore** signifies evil that appears in the "ultimates" or most outward life, which has grown out of an internal infection. This is the state of all who convince themselves that **faith alone** saves, and...

Since truths are a matter of faith, the "soul" signifies the truth of faith. This meaning is evident from many passages in the <term>Word</term><note>The "Word" is the term used by Swedenborg to refer to the Sacred Scriptures or the Bible, emphasizing its role as Divine Truth.</note>, especially where "soul" and "heart" appear together. It is clear that "soul" and "heart" refer to a person's life; however, that life stems from two sources: the **will** and the **understanding**. Speaking in spiritual terms, life comes from **love** and **wisdom**, or **charity** and **faith**. 

The life of the will—which comes from the "good" of love or charity—is meant by the **heart**. The life of the understanding—which comes from the "truths" of wisdom or faith—is meant by the **soul**. This distinction is intended in passages such as Matthew 22:37; Mark 12:30, 33; Luke 10:27; Deuteronomy 6:5, 10:12, 11:13, 26:16; Jeremiah 32:41, and others, as well as in places where the heart or soul is mentioned alone. The reason they are named this way is due to <term>correspondence</term><note>Correspondence is the spiritual law that physical things in the world or the body represent specific spiritual realities.</note>: the heart corresponds to the will and love, while the breathing of the lungs corresponds to the understanding and wisdom. This relationship is explored in the work *Angelic Wisdom concerning the Divine Love and Divine Wisdom* <note>original: "Sapientia Angelica de Divino Amore et de Divina Sapientia"</note>, Part V.

683. ***And the third angel poured out his vial upon the rivers and fountains of waters,*** signifies <term>influx</term><note>A spiritual "flowing in" of divine energy or truth from the Lord into the human mind.</note> into the understanding of the Word among them. The third angel pouring out his vial signifies—just like the previous angels—an influx from the Lord of truth and good. In this specific case, it is an influx into the understanding of the Word. This is because **rivers** signify truths in abundance that serve the rational mind (and thus the understanding) for the sake of doctrine and life (n. 409). A **fountain of waters** signifies the Lord in His role as the Word, and therefore the Word itself; consequently, "fountains of waters" signify the Divine truths that come from the Word (n. 384, 409).

684. ***And they became blood,*** signifies the truths of the Word <term>falsified</term><note>In this context, to "falsify" means to twist or misinterpret the truths of the Bible to fit a wrong belief system, such as "faith alone" without a life of good actions.</note>. In a positive sense, "blood" signifies Divine Truth, but in the opposite sense, it signifies that same truth when it has been corrupted or falsified, as seen previously (n. 379).

<term>Divine Truth</term><note>In Swedenborg's writings, Divine Truth is the spiritual light that flows from God, providing wisdom and order to the universe.</note> itself (numbers 173, 586, 666). It is manifest from these things, that by "*Thou art just, O Lord, who art and who wast, and art Holy, because thou hast judged these things,*" is signified that this is from the **Divine Providence** of the Lord, who is and was the Word and the Divine Truth itself. That it is of the Lord's **Divine Providence**, that they who are in **faith alone** should falsify the truths of the Word, is because if they knew them, so as to think them interiorly, they would <term>profane</term><note>To "profane" something holy is to acknowledge its truth but then live in direct opposition to it, which Swedenborg considers a devastating spiritual state.</note> them; for they are in evils, because they do not shun evils as sins, nor approach the Lord immediately: on which account, if they were to receive the genuine truths of the Word, they would mix them up with the evils of their life; whence would arise the profanation of what is holy. It is therefore among the **laws of permission**, which are also laws of the **Divine Providence**, that they should of themselves falsify the truths, and so far as they are in evils of life. That it is the **Divine Providence** that they who are in evils of life should be in nothing but falsities of doctrine, to the end that they may not profane the Divine Truths of the Word, may be seen in the *Angelic Wisdom concerning the Divine Providence* (numbers 221–233, and 257 at the end).

687. *For the blood of saints and prophets have they poured out*, signifies that this is for the reason that that single point, that **faith alone** without the works of the law saves, being received, perverts all true <term>doctrinals</term><note>Doctrinals are the systematic teachings or formal principles of the church derived from the Bible.</note> from the Word. By **shedding blood** is signified here as above (number 684), to falsify the truths of the Word, thus to pervert them. By **saints** are signified those in the church who are in truths, and thus also abstractly the truths of the church (number 586). By **prophets** are signified they who are in doctrinals from the Word, thus also abstractly doctrinals from the Word (number 133).

alone both in doctrine and in life, to <term>falsify</term><note>To "falsify" the Word, in Swedenborg's view, is to twist the meaning of Scripture to support one's own selfish desires or incorrect theological ideas.</note> the truths of **the Word**<note>Swedenborg uses the term "the Word" to refer to the Sacred Scriptures or the Bible, which he believes contains a deep spiritual meaning beneath the literal text.</note>, and to imbue their life with them so falsified. 689. *And I heard another out of the altar say, Yea, Lord God Almighty, true and just are thy judgments,* signifies the **Divine Good** of **the Word** confirming that **Divine Truth**. By *another*, that is, another angel, the **Divine Good** of **the Word** is signified. By an angel something Divine from the Lord is signified (n. 415, 631, 633): and by an angel out of the altar is signified the **Divine Good** of love (n. 648); here the **Divine Good** of **the Word**, because **the Word** is still treated of; and because the **Divine Truth** of **the Word** is signified by the **angel of the waters** (n. 685). Now as the **Divine Good** of **the Word** and the **Divine Truth** of **the Word** make one, similar things are therefore signified by the things spoken by the **angel of the waters** and those by the angel out of the altar: for the **angel of the waters** said, “Thou art just, O Lord, who art and who wast, and art Holy, because thou hast judged these things;” the angel from the altar, “Yea, Lord God Almighty, true and just are thy judgments.” The latter and the former signify similar things, only with the difference, that the one spoke from truth, and the other from good; and that the one confirmed what the other spoke, though by different words; the one by words which belong to the class of truth, and the other by words that belong to the class of good: for there is a <term>marriage of truth and good</term><note>A central concept in Swedenborgian thought, suggesting that every part of the Bible and the universe contains a balance of "Truth" (related to the intellect) and "Good" (related to the will or love).</note> in every thing of **the Word** (n. 97); and there are words of good and words of truth, which appear different, but still involve similar things.

690. *And the fourth angel poured out his vial upon the sun*, signifies <term>influx</term><note>A spiritual "flowing in." In Swedenborg’s view, all human thought and affection are the result of spiritual influences flowing from the Divine or from spiritual realms into the mind.</note> into their love. By pouring out the <term>vial</term><note>Also translated as "bowl," representing the manifestation of Divine truth being applied to a specific state of the church.</note> is signified here, as before, influx from goods and truths—in this case, into their love. This is because the **sun** signifies the **Divine Love** of the Lord, but in the opposite sense, it signifies the **love of self** (n. 53, 382, 414); here it refers to the love of self, because it follows in the text that men were afflicted with heat by the fire, and were scorched with a great heat; by which the <term>lusts</term><note>Selfish or harmful desires and cravings that oppose spiritual goodness.</note> of that love are signified.

691. *And it was given him to scorch men with fire*, signifies that love to the Lord tortured them, because they were in the lusts of evils from the enjoyment of their love. Since by pouring out the vial is signified influx from the Lord from goods and truths, hence by pouring out the vial upon the sun is signified influx from the Lord from the **Divine Love**, to disclose what kind of love there was with the men of that church. From this, by the angel being "given to scorch men with fire," it is signified that the Lord's Divine Love tortured them. As the Lord's Divine Love tortures no others but those who are in the lusts of evil from the enjoyment of the love of self, it follows that this "scorching" signifies that love to the Lord was felt as torture by them because they were immersed in the pleasures of their own selfish desires. That **heat** signifies lusts for evils and the resulting falsities may be seen above (n. 382); and that **fire** signifies the Divine Love, or in the opposite sense, hellish love, see above (n. 494). That the love of self is hellish love, and its enjoyment is a hellish enjoyment consisting of innumerable lusts for evils, has been shown extensively in the works *Angelic Wisdom concerning the Divine Providence* and *Angelic Wisdom concerning the Divine Love and Divine Wisdom*<note>original titles: "Sapientia Angelica de Divina Providentia" and "Sapientia Angelica de Divino Amore et de Divina Sapientia."</note>. This fact is not known in the Christian world because it is not known what true love to the Lord is; yet it is this love that teaches the true nature of the love of self.

<summary>This page explains that the "sun" in Revelation 16:8 represents self-love when turned away from God, and that the "fire" of Divine Love acts as a source of torment to those who are consumed by their own selfish lusts.</summary>

692. ***And men were scorched with great heat, and blasphemed the name of God who hath power over these plagues***, signifies that on account of the enjoyment of the **love of self** arising from grievous <term>lusts</term><note>In this context, "lusts" refer to intense, compulsive desires for things that are spiritually or morally harmful.</note> of evils, they did not acknowledge the Divinity of the <term>Lord’s Human</term><note>A central concept in Swedenborg’s theology: the belief that Jesus Christ made his human nature entirely Divine, and that God is visible and approachable in this Divine Humanity.</note>, from which nevertheless flows all good of love and truth of faith. By **blaspheming the name of God** is signified to deny or not to acknowledge the Divinity of the Lord’s Human, and the holiness of the **Word** (n. 571, 582): to blaspheme is to deny or not to acknowledge; and the **name of God** is the Lord’s Divine Human and at the same time the **Word**<note>The "Word" refers to the Sacred Scripture or the Bible, viewed as Divine Truth itself.</note> (n. 584).

It shall be told in few words what the quality of the **love of self** is. The enjoyment of it exceeds every enjoyment in the world; for it is made up of mere lusts of evils, and every lust breathes out its own enjoyment. Into this enjoyment every man is born; and as it drives the mind of man to think continually of himself, it draws it away from thinking of God and the neighbor—except when thinking from himself and concerning himself. On which account, unless God favors his lusts, he is angry with God, just as he is angry with his neighbor who does not favor him. That enjoyment, when...

*until the thrones were cast down, and the Ancient of Days did sit (Daniel 7:9). I will overturn the throne of kingdoms, and the strength of the kingdoms of the nations (Haggai 2:22). Lucifer said, Above the stars will I exalt my throne (Isaiah 14:13; and elsewhere).*

695. ***And his kingdom became dark***, signifies that nothing but falsities appeared. **Falsities** are signified by **darkness**, because truth is signified by **light**. That darkness signifies falsities by which come evils, and thick-darkness signifies falsities from evils, may be seen above (n. 413); hence by the kingdom of the beast being made dark, it is signified that nothing but falsities appeared. That those who have confirmed <term>faith separated from charity</term><note>The theological position that belief alone is sufficient for salvation, without the need for good works or moral living.</note> falsify the whole **Word**, may be seen above (n. 136, 610): and that they do not possess any truths (n. 489, 501, 653); but mere falsities (n. 563, 597, 602). 

But in their own sight, the falsities of their faith do not indeed appear dark—that is, as false—but lucid—that is, as true—after they have confirmed them. However, when they are viewed from the light of heaven, which discloses all things, they appear dark. For this reason, when the light of heaven flows into the chambers of those who are in hell, it becomes so dark that they cannot see one another; therefore, all hell is closed, so that not even a chink is open; and then they are in their own <term>light</term><note>original: "lumen". Swedenborg distinguishes between "lux" (spiritual light from the Lord) and "lumen" (natural light, which in the case of hell is a deceptive or "fatuous" light based on the ego).</note>. 

That they do not appear to themselves to be in darkness, but in light, although they are in falsities, is because their falsities appear to them as truths once they have confirmed them; this is the source of their light. But it is a fatuous or deceptive light, such as the light that comes from justifying a lie. This light corresponds to the eyesight of **owls and bats**, to which darkness is light, and light is darkness; indeed, to them the sun is nothing but thick darkness. Such eyes do they have after death—those who have confirmed themselves in falsities in the world to such a degree that they see falsity as truth, and the truth as falsity.

697. ***And blasphemed the God of heaven for their distresses and for their sores***, signifies that they could not acknowledge the Lord alone to be God of heaven and earth, on account of resistance from interior <term>falsities</term><note>In this context, 'falsities' refer to incorrect religious beliefs that have been deeply internalized.</note> and evils, arising from the acknowledgment and reception of the <term>dogma concerning faith alone</term><note>The theological view that salvation is granted through belief alone, without the necessity of good works or moral behavior.</note>. 698. ***And they did not repent of their works***, signifies that even though they are instructed by the Word <note>Swedenborg uses the term "the Word" to refer specifically to the Sacred Scriptures or the Bible.</note>, they still do not turn away from the <term>falsities</term><note>A technical term in Swedenborg’s writing referring to incorrect religious doctrines or distorted truths that lead a person away from a good life.</note> of their faith and the resulting evils in their lives. By "not repenting" is signified not turning away from these things, as mentioned above (no. 693); and by "works" are signified the false beliefs of their faith and the evil actions they produce (no. 641). According to the literal sense of the text, it appears that pain and suffering cannot force people to repent for their mistakes. However, according to the spiritual sense, this means that even instruction from the Bible cannot drive them away from these false beliefs and evils because these things are "infernal"—meaning they are rooted in a hellish nature. Therefore, when it says they did not repent of their works, it means that despite being shown the truth in the Word, they refuse to abandon their false doctrines and the bad lives they lead because of them. It is framed this way because a false belief usually comes first, and a bad life follows; for example, it is a false belief that "evil does not condemn a person who has faith." Because of this idea, a person might live without concern, never thinking about their own faults and therefore never truly repenting. The same thing happens if a person convinces themselves that good actions contribute nothing to salvation, and that "faith alone" is enough.

699. ***And the sixth angel poured out his vial upon the great river Euphrates***, signifies an <term>influx</term><note>The process of spiritual life or influence flowing from the Lord into the human mind.</note> from the Lord into their inner reasonings, through which they try to justify the idea of "salvation by faith alone." The "sixth angel pouring out his vial" signifies this divine influence. The "great river Euphrates" represents these inner reasonings (no. 444, 445). In this specific case, it refers to the deep-seated arguments within the church used to defend the doctrine of justification by faith alone, which is what the following verses describe.

700. ***And its water was dried up, so that the way of the kings from the rising of the sun might be prepared***, signifies that the false arguments of those reasonings were removed for those who live in truths and goodness from the Lord, and who are to be introduced into the New Church. That the "water" <note>In Swedenborg’s symbolic language, "water" often represents truths, but when a river is "dried up," it signifies the removal of the "waters" of false reasoning.</note>...

...was dried up signifies that the <term>falsities</term> <note>In this context, "falsities" refers to incorrect religious doctrines or distorted logic that leads people away from spiritual truth.</note> of those interior reasonings were removed: by being "dried up" is signified that they were removed; and by the "water" is signified truths, and in the opposite sense, falsities (no. 50, 614); here it refers to the falsities of interior reasonings, because it was the water of the river Euphrates, which symbolizes those very reasonings (no. 699). By the rising of the <unclear>sun</unclear> is signified <unclear>the</unclear> beginning of the <term>New Church</term> <note>Swedenborg used the term "New Church" to describe a new spiritual era or a new understanding of Christianity that he believed was beginning in his time.</note> from the <unclear>Lord</unclear>, which is the same as what is meant by "the morning" (no. 151). By "preparing the way" is signified to prepare for introduction. 

From these things it is manifest, that by the water being dried up so that the way of the kings from the rising of the sun might be prepared, is signified that the falsities of the interior reasonings were removed for those who are in truths from good from the Lord, and who are to be introduced into the New Church. This is the progression of these spiritual events. 

The consummation or end of the present church, and the institution or beginning of a New Church, along with their conflicts, are treated of here. Those of the present church who focus on "faith alone" <note>A theological position that suggests salvation is achieved through belief alone, without the necessity of good works or a moral life.</note> are represented by the **dragon**, the **beast**, and the **false prophet**, which will be discussed in the following sections; their conflicts with those who will belong to the New Church are signified by the "gathering together of the kings of the earth to the battle." 

However, those who will be part of the New Church—the ones they will contend with—are represented by those for whom the water of the river Euphrates was dried up, so that a way might be prepared for the "kings from the rising of the sun." This carries a similar meaning to the introduction of the children of Israel into the land of Canaan, with the difference being that for the Israelites, the river Jordan was dried up, but for these people, it is the river Euphrates. The reason the river Euphrates is mentioned here is that, in this case, the conflict involves interior reasonings; these must be "dried up"—that is, removed—before a person can be introduced into the church. The false prophet has not before been mentioned, but the beast from the earth is now so called, see above (no. 594). The reason that the frogs were produced from the waters of Egypt, and remained in the river, was that the waters in Egypt—and especially the waters of its river, the Nile—signified the false doctrines from which they constructed their reasonings.

**703.** ***For they are the spirits of demons***, signifies that they were the lusts of distorting truths and of reasoning from falsities. By "the kings of the earth and of the whole world" are signified those who are primarily in falsities stemming from evil—here meaning all who hold these same falsities throughout the entire church. This is because "kings" signify those who are in truths derived from good, or, in the opposite sense, those who are in falsities derived from evil (no. 483). By "the earth" the church is signified (no. 285), and the "world" signifies the same (no. 551). *Alas, the great day of Jehovah, and there shall not be like it* (Jeremiah 30:7).

*They shall not stand in the battle of the day of Jehovah* (Ezekiel 13:5).

**707.** *And he gathered them together into a place called in Hebrew Armageddon*, signifies the state of combat from falsities <note>In this context, "falsities" refers to incorrect religious doctrines or untruths that oppose spiritual reality.</note> against truths, and the purpose of destroying the **New Church** <note>The author uses "New Church" to describe a new era of spiritual understanding and internal worship.</note>, arising from the love of dominion and superiority. By gathering together into a place—in this instance, for battle—is signified the act of inciting them to fight using falsities against truths. It represents a state of combat because "place" signifies the specific state of a matter. The reason it is for the purpose of destroying the **New Church** is that a conflict between the **Old Church** and the **New** is intended here, and the goal of such combat is destruction. The specific meaning of **Armageddon** will be explained further below. 

It has been stated previously that *the Dragon went away to make war with the rest of the seed of the Woman, that keep the commandments of God, and that have the testimony of Jesus Christ* (Apoc. xii. 17); also, that *it was given to the beast out of the sea to make war with the saints* (xiii. 7); and in this chapter that *the spirits of demons that came out of the mouth of the dragon, of the beast, and of the false prophet, went away to the kings of the earth, to gather them together to the war of that great day of God Almighty* (verses 13, 14). <note>The "Dragon," "Beast," and "False Prophet" are symbolic figures representing different forms of corrupted belief and worldly power that oppose genuine spiritual life.</note> 

Here, the battle itself is now addressed. The outcome is not described at this point, but only the state of the battle, which is signified by **Armageddon**. In heaven, **Armageddon** signifies the love of honor, of dominion, and of superiority. Furthermore, in the Hebrew language, "loftiness" is signified by the words *Aram* or *Arom*, and "love from loftiness" is signified by *Megiddo* in the ancient Hebrew tongue, as is evident from its meaning in the Arabic language. <note>The author frequently uses linguistic roots to uncover what he believes are the "spiritual correspondences" or deeper meanings of biblical names.</note> 

The same meaning is conveyed by **Hadadrimmon** in the valley of **Megiddo** in Zechariah xii. 11. In that chapter, the coming of the **Lord** is also discussed, along with the end of the **Jewish Church** at that time, and the beginning of a **New Church** to be established by the **Lord**, as well as the collision between those Churches. For this reason, the expression *in that day* occurs frequently in that chapter; and by "that day" is signified the **Lord's Coming**, as mentioned previously (n. 704). <note>The "n. 704" refers to a specific numbered section in the author's larger theological work for cross-reference.</note> This is done so that it may be seen,

Experience teaches this: for evils are enjoyments, because they are loves; and no one wishes to recede from enjoyments, unless he looks to the life after death, and first to hell to see what it is, and afterwards to heaven, what that is, and thinks of them aside from any evil act. If he then looks to the Lord also, and thinks, “What is the temporal in comparison with the eternal? is it not as nothing?” he can then reflect upon his evils, and wish to know them, and to recede from them. 

But if he had confirmed himself in **faith alone**, he will then say in his heart, “Our theological faith—that God the Father has mercy for the sake of the Son who suffered for our sins, if I supplicate this with some confidence—effects all things;” he then does not reflect upon any evil in himself: he also says with himself from that faith, that evil does not condemn, and that salvation is pure mercy, besides other similar things: he thus remains

*   *Concerning Heaven and Hell*

*   *Concerning the Last Judgment*
*   *Concerning the White Horse*

These small works were presented to all the bishops and to many of the nobles or lords. The bishops said that they received them and saw them, but did not think them valuable—although they admitted they were skillfully written. These things have been revealed by the Lord for those who will belong to His **New Church**, which is the **New Jerusalem** <note>The "New Jerusalem" refers to the new spiritual era or community described in the closing chapters of the Book of Revelation.</note>."

Because of this, they all stick together like a single bundle. They were treated so poorly that they were not even considered worthy of being listed in their library catalogs.

**...upon a scarlet beast, full of names of blasphemy,** signifies that this Religion is founded upon the <term>Word</term> <note>The Word: Referring to the Sacred Scriptures or the Bible.</note> which they have profaned. By **scarlet** is signified the truth of the Word from a heavenly origin <note>original: "coelestis" (celestial). In Swedenborg's writing, "celestial" refers to the highest level of heaven, characterized by love rather than just intellectual understanding.</note>. That the **scarlet beast** signifies the Word in terms of its Heavenly Divine Truth may at first seem remote, strange, or even absurd, because it is called a "beast." However, in a spiritual sense, a "beast" signifies natural affection <note>Natural affection: The basic emotional or instinctive drive in a person or a religious system.</note>. This term is applied to the Word, to the church, and to man, as seen previously (in sections 239, 405, 567).

Recall that the four animals in Ezekiel—one a lion, another a calf, and the fourth an eagle—signify the Word, and they are also called "beasts" in that prophecy (see sections 239, 275, 286, 672). Furthermore, a **horse**, which is also a beast, signifies the understanding of the Word (see section 298). It is well known that a **lamb** signifies the Lord, a **sheep** signifies a person of the church, and a **flock** signifies the church itself. These examples are provided so that no one should wonder why the Word is signified by the **scarlet beast**. 

Because the Roman Catholic Religion bases its strength and dignity upon the Word, the "Woman" was seen sitting upon a scarlet beast, just as she was previously seen sitting "upon many waters" (verse 1), which signifies the truths of the Word being adulterated and profaned (see section 719). That the Word is signified by this beast is clearly evident from what is said later in this chapter:

> *The beast which thou sawest was and is not; and they that dwell upon the earth shall wonder when they behold the beast which was and is not, but yet is.* (Verse 8)
>
> *The beast which was and is not, is itself the eighth king, and is of the seven, and goeth into perdition.* (Verse 11)
>
> *That the ten horns are ten kings, who shall give their power and authority to the beast.* (Verses 12 and 13)
>
> *God hath put into their hearts to give their kingdom unto the beast.* (Verse 17)

Such descriptions can be applied to nothing except the Word.

...scarlet, and of gold, precious stones, and pearls, upon a harlot holding a golden cup in her hand, full of abominations and filthiness of whoredom. Since "**purple and scarlet**" are mentioned, and then "**gold, precious stones, and pearls**," and by purple and scarlet <term>Heavenly Divine Good and Truth</term> <note>In this context, "Good" refers to the essence of love, and "Truth" refers to the essence of wisdom.</note> are signified, and by gold and precious stones <term>Spiritual Divine Good and Truth</term>, both from the <term>Word</term> <note>The "Word" refers to the Sacred Scriptures or the Bible.</note>, something shall therefore be said concerning the Heavenly Divine and concerning the Spiritual Divine. 

There are two kingdoms into which the whole heaven of the Lord is distinguished, the **Heavenly Kingdom** and the **Spiritual Kingdom**. The heavenly kingdom consists of angels who are in love from the Lord, and the spiritual kingdom consists of angels who are in wisdom from the Lord. In each kingdom there is good and truth. The good and truth that are with the angels of the heavenly kingdom are signified by **purple** and **scarlet**, and the good and truth that are with the angels of the spiritual kingdom are signified by **gold** and **precious stones**. 

The latter and the former goods and truths the angels have from the Lord through the Word; wherefore there are two interior senses in the Word, the heavenly and the spiritual. Hence then it is, that the Woman sitting upon the scarlet beast was seen arrayed in purple and scarlet, and also adorned with gold, precious stones and pearls. 

The same which is signified by this woman, is signified by *the rich man, who was clothed in purple and fine linen, and fared sumptuously every day, at whose gateway Lazarus was cast, desiring to be filled with the crumbs that fell from his table* (Luke xvi. 19-21). By the **rich man** clothed in purple and fine linen the Jews are meant, who had the Word; and by **Lazarus** are meant the Gentiles, who had it not. Similar things are signified in the following passages: 

*They that have eaten luxuries are devastated in the streets; they that were brought up in scarlet have embraced the dunghill* (Lam. iv. 5). 

*Therefore, thou wasted one, what will thou do? though thou clothest thyself in scarlet, though* <note>original: catchword "i" refers to the first word of the next page.</note>

## 727.
*And pearls*, signifies the knowledges <note>term: **knowledges**; the Latin *cognitiones* refers to specific spiritual facts or data learned from the Bible, as opposed to general understanding.</note> of good and truth from the Word <note>In this context, "the Word" refers to the Holy Scriptures.</note> which they possess. ...from the holy things of the **Word** <note>In this work, "the Word" refers to the Holy Scriptures (the Bible).</note> profaned, and from its goods and truths defiled by direful falsities. That the same is signified by a **cup** or **goblet** as by wine, because it is the container, may be seen above (section 672); and by the **wine of Babylon** is signified that Religion as to its direful falsities (sections 632, 635). By **abominations** are signified the profanations of what is holy; and by the **filthiness of whoredom** the defilements of the good and truth of the Word are signified. 

Hence, by "having a golden cup in her hand full of abominations and filthiness of her whoredom," is signified that Religion consisting of the holy things of the church profaned, and of the goods and truths of the Word defiled by direful falsities. These things are similar to those which the Lord said to the Scribes and Pharisees:

> *Woe unto you, hypocrites, for ye make yourselves like unto whitened sepulchres, which indeed appear beautiful outwardly, but within are full of dead men’s bones and of all uncleanness (Matthew 23:27).*

It can be seen from these points that by the name "written upon her forehead, **Mystery, the great Babylon, the mother of whoredoms, and abominations of the earth**," the **Roman Catholic Religion** is signified <note>As in the previous section, the author identifies "Babylon" with the Roman Catholic Church, specifically regarding its pursuit of worldly and spiritual power during his era.</note> in terms of its hidden, interior quality. This quality stems from its origin in the desire to rule—rooted in self-love—over the holy things of the church and heaven, and thus over everything belonging to the Lord and His Word. Consequently, it has defiled and profaned the things that belong to the Word and the church. 

That this is a desire to rule over all things of the church is known from the authority it claims over the souls of men and every aspect of their worship. That it is over heaven is known from the assumed power of "loosing and binding" <note>original: "potestas ligandi et solvendi." This refers to the "Power of the Keys" from Matthew 16:19, which the author argues has been used to claim control over who is permitted to enter heaven.</note>, and thus of opening and shutting the way to salvation. That it is over all things of the Lord is known from the **vicarship** <term>vicarship: the office of the "Vicar of Christ," a title for the Pope claiming he acts as the earthly representative of Jesus Christ, which the author argues transfers divine authority to a human office</term>, through which they claim for themselves all that belongs to Him. That it is over all things of the Word is also known because the interpretation of the Scriptures is reserved for them alone. 

It is specified as the "desire to rule from self-love," because there is also a desire to rule from the **love of uses** <term>love of uses: in Swedenborg's theology, this is the desire to lead or govern specifically for the purpose of serving others and doing good for society</term>. These two types of love are diametrically opposite to one another. For the desire to rule from self-love is diabolical; it cares only for itself and the world for its own sake. But the desire to rule from the love of uses is heavenly; it regards the Lord, from whom all things that proceed are "uses." To this love, "uses" mean doing good to the church for the sake of the salvation of souls. For this reason, this heavenly love finds the desire to rule from self-love to be an abomination.

This is because numbers in the **Apocalypse**, and in the **Word** generally, signify the specific quality or nature of the things they are connected to. They function like adjectives joined to nouns, or like descriptions added to subjects; this can be seen from the numbers two, three, four, six, seven, ten, twelve, and 144, which have been explained previously. 

In this context, therefore, "five" signifies all the rest, because "seven" signifies all the holy things of the **Word**.
