From this, it is clear that the phrase "five have fallen" means that all the other truths have been destroyed. They are described as "falling" because the text is speaking of kings, who are traditionally said to "fall" by the sword in battle. 

By the phrase "one is," nothing else is meant but this specific **Divine Truth**: that *all power in heaven and on earth was given to the Lord*, according to the words of the Lord Himself (Matthew 28:18; John 13:3; 17:2, 3, 10), as was seen above (section 618). The reason this one truth has not been destroyed is that, without it, they <note>The religious authorities represented by Babylon.</note> could not claim for themselves the power to rule over every aspect of the church, the **Word**, and even heaven itself. 

By "the other who has not yet come, and when he comes must remain but a short time," is signified the **Divine Truth** which has not yet been brought into question, and which, when it finally is, will not remain permanently with them. This truth is that *the Lord’s Human is Divine*. It is said that it must remain only a short time because this is according to <term>Divine Providence</term> <note>The laws by which God governs human history and spiritual development.</note>, which was discussed previously (section 686). That they have seen this other truth—which is that the Lord’s <term>Human</term> <note>The physical and human nature of Jesus Christ.</note> is Divine, though as if with closed eyes—is manifest from this: they say that in the <term>Eucharist</term> <note>The sacrament of the Lord's Supper or Holy Communion.</note> there is not only the Body and Blood of the Lord, but also His Soul and Divinity. It is manifest from this, that by "these shall fight with the Lamb and the Lamb shall overcome them because He is Lord of lords and King of kings," is signified the Lord’s combat with them concerning the acknowledgment of the Lord’s Divine Human, because the Lord in His Divine Human is God of heaven and earth. 

That the Lord is God of heaven and earth, He teaches in plain words; for He says, *All things whatsoever the Father hath are mine* (John xvi. 15). *The Father hath given all things into the hand of the Son* (John iii. 35, 36; xiii. 3). *Father, thou hast given me power over all flesh: all Mine are Thine and Thine are Mine* (John xvii. 2, 3, 10). *All power is given unto Me in heaven and in earth* (Matt. xxviii. 18). *I am the way, the truth, and the life: no one cometh unto the Father but by Me; He that knoweth and seeth Me, knoweth and seeth the Father; for I am in the Father, and the Father in Me* (John xiv. 6-11). *The Father and I are one* (John x. 30). *That every one that believeth in the Lord, should have everlasting life; and he that believeth not in Him, shall not see life* (John iii. 15, 17, 18, 36; vi. 47; xv. 26; and elsewhere).

### 747.
***And shall make her desolate and naked***, signifies that they will divest themselves of her falsities and evils. By **making her desolate** is signified to divest themselves of her falsities <term>falsities</term><note>In this theological context, "falsities" refer to incorrect or distorted spiritual teachings.</note>: and by **making her naked** is signified to divest themselves of her evils: for they make her desolate and naked among themselves. **Desolation** in the Word is predicated of truths and falsities, and **nakedness** of goods and evils; as may be evident from the passages that were adduced above concerning nakedness (n. 213, 706). From these things it may be evident that by their making her **desolate and naked** is signified that they will divest themselves of all the falsities and evils of that Religion. That the **Protestants** or the **Reformed** have done so, is known.

### 748.
***And shall eat her flesh, and burn her with fire***, signifies that from hatred they will condemn and destroy among themselves the evils and falsities which are proper to that Religion, and will hold the Religion itself accursed, and will blot it out from among them. This is concerning the **Protestants**, who will do thus with the **harlot**, that is, with the **Roman Catholic Religion**. By **eating her flesh** is signified to condemn from hatred and to destroy among themselves the things proper to that Religion, which are evils and falsities, as treated of in what follows: and by **burning her with fire** is signified to accurse that Religion as **profane** <term>profane</term><note>To treat something sacred with irreverence or to use spiritual things for selfish, worldly ends.</note>, and to blot it out among themselves. That to **burn with fire** has this meaning, is because the punishment of the **profanation** of what is holy was burning; wherefore it was of the **Divine law**, *that they who profaned the name of Jehovah by worshipping other gods, should themselves and all that they had be burned with fire* <note>original: "Deut. xiii. 12-18"</note> (Deuteronomy 13:12-18).

From these things it is manifest that by these words, “**the woman whom thou sawest is the great city which reigneth over the kings of the earth**,” is signified that the Roman Catholic Religion reigns as to doctrine in the Christian world, and in some respect even with the Reformed, although they are not under the papal Dominion.

To this I will add this **RELATION** <note>In Swedenborg's writings, a "Relation" (Latin: *Memorabile*) is a recorded account of a vision or conversation experienced in the spiritual world.</note>. I was permitted to speak with Pope **SIXTUS V** <note>original: "SIXTUS QUINTUS"</note>. He came out of a certain society in the west, toward the left. He told me that he was appointed as the chief Governor over a society gathered from those Catholics who surpass the rest in judgment and industry; and that he was made their chief Governor for the reason that, for half a year before his death, he had believed that the <term>vicarship</term> <note>The claim that the Pope is the "Vicar of Christ," acting as His representative on Earth with supreme authority.</note> was an invention created for the sake of gaining power; and that the Lord the Savior, because He is God, is He who alone is to be adored and worshipped. He also believed that the sacred Scripture is Divine, and thus more holy than the edicts of popes. He said that he remained firm in the belief of these two fundamentals of religion until the end of his life. 

He also said that their saints are of no account. He was astonished when I related that it had been decreed in a <term>synod</term> <note>A council of church officials convened to decide matters of doctrine.</note>, and confirmed by a <term>bull</term> <note>A formal public decree or charter issued by a pope.</note>, that the saints should be invoked. He said that he led an active life just as he had done in the world; and that he proposed to himself every morning nine or ten things which he wished should be accomplished before evening. 

I asked whence he obtained in so few years so great a treasure as he had laid up in the **Castel Sant'Angelo** <note>original: "castle of Angelo"; the fortress in Rome used by popes as a castle and treasury.</note>. And when I said that that treasure was still remaining, he said, “Whom can it benefit now?”

## CHAPTER EIGHTEENTH.

1. And after these things I saw an angel coming down from heaven, having great power, and the earth was lightened by his glory. <note>In Swedenborg's system, "lightening the earth with glory" signifies the arrival of new spiritual truth that exposes the hidden corruption of the old church.</note>

2. And he cried mightily with a great voice, saying, **Babylon the great** <term>Babylon</term> <note>original: "Babylon." In this theological work, Babylon represents "spiritual dominion," specifically the Roman Catholic Church of Swedenborg’s time, which he believed had substituted human authority for divine truth.</note> is fallen, is fallen, and is become the habitation of demons, and the hold of every unclean spirit, and the cage of every unclean and hateful bird.

3. For all the nations have drunk of the wine of the anger of her **whoredom** <note>original: "scortationis." This term is used throughout the work to describe the spiritual act of twisting or perverting the truths of the Bible to serve selfish or worldly desires.</note>, and the kings of the earth have committed whoredom with her, and the merchants of the earth are waxed rich through the abundance of her delicacies.

4. And I heard another voice from heaven, saying, **Come out of her my people** <note>A call for those who truly believe to separate themselves from a corrupt religious institution before its spiritual collapse affects them.</note>, that ye be not partakers of her sins, and that ye receive not of her plagues.

5. For her sins have reached even unto heaven, and God hath remembered her iniquities.

6. Render unto her as she hath rendered unto you; and double unto her double according to her works; in the cup which she hath filled, fill to her double.

7. As much as she hath glorified herself and lived deliciously, so much torment and sorrow give her; for she saith in her heart, I sit a queen, and am not a widow, and shall not see sorrow. <note>The "queen" represents the church’s pride in its own power and its belief that it can never be overthrown.</note>

### THE EXPLANATION.

753. **And after these things I saw**, signifies a manifestation concerning the destruction and condemnation of those who were in the Roman Catholic Religion, and exercised power over the holy things of the church and over heaven, with the purpose of ruling over all, and of possessing all the goods of others. These things are here signified by “after these things I saw,” because they are treated of in this chapter. The Dogmas <note>Dogmas refer to the official, authoritative doctrines or beliefs held by the Church.</note> of that Religion are prefixed to this work, that they who are in enlightenment from the Lord may see that they look to nothing else but dominion over the souls of men, to the end that they may be worshipped as gods, and may alone possess the goods of the whole world. And as that was their end, and not at all the salvation of souls, they could take their dogmas from nowhere else but from hell; for they could not from heaven, that is, from the Lord, but from themselves, because they transferred all things of the Lord to themselves. 

What is more detestable than to separate the Body and Blood of the Lord, or the Bread and Wine in the <term>Holy Supper<note>Also known as the Eucharist or Communion. Swedenborg is critiquing the "communion under one kind," where the laity received the bread but not the wine.</note></term>, manifestly against its institution, and this by fictions, and solely for the sake of the daily and nightly sacrifices of the <term>Mass<note>The central liturgical ritual of the Catholic Church. Swedenborg argues here that the practice was being used for financial profit through "Mass stipends" or payments for prayers.</note></term>, by which they make worldly gains? What is more detestable than to worship dead men with Divine invocation, and to fall down on the knees before their images, and to kiss them reverently, yea, even the bones and remains of their dead

These are the things which are treated of in this chapter of the Apocalypse.

Similar individuals from that religious system have been gathered since the Last Judgment and are sent to join those like themselves from time to time.

The Divine can reside within a person, but it cannot belong to the <term>proprium</term> <note>A term used by Swedenborg to describe the "self" or the ego—everything that belongs to a human being's own nature, which he considers to be inherently selfish or evil.</note>; for a person's own nature is nothing but evil. 761. ***For her sins have reached even unto heaven, and God hath remembered her iniquities***, signifies that their evils and falsities infest the heavens, and that the Lord will protect these from the violence originating there. By "her sins reaching to the heavens," it is signified that their evils and falsities disturb the angels. By "God’s remembering her iniquities," it is signified that the Lord will protect the heavens from the violence caused by those sins.

This is the meaning because all things in the heavens are goods and truths, while all things in the hells are evils and falsities. Because of this, the heavens and the hells are completely separated, existing in an inverted relationship like <term>antipodes</term> <note>People who live on the opposite side of the globe; here used to describe how heaven and hell are diametrically opposite states of being.</note>. Therefore, under normal conditions, evils and falsities cannot reach the heavens. However, when evils and falsities are multiplied beyond the natural degrees of opposition—growing beyond due measure—the heavens become infested. Unless the Lord then protects the heavens, which He does through a more powerful <term>influx</term> <note>The constant flow of life, love, and wisdom from God into the spiritual and natural worlds.</note> from Himself, the heavens would suffer violence. By Babylon, that specific Religious system is signified; here, as previously mentioned <note>See section number 751.</note>, Babylon is personified as a woman or harlot, because the text speaks of “her torment.” By the **“mighty city”** is signified that Religious system so strongly fortified. By the phrase **“in one hour is thy judgment come”** is signified that it could be overturned so suddenly, and that those within it could perish. **“In one hour”** signifies such suddenness; and by the **“judgment”** is signified its overthrow and the destruction of those who committed "whoredom" <note>In this spiritual context, "whoredom" refers to the falsification of religious truths for personal gain.</note> and lived luxuriously with the harlot, who are the subjects of this passage. That they perished by the last judgment may be seen in the small work titled *The Last Judgment and the Destruction of Babylon*, published in London in 1758 <note>original title: "De Ultimo Judicio et de Babylonia destructa." This is a reference to Swedenborg’s own published eyewitness account of events he claimed to see in the spiritual world.</note>. These things are said regarding that destruction. 

The reason that their **“standing afar off for fear of her torment”** signifies a state that is still remote from the state of those who are under condemnation (because they are in fear of the torment), is that by **“afar off”** the scripture does not mean physical distance in space, but a remoteness of *state*. This occurs when one is in fear of punishments: for as long as a person is in a state of fear, they observe, weigh the situation, and lament. Remoteness of state, which is what is meant by "distance" in the <term>spiritual sense: the deeper, symbolic meaning of the Bible that relates to the soul and the afterlife rather than physical objects</term>, is also signified by the term **“afar off”** elsewhere in the Word <term>the Word: a term used here to refer to the Sacred Scripture or the Bible</term>, as seen in these passages: 

*Hear, ye that are afar off, what I will do; and ye that are near acknowledge my might* (Isaiah 33:13). 
*Am I a God at hand and not a God afar off?* (Jeremiah 23:23). 
*He found grace in the wilderness, even Israel; Jehovah hath appeared unto me from afar off* (Jeremiah 31:2, 3). 
*Bring my sons from afar* (Isaiah 43:6). 
*Hearken, ye people, from afar* (Isaiah 49:1). 
*Peoples and nations that came from a far land* (Isaiah 5:26). 

This is seen in many other places as well, such as Jeremiah 4:16; 5:15; and Zechariah 6:15; where by nations and peoples **“from afar”** are meant those who are more remote from the truths and goodness of the church. In everyday speech, we also use this logic: relatives are said to be “near,” while those with a more remote relationship are said to be “distant.”

By the items now mentioned, which are <term>thyine wood</term> <note>A fragrant, costly wood from North Africa, often used in ancient woodworking and mentioned in the Bible as a luxury item.</note> and <term>vessels of ivory</term>, natural goods and truths are meant. These three degrees are in every man from birth, and they are also in general in heaven and in the church; which is the cause of there being three heavens—the highest, the middle, and the lowest—altogether distinct from each other according to those degrees; and so, too, of the Lord’s church on earth.

### THE APOCALYPSE REVEALED. [CHAPTER XVIII]

...because they do not possess the spiritual goods and truths of knowledge regarding the church, which these physical objects represent. These concepts are similar to those explained previously (sections 772-774), with the following distinction: here, these materials represent <term>knowledges</term> <note>The term "knowledges" (Latin: *cognitiones*) refers to the specific facts, data, and information about spiritual matters stored in the mind.</note> that form the most basic or "ultimate" parts of a person's natural mind. Because these facts vary in quality depending on the inner essence within them, they are called **vessels of precious wood, of brass, of iron, and of marble.**

In the language of the spirit, **vessels** signify knowledges—specifically those concerning the church. This is because these pieces of information act as containers for "good" and "truth," just as physical vessels are the containers for oil and wine. These knowledges exist in great variety, and their storage place is the **memory**. They are so diverse because a person’s inner thoughts are present within them; they are introduced into the memory through intellectual thought, through hearing, or through reading, and are then shaped by how the person perceives them using their <term>rationality</term> <note>Rationality here refers to the human ability to analyze information and distinguish between what is true and what is false.</note>. All of these internal factors are contained within these knowledges, and they are revealed whenever a person speaks or thinks.

The specific meanings of **vessels of precious wood, of brass, of iron, and of marble** are as follows:
*   A **vessel of precious wood** signifies knowledge derived from rational good and truth (goodness and truth understood through reason).
*   A **vessel of brass** signifies knowledge derived from natural good (goodness on a practical, physical level).
*   A **vessel of iron** signifies knowledge derived from natural truth (facts about the physical world and its laws).
*   A **vessel of marble** signifies knowledge derived from the *appearance* of good and truth.

As established just above (n. 774), **wood** signifies good. The reason that rational truth is also implied here by **precious wood** is that while "wood" signifies good, the word "precious" is a quality attributed to truth. Just as different kinds of good are represented by different trees—such as the olive, cedar, fig, fir, poplar, and oak—so it is with metals.

The reason that **vessels of brass and iron** signify knowledge from natural good and truth is that all metals mentioned in the Word <note>The "Word" refers to the Sacred Scripture or the Bible.</note>—including gold, silver, brass, iron, tin, and lead—signify specific types of goods and truths. They carry these meanings because they <term>correspond</term> <note>Correspondence is the spiritual law where every natural object is a physical manifestation of a specific spiritual reality.</note> to them. Furthermore, because they correspond, these materials actually exist in heaven; for all things there are...

In the previous verse, the text dealt with matters of the church's **doctrine**. In this verse, however, the focus shifts to the **worship** of the church. The teachings of doctrine are presented first, and the acts of worship follow, because the actual quality of worship is determined by the goods and truths found in its doctrine. Worship is essentially an external act; for it to be meaningful, it must contain "internals," which are the principles of doctrine. Without these, worship is stripped of its essence, life, and soul.

Now, all aspects of doctrine relate to "goods" (which come from love and charity) and to "truths" (which come from wisdom and faith). These goods and truths are categorized into degrees: **heavenly** <term>Celestial</term> <note>The highest degree of the human mind or heaven, characterized by direct love for the Lord.</note>, **spiritual**, and **natural**. The components of worship follow this same order:

1.  **Spiritual things of worship:** These are mentioned first in this verse as **cinnamon**, **incense**, **perfume**, and **frankincense**.
2.  **Heavenly things of worship:** These are named second: **wine**, **oil**, **fine flour**, and **wheat**.
3.  **Natural things of worship:** These are named third: **cattle** and **sheep**.

That all these elements of worship must be derived from the Word is symbolized by the mention of **horses**, **chariots**, and the **bodies** and **souls of men**. This is the sequence of the spiritual sense <note>The "spiritual sense" refers to the deeper, symbolic meaning Swedenborg believes is hidden beneath the literal text of the Bible.</note> within this verse. 

Ultimately, all the items listed here carry the same underlying meaning as those in the previous verse: they signify that these genuine spiritual goods and truths are not found among those in this "religion" <note>Here, "religion" refers specifically to the Roman Catholic system, which Swedenborg calls "Babylon."</note>, because their internal states do not correspond to these holy things. But still, because they have practiced external Divine worship as part of their religion, they are first instructed as to what heaven is like and the nature of the happiness of eternal life—specifically, that these are nothing but blessings flowing in from the Lord to everyone in heaven, according to the quality of their heavenly affection for what is good and true. 

However, because these individuals have not approached the Lord, and therefore are not conjoined with Him, and because they have lacked any such affection for good and truth, they find these heavenly things repulsive. They turn themselves away and instead desire the pleasures of the love of self and the world, which are merely natural and physical. But since it is inherent in those selfish pleasures to do evil—especially toward those who worship the Lord and toward the angels of heaven—they are eventually deprived of these pleasures as well. They are then cast down among companions who live in contempt and wretchedness in the <term>infernal workhouses</term> <note>original: "ergastula". In Swedenborg’s descriptions of the afterlife, these are places where those who refuse to act from a love of use are compelled to perform basic labor.</note>.

These things happen to them according to the degree of their love of dominion over the Divine things of the Lord; the greater their desire for power, the more complete is their rejection of the Lord.

It is now evident from these points that the phrase, "the fruits of the desire of thy soul have departed, and all things fat and splendid have departed from thee, and thou shalt find them no more at all," signifies that all the blessings and happiness of heaven—even the external ones they once desired—will completely flee away and no longer appear, because these individuals possess no genuine affection for what is good and true.

The fact that **fat things** signify heavenly goods <note>original: "pinguia". In the symbolic language of the Bible, "fatness" represents the richness of spiritual love and the internal satisfaction that comes from goodness.</note>, their affections, and the resulting enjoyments, can be seen from the following passages: *Hearken unto Me, eat ye that which is good, that your soul may be delighted with fatness* (Isaiah 55:2). *I will satisfy the soul of the priests with fatness, and My people shall be satisfied with good* (Jeremiah 31:14). *My soul shall be satisfied with marrow and...*

There are innumerable societies in that world, and joys in them similar to those on earth, for the reason that they who are there are conjoined with men on the earth, who are also in the midst...

790. ***Rejoice over her, O heaven, and you holy apostles and prophets; for God has judged your judgment upon her***, signifies that the angels of heaven and the people of the church, who live in <term>goods and truths</term> <note>In Swedenborg’s terminology, "goods" refer to intentions and actions of love, while "truths" refer to matters of faith and wisdom.</note> from the Word, should rejoice in their hearts that those who are in the evils and falsities of that Religion <note>Original: "Religiosi"; referring specifically to the Roman Catholic system, which Swedenborg often calls "Babylon" or "Babel."</note> are removed and rejected. They are called **holy** because the apostles and prophets, as stated, represent in an abstract sense the goods and truths of the Word, which are holy in themselves because they belong to the Lord (n. 586, 666).

"For God has judged your judgment upon her," signifies that those who are in the evils and falsities of that Religion are removed and rejected. The fact that no others are rejected can be seen above (n. 786). The joy of the angels over the removal and rejection of those in the evils and falsities of that system is discussed in the next chapter (19:1–9); here, it only mentions that they should rejoice. However, angelic joy is not caused by the condemnation of others, but by the establishment of the **New Heaven** and **New Church**, and the salvation of the faithful. These things cannot be established until the corrupt systems are removed, which is accomplished by the <term>Last Judgment</term> <note>Swedenborg taught that a Last Judgment occurred in the spiritual world in 1757, clearing away "clouds" of corrupt spirits to allow for a new spiritual era.</note>; on which subject something further is said below.

### THE APOCALYPSE REVEALED [CHAP. XVIII.

...truths from the Word. This will be further clarified in the explanation of verses 7, 8, and 9 of the following chapter. From this, it is evident that the phrase "rejoice over her, O heaven, and you holy apostles and prophets, for God has judged your judgment upon her," signifies that the angels of heaven and the people of the church—who live in <term>goods and truths</term> <note>In Swedenborg’s theology, "goods" refers to the intentions and actions of love, while "truths" refers to the insights and principles of faith.</note> from the Word—should rejoice in their hearts. They rejoice because those who remain in the evils and falsities of that Religion <note>Swedenborg uses "Religion" (Latin: *Religiosi*) here to refer specifically to the Roman Catholic system, which he identifies as "Babylon."</note> are removed and rejected. 

It is clear that the literal apostles and prophets mentioned in the Word are not meant here. They were few in number and were not more inherently holy than others. Instead, they represent everyone in the Lord's church who lives according to the goods and truths of the Word; this is the same meaning as the "twelve tribes of Israel" discussed earlier (n. 349). Specifically, the **apostle Peter** signifies the truth or faith of the church; the **apostle James** signifies the charity (love in action) of the church; and the **apostle John** signifies the actual works of charity performed by those in the church.

791. ***And a mighty angel took up a stone like a great millstone, and cast it into the sea, saying, Thus with violence shall that great city, Babylon, be thrown down, and shall be found no more at all***, signifies that by a powerful <term>influx</term> <note>The spiritual process where life, light, and power flow from the Lord through the heavens into the human mind or the world of spirits.</note> of the Lord out of heaven, that Religion, along with all its corrupted truths of the Word, will be cast headlong into hell and will never again appear to the angels. 

The phrase "a mighty angel took up" signifies a powerful influx from the Lord out of heaven, for an "angel" symbolizes the Lord and His operation through heaven (n. 258, 415, 465, 649). Because he is called a "mighty" angel and takes up a stone like a "great millstone," a powerful operation—specifically a powerful influx—is indicated. 

A "stone like a great millstone" signifies the truths of the Word that have been corrupted and profaned. Generally, a **stone** signifies truth, and a **mill** signifies the search for, investigation of, and confirmation of truth from the Word (as will be shown in n. 794). However, in this context, it refers to the corruption and profanation of that truth, as it is applied to Babylon. Being "cast into the sea" signifies being thrown into hell.

### THE APOCALYPSE REVEALED. [ CHAPTER 18 ]

...heavenly truth and good. By "voice" is meant sound, and every sound corresponds to an **affection** <note>In Swedenborg's vocabulary, an "affection" is a deep-seated emotion or inclination of the will, often specifically related to love or desire.</note> which is of love, since it arises from it. Because of this, the sounds of the harp, of music, and of the pipe signify specific affections through **correspondence**. <term>Correspondence: The spiritual principle that physical things in our world (like sounds or objects) reflect and represent specific spiritual realities.</term> 

But these affections are of two kinds, spiritual and heavenly: **spiritual affections** are the affections of wisdom, and **heavenly affections** are the affections of love. They differ from each other just as the heavens do, which are distinguished into two kingdoms—the heavenly and the spiritual—as has been stated several times before. There are, therefore, musical instruments whose sounds relate to spiritual affections, and there are those which relate to heavenly affections. 

The voice or sound of **harpers and musicians** relates to spiritual affections, while the voice or sound of **pipers and trumpeters** relates to heavenly affections. This is because instruments whose sounds are "discrete" (distinct or plucked), such as stringed instruments, belong to the class of spiritual affections; however, instruments whose sounds are "continuous," such as wind instruments, belong to the class of heavenly affections. 

Hence it is that the sound of harpers and musicians signifies an affection for spiritual good and truth, and the sound of pipers and trumpeters signifies an affection for heavenly good and truth. That the sound of the harp, through correspondence, signifies confession from an affection for spiritual truth, may be seen in sections 276 and 661. 

It is here meant that those who remain in the evils and falsities of the **Roman Catholic Religion** <term>Roman Catholic Religion: Swedenborg uses this term (Latin: *Religiosum Catholicum Romanum*) to describe the institutional church of his day, which he believed had prioritized political power over the spiritual truths of the Bible.</term> have no affections for spiritual truth and good, nor any affections for heavenly truth and good. This is indicated by the prophecy stating that the "voice of harpers, and of musicians, and of pipers and trumpeters shall be heard no more at all in thee" [Revelation 18:22]. 

The reason they do not have these affections is because they cannot be given to them; for they possess no truth from the **Word** <note>The Word: A term for the Bible, which Swedenborg emphasizes as the only source of genuine spiritual truth.</note>; and because they have no truth, they likewise have no good. This "good" is given only to those who truly desire truths—but no others desire truths from a spiritual affection except those who go...

### THE APOCALYPSE REVEALED. [CHAP. XVIII]

...which no other light can proceed than that of the **Divine Wisdom**, nor any other heat than that of the **Divine Love**. That it is so, is demonstrated in the work *Angelic Wisdom concerning the Divine Love and Divine Wisdom* <note>original: "Sapientia Angelica de Divino Amore et de Divina Sapientia." One of Swedenborg's primary philosophical works, published in 1763.</note> (numbers 83–172).

&emsp;&emsp;Since that light is from the Lord, and the Lord is omnipresent by means of it and in it, therefore all enlightenment is effected through it, and thence the perception of spiritual truth, which those have who love **Divine Truths** spiritually—that is, who love truths because they are true, and thus because they are Divine. That this is to love the Lord, is manifest: for in that light the Lord is omnipresent, because the **Divine Love** and **Divine Wisdom** are not in place <note>That is, they are not limited by physical space or geography.</note>, but are where they are received, and according to the reception. That they who are in the <term>Roman Catholic Religion</term> <note>Swedenborg distinguishes between individual faith and the institutional "religion" or power structure of the Church.</note> have not any enlightenment, and perception of spiritual truth therefrom, may be evident from their not loving any spiritual light: for the origin of spiritual light is, as was said, from the Lord; and no others can accept that light, nor receive it, but they who are conjoined to the Lord: and conjunction with the Lord is effected solely by the acknowledgment and worship of Him, and at the same time by a life according to His precepts from the **Word** <note>The term "the Word" refers to the Sacred Scriptures or the Bible.</note>. The acknowledgment and worship of the Lord, and the reading of the Word, cause the presence of the Lord; but these two together with a life according to His precepts, effect conjunction with Him.

&emsp;&emsp;In <term>Babylon</term> <note>In Swedenborg’s biblical interpretation, "Babylon" signifies those who use the holy things of the church as a means to gain power and dominion over others.</note> it is the contrary. There the Lord is acknowledged, but without dominion; and the Word is acknowledged, but without the reading of it. In place of the Lord the **pope** is there worshipped, and in place of the Word the <term>papal bulls</term> <note>Formal decrees or edicts issued by the Pope; Swedenborg argues these are placed above Scripture.</note> are acknowledged; according to which they live, and not according to the precepts of the Word; and the bulls have for their end the dominion of the pope and his ministers over heaven and the world, and the precepts of the Word have for their end the Lord's dominion over heaven and the world; and these are diametrically opposite to each other, like hell and heaven. 798. Since it is said that they have no union of goodness and truth—because the "marriage" of the Lord and the church does not exist among them—we should speak here about the power of opening and shutting heaven. This power is the same as the power to forgive or retain sins, which they claim for themselves as the successors of Peter and the apostles. The Lord said to Peter:

*“Upon this same **Rock** <note>original: "Petra"; the Greek and Latin word for a mass of rock, used here as a play on Peter’s name, Petros.</note> will I build my church, and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it: I will give unto thee the keys of the kingdom of the heavens, and whatever thou shalt bind on earth shall be bound in the heavens, and whatever thou shalt loose on earth shall be loosed in the heavens”* (Matthew 16:18, 19). 

The **Divine Truth** (which is meant by the **Rock** <note>original: "Petra"</note> upon which the Lord will build His Church) is what Peter had just confessed, namely: *“Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God”* (verse 16). By the **keys of the kingdom of the heavens**—meaning that whatever that **Rock** (which is the Lord) shall bind or loose on earth shall be bound or loosed in the heavens—is meant that the Lord has power over both heaven and earth, as He also states in Matthew 28:18. Thus, He has the power to save those who, from a sincere faith, join in that same confession of Peter. 

The Lord’s Divine work to save humanity operates from **firsts** through **ultimates** <term>ultimates: in this context, "ultimates" refers to the lowest or most external level of reality, specifically the physical world and the lives of people on earth.</term>. This is what is meant by saying that whatever He binds or looses on earth shall be bound or loosed in heaven. The "ultimates" through which the Lord works are here on earth, and specifically within human beings. It was for this very reason—so that the Lord Himself might be present in the lowest things just as He is in the highest—that He came into the world and took on the **Human** <note>Refers to the Lord's incarnation and physical existence as a human being.</note>. That all of the Lord’s Divine operation proceeds from firsts through ultimates (and thus from Himself in the highest and from Himself in the lowest) can be seen in the work *Angelic Wisdom concerning the Divine Love and Divine Wisdom* <note>The original text contains a typo, "Wisdon" for "Wisdom."</note> (numbers 217–219, 221). It is for this reason that the Lord is called the First and the...

He explains that God became human to work through the "ultimates" (the physical level of existence) to save humanity.</summary>

### No. 798.

Lastly, that the Lord is the **Alpha and the Omega, the Beginning and the End, the Almighty**, can be seen above (see numbers 29–31, 38, 57). Who cannot see, if they are willing, that the salvation of humanity is a continuous operation of the Lord within a person from earliest infancy even to the end of life? This is purely a Divine work and can never be delegated to any human being. It is Divine in such a way that it requires the simultaneous work of omnipresence, omniscience, and omnipotence. That a person's **reformation** <term>reformation: the initial stage of spiritual growth where one begins to think and act according to truths from the Word</term> and **regeneration** <term>regeneration: the process of being "born again" spiritually, where the Lord creates a new heart and spirit within the person</term>—and thus their salvation—are entirely the work of the Lord's **Divine Providence** <term>Divine Providence: the government of the Lord's Divine Love and Wisdom, ensuring the salvation of those who are willing</term>, can be seen in the work *Angelic Wisdom concerning the Divine Providence* from beginning to end. 

The very coming of the Lord into the world was solely for the sake of human salvation. For this reason, He assumed the **Human** <note>original: "Humanum"; refers to the physical and mental nature the Lord took on through Mary</note>, removed the power of the hells, and **glorified** Himself—meaning He made His human nature Divine. By doing so, He took on all power even in **ultimates** <term>ultimates: the lowest or most external levels of reality, including the physical world and the literal sense of the Word</term>, which is what is meant by "sitting at the right hand of God." 

What, therefore, is more abominable than to establish a religion which decrees that this Divine authority and power belong to man and no longer to the Lord? Such a religion claims that heaven will be opened or shut simply because a priest says, "I absolve," or "I excommunicate," and that even the most enormous sin is **remitted** <note>original: "remitti"; forgiven or put away</note> provided he says, "I remit." There are many "devils" in the world who, in order to escape worldly punishments, seek and obtain absolution for diabolical crimes through cleverness or bribes. Who could be so insane as to believe that humans have been given the power to admit such "devils" into heaven?

It was stated previously (at the end of number 790) that **Peter** represented the truth of faith in the Church, **James** represented the good of charity in the Church, and **John** represented the good works performed by those in the Church. Together, the twelve apostles represented the Church in its entirety. It is clearly evident that they served as these representatives from the Lord's words to them in Matthew: 

*When the Son of Man shall sit upon the throne of His glory, ye also shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel* (Matthew 19:28; Luke 22:30).

The reason they lack these spiritual qualities is that even the leaders of the order are focused on "merchandise"—trading in sacred things for personal gain—and thus they set a corrupt example for those under them. That many falsities have emanated from the Babylonish Religion into the churches of the Reformed <note>The "Reformed" refers to the Protestant denominations that broke away from the Roman Catholic Church during the Reformation.</note>, may be seen above (n. 751); where this passage was explained, that *the Woman whom thou sawest is the great city which reigneth over the kings of the earth* (Apoc. xvii. 18).

### THE SPIRITUAL SENSE.

**THE CONTENTS OF THE WHOLE CHAPTER.** The glorification of the Lord by the angels of heaven, because the Roman Catholic Religion is removed in the world of spirits <note>In the author's theology, the "world of spirits" is an intermediate state between heaven and hell where people are prepared for their final destination.</note>, whereby they have come into the light and into their blessedness (verses 1–5). Annunciation of the Lord’s coming, and of a New Church from Him (verses 6–10). The opening of the Word as to the spiritual sense <term>spiritual sense: the deeper, symbolic meaning of the Bible that lies beneath the literal stories</term> for that church (verses 11–16). The calling of all to it (verses 17, 18). Resistance by those who are in faith separated from charity <note>This refers to a theological stance that prioritizes intellectual belief over active love and good works.</note> (verse 19). Their removal and damnation (verses 20, 21).

**THE CONTENTS OF EACH VERSE.** “After these things I heard as it were a voice of a great multitude in heaven, saying, Alleluia,” <note>original: "Alleluia." A Hebrew phrase meaning "Praise the Lord."</note> *signifies* thanksgiving, confession and celebration of the Lord by the angels of the lower heavens on account of the removal of the Babylonians <note>Here, "Babylonians" is a symbolic term for those who use religion to gain power over others.</note>. “Salvation and glory and honor and power unto the Lord our God,” *signifies* that now there is salvation from the Lord, because there is now reception of **Divine Truth** and **Divine Good** <term>Divine Truth and Good: the two fundamental energies of God, often compared to light and heat</term> from His Divine power. “For true and just are His judgments; for He hath judged the great harlot, who corrupted the earth with her whoredom,” *signifies* because in justice the profane Babylonish religion is condemned, which has destroyed the Lord’s Church by filthy adulterations of the Word. “And hath avenged the blood of His servants at her hand,” *signifies* retribution for the injuries and violence offered to the souls of the worshippers of the Lord. “And a second time they said, Alleluia; and her smoke rose up for ever and ever,” *signifies* thanksgiving and celebration of the Lord from joy that that profane religion is condemned.

### THE EXPLANATION.

803. **After these things I heard as it were a voice of a great multitude in heaven, saying, Hallelujah <note>original: "Alleluia"</note>,** signifies thanksgiving, confession and celebration of the Lord by the angels of the lower heavens on account of the removal of the Babylonians <note>Babylonians: in Swedenborg’s terminology, this refers to those who use religion to gain power and dominion over others</note>. 809. ***And a voice came out of the throne, saying, Praise our God, all ye His servants, and ye that fear Him,*** signifies <term>influx</term> <note>Influx refers to the spiritual process where life and wisdom flow from the Lord into the minds of angels and people, similar to how light and heat flow from the sun.</note> from the Lord into heaven, and thus the unanimity of the angels, that all who are in the truths of faith and the goods of love should worship the Lord as the only God of heaven. By the voice which came out of the throne is signified influx from the Lord into heaven. That it is from the Lord is because He that sat upon the throne was the Lord, as was shown just above (n. 808). Therefore, by the voice that came out therefrom is meant influx: for the Lord, inasmuch as He is above the heavens and appears before the angels as a Sun, does not speak from there directly to the angels, but flows in; and that which flows in is received in heaven and is spoken. For this reason, that voice, although coming from the throne, was heard by John out of heaven, and thus from the angels there; and whatever the angels speak out of heaven is from the Lord.

By "**Praise our God**" is signified that they should worship the Lord as the only God of heaven. That to praise God is to worship Him will be seen below. acknowledged to be Divine, there is a full marriage of the Lord and the Church; for it is known in the Reformed Christian world, that the Church is a Church from the marriage of the Lord with her: for the Lord is called the lord of the Vineyard, and the Church is the Vineyard; and the Lord is called the Bridegroom and Husband, and the Church is called the Bride and Wife. That the Lord is called the Bridegroom, and the Church the Bride, may be seen, section 797. That there is then a full marriage of the Lord and the Church, when His <term>Human</term> <note>The term "Human" (Latin: *Humanum*) refers to the Lord's physical and mental existence on earth, which Swedenborg explains was made completely Divine after the Resurrection.</note> is acknowledged to be Divine, is manifest: for then God the Father and He are acknowledged to be one, as the soul and the body. Before the Lord’s Human is acknowledged to be Divine, there is indeed a marriage of the Lord with the Church; but only with those who go to the Lord, and think of His Divine, and not at all whether His Human is Divine or not. ### 814.

**And to her was granted that she should be arrayed in fine linen, clean and bright**, signifies that those who will belong to this Church are instructed by the Lord in genuine and pure truths through the Word. By being "arrayed" is signified to be instructed in truths, because truths are symbolized by garments (number 166); specifically, white garments represent genuine truths (number 212). 

By "fine linen, clean and bright" is signified a quality that is shining from goodness and pure from truths. Because pure truth is not provided from any other source than from the Lord through the Word, this source is also signified here. It is described as "clean and bright" because "clean" signifies that which is devoid of evil—and thus shines from a heart of goodness—while "bright" signifies what is devoid of falsity—and thus is pure in its truth. 

Fine linen or linen cloth signifies genuine truth in the following passages of Scripture as well: 

* *O Jerusalem, I have clothed thee with needlework, I have girded thee with fine linen, and I have covered thee with silk; thus wast thou decked with gold and silver, and thy raiment was fine linen and silk* (Ezekiel 16:10, 13). 
* *Fine linen with needlework from Egypt was thy clothing* (Ezekiel 27:7). This passage concerns Tyre, by which the Church is signified in regards to its <term>knowledges</term> <note>original: "cognitiones." In Swedenborg's specialized vocabulary, this refers to the specific facts or data of spiritual information one learns from the Word.</note> of truth and goodness. 
* *The armies in heaven followed Him upon white horses, clothed in fine linen, white and clean* (Apocalypse 19:13, 14). 

The fact that Joseph was dressed in garments of fine linen by Pharaoh (Genesis 41:42) carries the same spiritual meaning. Conversely, truth from the Word that is possessed by people externally, though it is not living within them, is signified by the *fine linen at Babylon* (Apocalypse 18:12, 16) and by the clothing of *the rich man* (Luke 16:19). 

Fine linen is also called cotton <note>original: "xylinum." Derived from the Greek word for wood or tree-cloth, referring to the cotton plant.</note>; therefore, genuine truth is also signified by cotton in these passages from the laws of Moses: 

* *Thou shalt weave a tunic of cotton for Aaron; and thou shalt make a mitre of cotton* (Exodus 28:39). 
* *They made tunics of cotton for Aaron and for his sons* (Exodus 39:27). 
* *Thou shalt make the tabernacle of interwoven cotton, and blue, and purple, and double-dyed scarlet* (Exodus 26:1; 36:8). 
* *Thou shalt make hangings for the court of interwoven cotton* (Exodus 27:9, 18; 38:9); and also *the veil of the court with interwoven cotton* (Exodus 38:18).

### 815. 

***For the fine linen is the justice of the saints***, signifies that through truths from the Word those who are of the Lord’s Church have goods of life. By **fine linen** are signified genuine truths, which are truths from the Lord through the Word, as mentioned just above (number 814). By <term>justice</term> <note>original: "justitia." In this context, it refers to "righteousness" or the state of being right with God through one's actions.</note> are signified **goods of life** <note>A technical term in Swedenborg's writing referring to the practical acts of love and charity that a person performs.</note> with those who are in truths (number 668). By "the saints" are signified those who are of the Lord’s Church (numbers 173, 586). 

The reason that **justice** is the **goods of life** with those who are in truths, is because no one can be called just, unless he lives according to truths: for in the natural sense every one is called just, who lives well according to the civil and moral laws; but in the spiritual sense he is called just who lives well according to the Divine laws, and the Divine laws are truths from the Word. 

He who believes himself to be just, and consequently in a good state of life, without truths according to which he lives, is much deceived; for a man cannot be <term>reformed and regenerated</term> <note>The process of spiritual rebirth: reformation is the correction of the intellect, while regeneration is the renewal of the will or heart.</note>, and consequently be made good, except by truths, and by a life according to them. Hence it is manifest, that by "the fine linen is the justice of the saints," it is signified that those who are of the Lord’s Church have goods of life through truths from the Word. This is plainly manifest from the angels of heaven. The more they are in truths and in a life according to them, the brighter the garments in which they appear attired. The reason is, that they are in brighter light.

*He was clothed with a <term>vesture</term> <note>A traditional term for a robe or garment; here it represents the outer "clothing" or literal stories of the Bible.</note> dipped in blood, and His name is called The Word of God.* By “faithful and true” are signified the <term>Divine Good</term> <note>The Lord's infinite love and essence.</note> and the <term>Divine Truth</term> <note>The Lord's infinite wisdom and the way that love is expressed.</note>; by “faithful” is meant the Divine Good, because this is the bedrock of trust. That “faithful,” when speaking of people, means someone who is in the inmost or third heaven—and thus someone who lives in <term>heavenly (celestial) good</term> <note>Swedenborg categorizes heaven into three levels; "celestial" is the highest, where love is the primary motivation.</note>—may be seen above (n. 744). That by "true," when speaking of the Lord, the Divine Truth is signified, is obvious. That by <term>justice</term> <note>original: "justitia," often translated as righteousness.</note> both are signified, both good and truth, and, when speaking of the Lord, the Divine Good and Divine Truth, may be seen above (n. 805). Hence it follows, that by "judging in justice" is signified to carry out judgment based on Divine Good and Divine Truth. That all judgment is carried out by the Lord through the Word, and thus that the Word itself judges everyone, may be seen above (n. 233). That "to make war in justice" signifies to separate the good from the evil, is because the Lord does not literally go to war against anyone, but simply separates the good from the evil: and once the good are separated from the evil, the evil then cast themselves into hell.

822. ***And His eyes were as a flame of fire***: this signifies the Divine Wisdom of the Lord’s Divine Love, as can be seen in the earlier discussion (n. 48), where similar things are mentioned; these are spoken of the <term>Son of Man</term> <note>A title for the Lord specifically emphasizing His role as the Word or Divine Truth.</note>, by whom the Lord in His role as the Word is meant (n. 44).

823. ***And upon His head were many diadems***, signifies the Divine Truths of the Word coming from Him. By “upon His head” is signified anything coming from the Lord, for the head signifies wisdom born from love; just as a person is guided from the head by their own wisdom and love. The <term>diadems</term> <note>Royal crowns or jeweled headbands, representing the beauty and authority of spiritual truths.</note> were seen upon His head because the Divine Truths of the Word, which are signified by the diadems, originate from Him. That diadems signify the Divine Truths of the Word may be seen in sections 231 and 540. That the head, when speaking of the Lord, signifies the Divine Wisdom of the Divine Love, see section 47: for more on what the head signifies, see sections 538 and 568.

In the spiritual world, the <term>Divine Truths</term> <note>Infinite wisdom as expressed by God.</note> of the Word <note>The "Word" refers to the Sacred Scripture or the Bible.</note> correspond to <term>diadems</term> <note>Jeweled crowns or headbands representing the beauty and authority of truth.</note>. They appear there through <term>correspondence</term> <note>The symbolic relationship between a spiritual reality and a physical object; for example, light corresponds to truth.</note>, and are seen in heaven on the heads of those who hold the Word as holy. This is why diadems signify the Divine Truths of the Word in its literal sense: the literal sense shines with light from its inner <term>spiritual</term> and <term>heavenly (celestial)</term> <note>Swedenborg categorizes the Bible's meaning into three levels: literal, spiritual (relating to the soul), and celestial (relating to pure love).</note> meanings, just as a diadem sparkles with light.

*824. Having a name written which no man knew but Himself*, signifies that no one can see the true nature of the Word in its inner spiritual and heavenly meanings except for the Lord, and those to whom He reveals it. A "name" signifies the nature or quality of a person (see reference number 165, and elsewhere); in this case, it refers to the nature of the Word—what the Word is on the inside. It mentions "a name written" because the Word exists among people on earth just as it does among the angels in the heavens (see the work *Doctrine of the New Jerusalem concerning the Sacred Scripture*, numbers 70-75). "No one knowing it but Himself" signifies that no one perceives it except the Lord and those He enlightens. No one can see the spiritual meaning of the Word unless they receive Divine Truths from Him (see *Doctrine of the Sacred Scripture*, number 26).

A "vesture" signifies the truth that "clothes" or protects what is good (see numbers 166, 212, 328); when applied to the Word, it signifies the literal sense, which acts like a garment covering the inner spiritual and heavenly meanings. In the Word <note>The "Word" refers to the Sacred Scripture or the Bible.</note>, blood signifies <term>Divine Truth</term> (see reference numbers 379, 654); therefore, "shedding blood" signifies offering violence to the Lord’s Divinity and to the Word. By the "Word of God" is meant here the Word in its <term>literal sense</term> <note>The plain, surface-level meaning of the text.</note>; for violence has been offered to this literal meaning, but not to the Word in its <term>spiritual sense</term> <note>The deeper, symbolic meaning intended for the soul and the afterlife.</note>. This is because the spiritual sense has been unknown until now; and if it had been known, violence would have been offered to it as well. 

For this reason, that sense was not revealed until after the <term>Last Judgment</term> <note>A spiritual event Swedenborg claimed took place in the spiritual world in 1757, clearing the way for a new era.</note> was accomplished, and a <term>New Church</term> <note>A new spiritual era or "dispensation" of Christian understanding.</note> was to be established by the Lord. Nor is it revealed to anyone today except those who are in Divine Truths from the Lord (see the work *The Doctrine of the New Jerusalem concerning the Sacred Scripture*, number 26). 

That violence has been offered to the Lord’s Divinity and to the Word is clearly evident from the Roman Catholic religion, and from the religion of the <term>Reformed</term> <note>Protestant denominations stemming from the Reformation.</note> concerning <term>faith alone</term> <note>The doctrine that salvation is achieved through belief or "faith" without the necessity of living a life of good works.</note>. The Roman Catholic religion teaches that the Lord’s <term>Human</term> <note>His physical and psychological life as a man on earth.</note> is not Divine; consequently, they have transferred all things belonging to the Lord to themselves. They also claim that the Word is to be interpreted only by them; and their interpretation is everywhere contrary to the Divine Truth of the Word, as was shown in the explanation of chapter 18. It is manifest from this that violence is offered to the Word by that religion. 

In the same way, violence is offered by the religion of the Reformed regarding faith alone. This system also does not acknowledge the Lord’s Human as Divine, and it founds its entire theology upon a single saying of Paul <note>Likely referring to Romans 3:28, "a man is justified by faith without the deeds of the law."</note> which has been falsely understood. Because of this, it treats as nothing all the things which the Lord taught concerning love, charity, and good works—which are nevertheless so prominent in Scripture that anyone, if they only have eyes, can see them. 

The same was done with the Word by the Jews. Their religion held that the Word was written for no one but themselves, and thus that no others are meant within it. They believed that the <term>Messiah</term> <note>The "Anointed One" or Savior.</note> who was to come would exalt them above everyone else in the whole world. By these and many other ideas, they falsified and <term>adulterated</term> <note>Corrupted or polluted the original purity of the truth.</note> everything in the Word. This is what is meant by these words.

# THE APOCALYPSE REVEALED [CHAP. XIX.]

<page-num>948</page-num>

(section 337). By "the mighty," those who possess <term>erudition</term> <note>Deep, scholarly learning or knowledge.</note> from the <term>doctrine</term> <note>The formal teachings and principles derived from sacred texts.</note> of the Word are signified; in an abstract sense, this refers to such learning itself (section 337). By horses, the understanding of the Word is signified; and by "those who sit upon horses," those who possess wisdom from understanding the Word are signified; and abstractly, it refers to that wisdom itself (sections 298, 820). By "the free and bond," those who know truth from their own reflection and those who learn it from others are signified (sections 337, 604). By "the small and the great," those who possess these qualities in a lesser or greater degree are signified (sections 527, 810). 

It is clear from these explanations that "eating their flesh" signifies the <term>appropriation</term> <note>The process of making spiritual values a part of oneself by living according to them.</note> of "goods" <note>In this context, "goods" refers to spiritual benefits, virtues, or the practical application of love and kindness.</note> from the Lord through the truths of the Word and the resulting doctrine in every sense, degree, and kind. It must be understood that no person possesses any spiritual good from the Lord except through the truths of the Word. This is because the truths of the Word exist in the **light of heaven**, and its goods exist in the **heat of that light**. Therefore, unless a person’s understanding is within the sight of heaven through the Word, their will cannot enter into the heat of heaven. 

**Love** and **charity** cannot be formed except through truths from the Word; a person cannot be reformed except through these same truths. The church itself is formed within a person by them—not by these truths existing in the understanding alone, but by a life lived according to them. In this way, truths enter the **will** and become **goods**. Thus, the form of truth is transformed into a form of good; for whatever belongs to the will, and therefore to love, is called "good," and everything belonging to the will or love constitutes a person’s life. 

From this, it can be seen that the "eating of the flesh" of those named here actually means the appropriation of good by means of truths in every sense, degree, and kind from the Lord through the Word. Who cannot see that "flesh" here does not literally mean meat? Who could be so irrational as to believe that the Lord calls and summons everyone to a great supper merely to feed them the literal flesh of kings, commanders of thousands, mighty men, horses, those who sit on them, and the free and the bond?

**833.** *And I saw the beast and the kings of the earth and their armies gathered together to make war with Him that sat upon the horse, and with His army*, signifies that all those who are inwardly evil—specifically those who have claimed that **faith alone** <note>The theological doctrine that salvation comes through belief alone, regardless of a person's actions or "works."</note> is sufficient for salvation—along with their leaders and followers, will struggle against the Lord’s <term>Divine Truths</term> <note>The spiritual wisdom and laws of life contained within the Bible.</note> found in His Word. They will harass and oppose those who belong to the Lord’s New Church. 

The **beast** symbolizes those who belong to a religion focused on faith alone, as previously explained (see sections 567, 576, 577, 594, 598, 601). Below, we will see that this specifically refers to those who are inwardly evil despite their religious profession. The **kings of the earth** signify those who are most deeply rooted in the false ideas of that religion—the leaders. In the Word, "kings" often represent those in the truths of the church, but in an opposite sense, they represent those in <term>falsities</term> <note>Spiritual errors or mistaken beliefs that lead one away from a good life.</note> (see sections 20, 483, 704, 707, 720, 740). Here, it refers to those in errors. 

Their **armies** represent the followers who are likewise caught in these false beliefs (see section 447). To **make war** signifies a spiritual struggle or contention; in the Bible, "war" represents the conflict between false ideas and the truth (see sections 500, 536, 707). **Him that sat upon the horse** refers to the Lord as the Word <note>The horse symbolizes the understanding of the Word; the rider represents the Lord as the source of that understanding.</note> (see sections 820, 821). Since no one can physically fight against the Lord Himself, they fight against His Truths in the Word. Because the Lord *is* the Word, fighting the Scripture is effectively fighting the Lord. Finally, the **army** of the rider signifies those who possess Divine truths—those in the Lord’s New Heaven and New Church (see section 826).

...on faith alone, and who were internally evil. This includes both the everyday people (the laity) and the church leaders and scholars (the clergy). Through complicated arguments and forceful assertions (<note>original: "asseverations"</note>) that **faith alone** is the only way to be saved, they have convinced others to adopt this perspective and live by it. 

In this passage, the **beast** refers to the "beast coming out of the sea" mentioned in <term>Apocalypse</term> <note>The Book of Revelation; from the Greek 'apokalypsis,' meaning an uncovering or revealing.</note> 13:1–10. The **false prophet** refers to the "beast coming out of the earth" from the same chapter, specifically verses 11–18. This matches the description in chapter 13: *that he did great signs before the beast out of the sea, and seduced them that dwell upon the earth, that they should worship his image, and receive his mark upon the right hand and upon the forehead* (verses 12–17). 

From this, it is obvious that the clergy and the learned are symbolized here by the false prophet—those who have convinced themselves of the religion of faith alone and have led the common people astray. They are called a **false prophet** because, in spiritual symbolism, a "prophet" represents those who teach and preach. In this case, it refers to those who preach <term>falsities</term> <note>Spiritual errors or mistaken beliefs that lead one away from a good life.</note> by twisting the true meaning of the <term>Word</term> <note>The Sacred Scripture or Bible.</note> (see sections 8, 701). 

The **signs** performed by that beast symbolize the persuasive reasonings and claims that faith alone is the only means of salvation (see sections 598, 599, 704). Taking the **mark of the beast** and worshipping his **image** signifies the act of acknowledging and fully accepting that faith (see sections 634, 637, 679).

...with brimstone, signifies that all those, exactly as they were, were cast into the hell where the love of falsities and the cravings (<note>original: "lusts"</note>) for evil exist. The term **alive** signifies they were cast in just as they were in their internal state. By these two figures—the **beast** and the **false prophet**—are signified all those who claimed that "faith alone" was the path to salvation while remaining inwardly evil, including both the common people and the church scholars (<note>original: "laity as clergy"</note>), as mentioned previously (n. 834).

It should be understood that the hell where such people dwell appears from a distance like a fiery lake with a green flame, much like burning sulfur. However, those who are actually inside do not see this; they are confined to their workhouses, where they argue with one another or "wrangle" intensely. Sometimes knives appear in their hands, which they use to threaten others if they do not submit. It is their internal love of falsity and their evil cravings that create the outward appearance of such a lake. This appearance is the result of <term>correspondence</term> <note>The spiritual law where a person’s internal state of mind is mirrored by their external environment in the afterlife.</note>.

That a **lake** signifies a place where there is an abundance of truth—and in the opposite sense, an abundance of falsity—is evident from the Word <note>The Bible or Sacred Scripture.</note> in passages where truth is plentiful:

> *From the wilderness shall waters break forth and rivers in the plain of the desert, and the dry place shall become a lake* (Isaiah 35:6, 7).
> *I will make the wilderness a lake of waters, and the dry land springs of waters* (Isaiah 41:18; Psalms 107:33, 35).

## CHAPTER TWENTIETH.

1. And I saw an angel coming down from heaven having the key of the abyss, <note>In Swedenborg's interpretation, the "abyss" represents a state of deep spiritual confusion and the "key" signifies the power of divine truth to reveal or conceal these states.</note> and a great chain in his hand.
2. And he laid hold on the dragon, <note>The "dragon" is a symbolic term for those who possess the Word of God but separate faith from a life of charity or good works.</note> the old serpent, which is the Devil and Satan, <note>Swedenborg distinguishes between the two: "the Devil" refers to those motivated by evil love, while "Satan" refers to those motivated by false thinking.</note> and bound him a thousand years;
3. And cast him into the abyss, and shut him up, and set a seal upon him, that he should seduce the nations no more until the thousand years were ended: and after this he must be loosed a little time.

"And he laid hold on the dragon, the old serpent, which is the devil and satan," *signifies* that those were held back who are meant by the dragon; who, because they think sensually <note>focused on physical senses and outward appearances rather than spiritual reality</note> and not spiritually concerning the things of faith, are called the old Serpent; and because they are in evils as to life, are called the Devil; and because they are in falsities as to doctrine, are called Satan.

"And cast him into the abyss, and shut him up, and set a seal upon him, that he should seduce the nations no more," *signifies* that the Lord altogether removed those who were in <term>faith alone</term>, <note>The theological position that salvation is achieved through belief only, without the necessity of good works.</note> and took away all their communication with others, lest they should inspire something of their heresy into those who would be elevated into heaven.

"Until the thousand years were ended; and after this he must be loosed a little time," *signifies* that this is for a while or for some time, until they who were in truths from good <note>those whose intellectual understanding of truth is united with a heart that desires what is good</note> should be taken up into heaven by the Lord, after which they who are meant by the dragon are to be loosed a short time, and communication with others is to be opened to them.

"And I saw thrones, and they sat upon them, and judgment was given unto them," *signifies* that the truths of the Word, according to which all are judged, were opened; and that then those were taken up from the <term>lower earth</term>, <note>A region of the spiritual world where many were "kept concealed" or protected until the corrupting influences of the dragon were removed.</note> who had been kept concealed by the Lord, lest they should be seduced by the dragon and his beasts.

"And [I saw] the souls of them that were beheaded for the testimony of Jesus, and for the Word of God," *signifies* those who were rejected by them that are in falsities from their own intelligence, <note>the tendency to trust one's own reasoning over divine revelation</note> because they worshipped the Lord, and lived according to the truths of His Word.

...the great chain in His hand signifies the effort and the resulting act of binding and releasing. From this, it follows that there was no literal key or chain in the Lord’s hand; rather, its appearance to John was a <term>representative</term> <note>In this context, a "representative" is a symbolic vision shown to a prophet that mirrors a deeper spiritual reality or divine action.</note> of the Lord’s Divine Power. The opening and closing of hell is also discussed several times in this chapter.

841. **And he seized the dragon, that ancient serpent, who is the devil and Satan,** signifies that those meant by the "dragon" were restrained. They are called the **ancient serpent** because they think <term>sensually</term> <note>To think "sensually" means to rely entirely on the physical senses and outward appearances, making it impossible to understand deeper spiritual truths.</note> and not spiritually regarding matters of faith. They are called the **Devil** because their lives are rooted in evil, and they are called **Satan** because their doctrines are rooted in <term>falsities</term> <note>A "falsity" is a spiritual error or a corrupted truth that is used to justify wrong behavior.</note>. The identity of those meant by the "dragon" can be seen above (no. 537). The reason he is called the ancient Serpent, the Devil, and Satan here (as he was previously) is because a "serpent" signifies those who think sensually rather than spiritually (nos. 455, 550); the "devil" signifies those who live evilly; and "satan" signifies those who follow false doctrines (nos. 97, 550).

For everyone who does not go directly to the Lord thinks sensually about church matters and is unable to think spiritually. This is because the Lord is light itself (nos. 796, 797). Consequently, those who do not go directly to the Lord cannot think from <term>spiritual light</term> (which is the light of heaven), but only from natural light separated from spiritual light—which is what it means to think sensually. This is why they are called the "ancient Serpent." Those who do not go directly to the Lord, nor avoid evils as sins, remain in their sins; this is why the dragon is called the "Devil." And because these same people hold false doctrines, the dragon is called "Satan."

842. **And bound him a thousand years,** signifies that those meant by the "dragon" were withdrawn and separated from everyone else in the <term>world of spirits</term>, so that there would be no communication with them for a certain period of time. In this context, "binding" signifies to draw back and...

...separating them from everyone else in the spiritual world so that no communication with them remains, as will be seen in the following paragraph. The reason that the **thousand years** does not mean a literal thousand years, but rather "for a while" or "for some time," is because in the spiritual world, a "thousand"—when not added to other numbers—signifies a general period of time. 

Anyone who believes that a thousand years literally means a thousand years does not realize that all numbers in the Word <note>Swedenborg refers to the Bible as "the Word."</note> signify specific spiritual qualities or concepts. Without this understanding, a reader can be easily misled regarding the meaning of the things described in the Apocalypse where numbers appear, such as 5, 7, 10, 12, 144, 666, 1200, 1600, 12000, 144000, and many others. In these larger numbers, "a thousand" acts as a qualifier; when applied to time, it signifies a general duration. When mentioned alone, as it is here, it simply means "for a while." 

I have been informed of this directly from heaven. In the version of the Word used by angels, no literal numbers are read; instead, the spiritual concept behind the number is perceived. Where we see "a thousand," they perceive "for a while." The inhabitants of heaven find it strange that even though members of the church have seen so many numbers in the Apocalypse that clearly must have symbolic meanings, they have still clung to the guesses of the <term>chiliasts</term> <note>From the Greek "chilioi" (a thousand); another name for millennialists who believe in a literal thousand-year reign of Christ on earth.</note> or **millennialists**. By doing so, they have developed empty and mistaken ideas about the final state of the church.

843. **And cast him into the abyss, and shut him up, and set a seal upon him, that he might seduce the nations no more,** signifies that the Lord completely removed those who were in <term>faith alone</term> <note>The doctrine that salvation is granted by belief alone, regardless of a person’s actions or moral life.</note> and took away all their ability to communicate with others. This was done to prevent them from spreading their false ideas to those who were being prepared for heaven. 

By the **dragon**, those who hold false views of faith are meant here, as mentioned just above (n. 842). It is written that the dragon was "seized, bound, cast into the abyss, shut up, and sealed." This series of actions signifies that he was entirely removed and all communication between him and others was cut off. His being "seized" signifies that...

Those who are represented by the dragon were gathered together and restrained: his being **bound** signifies that they were withdrawn and separated; his being **cast into the abyss** signifies that they were lowered down toward hell; his being **shut up** signifies that they were completely removed; and a **seal being set upon him** signifies that all communication with others was entirely cut off. 

The reason that the dragon was completely removed for a time is so that those who had been kept hidden by the Lord might be taken up from the **lower earth** <note>In Swedenborg's theology, the "lower earth" is a specific region in the spiritual world where well-disposed souls were protected until they could be safely raised to heaven.</note>. These individuals are the subject of verses 4–6. This removal was necessary so they would not be seduced by the **dragonists** <note>Those who believe in the doctrine of "faith alone" without the necessity of a good life.</note> while they were being taken up. This is why the text says, "that he should seduce the nations no more," which signifies that he should not inspire them with any part of his **heresy** <note>Specifically the "heresy" of separating faith from charity/works.</note>. 

This process occurred in the <term>world of spirits</term> <note>A middle region between heaven and hell where every person arrives immediately after death to be prepared for their final destination.</note>, because it is there that the evil interact with the good. In that world, the good are prepared for heaven and the evil for hell; the good are tested by some degree of companionship with the evil, exploring their true character and how steadfast they remain. By the **nations** which were not to be seduced, the "good" are meant. That those who are in a state of "good" regarding their life are meant by "nations"—and in the opposite sense, the "evil"—may be seen in the earlier discussion (n. 483). From this it is clear that casting him into the abyss, shutting him up, and setting a seal upon him signifies that the Lord completely removed those who were in **falsities of faith** and took away all their communication with others, lest they should influence those being taken up into heaven with their heresy.

844. ***Until the thousand years should be ended, and after this he must be loosed a little time***, signifies that this state lasts for a while or for some time, until those who were in truths derived from a good life should be taken up into heaven by the Lord; after which, those represented by the dragon are to be released for a short time, and communication with others is to be opened again.
