### 845. 
*And I saw thrones, and they sat upon them, and judgment was given unto them*, signifies that the truths of the **Word** <note>The Holy Scripture or Bible, viewed here as the ultimate standard of divine truth.</note>, according to which everyone is judged, were opened. It further signifies that those who had been kept hidden by the Lord in the **lower earth** <note>In this theology, a protected region in the spiritual world where good people were kept safe from the influence of those with false doctrines until the Last Judgment.</note>—to prevent them from being led astray by the dragon and his **beasts** <note>Symbolic figures representing various false religious justifications and worldly powers.</note>—were then taken up into heaven. 

These words carry this meaning because the **thrones** seen in the vision do not represent literal chairs of state, but rather the process of judgment according to the truths of the Word. That judgment is represented by thrones seen in heaven has been discussed previously (n. 229). Furthermore, the same meaning applies to the thrones upon which the twenty-four elders sat, and those upon which the twelve Apostles are said to sit; all people are judged according to the truths found in the Word (n. 233). 

From this, it is evident that "judgment being given to them" signifies that authority was given to the truths of the Word. Those taken up from the lower earth into heaven by the Lord are the ones who had been kept concealed there in the meantime, so they would not be deceived by the dragonists. This is said concerning the "souls of them that were beheaded" and the "dead," as described in the following lines; this does not mean they were truly dead in themselves, but rather they were considered "dead" or were invisible to the eyes of others in the spiritual world. The place where they were kept hidden is called the **lower earth** <term>lower earth (Latin: terra inferior): In this theological system, a region in the spiritual world situated between heaven and hell where the faithful were protected before the Last Judgment.</term>, which is located directly above the various hells and beneath the world of spirits. There, through their communication with heaven and their connection with the Lord, they remain in safety. There are many such regions; those who dwell there live happily among themselves and worship the Lord, completely unaware of the existence of hell. These inhabitants are, from time to time, taken up by the Lord into heaven following a **last judgment** <term>Last Judgment: Here referring to a spiritual event that reorganizes the afterlife, separating the good from the evil.</term>. When they are raised up, those represented by the **dragon** <note>original: "draco"; a symbol for those who possess religious knowledge or "faith" but lack a life of practical love or charity.</note> are removed. It has very often been granted to me to witness them being taken up and joined with the angels in heaven. This is what is meant in the **Word** <note>The Holy Scriptures or the Bible.</note> by the descriptions of graves being opened and the dead being raised.

### 846.
**And [I saw] the souls of them that were beheaded for the testimony of Jesus and for the Word of God, signifies** those who were rejected by people who dwell in false beliefs stemming from their own intelligence, because they worshipped the Lord and lived according to the truths of His Word. By "the souls of them that were beheaded for the testimony of Jesus and for the Word of God," the text means people who have died and are now spirits—men and women clothed in spiritual bodies—who have been kept hidden by the Lord in the lower earth until the evil were removed by the last judgment. 

They are described as **beheaded** <note>The Latin term implies being "smitten with an axe." In a spiritual sense, this refers to being cut off or rejected by those who rely on self-derived intelligence rather than divine truth.</note> because they are rejected by those who hold false ideas based on their own cleverness. These "beheaders" are all those who live in evil and consequently believe what is false (or vice versa), even while maintaining the outward appearance of divine worship. That this specific type of falsity is symbolized by the "axe" will be explained in the next paragraph. 

By the **testimony of Jesus** and the **Word of God** is signified the acknowledgment of the Lord's **Divine Human** <term>Divine Human: The doctrine that Jesus Christ's humanity is itself Divine, making Him the visible God in whom the invisible Divine resides.</term>, just as in these earlier passages: 

*   *John testified the Word of God and the testimony of Jesus Christ* (Apoc. i. 2). 
*   *Michael and his angels overcame the dragon by the blood of the Lamb and the Word of their testimony* (xii. 11). 
*   *The dragon went away to make war with the remnant of her seed, who*

<meta>This page continues the explanation of Revelation Chapter 20, specifically defining the spiritual meanings of "blessedness" and "holiness" and clarifying that the "second death" refers to spiritual damnation rather than physical passing.</meta>

<page-num>981</page-num>

# THE APOCALYPSE REVEALED.

...*whoever believes in Me shall never die* (John xi. 25, 26). <note>original: "Me, shall never die"</note> That these things are meant by the first resurrection is also clear from the following verse.

**852.** *Blessed and holy is he that hath part in the first resurrection*, signifies that those who enter heaven experience the happiness of eternal life and are enlightened through their **conjunction** <term>Conjunction: A spiritual union or heart-to-heart connection with the Divine.</term> with the Lord. A person is called "blessed" if they possess the happiness of eternal life (n. 639); and they are called "holy" if they have received enlightenment in Divine truths through their connection with the Lord. This is because the Lord alone is Holy, and the **Divine proceeding** <term>Divine proceeding: The spiritual influence or "emanation" that flows from the Lord, similar to how light and heat flow from the sun.</term> from Him—which provides this enlightenment—is what is known as the **Holy Spirit** (n. 173, 586, 666). The "first resurrection" signifies being raised into heaven by the Lord, and thus, salvation (as mentioned in n. 851). Therefore, it is clear that being "blessed and holy" means that those who enter heaven receive eternal happiness and spiritual light from the Lord.

**853.** *Upon these the second death hath no power*, signifies that they are not condemned. The "second death" refers exclusively to **spiritual death**, which is damnation. The first death is natural death—the death of the physical body—but the second death is the death of the soul. It is well known that this second death is damnation. Because the second death is damnation and the first death is simply the end of physical life (which is not a spiritual death), the term "first death" is never actually used in the **Apocalypse** <note>The Book of Revelation.</note>. However, the "second death" is mentioned again in this chapter at verse 14, in the next chapter (xxi. 8), and previously in chapter ii. 11. If a reader does not notice this distinction, they might mistakenly believe there are two different types of spiritual death because a "second" one is mentioned; yet there is only one spiritual death. In the same way, one might think there are two literal resurrections because a "first" one is mentioned, when in fact there is only one true resurrection. For this reason, a "second resurrection" is never mentioned.

**854.** *But they shall be priests of God and of Christ,* signifies that they are kept by the Lord in the **good of love** <term>Good of love: The heartfelt impulse to act with kindness and charity, which flows into a person from the Divine.</term> and consequently in the **truths of wisdom**. <term>Truths of wisdom: The spiritual insights and understanding that provide a "map" for living a good life.</term> By "priests" in the **Word** <note>original: "Verbo"; in this context, the "Word" refers to the Holy Scriptures or the Bible.</note> are meant those who live in the good of love, and by "kings" those who live in the truths of wisdom. For this reason, it was stated previously that *Jesus Christ hath made us kings and priests* (Apoc. i. 6); and likewise, *the Lamb hath made us kings and priests, that we may reign upon the earth* (v. 10). It can be clearly seen that the Lord will not literally make men into kings and priests; rather, He will make angels out of those who receive truths of wisdom and the good of love from Him. 

That those who possess truths of wisdom from the Lord are meant by "kings," and that the Lord is called a "King" because of His **Divine Truth**, <note>Divine Truth: The light of heaven, which provides clarity and order.</note> may be seen in earlier sections (n. 20, 483, 664, 830). However, the reason those in the good of love from the Lord are meant by "priests" is because the Lord is both Divine Love and Divine Wisdom—or, what is the same thing, **Divine Good** and Divine Truth. The Lord is called a "Priest" from His Divine Love or Divine Good, and a "King" from His Divine Wisdom or Divine Truth. 

Because of this, the heavens are distinguished into two specific kingdoms: the **heavenly (celestial)** <term>Celestial: The highest level of heaven, characterized by a direct, heart-based love for the Lord.</term> and the **spiritual**. <term>Spiritual: The level of heaven characterized by an intellectual love for the neighbor and for truth.</term> The heavenly (celestial) kingdom is called the Lord’s **priestly kingdom**, for the angels there are recipients of Divine Love or Divine Good from the Lord. The spiritual kingdom is called the Lord’s **royal kingdom**, for the angels there are recipients of Divine Wisdom or Divine Truth from the Lord (for more on these two kingdoms, see n. 647, 725). 

It is said that they are "recipients" of Divine Good and Divine Truth from the Lord, but it must be understood that they are **perpetually recipients**. <note>This suggests a continuous flow; goodness and wisdom are not a permanent possession of the angel, but a constant gift from the Lord, like light from a sun.</note> Divine Good and Divine Truth cannot be "appropriated" by any angel or man so as to belong to them as their own; they are only held so that...

855. ***And they shall reign with Him a thousand years***, signifies that they were already in heaven, while the rest who did not yet "live again"—meaning they had not yet received heavenly life—remained in the **world of spirits**. <term>World of spirits: A transitional region in the spiritual realm where people reside immediately after death before moving to heaven or hell.</term> To "reign with Christ" does not mean to exercise worldly power or rule alongside Him, but rather to be integrated into His kingdom, which is heaven; see above (nos. 284, 849). Those who do not understand that the num<note>Page edge cut off: numbers</note>bers in the **Apocalypse** <note>original: "Apocalypsi"; the Book of Revelation.</note> refer to spiritual qualities rather than quantities will find these things difficult to grasp. I can state with certainty that angels do not perceive numbers in a natural way as humans do, but rather spiritually; in fact, they do not recognize what a "thousand years" is, only that it represents a certain interval of time, whether short or long, which can only be described as "for a while."

The phrase "when the thousand years were ended" signifies the point after those who were guarded in the lower earth were raised to heaven by the Lord. ### 859.
That those who are in external worship and not in any internal worship are meant by **Gog and Magog**, may be evident in the book of **Ezekiel**, from chapter 38, where Gog is treated of from the beginning to the end; and from chapter 39, verses 1–16. But that those groups are signified by Gog and Magog is not clearly manifest there except through the **spiritual sense** <term>Spiritual Sense: The deeper, symbolic meaning of the Bible that lies beneath the literal stories and historical accounts.</term>, which, as it has been disclosed to me, shall be opened: first, what the things that are contained in these two chapters signify. 

In the thirty-eighth chapter of Ezekiel: Those are treated of who are in the **literal sense of the Word** only, and in worship which is external without an internal, who are Gog (verses 1, 2): that each and every thing of that worship is to perish (verses 3–7): that that worship will take possession of the church, and **vastate** <term>Vastate: To empty a church or an individual of all genuine spiritual truth and goodness, leaving only the outward shell of religion.</term> it; and so it will be in externals without internals (verses 8–16): that the state of the church will thereby be changed (verses 17–19): that thence the truths and goods of religion will perish, and falsities succeed (verses 20–23).

(verses 20-23). The thirty-ninth chapter of the same book [Ezekiel] treats of those who focus only on the literal sense of the **Word** <note>The "Word" refers to the Sacred Scriptures or the Bible.</note> and on external forms of worship. It describes how they will enter the church represented by **Gog**, but will ultimately perish (verses 1-6). This will occur when the Lord comes and establishes a Church (verses 7-8). This new church will then cast away all their evils and false beliefs (verses 9, 10) and will completely destroy them (verses 11-16). The **New Church** <term>New Church: In Swedenborg's theology, this refers to a new spiritual era or "dispensation" of Christianity based on genuine love and the recognition of the Lord's divinity.</term> to be established by the Lord will be taught in truths and goods of every kind, and will be filled with goodness (verses 17-21). Meanwhile, the former church will be destroyed because of its evils and false teachings (verses 23, 24). Finally, a church will be gathered by the Lord from all nations (verses 25-29).

But something must be said regarding those who practice **external worship** <term>External Worship: Religious practice consisting only of outward rituals, ceremonies, and literal obedience, without an internal spiritual connection.</term> without **internal spiritual worship**. These are people who frequent churches on the Sabbath and festival days; they sing psalms and pray at such times; they listen to the preaching and pay attention to the preacher's eloquence, but pay little, if any, attention to the actual spiritual matter. They are somewhat moved by prayers uttered with feeling—such as when they confess they are "sinners"—yet they do not reflect at all upon themselves or their actual conduct. They also receive the **Sacrament of the Supper** <term>Also known as Holy Communion or the Eucharist.</term> once a year; they offer prayers morning and evening, and pray also at dinner and supper. They sometimes speak about God, heaven, and eternal life, and they know how to quote certain passages from the Word at those times to appear like Christians, even though they are not.

For after they have done all these things, they think nothing of committing adultery and obscenities, of seeking revenge and harboring hatred, or of committing secret thefts and robberies <note>original: "depredations"</note>, lies, and slander. They indulge in all kinds of **concupiscences** <term>Concupiscences: Strong, selfish desires or lusts that drive a person toward evil actions.</term> and evil intentions. People of such a character do not truly believe in any God, much less in the Lord. If they are asked what the "good" and "truth" of religion actually are, they do not know at all, and they do not believe it is of much importance that they should know. In a word, they live only for themselves.

865. **And I saw a great white throne, and Him that sat upon it, from whose face the heaven and the earth fled away**, signifies a **universal judgment** <note>A final, comprehensive assessment of all people in the spiritual world.</note> executed by the Lord upon all the **first heavens** <note>In this context, temporary spiritual realms formed by those who were not yet ready for their final destination.</note>, in which were those who were in **civil and moral good** <note>Living according to the laws of society and basic ethics, but without a genuine spiritual motivation or love for God.</note> and no **spiritual good** <note>Goodness that comes from a sincere faith and love for the Lord.</note>, and who thus simulated Christians in externals, but were devils in internals; which heavens with their earth were utterly dissipated, so that nothing of them appeared any more. Before these things are explained in order according to the letter, something is to be premised concerning the universal judgment which is here treated of. From the time when the Lord was in the world, when He executed a last judgment in person, it has been permitted that those who were in civil and moral good, although in no spiritual good, whence they appeared in externals like Christians, but in internals were devils, should remain longer than the rest in the **world of spirits** <note>A middle region between heaven and hell where people go immediately after death for preparation.</note>, which is midway between heaven and hell: and it was at length granted them to make for themselves homes there, and likewise, by the abuse of **correspondences** <note>term: the relationship between spiritual causes and natural effects; here, used deceptively to mimic heavenly appearances.</note> and by **fantasies** <note>term: the use of imagination or spiritual "illusions" to create deceptive environments.</note>, to form for themselves as it were heavens; which also they formed in great abundance. In like manner, take away affection from thought, and there is nothing of thought left. ...was permitted to enter, and it was said that it was <note>Continuing from the previous page: it was said that his wisdom was "almost nothing."</note>. I therefore ascended; and when I entered, I saw what appeared to be **cherubs** <note>In this context, symbolic figures representing the protection and providence of the divine</note> flying under the roof, though they soon vanished. The floor upon which we walked was made of cedar; and the entire temple, because the roof and walls were transparent, seemed to be built of light itself.

The **angelic spirit** entered with me, and I told him what I had heard from the two angels regarding love and wisdom, as well as charity and faith. He then asked, "Did they not speak of a third also?" I said, "What third?" He answered:

"It is *Use*: love and wisdom without use are not anything. They are only <term>ideal entities: things that exist only as concepts or thoughts in the mind, lacking physical or actual reality</term>; nor do they become real until they are in use. For love, wisdom, and use are three things which cannot be separated. If they are separated, none of them remains. Love is not anything without wisdom, but within wisdom, it is shaped for something. This 'something' for which it is shaped is **use**. Therefore, when love, through wisdom, exists in use, it then becomes something; indeed, it only then truly exists.

They are exactly like the **end**, the **cause**, and the **effect** <note>A classic philosophical triad: the 'end' is the goal, the 'cause' is the method, and the 'effect' is the result. One cannot exist in reality without the others</note>. The goal (the end) is nothing unless it reaches the result (the effect) through the method (the cause). If one of the three is removed, the whole structure collapses and becomes nothing. It is the same with charity, faith, and works. Charity without faith is nothing; nor is faith anything without charity; nor are charity and faith anything without works. But in **works** they become something, and their quality depends on the usefulness of those works. 

It is the same with affection, thought, and operation; and it is the same with will, understanding, and action. That this is true may be seen clearly in this temple, because the light we are in here is a light that enlightens the inner reaches of the mind. Geometry also teaches that a thing is not complete and perfect unless it is a <term>trine: a threefold set or a trinity of parts making a whole</term>. For a line is nothing unless it becomes an area; and an area is nothing unless it becomes a solid. For this reason, one must be produced into the other so that they may exist; and they co-exist in the third. As it is in geometry, so it is in the spiritual life."

<summary>In this vision, the narrator enters a transparent temple where an angelic spirit explains that spiritual concepts like love and wisdom are incomplete until they are manifested as "use" or practical action. Using the logic of "end, cause, and effect," the text argues that faith and charity only become real when expressed through good works.</summary>

These flow in from God and are received by a person, and they are felt by the person as if they were within them. Because they are felt this way, they also seem to proceed from the person. 876. ***And I saw a New Heaven and a New Earth***, signifies that a New Heaven was formed by the Lord from Christians, which at this day is called the Christian Heaven, where those are who worshipped the Lord, and lived according to His precepts in the Word, who thence have <term>charity and faith<note>In this context, charity is the desire to do good for others, and faith is the inner recognition of truth from the Lord.</note></term>; in which heaven are also all the infants of Christians. By a New Heaven and a New Earth, is not meant a natural heaven visible before the eyes, nor a natural earth inhabited by men; but a spiritual heaven and the earth of that heaven, where the angels are, is meant. That this heaven and the earth of that heaven are meant, every one sees and acknowledges, if he can only be withdrawn somewhat from merely natural and material ideas, when he reads the Word. That an angelic heaven is meant, is manifest; because in the verse next following it is said that he saw the holy city New Jerusalem coming down from God out of heaven, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband; by which is not meant any Jerusalem coming down, but a Church: and the church on earth descends from the Lord out of the angelic heaven, because the angels of heaven and the men of the earth in all things of the church make one (<note>Original: "n. 626," referring to section number 626 in this same work.</note>). It may be seen from this, how naturally and materially they have thought and do think, who from these words and those that follow in this verse have framed for themselves the <term>dogma<note>A fixed set of beliefs; here referring to the traditional religious view of "Judgment Day" or the physical end of the world.</note></term> concerning the destruction of the world and a new creation of all things. This New Heaven has been several times treated of above in the Apocalypse, especially in chapters xiv. and xv. It is called the Christian Heaven, because it is distinct from the ancient heavens, which existed from the men of the church before the coming of the Lord. These ancient heavens are above the Christian Heaven; for the heavens are like expanses one above another, and in like manner

878. ***And the sea was no more***, signifies that the <term>external of heaven<note>In Swedenborg’s vision, heaven is layered; the "external" is the outer or most basic level, inhabited by those who lived good lives but understood religious truths only in a simple, literal way.</note></term> collected from Christians since the first establishment of the Church—after those were taken out and saved who were written in the Lord’s <term>book of life<note>A symbolic record of those whose inner lives are in harmony with divine love and truth.</note></term>—was in like manner dissipated. By the sea the external of heaven and the church is signified, in which are the simple, who have thought respecting the things of the Church naturally, and very little spiritually. The heaven in which these are, is called external (see n. 238, 239, 403, 404, 420, 466, 470, 659, 661). Here the external of the heaven that was collected from Christians since the first establishment of the Church, is meant by the sea.

But the internal of the heaven from Christians was not fully formed by the Lord earlier than some before the last judgment, and likewise after it; as may be evident from chap. xiv. and xv., where that is treated of; and from chap. xx., vers. 4, 5: see the explanations. The reason that it was not formed sooner was that the <term>dragon<note>The "dragon" symbolizes those in the church who separate faith from a life of charity (good works).</note></term> and his two beasts had dominion in the <term>world of spirits<note>The "world of spirits" is an intermediate state between heaven and hell where everyone first goes after death to be prepared for their final home.</note></term>, and burned with the lust of seducing whomsoever they could; on which account there was danger in collecting them into any heaven before. 

The separation of the good from the <term>dragonists<note>A term for those who follow the "dragon" theology, prioritizing intellectual belief over moral living.</note></term>, and the damnation of the latter, and at length their rejection into hell, are treated of in many places, and at last in chap. xix., vers. 20, and in chap. xx., vers. 10; and after this it is said that ***the sea gave up the dead in it*** (vers. 13); by which are meant the external and natural men of the church convoked to judgment, see above (n. 869): and those were then taken out and saved, who were written in the Lord’s book of life; which subject also is treated of there: it is this sea which is here meant. Elsewhere also, where the New Heaven is treated of, it is said that it extended to the ***sea of glass mingled with fire*** (chap. xv. 2); by which sea the external of the heaven from Christians is also signified, see the explanation (n. 659–661). The reason that "thirsting" signifies a desire for spiritual use is because there are two kinds of desire for the knowledge of truth from the Word: one from "natural use" and one from "spiritual use." A "natural use" is found in those who seek learning for the sake of their own ends, such as fame, honor, and profit—focusing on themselves and the world. However, a "spiritual use" is found in those who seek to serve their neighbor out of love for them, seeking the good of their neighbor's soul and their own, for the sake of the Lord and salvation. To these people, as much truth as is needed for that service is given from the fountain of the water of life—that is, from the Lord through the Word. To others, truth is not given. They may read the Word, but they either fail to see any doctrinal truth or, if they do, they turn it into <term>falsity</term> <note>Falsity is not just a mistake, but a distortion of truth to fit one's own selfish desires.</note>; this happens not so much in the words they repeat from the text, but in the underlying ideas in their thoughts. That "to hunger" signifies a desire for what is good, and "to thirst" signifies a desire for what is true, may be seen in sections 323 and 381.

By **liars** are signified those who live in falsehoods that spring from evil intentions (section 924).

898. ***Having a wall great and high***, signifies the <term>Word</term> <note>The "Word" refers to the Holy Scripture or Bible.</note> in the <term>literal sense</term> <note>The "literal sense" is the plain, grammatical meaning of the Bible's text, as opposed to its hidden spiritual meaning.</note> from which the doctrine of the New Church is derived. When the Lord’s New Church, in terms of its teachings, is represented by the holy city Jerusalem, its "wall" signifies nothing other than the Word in its literal sense. This is because the literal sense protects the <term>spiritual sense</term> <note>The internal or symbolic meaning that Swedenborg believes lies hidden within the physical words of the Bible.</note> which lies hidden within, just as a wall protects a city and its inhabitants. That the literal sense is the basis, the container, and the support of the spiritual sense, may be seen in the work *Doctrine of the New Jerusalem concerning the Sacred Scripture* (sections 27-36). It is also shown there that this literal sense serves as a guard, preventing the interior Divine Truths—those of the spiritual sense—from being violated or injured (section 97). Furthermore, the doctrine of the church must be drawn from the literal sense of the Word and confirmed by it (sections 50-61). 

It is called a **"wall great and high"** because the Word is described here in terms of Divine Good and Divine Truth; for in the symbolic language of the Bible, "great" refers to good, and "high" refers to truth, as mentioned previously (section 896). A wall signifies that which protects; and when speaking of the church, it signifies the Word in its literal sense, as seen in the following passages:

*Jehovah will be a wall of fire round about, and a glory in the midst of her* (Zechariah 2:5).

*Run to and fro through the streets of Jerusalem, and see if there is any that seeketh truth; go up on her walls, and cast down* (Jeremiah 5:1, 10). 

*Jehovah hath purposed to destroy the wall of the daughter of Zion, He made the rampart and the wall to*... <note>The text breaks off here as the author prepares to discuss the destruction of the wall as a symbol of the loss of the Word's protection.</note>

<meta>This page continues the detailed symbolic interpretation of the New Jerusalem’s architecture from Revelation 21. -># No. 902.] THE APOCALYPSE REVEALED. 1047<-

The gates signify the <term>knowledges</term> <note>From the Latin *cognitiones*: these are the specific spiritual facts or insights learned from the Word that allow a person to enter into a deeper understanding of faith.</note> of truth and good, through which introduction into the New Church is made possible, as can be seen above (n. 899). There were three gates on the east, three on the north, three on the south, and three on the west, because love and an affection for what is good in a higher degree is signified by the east—meaning "more"—while the west signifies love and affection for good in a lower degree—meaning "less." Similarly, wisdom and an affection for truth in a higher degree is signified by the south ("more"), and the north signifies wisdom and affection for truth in a lower degree ("less"). 

These things are signified by the east, west, south, and north because the Lord is the Sun of the spiritual world. In front of Him are the east and the west, and on His sides are the south and north; the south is on the right side, and the north is on the left. Therefore, those who are more in love toward the Lord (and consequently in a state of affection) dwell in the east, while those who are less so dwell in the west. Those who are more in wisdom derived from an affection for truth dwell in the south, and those who are less so dwell in the north. That the homes of the angels of heaven are arranged in such an order may be seen in the work *Heaven and Hell*, published in London, 1758 (numbers 141–153). There were three gates facing each direction because the number three signifies "all" or "completeness" (n. 400, 505).

902. ***And the wall of the city having twelve foundations, signifies that the Word in the literal sense contains all things of the doctrine of the New Church.*** By the wall of the city is signified the **Word** <note>The "Word" refers to the Sacred Scriptures or the Bible.</note> in its literal sense (n. 898), and by the twelve foundations are signified all aspects of the church’s doctrine. Foundations represent <term>doctrinals</term> <note>The formal teachings or principles of a religious system.</note>, and the number twelve represents "all." The church is founded upon doctrine because doctrine teaches how one must believe and how one must live. Furthermore, this doctrine must be drawn from no other source than the **Word**; that it is derived specifically from the <term>literal sense</term> <note>The plain, surface-level meaning of the biblical text, which Swedenborg argues serves as the necessary foundation for all spiritual interpretation.</note> of the **Word** may be seen in the *Doctrine of the New Jerusalem respecting the Sacred Scripture*.

**903.** *And in them the names of the twelve apostles of the Lamb,* signifies all aspects of the church's teaching (its <term>doctrine</term> <note>From the Latin *doctrina*: the systematic body of teachings or principles held by the church, specifically those drawn from the Bible.</note>) derived from the Word concerning the Lord and a life lived according to His precepts. The reason the names of the **twelve apostles of the Lamb** were written on the foundations is that the Lord’s church, in all its various aspects, is represented by the twelve apostles (see points 79, 233, 790). In this specific context, they represent all elements of its doctrine, because their names were written upon the **twelve foundations**, which represent every part of the teaching of the **New Jerusalem** (point 902). 

By the **twelve names**, the text signifies the total quality or character of the church. This quality is centered on two fundamental principles within the doctrine and the church itself: knowledge concerning the Lord, and a life lived according to His precepts. These, therefore, are what the names represent. 

The reason all teachings of the **New Church** point back to these two principles is that they are its <term>universals</term> <note>In this context, "universals" refers to the broad, overarching principles that apply to every specific detail of a system.</note>, upon which every specific detail depends. They are its <term>essentials</term> <note>The "essentials" are the core components or "heart" of the matter, without which the church cannot exist.</note>, from which all formal structures emerge. Thus, they are like the soul and the life within all the church's teachings. They are indeed two distinct things, but one cannot be separated from the other; for to separate them would be like trying to separate the Lord from humanity, or humanity from the Lord—and in such a state, there is no church. 

These two principles are joined together like the **two tables of the law** <note>This refers to the two stone tablets of the Ten Commandments given to Moses.</note>. One table contains the things that belong to the Lord, and the other contains the things that belong to man. This is why they are called a **covenant**, and a covenant signifies a <term>conjunction</term> <note>The spiritual union or "joining together" of the Divine and the human through mutual love and obedience.</note> or binding together. Consider what would happen to these tables of the law if only the first one existed and the second were removed, or if the second existed and the first were removed. Would it not be as if God did not see man, or as if man did not see God, and as if they both moved away from each other? These points are made so that it may be understood that all teachings of the New Jeru-

-># [No. 903 cont.] THE APOCALYPSE REVEALED. [CHAP. XXI]<-

...salem relate to love for the Lord and love for one’s neighbor. Loving the Lord means having faith in Him and following His <term>precepts</term> <note>From the Latin *praecepta*: specific rules or instructions for living, such as the Ten Commandments.</note>, and following His precepts is the same as loving one's neighbor; for to follow His precepts is to perform useful services for others. That those who follow His precepts are the ones who truly love the Lord is taught by the Lord Himself in the Gospel of John (14:21–24). Furthermore, love for God and love for one's neighbor are the two commandments upon which "hang all the Law and the Prophets" (Matthew 22:35–38). By the phrase **the Law and the Prophets**, the text refers to the Word in its entire complexity.

**904.** ***And he that spake with me had a golden reed to measure the city and the gates thereof and the wall thereof,*** signifies that the Lord grants those who are grounded in the "good of love" the faculty of understanding and knowing the nature of the Lord's New Church—both its <term>doctrine</term> <note>The systematic body of teachings or principles of the church.</note> and the introductory truths that lead into it, as well as the Word from which these are derived. 

"And he that spake with me" signifies the Lord speaking from heaven, because the angel mentioned was one of the seven angels who held the seven vials (mentioned previously in verse 9), which represents the Lord speaking from the heavens (see point 895). 

The **reed** signifies a power or faculty derived from the "good of love"; a **reed** represents power or ability (point 485), while **gold** represents the "good of love" (points 211, 726). To **measure** something signifies to know its quality, and thus to understand and recognize it (point 486). By the **city** (which was the holy Jerusalem), the text signifies the church in terms of its doctrine (points 879, 880). By the **gates** are signified the knowledge of truth and goodness found in the <term>literal sense</term> <note>The plain, surface-level meaning of the Bible's text, which contains deeper spiritual truths within it.</note> of the Word; because these contain spiritual life, they are considered true and good (point 899). Finally, by the **wall** is signified the Word in its literal sense, which serves as the foundation and protection of the church (point 898). 

From these points, it is clear that the phrase "he that spake with me had a golden reed, to measure the city and the gates thereof and the wall thereof," signifies that the Lord provides those who live in love the ability to understand and know the true quality of the New Church’s teachings.

...<insert>doc</insert>trine and its introductory truths, as well as the Word from which they originate. The fact that this is the meaning cannot be seen at all in the literal sense of the text; for on the surface, it only appears that the angel speaking with John used a golden reed to measure the city, its gates, and its wall. However, it is clear that there is another meaning within these things, which is the **spiritual sense** <note>The "spiritual sense" refers to a deeper, symbolic meaning within the Bible that relates to the inner life and the church, rather than just historical or physical events.</note>. This is evident because the "City of Jerusalem" does not refer to a physical city, but to the <term>church</term> <note>In this context, the "church" refers to the internal spiritual state of humanity and the organized body of religious teaching.</note>. Therefore, everything described regarding Jerusalem as a city actually symbolizes things belonging to the church, which are spiritual in their essence.

This same spiritual meaning is present in the words found earlier in chapter 11: *There was given to me a reed like a rod, and the angel stood, saying, "Rise and measure the temple of God, the altar, and those who worship there"* (verse 1). Similar spiritual meanings are found in all the measurements the angel took with a reed in the book of **Ezekiel** (chapters 40 to 48). We see this also in the book of **Zechariah**: *I lifted my eyes and saw, and behold, a man with a measuring line in his hand; and I said, "Where are you going?" and he said to me, "To measure Jerusalem, to see its width and its length"* (2:1, 2). Indeed, such a spiritual sense exists in all the details of the **Tabernacle** and the **Temple at Jerusalem** whose measurements we read about, and even in the specific numbers of those measures; yet none of this is visible in the literal meaning.

**905.** ***And the city lieth four square,*** signifies the quality of **justice** within it. The reason the city appeared quadrangular (square) is because a square symbolizes what is **just**, whereas a triangle symbolizes what is **right** <note>In the author's symbolic language, "just" often refers to the goodness of the heart, while "right" or "rectitude" refers to the accuracy of one's understanding.</note>. These shapes represent these qualities in their most external or <term>ultimate degree</term> <note>The "ultimate degree" refers to the natural or physical world, where spiritual principles take their final, concrete form.</note>. 

A square signifies justice because it has four sides, and these four sides face the **four quarters** <note>The four cardinal directions: North, South, East, and West.</note>. To face all four directions equally is to view all things from a perspective of justice. For this reason, three gates stood open into the city from each direction. It is as written in **Isaiah**: *Open the gates, so that the just nation which keeps the truth may enter* (26:2).

...must be the **good of love** <note>A state of being where one acts from selfless love toward others and God.</note>; it must be formed, and it is formed by the **truths of wisdom**. Therefore, it is described here as **"pure gold like unto pure glass."** This is because the **good of love** without the **truths of wisdom** has no distinct quality, because it has no form. Its form is determined by those truths in their proper order and connection, flowing together with the **good of love** from the Lord, and thus existing within a person according to how they receive it. It is said "within a person," but this does not mean it belongs to the person; rather, it belongs to the Lord within them. From this, it is now clear that the city being **pure gold like unto pure glass** signifies that everything within that church is the **good of love** flowing in with light out of heaven from the Lord.

913. **Gold** signifies the **good of love**, because metals—like everything else that appears in the natural world—have **correspondences** <note>Swedenborg’s theory that every physical thing reflects a spiritual reality; for example, a physical seed corresponds to a spiritual truth or idea.</note>:

*   **Gold** corresponds to the **good of love**
*   **Silver** corresponds to the **truths of wisdom**
*   **Copper** or **brass** corresponds to the **good of charity** <note>Acting with kindness and justice toward one’s neighbor.</note>
*   **Iron** corresponds to the **truths of faith**

Because of this, these metals also exist in the **spiritual world** <note>The dimension of existence where the soul goes after the death of the physical body.</note>; all things appearing there are correspondences, for they reflect the affections and the resulting thoughts of the angels, which are spiritual in their essence. That **gold**, through correspondence, signifies the **good of love** is evident from these passages:

*I counsel you to buy from Me **gold refined in the fire**, so that you may be rich* (Revelation 3:18). <note>original: "Apoc. iii. 18"</note>

*How the **gold** has become dim, and the **refined gold** changed! The **stones of holiness** are poured out at the head of every street; the sons of Zion were valued as equal to **pure gold*** (Lamentations 4:1–2).

*He shall save the souls of the poor, and shall give them the **gold of Sheba*** (Psalm 72:13, 15).

*For **brass** I will bring **gold**, and for **iron**, **silver**; for **wood**, **brass**, and for **stones**, **iron**; and I will make your officers peace, and your overseers justice* (Isaiah 60:17).

*Behold, you are wise; no secret lies hidden from you. With your **wisdom** and with your **understanding** you have acquired **gold and silver** in your treasuries; you have been in Eden; every **precious stone** was your covering, and **gold*** (Ezekiel 28:3, 4, 13).

*The multitude of camels shall cover...*

919. **And the city hath no need of the sun and of the moon to shine in it, for the glory of God did lighten it, and the lamp thereof is the Lamb,** signifies that the people of that church will not be driven by self-love or by their own cleverness, nor will they rely on natural light alone, but will live in spiritual light from the Divine Truth of the Word, which comes from the Lord alone. In this context, the "sun" signifies natural love when it is cut off from spiritual love—which is essentially the love of self. The "moon" signifies natural intelligence and faith when they are separate from spiritual intelligence and faith—meaning a person’s own cleverness and beliefs derived only from themselves. This kind of love, intelligence, and faith are symbolized here by the sun and the moon; their "shining" will not be needed by those who belong to the Lord’s New Church. The "glory of God" that brings light signifies the Divine Truth of the Word (n. 629). Since this enlightenment comes from the Lord, it is stated that "the lamp thereof is the Lamb." Similar meanings are found in these words from Isaiah: *Thou shalt call thy walls salvation, and thy gates praise; the sun shall be no more thy light by day, neither for brightness shall the moon give light unto thee; but Jehovah shall be unto thee an everlasting light, and thy God thy glory: thy sun shall no more go down, neither shall thy moon withdraw itself; for Jehovah shall be thine everlasting light; thy people shall be all righteous* (Isaiah 60:18–21). Here, the sun and moon that no longer give light represent self-love and one's own cleverness. Conversely, the "Sun and Moon" that never set represent love for the Lord (which comes from the Lord) and intelligence and faith from Him. Jehovah being an "everlasting light" carries the same meaning as the "glory of God" enlightening the city and the "Lamb" being its lamp. That the "sun" signifies love to the Lord, and in its opposite sense signifies the love of self, can be seen in earlier discussions (n. 53, 414); and

920. ***And the nations which are saved shall walk in the light of it,*** signifies that all who are in the <term>good of life</term> <note>The "good of life" refers to living according to one's conscience and religious principles through practical actions of kindness and service.</note> and believe in the Lord, will there live according to Divine truths, and will see them within in themselves, as the eye sees objects. To "walk in the light" signifies to live according to Divine truths, and to see them within in one's self, as the eye does objects: for the objects of the spiritual sight, which is that of the interior understanding, are spiritual truths; which are seen by those who are in that understanding, as natural objects are seen before the eyes. By "light" is signified here the perception of Divine Truth from interior enlightenment from the Lord in them (n. 796); and by "walking" is signified to live (n. 167). Hence it is manifest that by walking in the light of the New Jerusalem is signified to perceive and see Divine Truths from interior enlightenment, and to live according to them. <meta>This page continues the commentary on Chapter 21 of the Apocalypse, specifically elaborating on the requirements for entering the New Jerusalem. 1072

church and the good of religion, because the church is one thing and religion another. <note>The author distinguishes between the intellectual system of a faith and the actual practice of its tenets.</note> The church is called the church from its doctrine, and religion is called religion from a life lived according to that doctrine. Everything belonging to doctrine is called truth; and its good is likewise truth, because it only teaches what is good. However, everything of life lived according to the things which the doctrine teaches is called good; also, to act upon the truths of doctrine is good. This is the distinction between the church and religion. But still, where there is doctrine but no life, it cannot be said that there is either a church or a religion. This is because doctrine views the life as being one with itself—just like truth and good, or like faith and charity, wisdom and love, and like the understanding and the will. Therefore, where there is doctrine but no life, there is no church.

924. **And there shall not enter into it any thing unclean, and that doeth abomination and a lie**, signifies that no one is received into the Lord’s New Church (which is the New Jerusalem) who adulterates the goods and falsifies the truths of the Word, and who performs evils from a place of confirmation, and thus also falsifies. <note>In this context, "confirmation" refers to the internal process of justifying one's wrong actions or false beliefs until they are fully accepted as right or true.</note> By "not entering in" is signified not being received, as stated above. By "unclean" is signified spiritual whoredom, <note>original: "scortatio spiritualis"</note> <note>This term refers to the corruption or "prostitution" of sacred truths for selfish or worldly ends.</note> which is the adulteration of the good and the falsification of the truth of the Word (see numbers 702 and 728); for this is uncleanness and impurity itself. This is because the Word is cleanness itself and purity itself, and it is defiled by evils and falsities when it is perverted. That adultery and whoredom correspond to the adulteration of the good and the falsification of the truth of the Word may be seen in numbers 134 and 632. By "doing abomination and a lie" is signified to do evils and thus also falsities. By abominations are signified evils of every kind, especially those which are named in the <term>Decalogue</term> <note>The Ten Commandments.</note> (number 891); and by a lie is signified falsities of every kind—here specifically the falsities of evil, which in themselves are evils, and thus falsities that confirm evil; these are the same as confirmed evils.

It also interprets the biblical exclusion of the "unclean" from the New Jerusalem as a rejection of those who intentionally corrupt spiritual truths or justify immoral behavior.</summary>

To this I will add this **RELATION**. <note>Swedenborg used the term "Relation" (Latin: *Memorabile*) to denote first-hand accounts of his visions and interactions within the spiritual world.</note> When I was upon the explanation of chapter xx., and was meditating about the dragon, the beast, and the false prophet, a certain one appeared to me, and asked, "What are you meditating upon?" I said that it was upon the <term>false prophet</term>. <note>In Swedenborg’s interpretation, the "false prophet" represents those who distort religious teachings to justify a life without good works.</note> He then said to me, "I will lead you to the place where they are who are meant by the false prophet." He said that they were the same as are meant in chapter xiii. by the beast out of the earth, which had two horns like a lamb, and spoke as a dragon. I followed him; and behold, I saw a multitude, in the midst of which were bishops, who taught that nothing else saves man but faith; and that works are good, but not for salvation; and that still they are to be taught from the Word, that the laity, especially the simple, may be held the more strictly in the bonds of obedience to the magistrates, and as from religion, and thus interiorly, may be compelled to exercise <term>moral charity</term>. <note>Here, "moral charity" refers to outward good behavior used as a tool for social control rather than a sincere spiritual practice.</note> And then one of them, seeing me, said, "Do you wish to see our Temple in which there is an image representative of our Faith?" 

I drew near, and saw; and behold, it was magnificent, and in the midst of it the image of a Woman, clothed in a scarlet garment, <note>Scarlet in the Apocalypse often symbolizes the external appearance of sanctity masking inner corruption.</note> and holding a golden coin in the right hand; and in the left a chain of large pearls. But both the temple and the image were produced by <term>fantasies</term>, <note>In Swedenborg's vocabulary, "fantasies" are spiritual illusions or hallucinations projected by spirits to make their surroundings look beautiful or powerful to those who share their delusions.</note> for infernal spirits can by fantasies represent magnificent things, by closing up the interiors of the mind and opening only its exteriors. 

But when I noticed that they were such illusions, I prayed to the Lord, and suddenly the <term>interiors</term> <note>The "interiors" refer to the higher levels of the human mind capable of perceiving spiritual truth.</note> of my mind were opened; and I then saw in place of the magnificent temple a house full of chinks from the top to the bottom, in which nothing held together; and instead of a woman I saw hanging in that house an image, the head of which was like a dragon's, the body like a leopard's, and the feet like a bear's, thus like the description of the beast out of the sea (<note>original: "Apoc. xiii." (Revelation chapter 13)</note>); and instead of the floor was

### THE SPIRITUAL SENSE.

**THE CONTENTS OF THE WHOLE CHAPTER.** The Church is still described in terms of the intelligence it receives from Divine truths, which come from the Word through the Lord (verses 1–5). It is stated that the Apocalypse <note>The word "Apocalypse" comes from the Greek *apokalypsis*, meaning "unveiling" or "revelation."</note> was made manifest by the Lord, and that it is destined to be revealed at its proper time (verses 6–10). Concerning the coming of the Lord, and His conjunction <note>In this context, "conjunction" refers to a spiritual marriage or deep internal connection between God and humanity.</note> with those who believe in Him and live according to His precepts (verses 11–17). It is emphasized that the things which are revealed must by all means be preserved and kept (verses 18, 19). The Betrothal (verses 17, 20, 21).

**THE CONTENTS OF EACH VERSE.** “And he showed me a pure river of water of life, clear as crystal, proceeding out of the throne of God and of the Lamb,” *signifies* <note>The term "signifies" is used here to indicate the transition from the literal image to its internal, spiritual meaning.</note> the Apocalypse now opened and explained as to its spiritual sense, where Divine Truths in abundance are revealed by the Lord for those who will belong to His New Church, which is the New Jerusalem. “In the midst of the street of it, and of the river, on this side and on that, was the tree of life, bearing twelve fruits,” *signifies* that in the inmost parts of the truths of doctrine—and thus of life in the New Church—is the Lord in His Divine Love, from Whom all the good actions which a person performs (appearing as if from themselves) actually flow. “Yielding its fruit every month,” *signifies* that the Lord produces good in man according to every state of truth within him. “And the leaves of the tree were for the healing of the nations,” *signifies* rational truths derived from that source, by which those who are in evils and consequent falsehoods are led to think soundly and to live becomingly. “And no accursed thing shall be there; and the throne of God and of the Lamb shall be in it, and His servants shall minister unto Him,” *signifies* that in the Church which is the New Jerusalem, there will not be any who are separated from the Lord, because the Lord Himself will reign there, and

"...servant, and of thy brethren the prophets, and of them that keep the words of this book, worship God," *signifies* that the angels of heaven are not to be worshipped and invoked, because nothing Divine belongs to them; but that they are associated with men as brethren with brethren, specifically with those who follow the doctrine of the New Jerusalem <note>The "New Jerusalem" refers to a new spiritual era or a New Church based on the teachings revealed in this work.</note> and live by its precepts; it also signifies that the Lord alone is to be worshipped in company with them. 

"And he said unto me, Seal not the words of this prophecy, for the time is at hand," *signifies* that the Apocalypse <note original: "Apocalypsis">Meaning "the uncovering" or "revelation."</note> must not be hidden or closed up, but is to be opened and made understood; and that this is necessary at the end of the Church so that anyone may be saved. 

"He that is unjust, let him be unjust still; and he that is filthy, let him be filthy still; and he that is just, let him be just still; and he that is holy let him be holy still," *signifies* the state of every individual after death and before their judgment—and generally before the Last Judgment <note>In this context, the "Last Judgment" is viewed as a spiritual event that sorts the inner qualities of those in the spiritual world.</note>. It means that goodness will be taken away from those who are in evil, and truths will be taken away from those who are in falsehoods; conversely, evils will be removed from those who are in goodness, and falsities will be removed from those who are in truths. 

"And behold, I come quickly, and my reward is with Me, to render to every one according as his work shall be," *signifies* that the Lord will certainly come, and that He Himself is heaven and the source of eternal happiness for everyone, according to their faith in Him and how they have lived according to His commandments. 

"I am the Alpha and the Omega, the Beginning and the End, the First and the Last," *signifies* <note original: "Alpha et Omega">These are the first and last letters of the Greek alphabet. In this context, they represent the Lord as the God of the entire universe, from the very first cause to the final effect.</note> that the Lord is the God of heaven and earth, and that by Him all things in the heavens and on earth were created, are governed by His Divine Providence, and occur according to it. 

"Blessed are they that do His commandments, that they may have right to the tree of life, and may enter in through the gates into the city," *signifies* that those who live according to the Lord's precepts enjoy eternal happiness, for the purpose that they may live in the Lord and the Lord in them through love, and that they may belong to His New Church <note>The "New Church" is the spiritual community of those who worship the Lord and live a life of charity.</note>.

By the pure river of water of life clear as crystal, is signified the Divine Truth of the Word in abundance translucent from its spiritual sense, which is in the light of heaven. *...the water that I shall give him, shall never thirst; but the water that I shall give him shall be in him a fountain of water springing up into everlasting life* (John 4:14). *I will give unto him that is athirst of the water of life freely* (Revelation 21:6; 22:17). *And the Lamb who is in the midst of the throne shall feed them, and shall lead them unto living fountains of waters* (Revelation 7:17). *In that day shall living waters go out from Jerusalem; Jehovah shall be King over all the earth; in that day shall Jehovah be one, and His name one* (Zechariah 14:8, 9). By "living waters," or "waters of life," the Lord signifies **Divine Truths** coming from Him.

933. **In the midst of the street of it and of the river, on this side and on that, was the tree of life bearing twelve fruits**, signifies that in the deepest parts <note>original: "inmosts"</note> of the truths of doctrine—and therefore in the life of the church—is the Lord in His **Divine Love**. It is from this Love that all the "good works" that a person appears to do by their own effort actually flow. 

By "in the midst" is signified the center or inmost heart of a thing, which then influences everything around it (see paragraph numbers <note>The "n." followed by a number refers to specific cross-references in the author's theological system.</note> 44, 383). By "street" is signified the truth of the church's **doctrine** <note>The formal teachings or system of beliefs held by the church.</note> (n. 501, 917). By "the river" is signified **Divine Truth** in great abundance (n. 409, 932). 

"On this side and on that" signifies on the right and on the left. In the spiritual layout of heaven, truth on the right is in "clearness" (bright light), while truth on the left is in "obscurity" (dimmer light). This is because the "south" in heaven, which represents clear truth, is to the right; and the "north," representing obscure truth, is to the left (n. 901). 

By "the tree of life" is signified the Lord in terms of His **Divine Love** (n. 89). By "fruits" are signified the "goods" of love and **charity** <note>Active neighborly love or good-heartedness in practice.</note>, which are commonly called "good works"; these are explained further in the next paragraph. By "twelve" is signified "all," and it is a number specifically used when talking about the various goods and truths of the church (n. 348). 

When these pieces are brought together into a single meaning, it follows that the phrase "in the midst of the street and of the river, on this side and on that, was the tree of life bearing twelve fruits" means that at the very heart of the church's teachings and the life of its members is the Lord in His Divine Love, from Whom all...

<meta>This page continues the internal spiritual explanation of Revelation 22:2. It focuses on how spiritual "goodness"—the helpful things people do—originates from the Lord and flows outward from the center of a person's life. It emphasizes that a direct relationship with the Lord and the practice of His commandments are essential for this spiritual growth.</meta>

<page-num>1086</page-num>
<header>THE APOCALYPSE REVEALED. [CHAP. XXII.]</header>

the good deeds that a person does seemingly by their own effort actually flow from Him. This happens for those who approach the Lord directly and avoid evil actions because they are sins; thus, it applies to those who will be part of the Lord’s New Church <note>Swedenborg uses "New Church" or "New Jerusalem" to describe a new spiritual state of humanity based on direct love and truth.</note>, which is the New Jerusalem. Those who do not go directly to the Lord cannot be spiritually united to Him, and therefore cannot be united to the Father. Consequently, they cannot live in a state of love that comes from the Divine. Simply thinking about God is not enough to create this connection; it requires a mental focus that springs from the heart's desire. Such a desire of the heart is only possible when a person keeps His commandments. This is why the Lord says: *He that keepeth my commandments, he it is that loveth me; and I will come unto him, and make an abode with him* (John 14:21–24).

It is said that these things reside in the deepest parts <note>original: "inmosts"</note> of the truths of doctrine <note>The underlying principles or system of religious teaching.</note> and, consequently, in the life of the New Church. This is because, in spiritual matters, everything originates and flows from the center—the deepest heart—out toward the outer layers, much like fire and light radiate from a center point to the surrounding area, or how heat and light from the sun flow into the universe. This process is the same in the smallest details as it is in the largest systems. Because this represents the deepest heart of all truth, the text says "in the midst of the street and of the river," rather than "on both sides of the river," even though that is the implied meaning. That all the "goodness" of love and charity comes from the Lord—provided He is at the center of one's life—is clear from the Lord's own words in the Gospel of John: *As the branch cannot bear fruit of itself, except it abide in the vine, so neither can ye, except ye abide in Me: I am the Vine, ye are the branches; he that abideth in Me, and I in him, the same bringeth forth much fruit; for without Me ye can do nothing* (John 15:4–6).

934. **That fruits signify the goods** <note>In this context, "goods" refers to the beneficial actions and kind intentions a person carries out.</note> **which man does from love or charity**, is a concept easily understood even without looking for confirmation in the Bible; for any reader understands "fruit" in the Word to mean the results of a good life. The reason that the "goodness" of love or charity is meant by "fruits" is that a human being is often compared to a tree, and is even called a tree in various passages (see paragraph numbers 89, 400). ### THE APOCALYPSE REVEALED. [CHAP. XXII.]

It will now be explained how we should understand that the Lord produces the goods of charity within a person according to the state of truth they possess. Anyone who believes that a person can do good that is acceptable to the Lord—which is called **spiritual good**—without having truths from the Word within them, is greatly mistaken. Good deeds without truths are not truly "good," and truths without good are not truly "truths" in a person, even though they may be true in an abstract sense.

This is because good without truth is like the <term>voluntary<gloss>The faculty of the mind associated with the will and desires.</gloss></term> of a person without the <term>intellectual<gloss>The faculty of the mind associated with thought, reason, and understanding.</gloss></term>. Such a will is not conscious; it is like the instinct of a beast, or like a carved statue that a craftsman causes to move. However, the will and the understanding together become truly human according to the state of the understanding through which the will exists. Every person's state of life is such that their will cannot do anything except through the understanding, nor can the understanding think anything except from the will. It is the same with **good** and **truth**, since good belongs to the will and truth belongs to the understanding.

From this, it is clear that the good which the Lord produces in a person is determined by the state of truth in them, which forms their understanding. The reason this is signified by "the tree of life yielding its fruit every month" is that "month" signifies the state of truth in a person. That states of life are signified by various measures of time—such as hours, days, weeks, months, years, and ages—can be seen in earlier sections <note>The author refers to his own cross-references: numbers 476 and 562.</note>. The reason that states of life regarding *truths* are specifically signified by "months" is that months are determined by the moon; in spiritual symbolism, the **moon** signifies the truth of the understanding and of faith <note>See references 332, 413, 414, and 919.</note>. Similar meanings for "months" can be found in these passages:

> *Blessed of Jehovah is the land of Joseph for the precious things of the produce of the sun, and for the precious things of the produce of the months* (Deuteronomy 33:14). <note>The "produce of the sun" refers to goods of love, while "produce of the months" refers to truths from the Word.</note>
> 
> *It shall come to pass that from month to month, and from sabbath to sabbath, all flesh shall come to bow themselves down before Jehovah* (Isaiah 66:23).

936. **And the leaves of the tree were for the healing of the nations**, signifies rational truths derived from that Word, by which those who are in evils and the resulting falsities are led to think soundly and to live in a becoming manner. By the "leaves of the tree" are signified rational truths <note>In this context, rational truths refer to ideas that appeal to human reason and common sense, serving as a bridge to deeper spiritual understanding.</note>, as discussed below. By "the nations," those who are in states of good and the resulting truths are signified—and in the opposite sense, those who are in evils and the resulting falsities (n. 483). Here, "nations" refers to those in evils and falsities, because the text mentions "the healing of the nations." Those who are in evils and falsities cannot be healed directly by the Word because they do not read it; however, if they possess sound judgment, they can be healed by rational truths. 

Similar things to those in this verse are signified by these words in Ezekiel: *Behold, waters went forth from under the threshold, from which was a river, upon whose bank on this side and on that were very many trees for food, whose leaf falls not, nor is consumed; it is renewed every month, whence its fruit is for food, and its leaf for medicine* (Ezekiel 47:1, 7, 12). That passage also treats the New Church <note>The "New Church" refers to a new spiritual era or a renewed state of religious understanding and life.</note>. 

The reason that rational truths are signified by "leaves" is because all parts of a tree correspond to specific aspects of a person, such as the branches, leaves, flowers, fruits, and seeds. By the **branches**, a person's <term>sensual<gloss>Related to the immediate perception of the five senses.</gloss></term> and natural truths are signified; by the **leaves**, their rational truths; by the **flowers**, the first spiritual truths within the rational mind; by the **fruits**, the goods of love and charity; and by the **seeds** are signified the ultimate and primary things of a person. A man not rational is nothing else but such a tree. 

**Rational truths** <note>These are ideas that align with common sense and logic, serving as the bridge through which higher spiritual insights can enter human understanding.</note> are those which proximately receive spiritual truths, for the rational of man is the first receptacle of spiritual truths: for in man's rational is the perception of truth in some form, which the man himself does not see in thought, as he does the things which are beneath the rational in the lower thought, which conjoins itself with the external sight. Rational truths are also signified by leaves (Genesis 3:7; 8:11; Isaiah 34:4; Jeremiah 8:13; 17:8; Ezekiel 47:12; Daniel 4:12, 14; Psalms 1:3; Leviticus 26:36; Matthew 21:19; 24:32; Mark 13:28). 

But their signification is according to the species of the trees. The leaves of the **olive** and the **vine** signify rational truths from heavenly and spiritual light; the leaves of the **fig**, rational truths from natural light; and the leaves of the **fir**, the **poplar**, the **oak**, the **pine**, rational truths from **sensual light** <note>Sensual light refers to a way of thinking based entirely on the physical senses and outward appearances.</note>. The leaves of these strike terror in the spiritual world, when they are shaken by a strong wind: these are meant in Leviticus 26:36 and Job 13:25. But it is not so with the leaves of the former.

# No. 943.] THE APOCALYPSE REVEALED

[The word ser-]vants refers to those who live in truths that come from the Lord <note>original: "n. 3, 380, 937" refers to specific paragraph numbers in this work</note>. By the word "shortly" is meant "certainly" (n. 4). Therefore, the phrase "things which must shortly be done" refers to events that will certainly come to pass. 

The reason an angel here represents heaven is that the Lord spoke to John through heaven, just as He spoke through heaven to the ancient prophets. In fact, whenever the Lord speaks to anyone, He speaks through heaven. This is because the entire angelic heaven, in a general sense, is like one single man whose soul and life is the Lord Himself. For this reason, everything the Lord speaks, He speaks through heaven, much like a person’s soul and mind speak through their physical body. 

That the entire angelic heaven together resembles one man—and that this comes from the Lord—can be seen in earlier sections (n. 5), as well as in the book *Heaven and Hell*, published in London in 1758 (n. 59–86). It is also discussed in <term>Divine Providence</term><note>Referring to Swedenborg's work *Angelic Wisdom concerning the Divine Providence*.</note> (n. 64–69, 162–164, 201–204) and in <term>Divine Love and Wisdom</term><note>Referring to Swedenborg's work *Angelic Wisdom concerning the Divine Love and Divine Wisdom*.</note> (n. 11, 19, 133, 288).

However, I will explain this mystery. While the Lord speaks through heaven, the angels there do not actually speak the words themselves. In fact, they do not even know what the Lord is saying unless they are specifically present with the person to whom the Lord is speaking directly from heaven, as happened with John and some of the prophets. This happens because there is an <term>influx</term><note>The spiritual process by which life or thought flows from a higher level (like the soul or the spiritual world) into a lower level (the body or the natural world).</note> from the Lord through heaven, similar to how the soul flows into the body. The body certainly speaks and acts, and even feels something of this flow, yet the body does not do anything on its own; it is acted upon. 

I have been allowed to know through much personal experience that this is how speech—and indeed all the Lord's influence through heaven—works with human beings. The angels in heaven, and even the spirits below them, know nothing about humanity, just as humanity knows nothing about them. This is because the state of spirits and angels is spiritual, while the state of human beings is natural. These two distinct states are joined together solely through <term>correspondences</term><note>The symbolic and functional relationship between the spiritual and natural worlds.</note>; and this associa-

# THE APOCALYPSE REVEALED. [CHAP. XXII]

Communication through <term>correspondences</term><note>A central concept in Swedenborg’s theology: the relationship between the spiritual world and the natural world, where every physical thing reflects a spiritual reality.</note> brings spirits and humans together in their affections, but not in their thoughts. For this reason, one is not consciously aware of the other. In other words, a person knows nothing of the spirits with whom they are connected through their feelings, and spirits know nothing of the person. This is because anything that exists only in the affection, and not in the conscious thought, does not appear and remains unseen. The Lord alone knows the thoughts of all people.

**944.** *Behold, I come quickly; blessed is he that keepeth the words of this prophecy*, signifies that the Lord will certainly come and will grant eternal life to those who observe and practice the truths and precepts found in the teachings of this book, which have now been opened by the Lord. "Behold, I come quickly," signifies that the Lord's coming is certain. In this context, "quickly" means "certainly" (see n. 4, 943). His "coming" does not mean a physical appearance in person, but His presence in **the Word**, where He will be revealed to everyone who belongs to His <term>New Church</term><note>Refers to the new spiritual era or community that Swedenborg believed was beginning through his revelations.</note>. That this is the true meaning of His "coming in the clouds of heaven" can be seen in earlier sections (n. 24, 642, 820).

"Blessed is he that keepeth the words of this book" signifies that He will give eternal life to those who follow the truths and instructions in these teachings. To be "blessed" means to receive eternal life (n. 639, 852). To "keep" means to observe and live by those truths; the "words" are the truths and precepts themselves. "The prophecy of this book" refers to the teaching of this book, which the Lord has now made clear; "prophecy" signifies teaching or doctrine (n. 8, 133, 943). 

Anyone who reflects on this can see that "keeping the words of the prophecy" does not mean memorizing the text itself. Rather, it means observing and putting into practice the truths and spiritual laws explained in this book. Without this explanation, the Book of Revelation contains very little that a person could actually "keep" or live by, as these prophecies have not been understood until now. For example, one cannot "keep" the descriptions in Chapter 6 regarding the horses that emerged from the book; those things...

<meta>This page continues the interpretation of Revelation 22:10, specifically explaining how spiritual concepts of time and space differ from physical ones, and why the Apocalypse must be "unsealed" or explained for the sake of human salvation.</meta>

<page-num>1105</page-num>

->No. 947.] THE APOCALYPSE REVEALED. 1105<-

be illustrated. The <term>Word</term> <note>The Bible or Divine Revelation.</note> in the <term>purely spiritual sense</term> <note>A deeper level of meaning within the Bible that relates entirely to the soul and heaven, rather than physical things.</note> derives nothing from the idea of time, nor from the idea of space; because although times and spaces do appear in heaven just as they do in the world, they do not actually exist there. For this reason, the angels cannot measure time and space—which are only appearances in their world—in any way other than by <term>states</term> <note>In this context, "states" refers to the internal condition of a person's mind or heart, such as their level of love or wisdom, which changes like the seasons or times of day.</note>, as these progress and change. From this it is clear that in the purely spiritual sense, the words "quickly" and "at hand" do not refer to the speed or nearness of time, but to the speed and nearness of a state of being. 

This may indeed seem as if it were not the case. The reason is that in every idea of a person’s lower thought, which is merely natural, there is always something involving time and space. It is different in the "higher thought," which people experience when they consider natural, civic, moral, and spiritual matters in the light of their inner reason; for then spiritual light, which is separate from time and space, flows in and provides enlightenment. You can test this yourself and confirm it if you wish, provided you pay close attention to your own thoughts. You will then also be confirmed in the fact that there is both a "higher" and a "lower" thought; for simple, lower thought cannot examine itself except from a higher perspective.
